### Printed p. 137  (PDF 155)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 4, continued.)*

In this ṛk the presiding deities of night and of early morning, called नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*), are invoked. Yāska's explanation of the word नक्तोषसा (*naktoṣasā*) is as follows:

> उषासानक्ता । उषासानक्तोषाश्च नक्ता चोषा व्याख्याता । नक्तेति रात्रिनामानक्ति भूतान्यवश्यायेनापि वा नक्ताव्यक्तवर्णा ॥

> *uṣāsānaktā | uṣāsānaktoṣāśca naktā coṣā vyākhyātā | nakteti rātrināmānakti bhūtānyavaśyāyenāpi vā naktāvyaktavarṇā ‖*

Although it is read in two ways, नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*) and उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*), the meaning is one and the same. We have already given the explanation of the word उषाः (*uṣāḥ*) earlier. नक्ता (*naktā*) is a name of night. For नक्ता (*naktā*) means अव्यक्तवर्णा (*avyaktavarṇā*): because it is dark, things are unmanifest, that is, they are not seen well. Therefore night, joined with darkness, has the name नक्ता (*naktā*). And in this night-time creatures are unable to carry on their several activities. अनक्ति, क्लेदयति भूतानि अवश्यायेन इति । अपि वा नक्ता अव्यक्तवर्णा । यथा अहः सर्वमभिव्यक्तरूपं भवति न तथा रात्रिः ॥ (*anakti, kledayati bhūtāni avaśyāyena iti | api vā naktā avyaktavarṇā | yathā ahaḥ sarvamabhivyaktarūpaṃ bhavati na tathā rātriḥ ‖*) Because darkness hinders creatures so that there is no room for their activities to go on properly, night joined with such darkness has the name नक्ता (*naktā*). Or, because it is unmanifest so that nothing is seen well, it has the name नक्ता (*naktā*). In the day the forms of all things are seen clearly; in the night they are not seen so. Therefore (Yāska) has explained that night-time has the name नक्ता (*naktā*) (Ni. 8-11, zoomed).

(Yāska) has said that the explanation of the word उषाः (*uṣāḥ*) has already been given earlier. That explanation is as follows: the sixteen words beginning with विभावरी (*vibhāvarī*), सूदरी (*sūdarī*) (so printed, zoomed) are names of the dawn (Ni. 2-19, zoomed), and

> उषाः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः ॥

> *uṣāḥ kasmāducchatīti satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ ‖*

Because it removes the darkness of night-time it has the name उषाः (*uṣāḥ*); that is, it is the latter time, the last part, of the night. To support this meaning he has given an example:

> इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागाच्चित्रः प्रकेतो अजनिष्ट विभ्वा ।
> यथा प्रसूता सवितुः सवायँ एवा रात्र्युषसे योनिमारैक् ॥

> *idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāgāccitraḥ praketo ajaniṣṭa vibhvā |*
> *yathā prasūtā savituḥ savāya~ evā rātryuṣase yonimāraik ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-1, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "This best light of lights has come; the bright sign has been born, far-reaching. As (night) is brought forth for the impulse of Savitṛ, so night has vacated her place for the dawn.")

The Nirukta of this ṛk:

> इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागमत् । चित्रं प्रकेतनं प्रज्ञाततममजनिष्ट विभूततमं यथा प्रसूता सवितुः प्रसवाय रात्रिरादित्यस्य

> *idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāgamat | citraṃ praketanaṃ prajñātatamamajaniṣṭa vibhūtatamaṃ yathā prasūtā savituḥ prasavāya rātrirādityasya*

*(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 138  (PDF 156)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 4, continued: the Nirukta passage concluded.)*

> एवं रात्र्युषसे योनिमरिचत् स्थानं । स्त्रीयोनिरभियुत एनां गर्भः ॥

> *evaṃ rātryuṣase yonimaricat sthānaṃ | strīyonirabhiyuta enāṃ garbhaḥ ‖*

The excellent and exceedingly brilliant light of the sun is rising. The dawn-time, which comes before such light of the sun, appears in advance of the light like the निकेतन (*niketana*) (like the banner) of that light. Just as the sun's light, having shone all through the day, at the time of setting becomes the योनि (*yoni*), that is, the cause, of night, so night at the time of its end becomes the योनि (*yoni*), that is, the cause, of dawn-time; योनि (*yoni*) means the place of birth. The chief intention is that at the end of the day night, and at the end of night dawn, come one after the other in the form of a cycle. Therefore उषः (*uṣaḥ*) means the light, the brightness, which appears pervading all the quarters before sunrise, after night has passed.

The commentator's (Sāyaṇa's) explanation is: नक्तशब्दः उषश्शब्दश्च लोके कालविशेषवाचिनौ । इह तु तत्कालाभिमानिवह्निमूर्तिद्वये प्रयुज्येते । नक्तोषासा नक्तोषोनामिके वह्निमूर्ती (*naktaśabdaḥ uṣaśśabdaśca loke kālaviśeṣavācinau | iha tu tatkālābhimānivahnimūrtidvaye prayujyete | naktoṣāsā naktoṣonāmike vahnimūrtī*) — that is, the two words नक्त (*nakta*) (night) and उषः (*uṣaḥ*) (morning) have in worldly usage the sense of denoting the particular times called night and morning. Here, that is, in this ṛk or in the Ṛgveda, these words convey the sense of the deities presiding over night and morning-time. Therefore the words नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*) or उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) are used in the sense of the two forms (shapes) of Agni, the deities presiding over night and dawn-time. The word सुपेशसा (*supeśasā*) ("having a good form or shape") used in this ṛk supports this meaning *(so printed; the word does not stand in the Saṃhitā of Ṛk 4)*. For night and morning, being divisions of time, have neither form nor shape. On the view that they are called the deities presiding over those times, a form can be ascribed to those deities. Since in this ṛk there is such an ascription, it should be understood that here the deities presiding over those times are meant. In the word नक्तोषसा (*naktoṣasā*) (so printed here) the syllable ṣa is long for the convenience of the metre.

सुदुघेव धेनुः (*sudugheva dhenuḥ*) — When the ṛṣi, addressing the deities, says "I wish to come near you", he has given a simile for it. The meaning of the simile is explained thus: just as a cow that yields milk well, as soon as it becomes evening, leaves its grazing outside and comes to its owner's house.

ईषे (*īṣe*) — The commentator's explanation is that the word ईषे (*īṣe*) may be formed either from the root इष गतौ (*iṣa gatau*), which has the sense of going, or from the root ईष (*īṣa*), which gives the same sense. ईषे (*īṣe*) means इच्छामि (*icchāmi*), "I desire", or "I desire to come near (you)".

### Printed p. 139  (PDF 157)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 4, continued.)*

समाने पयसि ऊधन् विषुरूपे (*samāne payasi ūdhan viṣurūpe*) — Two kinds of meaning are possible for these words. The commentator has explained that one meaning is possible, "milk, curds, ghee, oblation and the like, of various kinds, from the milk drawn on one and the same day", and another meaning, "in the sacrifice whose fruit is milk itself, joined with milk-preparations of various kinds, that is, joined with Soma juices (गवाशिर (*gavāśira*), दध्याशिर (*dadhyāśira*) and the like)". The chief intention is this: although milk of one kind is produced at one time from the udders of all the cows, it takes different forms such as milk, curds and ghee. The ṛṣi describes (himself as saying): "Reciting a hymn which is the means to food in the form of caru, puroḍāśa and the like joined with such milk-preparations, or to the Soma juice, I shall come near you."

विषुरूपे (*viṣurūpe*) — नानारूपे (*nānārūpe*) — "having many forms"; that is, although the milk is one, the things produced from it — milk, curds, ghee — are of many kinds.

अर्कं (*arkaṃ*) — With अन्नसाधनं स्तोत्रं (*annasādhanaṃ stotraṃ*) the commentator has here given the word अर्क (*arka*) the meaning "food". Yāska in his Nirukta —

> अर्को देवो भवति यदेनमर्चंति ।
> अर्को मंत्रो भवति यदनेनार्चंति ।
> अर्कमन्नं भवत्यर्चति भूतानि ।
> अर्को वृक्षो भवति संवृत्तः कटुकिम्ना ।

> *arko devo bhavati yadenamarcaṃti |*
> *arko maṃtro bhavati yadanenārcaṃti |*
> *arkamannaṃ bhavatyarcati bhūtāni |*
> *arko vṛkṣo bhavati saṃvṛttaḥ kaṭukimnā |*

(Ni. 5-4, zoomed; first digit the same glyph as the header's Adhyāya 5) — has thus given four kinds of derivation for the word अर्क (*arka*). That is: (1) देवः । तावत्सर्व एवार्क इत्युच्यते यत्-यस्मात् एनं देवं अर्चंति स्तोतारः । (*devaḥ | tāvatsarva evārka ityucyate yat-yasmāt enaṃ devaṃ arcaṃti stotāraḥ |*) अर्क (*arka*) means a deity; because the person whom the devotees use this to worship, or the god — that is, the object the devotee worships (the deity) — has the name अर्क (*arka*).

(2) अर्को मंत्रो भवति । यत् यस्मात् अनेन मंत्रेण अर्चंति स्तोतारः तस्मादर्कः । (*arko maṃtro bhavati | yat yasmāt anena maṃtreṇa arcaṃti stotāraḥ tasmādarkaḥ |*) अर्क (*arka*) also has the meaning "mantra". For those who praise worship the deity with this (with the अर्क (*arka*), the ṛk, the mantra). Therefore the word अर्क (*arka*) also has the name "mantra".

(3) अर्कमन्नं भवति । तद्धि अर्चति भूतानि, यो हि पूज्यः तस्यान्नमपि संस्कारविशेषेण संस्कृतं पूजायां क्रियते, पूज्यं च सर्वस्यैवान्नं । (*arkamannaṃ bhavati | taddhi arcati bhūtāni, yo hi pūjyaḥ tasyānnamapi saṃskāraviśeṣeṇa saṃskṛtaṃ pūjāyāṃ kriyate, pūjyaṃ ca sarvasyaivānnaṃ |*) अर्क (*arka*) also has the meaning "food". Because food (nourishment) is necessary for all living beings, food *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 140  (PDF 158)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 4, continued: Yāska's third derivation concluded.)*

… all respect and desire it. That is, because all desire it, honouring it with affection and regard, the word अर्क (*arka*) also has the meaning "food".

(4) अर्को वृक्षो भवति य एष प्रसिद्धः । संवृत्तः हि संगतः संव्याप्तः कटुकिम्ना कटुकभावेन भवति । (*arko vṛkṣo bhavati ya eṣa prasiddhaḥ | saṃvṛttaḥ hi saṃgataḥ saṃvyāptaḥ kaṭukimnā kaṭukabhāvena bhavati |*) Further, a name of the word अर्क (*arka*) for a kind of tree is indeed well known. The अर्क (*arka*) tree is called the *ekkada giḍa* in the Kannada language. Because its sacrificial sticks (samit) are used in homas, and because there is the custom of using it in medicines and the like, the अर्क (*arka*) tree is a thing known to all. Because it is bitter, they say कटुकिम्ना (*kaṭukimnā*) ("by its bitterness").

As an example for the explanation of the word अर्क (*arka*), Yāska has cited the ṛk गायंति त्वा (*gāyaṃti tvā*) and has given its explanation (nirvacana); as that is not necessary here, it has not been explained. (See Ṛ. Saṃ. Bhāga 2, pages 385, zoomed.)

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly; numerals read unzoomed). ईषे (*īṣe*) — root इष गतौ (*iṣa gatau*); by छंदसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः (*chaṃdasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*) liṭ in the sense of the present, first-person singular; nighāta accent because it stands after a non-tiṅanta (a word that is not a finite verb). जिगीषा (*jigīṣā*) — desiderative of जि जये (*ji jaye*) by धातोः कर्मणः समान- (*dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samāna-*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-7), reduplication, lengthening by अज्झनगमां सनि (*ajjhanagamāṃ sani*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-16), ku-substitution by सन्लिटोर्जेः (*sanliṭorjeḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-57), the affix a by अप्रत्ययात् (*apratyayāt*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-102), ṭāp, instrumental elided by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*). उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) — उषासोषसः (*uṣāsoṣasaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-31), देवताद्वंद्वे च (*devatādvaṃdve ca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-141). अहन् (*ahan*) — locative elided by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*); न ङिसंबुद्ध्योः (*na ṅisaṃbuddhyoḥ*) blocks loss of n. विमिमानः (*vimimānaḥ*) — root माङ् माने (*māṅ māne*), śānac, reduplication, भृञामित् (*bhṛñāmit*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-76), अभ्यस्तानामादिः (*abhyastānāmādiḥ*) … *(continues on the next page)*

## Sūkta 186, Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उत नोऽहिर्बुध्न्यो३ मयस्कः शिशुं न पिप्युषीव वेति सिंधुः ।
> येन नपातमपां जुनाम मनोजुवो वृषणो यं वहंति ॥ ५ ॥

> *uta no 'hirbudhnyo3 mayaskaḥ śiśuṃ na pipyuṣīva veti siṃdhuḥ |*
> *yena napātamapāṃ junāma manojuvo vṛṣaṇo yaṃ vahaṃti ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उत । नः । अहिः । बुध्न्यः । मयः । करिति कः । शिशुं । न । पिप्युषीऽइव । वेति । सिंधुः ।
> येन । नपातं । अपां । जुनाम । मनःऽजुवः । वृषणः । यं । वहंति ॥ ५ ॥

> *uta | naḥ | ahiḥ | budhnyaḥ | mayaḥ | kariti kaḥ | śiśuṃ | na | pipyuṣī 'iva | veti | siṃdhuḥ |*
> *yena | napātaṃ | apāṃ | junāma | manaḥ 'juvaḥ | vṛṣaṇaḥ | yaṃ | vahaṃti ‖ 5 ‖*

*(Pada: कः (*kaḥ*) is given with its repetition करिति कः (*kariti kaḥ*), as printed.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> उतापि च नोऽस्माकमहिरंतरिक्षगाम्यहंता वा हीनो वाहन्यमानो वैतन्नामको देवः स एव बुध्न्यः । बुध्नं बंधकमंतरिक्षं । तदर्हतीति बुध्न्योऽन्तरिक्षचार्येतन्नामको देवो मयः सुखं कः । करोतु ॥ करोतेर्लङि रूपं ॥ किंच पिप्युषी । इवशब्द एवार्थः पूरणो वा । अस्मान्रसेनाप्याययंती सिंधुर्नाम नदी वेतु । आगच्छतु । तत्र दृष्टांतः । शिशुं न यथा शिशुं प्याययंती गौर्गच्छति तद्वत् । अपां नपातमुदकानामपातयितारं वर्षकमेतन्नामकं यद्वोदकानां नप्तारं तृतीयं पुत्रं । अद्भ्य ओषधिवनस्पतयः तेभ्योऽग्निरिति नप्तृत्वं । तादृशमग्निं जुनाम । स्तुतिभिः संगच्छेम ॥ जु इति सौत्रो धातुर्गत्यर्थः ॥ यं देवं मनोजुवो मनोवेगा वृषणो वर्षका मेषा अश्वा वहंति स सुखं करोतु ॥

> *utāpi ca no 'smākamahiraṃtarikṣagāmyahaṃtā vā hīno vāhanyamāno vaitannāmako devaḥ sa eva budhnyaḥ | budhnaṃ baṃdhakamaṃtarikṣaṃ | tadarhatīti budhnyo 'ntarikṣacāryetannāmako devo mayaḥ sukhaṃ kaḥ | karotu ‖ karoterlaṅi rūpaṃ ‖ kiṃca pipyuṣī | ivaśabda evārthaḥ pūraṇo vā | asmānrasenāpyāyayaṃtī siṃdhurnāma nadī vetu | āgacchatu | tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | śiśuṃ na yathā śiśuṃ pyāyayaṃtī gaurgacchati tadvat | apāṃ napātamudakānāmapātayitāraṃ varṣakametannāmakaṃ yadvodakānāṃ naptāraṃ tṛtīyaṃ putraṃ | adbhya oṣadhivanaspatayaḥ tebhyo 'gniriti naptṛtvaṃ | tādṛśamagniṃ junāma | stutibhiḥ saṃgacchema ‖ ju iti sautro dhāturgatyarthaḥ ‖ yaṃ devaṃ manojuvo manovegā vṛṣaṇo varṣakā meṣā aśvā vahaṃti sa sukhaṃ karotu ‖*


*(करोतेर्लङि (*karoterlaṅi*) zoomed, as printed; मेषा (*meṣā*) zoomed, so printed (the sense expects मेघा (*meghā*), "clouds").)*

*Gist:* May Ahi Budhnya, the god moving in the mid-air, give us happiness; may the river Sindhu come to us as a cow nourishing her calf; may we reach with praises Apāṃ Napāt (Agni, the grandson of the waters), whom swift, showering steeds carry; may he give happiness.

### Printed p. 142  (PDF 160)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Ṛk 5, continued.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** उत (*uta*) — and; अहिर्बुध्न्यः (*ahirbudhnyaḥ*) — the deity Ahirbudhnya, who moves in the mid-air; नः (*naḥ*) — to us; मयः (*mayaḥ*) — happiness; कः (*kaḥ*) — may he make; यं (*yaṃ*) — which Agni; मनोजुवः (*manojuvaḥ*) — swift as the speed of the mind; वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*) — clouds that are showerers, or horses; वहंति (*vahaṃti*) — carry and bring; तं अपां नपातं (*taṃ apāṃ napātaṃ*) — such Agni, who is also the grandson of the waters; येन (*yena*) — by the help of which deity; जुनाम (*junāma*) — we approach, endowed with praises: may such a deity too make happiness for us; पिप्युषी इव (*pipyuṣī iva*) — she who (always) nourishes us; सिंधुः (*siṃdhuḥ*) — the deity Sindhu too; शिशुं न (*śiśuṃ na*) — like a cow going to satisfy its young (calf); वेति (*veti*) — may she come near us. *(The Kannada here has "clouds" (meghagaḷu) for the bhāṣya's मेषा (*meṣā*) as printed on p. 141.)*

**Bhāvārtha.** May the deity Ahirbudhnya, who moves in the mid-air, make happiness for us. May that deity too, with whose help we, endowed with praises, approach Agni, the grandson of the waters, whom the clouds (or horses), swift as the speed of the mind and showering, carry and bring, make happiness for us. May the deity Sindhu too, who always nourishes us, come to us like a cow going to satisfy its calf, and satisfy us.

**English Translation (as printed):**

May Ahirbudhnya grant us happiness: may Sindhu come, nourishing us as a (cow her) calf, whereby we may propitiate the grandson of the waters» [sic] (Agni), whom the clouds, swift as thought, convey· [sic]

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

अहिः बुध्न्यः (*ahiḥ budhnyaḥ*) — The word अहिः (*ahiḥ*) is read among the thirty names of the cloud (Ni. 2-21, zoomed) and among the hundred-and-one names of water (Ni. 2-24, zoomed). बुध्नमंतरिक्षं बद्धा अस्मिन्, धृता आप इति वा । बद्धा अस्मिन् धृताः प्राणा इति (*budhnamaṃtarikṣaṃ baddhā asmin, dhṛtā āpa iti vā | baddhā asmin dhṛtāḥ prāṇā iti*) (Ni. 10-44, zoomed) — that is, the word बुध्न (*budhna*) means the mid-air. For in this mid-air water is bound in the form of clouds, or is held; therefore the mid-air has the name बुध्न (*budhna*); or the body, in which the vital breaths are held, also has the name बुध्न (*budhna*): so Yāska has given the derivation. And,

> अहिर्बुध्न्यः । योऽहिः स बुध्न्यो बुध्नमंतरिक्षं तन्निवासात् ॥

> *ahirbudhnyaḥ | yo 'hiḥ sa budhnyo budhnamaṃtarikṣaṃ tannivāsāt ‖*

(Ni. 10-44, zoomed)

Giving the derivation of the word अहिर्बुध्न्यः (*ahirbudhnyaḥ*): the meaning "mid-air" which the word बुध्न (*budhna*) has belongs to the word अहि (*ahi*) too. Yāska has said that the deity dwelling in that mid-air has the name Ahirbudhnya, and in support of it *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 143  (PDF 161)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued.)*

> मा नोऽहिर्बुध्न्यो रिषे धान्मा यज्ञो अस्य स्रिधदृतायोः ।

> *mā no 'hirbudhnyo riṣe dhānmā yajño asya sridhadṛtāyoḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-34-17, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "May Ahirbudhnya not give us over to harm; may the sacrifice of this pious man not fail.")

— citing this ṛk, he has explained the meaning. This word Ahirbudhnya occurs in the Ṛgveda in the ṛks 1-86-5 (so printed; this ṛk is 1-186-5); 2-31-6; 5-41-16; 6-49-14; 6-50-14; 7-35-13; 7-38-5; 10-64-4; 10-66-11; 10-92-12; 10-93-5 (all zoomed). In some places the name of the deity Aja Ekapāt is also mentioned together with this deity.

Ahirbudhnya may be said to be the serpent of the ocean or of the nether world (Pātāla). This name occurs especially in the sūktas whose deity is the Viśvedevas. In all, the name of this deity is used in the Ṛgveda only twelve times: five times it is mentioned together with Aja Ekapād, three times with Apāṃ Napāt, three times with Samudra and twice with Savitṛ. Apart from other deities, this name has come in only three ṛks (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-41-16; 7-34-16, 17, zoomed). Generally the deity that comes together with this deity is Aja Ekapāt or Apāṃ Napāt. Aja Ekapāt and Ahirbudhnya both generally appear as if joined side by side. In the Nirukta (Ni. 5-4, zoomed) Ahirbudhnya is counted as one among the deities of the mid-air. Since it is said in the ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-34-16; 10-93-5 (zoomed), "I praise with song the serpent born in the waters, sitting at the bottom of the stream of the mid-air", it is indicated that this deity dwells in the mass of waters of the sky. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-34-17 (zoomed) there is the prayer that he should not harm those who worship him either. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-41-16 (zoomed) too there is mention of this same matter. From these sentences it becomes clear that wickedness is contained in his nature. The word अहि (*ahi*) is generally used about Vṛtra. Vṛtra too had enclosed the water in this same way; the water flowed, overpowering him; or there is the description that he lay in the water or at the bottom of the atmosphere. Therefore there is room for the idea that Ahirbudhnya and Ahi Vṛtra were one and the same. Although the idea arose gradually that Ahirbudhnya is a deity, his wicked nature is subtly indicated. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 4-4-10-3, zoomed), with प्रोष्ठपदानक्षत्रमज एकपाद्देवता प्रोष्ठपदानक्षत्रमहिर्बुध्नियो देवता (*proṣṭhapadānakṣatramaja ekapāddevatā proṣṭhapadānakṣatramahirbudhniyo devatā*), it is said that the deity Aja Ekapāt is the presiding lord of the Pūrvābhādra nakṣatra, and that Ahirbudhnya is the deity of the Uttarābhādra nakṣatra. In the Purāṇas and the like, Ahirbudhnya is well known as one among the names of Rudra.

मयः (*mayaḥ*) — Since the word मयः (*mayaḥ*) is read among the twenty names of happiness beginning with शिंबाता (*śiṃbātā*), शतरा (*śatarā*), मयः (*mayaḥ*) means happiness (Ni. 3-9, as printed, zoomed).

शिशुं न पिप्युषी (*śiśuṃ na pipyuṣī*) — For the river Sindhu a simile is given: "as a cow nourishes its calf by giving it milk". That is, just as a cow protects its calf by giving it milk, the river Sindhu *(continues on the next page)*


---

### Printed p. 144  (PDF 162)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued.)*

… providing water abundant for agriculture and other works and for food, drink and the like, protects people: this illustration is indicated here. What is special here is that a cow nourishes only its one calf by giving it milk, but the river Sindhu brings about the nourishment of many people.

सिंधुः (*siṃdhuḥ*) — The word सिंधु (*siṃdhu*) is read among the names of rivers (Ni. 2-24, zoomed). सिंधु (*siṃdhu*) means स्यंदनशीला (*syaṃdanaśīlā*), "a river that flows, that streams along". In the Ṛgveda, in this very sense,

> सुदेवो असि वरुण यस्य ते सप्त सिंधवः ।
> अनुक्षरंति काकुदं सूर्म्यं सुषिरामिव ॥

> *sudevo asi varuṇa yasya te sapta siṃdhavaḥ |*
> *anukṣaraṃti kākudaṃ sūrmyaṃ suṣirāmiva ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-69-12, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "You are a good god, Varuṇa, into whose palate the seven rivers flow, as into a hollow tube.")

> तमू षु समना गिरा पितॄ[?]णां च मन्मभिः ।
> नाभाकस्य प्रशस्तिभिर्यः सिंधूनामुपोदये सप्तस्वसा स मध्यमो नभंतामन्यके समे ॥

> *tamū ṣu samanā girā pitṝ[?]ṇāṃ ca manmabhiḥ |*
> *nābhākasya praśastibhiryaḥ siṃdhūnāmupodaye saptasvasā sa madhyamo nabhaṃtāmanyake same ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-41-2, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Him (I praise) well with a common song, with the thoughts of the fathers, with the praises of Nābhāka — him who is at the rising of the rivers, having seven sisters, he the middle one; may all the other foes perish.") *(पितॄ[?]णां (*pitṝ[?]ṇāṃ*): the subscript after ta is unclear in the zoom.)*

— in these and other ṛks the word सिंधु (*siṃdhu*) is explained as "flowing rivers"; in this ṛk under discussion, उत नो (*uta no*), and in

> अमंदान्त्स्तोमान्प्र भरे मनीषा सिंधावधि क्षियतो भाव्यस्य ।

> *amaṃdāntstomānpra bhare manīṣā siṃdhāvadhi kṣiyato bhāvyasya |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-126-1, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "With insight I bring forth unflagging praises for Bhāvya, who dwells on the Sindhu.")

and other ṛks, as the river Sindhu; and in

> श्रोतु नः श्रोतुरातिः सुश्रोतुः सुक्षेत्रा सिंधुरद्भिः ।

> *śrotu naḥ śroturātiḥ suśrotuḥ sukṣetrā siṃdhuradbhiḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-6, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "May she of the good fields, Sindhu, with her waters, hear us — she whose gift is for the one who listens, she who listens well.")

> इंद्रो द्यावापृथिवी सिंधुरद्भिरादित्यैर्नो अदितिः शर्म यंसत् ।

> *iṃdro dyāvāpṛthivī siṃdhuradbhirādityairno aditiḥ śarma yaṃsat |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-54-6, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "May Indra, Heaven and Earth, Sindhu with the waters, Aditi with the Ādityas, grant us shelter.")

— in these ṛks the commentator (Sāyaṇa) has explained the meaning as the deity presiding over the waters.

अपां नपातं (*apāṃ napātaṃ*) — अपां उदकानां नपातं नपातयितारं तासां नप्तारं वा अग्निं । अध्भ्यः ओषधिवनस्पतयः ताभ्यः अग्निः इत्यपां नप्तृत्वमग्नेः । (*apāṃ udakānāṃ napātaṃ napātayitāraṃ tāsāṃ naptāraṃ vā agniṃ | adhbhyaḥ oṣadhivanaspatayaḥ tābhyaḥ agniḥ ityapāṃ naptṛtvamagneḥ |*) (अध्भ्यः (*adhbhyaḥ*) so printed, zoomed) — Sāyaṇa has explained that because the plants and trees are produced from the waters and Agni is born from them, the name अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) ("grandson of the waters") is well known for Agni.

नपात् (*napāt*) — The word has the meanings "son" and "grandson"; the word is used in both meanings. But the Niruktakāra, with नपादित्यनंतरायाः प्रजाया नामधेयं । (*napādityanaṃtarāyāḥ prajāyā nāmadheyaṃ |*), has said that the meaning of the word is not the direct son but grandsons and the like (Ni. 8-5, zoomed). And when giving the derivation of the word तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*), आपः अत्र तन्व उच्यंते । तता अंतरिक्षे (*āpaḥ atra tanva ucyaṃte | tatā aṃtarikṣe*) *(continues on the next page)*

---


---

### Printed p. 145  (PDF 163)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued. Foot of page: signature mark "[10]" and "Vol. 14".)*

… ताभ्यः ओषधिवनस्पतयः जायंते ओषधिवनस्पतिभ्य एष जायते । (*tābhyaḥ oṣadhivanaspatayaḥ jāyaṃte oṣadhivanaspatibhya eṣa jāyate |*) — having explained thus, he has said that (तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*)) is the grandson of the waters, and, according to Śākapūṇi's view, a synonym of Agni.

> अनंतरं प्रजामाहुर्नपादिति कृपण्यवः ।
> नपादमुष्य चैवायमग्निस्तेन तनूनपात् ॥

> *anaṃtaraṃ prajāmāhurnapāditi kṛpaṇyavaḥ |*
> *napādamuṣya caivāyamagnistena tanūnapāt ‖*

(Gloss, mine and tentative: "The poets call the next offspring *napāt*; and this Agni is the *napāt* of that one: hence Tanūnapāt.")

— in the Bṛhaddevatā too this same view is followed. That there is a difference of opinion here, whether अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) is a synonym of Agni or the name of another deity, can be known from the Niruktakāra's statement अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः (*agniriti śākapūṇiḥ*). Or, showing the derivation अपां न पातयिता वैद्युताग्निरूपेण प्रवर्षकत्वादिति भावः (*apāṃ na pātayitā vaidyutāgnirūpeṇa pravarṣakatvāditi bhāvaḥ*), Sāyaṇa has explained that this is the name of the lightning-fire. The Niruktakāra has said that the explanation of अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) is just like the explanation of तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*).

> तनूनपादयं त्वेव नाम्ना यच्छत्यसौ तनुं ।
> नपादिति प्रजामाहुरमुतोऽस्य च संभवात् ॥

> *tanūnapādayaṃ tveva nāmnā yacchatyasau tanuṃ |*
> *napāditi prajāmāhuramuto 'sya ca saṃbhavāt ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-1, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "This one is Tanūnapāt by name, for he gives (himself) a body; they call offspring *napāt*, and his origin is from that one.")

As it is said in many places that, since he is born from himself, being his own son, the name तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) is well known, the same is the explanation for अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) too. Or —

अपां नपातं । जलस्य न पालकं । जलस्य शोषकं । (*apāṃ napātaṃ | jalasya na pālakaṃ | jalasya śoṣakaṃ |*) — because he is opposed to water and dries up water, the sun has the name अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*): this meaning the commentator has stated in the bhāṣya of the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-6 (zoomed). But Yāska, saying that the word अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) and the word तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) are words of one and the same meaning, has given two kinds of meaning for the word तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*): ājya (melted ghee) and Agni (Ni. 10-8 and 8-5, zoomed). Now there is a difference of opinion whether the deity अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) is other than Agni or a portion of Agni. In Ṛ. Saṃ. sūkta 1-142 (read unzoomed; the zoom missed), examining the subject of the deity तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*), an Āprī deity, and citing the Bṛhaddevatā sentences and the like which say that this deity is a transformed form of Agni, it was shown that this is not a separate deity. From some other evidence present in the Ṛksaṃhitā itself there is also room to say that at the beginning it was counted as a separate deity and afterwards, becoming one with Agni, must have come to be counted as a portion of Agni. According to the Niruktakāra's view, since the deity अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) and the deity तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) are one, one and the same explanation makes known the nature of both deities. In the present context, if one examines what place the deity अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) has in the Ṛksaṃhitā, the point emerges that in the sūktas addressed to the Viśvedevas the deity अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) is invoked many times.

### Printed p. 146  (PDF 164)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued: Apāṃ Napāt.)*

> प्र नः पूषा चरथं विश्वदेव्योऽपां नपादवतु वायुरिष्टये ।
> आत्मानं वस्यो अभि वातमर्चत तदश्विना सुहवा यामनि श्रुतं ॥

> *pra naḥ pūṣā carathaṃ viśvadevyo 'pāṃ napādavatu vāyuriṣṭaye |*
> *ātmānaṃ vasyo abhi vātamarcata tadaśvinā suhavā yāmani śrutaṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-92-13, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "May Pūṣan, dear to all the gods, and Apāṃ Napāt and Vāyu further our moving (life) for (our) wish; praise the wind, the breath, for the better; hear that, Aśvins, easy to invoke, on (your) course.")

— in this ṛk Pūṣan and then Apāṃ Napāt are prayed to together with the Viśvedevas. In the second ṛk of this sūkta (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-92-2, zoomed) Agni is praised as the increaser of the sacrifice. In the 13th ṛk of the 35th sūkta of the 7th maṇḍala (zoomed) the deities Aja Ekapāt, Ahirbudhnya, Samudra, Apāṃ Napāt and Pṛśni are invoked together, in the first ṛk Indra and Agni, and in the fourth ṛk Agni alone. In the 14th ṛk of the 52nd sūkta of the 6th maṇḍala (zoomed) other deities are invoked together with Apāṃ Napāt; in ṛks 6 and 12 (zoomed) Agni is prayed to. Likewise in the 31st sūkta of the 2nd maṇḍala and in the 50th sūkta of the 6th maṇḍala (zoomed) Agni and Apāṃ Napāt are mentioned separately. In none of these ṛks is it possible to speak of a 'tādātmya' (identity) of Agni and Apāṃ Napāt as one and the same deity.

The 35th sūkta of the 2nd maṇḍala (zoomed) has Apāṃ Napāt alone as its deity. Apart from the 15th ṛk (zoomed), where alone Agni is referred to, in the remaining ṛks to the end there is no name of Agni at all. Even so, only ṛks 11 and 12 could be interpreted as relating to Agni; but even there the description does not fit Agni directly. Taking these examples, the scholar Bloomfield gives his opinion thus —

While Agni became more and more conspicious [sic]. Apan Napat seems to have waned in popularity, until he was so far forgotten that a confusion arose concerning the two uses of the expression अपांनपात् (*apāṃnapāt*) *(printed in Kannada script)* " the son of the waters " was swallowed up in Agni, a son of the waters as he was occasionally (twice in the Rik) called, since he too. because of his original lightning nature, was supposed to have been born of the rain-clouds. To the same source is to be traced the myth of his hiding in the waters, for this myth probably had no connection originally with Apan Napat, beyond the mere fact that both he and Agni were forms of lightning which, appearing when the thunderstorm was at its hight [sic] seemed to disappear in the clouds from which they came.

The conclusion seems to be warranted, therefore, that Agni and Apan Napat were once distinct Gods—Gods, of the lightning, who were, however, associated with each other and were much alike in certain particulars and that this association, and resemblance ulti- *(continues on the next page)*

mately resulted, possibly at the close of the Vedic Period, in a confusion and union of the two, as a result of which Apan Napat was absorbed by Agni·

(Journal of American Oriental Society Vol. XIX (2) p. 144)

मनोजुवः (*manojuvaḥ*) — मन इव वेगयुक्तः । (*mana iva vegayuktaḥ |*) — "having speed like the mind". The mind can think in a mere instant of a thing that is however far away. Therefore, when great speed is to be indicated, the usage of stating the simile "having speed like the speed of the mind" is found in the Ṛgveda.

> इंद्रवायू मनोजुवा विप्रा हवंत ऊतये । सहस्राक्षा धियस्पती ॥

> *iṃdravāyū manojuvā viprā havaṃta ūtaye | sahasrākṣā dhiyaspatī ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-23-3, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Indra and Vāyu, swift as thought, the sages invoke for help — the thousand-eyed lords of thought.")

— in these and other ṛks the word मनोजुव (*manojuva*) is used in the meaning stated above.

वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*) — वर्षका मेघाः । (*varṣakā meghāḥ |*) — "clouds that pour rain": this is Sāyaṇa's explanation. *(Here मेघाः (*meghāḥ*) is printed; the bhāṣya on p. 141 has मेषा (*meṣā*).)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly; Pāṇini numerals read unzoomed). अहिः (*ahiḥ*) — root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*); by आङि श्रिहनिभ्यां ह्रस्वश्च (*āṅi śrihanibhyāṃ hrasvaśca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-5;66, so printed, zoomed) the affix इण् (*iṇ*), the ā shortened, the root's ṭi (an) elided because the affix is ḍit. बुध्न्यः (*budhnyaḥ*) — बुध्नमर्हतीति (*budhnamarhatīti*), chāndasa yat in the sense "deserving"; a elided by यस्येति च (*yasyeti ca*); svarita by तित्स्वरितम् (*titsvaritam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-185). कः (*kaḥ*) — root डुकृञ् करणे (*ḍukṛñ karaṇe*); laṅ in the sense of loṭ by छंदसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः (*chaṃdasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*); i elided by इतश्च (*itaśca*), luk of the vikaraṇa by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*), guṇa with r, ti elided by हल्ङ्याब्भ्यो दीर्घात् (*halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-68), visarga; no aṭ augment (chāndasa); nighāta accent.

पिप्युषी (*pipyuṣī*) — root ओप्यायी वृद्धौ (*opyāyī vṛddhau*); chāndasa liṭ, क्वसु (*kvasu*) by क्वसुश्च (*kvasuśca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-107), पी (*pī*) substituted for the root by लिड्यङोश्च (*liḍyaṅośca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-29), reduplication; ṅīp in the feminine by उगितश्च (*ugitaśca*); samprasāraṇa of the affix's v (bha-saṃjñā), pūrvarūpa, yaṇ of the root's ī; ṣ by शासिवसिघसीनां च (*śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-60); madhyodātta by the affix's ādyudātta accent.

### Printed p. 148  (PDF 166)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Grammar of Ṛk 5 concluded; Ṛk 6 begins.)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (continued; numerals read unzoomed). वेति (*veti*) — root वी गत्यादिषु (*vī gatyādiṣu*); leṭ, third person singular; tiṅanta-nighāta accent. नपातम् (*napātam*) — by नभ्राण्नपात्- (*nabhrāṇnapāt-*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-75) the absence of the loss of n is given as a nipātana; the nañ first member keeps its own accent. अपाम् (*apām*) — by ऊडिदंपदाद्- (*ūḍidaṃpadād-*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the genitive plural ending is udātta. जुनाम (*junāma*) — root जु गतौ (*ju gatau*) (given only in a sūtra), kryādi class, loṭ, first person plural; nighāta is blocked by यद्वृत्तान्नित्यम् (*yadvṛttānnityam*), so the word is madhyodātta by the vikaraṇa's accent. वहंति (*vahaṃti*) — no nighāta because of the connection with yad; by तास्यनुदात्तेत्- (*tāsyanudātteta-*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the la-sārvadhātuka is anudātta, so the root accent remains.

## Sūkta 186, Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उत न ईं त्वष्टा गंत्वच्छा स्मत्सूरिभिरभिपित्वे सजोषाः ।
> आ वृत्रहेंद्रश्चर्षणिप्रास्तुविष्टमो नरां न इह गम्याः ॥ ६ ॥

> *uta na īṃ tvaṣṭā gaṃtvacchā smatsūribhirabhipitve sajoṣāḥ |*
> *ā vṛtraheṃdraścarṣaṇiprāstuviṣṭamo narāṃ na iha gamyāḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उत । नः । ईं । त्वष्टा । आ । गंतु । अच्छ । स्मत् । सूरिऽभिः । अभिऽपित्वे । सऽजोषाः ।
> आ । वृत्रऽहा । इंद्रः । चर्षणिऽप्राः । तुविःऽतमः । नरां । नः । इह । गम्याः ॥ ६ ॥

> *uta | naḥ | īṃ | tvaṣṭā | ā | gaṃtu | accha | smat | sūri 'bhiḥ | abhi 'pitve | sa 'joṣāḥ |*
> *ā | vṛtra 'hā | iṃdraḥ | carṣaṇi 'prāḥ | tuviḥ 'tamaḥ | narāṃ | naḥ | iha | gamyāḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> त्वष्टा देवोऽपि नोऽस्मानच्छाभिप्राप्तुमीमिदानीमिमं यज्ञं वा गंतु । आगत्य च । स्मत्सहार्थे प्रशस्त्ये वा वर्तते । अत्र प्रशंसायां । प्रशस्तं यथा तथाभिपित्वेऽभिगंतव्ये यज्ञे निमित्तभूते सति सूरिभिः स्तोतृभिर्ऋत्विग्भिः सजोषाः समानप्रीतिर्भवत्विति शेषः । तथा वृत्रहा वृत्रघाती चर्षणिप्राः । चर्षणयो मनुष्या यजमानाः । कामैस्तेषां पूरकस्तुविष्टमो बहुतमो महत्तम इहास्मिन्कर्मणि नरां नृणां नोऽस्माकमुक्तगुणोपेतः सन्ना गम्याः । आगच्छतु ॥

> *tvaṣṭā devo 'pi no 'smānacchābhiprāptumīmidānīmimaṃ yajñaṃ vā gaṃtu | āgatya ca | smatsahārthe praśastye vā vartate | atra praśaṃsāyāṃ | praśastaṃ yathā tathābhipitve 'bhigaṃtavye yajñe nimittabhūte sati sūribhiḥ stotṛbhirṛtvigbhiḥ sajoṣāḥ samānaprītirbhavatviti śeṣaḥ | tathā vṛtrahā vṛtraghātī carṣaṇiprāḥ | carṣaṇayo manuṣyā yajamānāḥ | kāmaisteṣāṃ pūrakastuviṣṭamo bahutamo mahattama ihāsminkarmaṇi narāṃ nṛṇāṃ no 'smākamuktaguṇopetaḥ sannā gamyāḥ | āgacchatu ‖*

### Printed p. 149  (PDF 167)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Ṛk 6, continued.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** उत (*uta*) — and; त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*) — the deity named Tvaṣṭṛ; नः अभि (*naḥ abhi*) — facing towards us; ईं (*īṃ*) — to this sacrifice; आ गंतु (*ā gaṃtu*) — may he come; (then) अभिपित्वे (*abhipitve*) — in this sacrifice now being performed; सूरिभिः (*sūribhiḥ*) — with the ṛtviks, his praisers; सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*) — joined with equal affection; स्मत् (*smat*) — may he make the sacrifice praiseworthy; चर्षणिप्राः (*carṣaṇiprāḥ*) — fulfilling the desires of men; तुविष्टमः (*tuviṣṭamaḥ*) — of very great greatness; वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*) — who is also the slayer of Vṛtra; इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*) — Indra; इह (*iha*) — in this rite; नरां नः (*narāṃ naḥ*) — towards us who are men; आ गम्याः (*ā gamyāḥ*) — may he come. *(The headword वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*) appears printed like वृताहा (*vṛtāhā*); the zoom missed the line.)*

**Bhāvārtha.** May the deity named Tvaṣṭṛ come to this sacrifice, facing towards us. In this sacrifice now being performed, joined with equal affection with the ṛtviks who are his praisers, may he make the sacrifice praiseworthy. May Indra, who fulfils and protects the desires of men, who is of very great greatness and the slayer of Vṛtra, come in this rite towards us who are men.

**English Translation (as printed):**

Or may Twashtri come to this sacrifice, equally well pleased with those who praise (him) at the excellent (rite) at which he is present : may the most potent Indra the protector of man, the destroyer of Vritra, come to the (solemnity) of our leadrs [sic]·

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

In this ṛk Tvaṣṭṛ and Indra are praised. We have already spoken earlier about Tvaṣṭṛ, who is well known as the craftsman of the gods.

त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*) — For this word Yāska in his Nirukta has given the derivation thus —

> त्वष्टा त्वष्टा तूर्णमश्नुत इति नैरुक्ताः । त्विषेर्वा स्याद्दीप्तिकर्मणस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात्करोतिकर्मणः । माध्यमिकस्त्वष्टेत्याहुर्मध्यमे च स्थाने समाम्नातः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥

> *tvaṣṭā tvaṣṭā tūrṇamaśnuta iti nairuktāḥ | tviṣervā syāddīptikarmaṇastvakṣatervā syātkarotikarmaṇaḥ | mādhyamikastvaṣṭetyāhurmadhyame ca sthāne samāmnātaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*

(Ni. 8-14, zoomed)

That is, the Niruktakāras say that the word त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*) means "he who pervades quickly"; or "he who is shining"; or "he who does works (works of craft too)"; some say he is mādhyamika, that is, the meaning is "he who is between heaven and earth". Śākapūṇi says he is Agni.

---

### Printed p. 150  (PDF 168)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 6, continued: Tvaṣṭṛ.)*

Some say that Tvaṣṭṛ, like Viśvakarman, is the craftsman of the gods. For in the ṛk which Yāska has given as an example —

> य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भुवनानि विश्वा ।
> तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान्देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् ।

> *ya ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpairapiṃśadbhuvanāni viśvā |*
> *tamadya hotariṣito yajīyāndevaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yakṣi vidvān |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-9, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "He who adorned with forms these two parents, Heaven and Earth, and all the worlds — that god Tvaṣṭṛ, O Hotṛ, urged on, best at sacrificing, knowing, worship here today.")

— it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ is the maker of heaven and earth and the cause and agent of the form, beauty, prosperity, growth and the like fitting to each of the creatures in all the worlds. Besides this, the Śruti (Yajurveda) sentences beginning त्वष्टा वै पशूनां मिथुनानाग्ं रूपकृत् (*tvaṣṭā vai paśūnāṃ mithunānāgṃ rūpakṛt*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-8-3, zoomed), त्वष्टा रूपाणामधिपतिः (*tvaṣṭā rūpāṇāmadhipatiḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-3, so printed, zoomed), त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोति (*tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi vikaroti*) set forth Tvaṣṭṛ's skill in making things; and,

> मह्यं त्वष्टा वज्रमतक्षदायसं मयि देवासोऽवृजन्नपि क्रतुं ।

> *mahyaṃ tvaṣṭā vajramatakṣadāyasaṃ mayi devāso 'vṛjannapi kratuṃ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-48-3, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "For me Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the iron thunderbolt; in me the gods placed (their) resolve.")

— Indra has said that Tvaṣṭṛ made and gave him the thunderbolt-weapon of steel. In many mantras of the Ṛgveda it is said that he has made and given the gods the sacrificial implements they need and many other things. Tvaṣṭṛ is a very skilful workman; he has made various objects that display his skill. In truth there is no workman as skilful as he. Therefore —

> त्वष्टा यद्वज्रं सुकृतं हिरण्ययं सहस्रभृष्टिं स्वपा अवर्तयत् ।
> धत्ते इंद्रो नर्यपांसि कर्तवेऽहन् वृत्रं निरपामौब्जदर्णवं ॥

> *tvaṣṭā yadvajraṃ sukṛtaṃ hiraṇyayaṃ sahasrabhṛṣṭiṃ svapā avartayat |*
> *dhatte iṃdro naryapāṃsi kartave 'han vṛtraṃ nirapāmaubjadarṇavaṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Sa. 1-85-9, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "When Tvaṣṭṛ, the good worker, turned out the well-made golden thunderbolt with a thousand points, Indra takes it to do manly deeds; he slew Vṛtra and forced out the flood of the waters.") *(धत्ते (*dhatte*) so printed.)*

— in this ṛk it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ made the thunderbolt-weapon, very excellent, gleaming like gold and having a thousand edges, and gave it to Indra, and that with it Indra destroyed Vṛtra.

> त्वष्टा माया वेदपसामपस्तमो बिभ्रत्पात्रा देवपानानि शंतमा ।
> शिशीते नूनं परशुं स्वायसं येन। वृश्चादेतशो ब्रह्मणस्पतिः ॥

> *tvaṣṭā māyā vedapasāmapastamo bibhratpātrā devapānāni śaṃtamā |*
> *śiśīte nūnaṃ paraśuṃ svāyasaṃ yena| vṛścādetaśo brahmaṇaspatiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-53-9, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Tvaṣṭṛ, most skilled of the skilled, knows the arts, bearing the most auspicious cups from which the gods drink; he now sharpens the axe of good iron with which Brahmaṇaspati, the bright one, shall cut.") *(The stroke after येन (*yena*) is printed.)*

— in this ṛk it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ, being a very intelligent workman, made drinking-vessels for the gods to drink Soma, and besides that made Brahmaṇaspati's steel axe sharp *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 151  (PDF 169)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 5" (zoomed; Varga 5 now begins). Special Topics of Ṛk 6, continued.)*

… and gave it: there is such a description. Since the matters relating to Tvaṣṭṛ are many, they will be explained at length later.

सूरिभिः (*sūribhiḥ*) — सूरिः स्तोता । (*sūriḥ stotā |*) — the meaning is "praiser". Since it is read among the 13 names of the praiser beginning रेभः (*rebhaḥ*), जरिता (*jaritā*), कारुः (*kāruḥ*) (Ni. 3-19, as printed, zoomed), सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*) means hymn-makers, devotees able to recite hymns. The word सूरि (*sūri*) is also used in many places in contexts that can give the meaning "the wise, the discerning, the intelligent". When used of the ṛṣis, who have obtained a supernatural power of seeing, both of the eye and of the mind, that grasps the true nature of the deities and the secret truths of the universe, this epithet gives a special meaning.

> तद्विष्णोः परमं पदं सदा पश्यंति सूरयः । दिवीव चक्षुराततं ॥

> *tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyaṃti sūrayaḥ | divīva cakṣurātataṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-20, read unzoomed; two zooms missed the line) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The seers always see that highest step of Viṣṇu, like an eye spread out in the sky.")

— in such contexts it indicates not merely "those fit to make hymns" but also the extraordinary power of seeing of the ṛṣis. And it has been used not only of the ṛṣis but also as an epithet of Indra and the other deities.

> मंहिष्ठमच्छोक्तिभिर्मतीनां सुवृक्तिभिः सूरिं वावृधध्यै ॥

> *maṃhiṣṭhamacchoktibhirmatīnāṃ suvṛktibhiḥ sūriṃ vāvṛdhadhyai ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-63-3 as printed, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "… to strengthen the most bountiful sage with invitations of (our) thoughts, with well-turned praises.")

— in these and other ṛks, विपश्चितमिंद्रं (*vipaścitamiṃdraṃ*) *(so the Kannada says; the quoted line does not contain this word)*, the wisdom of Indra and the other deities is made known. Besides this, the word सूरि (*sūri*) is also used when indicating the meaning "lord, impeller, one who sets (men) going on the good path". For example —

> जनो यः पज्रेभ्यो वाजिनीवानश्वावतो रथिनो मह्यं सूरिः ।

> *jano yaḥ pajrebhyo vājinīvānaśvāvato rathino mahyaṃ sūriḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-8, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The man rich in mares who (gives) to me, to the Pajras, a lord with horses and chariots.")

> असद्यथा जरित्र उत सूरिरिंद्रो रायो विश्ववारस्य दाता ।

> *asadyathā jaritra uta sūririṃdro rāyo viśvavārasya dātā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-23-10, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "So that Indra may be for the singer a patron, giver of wealth desired by all.")

> मुह्यंत्वन्ये अभितो जनास इहास्माकं मघवा सूरिरस्तु ॥

> *muhyaṃtvanye abhito janāsa ihāsmākaṃ maghavā sūrirastu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-81-6, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Let the other people round about be bewildered; here may the bounteous one be our patron.") *(मुह्यं- (*muhyaṃ-*): the u-sign is distinct here, unlike मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*) in the line from 1-122-8.)*

— in such contexts, about the deities who are lords and promoters of the good path, this epithet describes the qualities of Indra and the others.

> अपस्य ते कृष्णासो दक्षि सूरयः शूरस्येव त्वेषथादीषते वयः ।

> *apasya te kṛṣṇāso dakṣi sūrayaḥ śūrasyeva tveṣathādīṣate vayaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Suṃ. (so printed) 1-141-8, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "… your dark (flames) burn, O sūri; like a hero's (army) the birds flee from (your) onrush.")

— in a few places such as this it has the meaning "path" (mārga). *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 152 (PDF 170)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". The page opens directly with the Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā heading: the Special Topics of Ṛk 6 (sūri) did not continue here, so the topic ended at the foot of p. 151. Ṛk 6 grammar; Ṛk 7 begins.)*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*) — root त्वक्षू तनूकरणे (*tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe*); suffix तृन् (*tṛn*) in the agent sense; ādyudātta because it is nit; nominative singular. गंतु (*gaṃtu*) — root गमॢ गतौ (*gamḷ gatau*); loṭ, third person singular, u by एरुः (*eruḥ*); luk of the vikaraṇa by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*); anusvāra and parasavarṇa for the root's m; tiṅanta-nighāta. अच्छ (*accha*) — lengthened in the Saṃhitā by निपातस्य च (*nipātasya ca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-1-36, so printed, zoomed). सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*) — root जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः (*juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*); auṇādika suffix असुन् (*asun*); समानं जोषः यस्य सः (*samānaṃ joṣaḥ yasya saḥ*); sa for samāna by समानस्य छंदसि (*samānasya chaṃdasi*); nominative singular. वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*) — root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*); क्विप् (*kvip*) with vṛtra as upapada by ब्रह्मभ्रूण- (*brahmabhrūṇa-*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-87, zoomed); वृत्रं हतवान् वृत्रहा (*vṛtraṃ hatavān vṛtrahā*); in the compound the kṛt final member keeps its own accent. चर्षणिप्राः (*carṣaṇiprāḥ*) — root प्रा पूरणे (*prā pūraṇe*); क्विप् (*kvip*) by क्विप् च (*kvip ca*); an ā-stem results; the kṛt final member keeps its own accent. नराम् (*narām*) — root नृ नये (*nṛ naye*); क्विप् (*kvip*); genitive plural; the case ending is udātta by सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (*sāvekācastṛtīyādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168, zoomed). गम्याः (*gamyāḥ*) — root गमॢ गतौ (*gamḷ gatau*); liṅ; by व्यत्ययो बहुलम् (*vyatyayo bahulam*) the second-person singular ending for the third-person singular; luk of the vikaraṇa by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*); the augment यासुट् (*yāsuṭ*) to sip; rutva and visarga of the s; tiṅanta-nighāta.

## Sūkta 186, Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उत न ईं मतयोऽश्वयोगाः शिशुं न गावस्तरुणं रिहंति ।
> तमीं गिरो जनयो न पत्नीः सुरभिष्टमं नरां नसंत ॥ ७ ॥

> *uta na īṃ matayo 'śvayogāḥ śiśuṃ na gāvastaruṇaṃ rihaṃti |*
> *tamīṃ giro janayo na patnīḥ surabhiṣṭamaṃ narāṃ nasaṃta ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥** *(The first line is on p. 152, the second on p. 153.)*

> उत । नः । ईं । मतयः । अश्वऽयोगाः । शिशुं । न । गावः । तरुणं । रिहंति ।
> तं । ईं । गिरः । जनयः । न । पत्नीः । सुरभिःऽतमं । नरां । नसंत ॥ ७ ॥

> *uta | naḥ | īṃ | matayaḥ | aśva 'yogāḥ | śiśuṃ | na | gāvaḥ | taruṇaṃ | rihaṃti |*
> *taṃ | īṃ | giraḥ | janayaḥ | na | patnīḥ | surabhiḥ 'tamaṃ | narāṃ | nasaṃta ‖ 7 ‖*

### Printed p. 153 (PDF 171)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 5". Ṛk 7 continued: second Pada line (above), bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English; Special Topics begin. Pada 'nasaṃta' zoomed: printed with plain ta, as in the Saṃhitā.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> उतापि चेमेनं तरुणं नित्ययुवानमिंद्रं मतयोऽस्मद्बुद्धयोऽश्वयोगा अश्वसमानप्राप्तयो रिहंति । आस्वादयंति । स्तुवंतीत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टांतः गावो दोग्ध्र्यो धेनवः शिशुं न शिशुमिव वत्समिव तं यथा लिहंति तद्वत् । तदेवाह । तमीं तमेवैनं नरां नराणां यजमानानां सुरभिष्टममतिशयेन सुरभिं जनयः फलस्योत्पादयित्र्यो गिरः स्तुतयो नसंत । व्याप्नुवंति । नसतिर्व्याप्तिकर्मा । तत्र दृष्टांतः । जनयो नोत्पादयित्र्यः पत्नीः पत्न्यः पतिमिव ॥

> *utāpi cemenaṃ taruṇaṃ nityayuvānamiṃdraṃ matayo 'smadbuddhayo 'śvayogā aśvasamānaprāptayo rihaṃti | āsvādayaṃti | stuvaṃtītyarthaḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ gāvo dogdhryo dhenavaḥ śiśuṃ na śiśumiva vatsamiva taṃ yathā lihaṃti tadvat | tadevāha | tamīṃ tamevainaṃ narāṃ narāṇāṃ yajamānānāṃ surabhiṣṭamamatiśayena surabhiṃ janayaḥ phalasyotpādayitryo giraḥ stutayo nasaṃta | vyāpnuvaṃti | nasatirvyāptikarmā | tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | janayo notpādayitryaḥ patnīḥ patnyaḥ patimiva ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** उत (*uta*) — and; ईं तरुणं (*īṃ taruṇaṃ*) — this ever-young Indra; अश्वयोगाः (*aśvayogāḥ*) — yoked together like horses; नः मतयः (*naḥ matayaḥ*) — our minds; गावः (*gāvaḥ*) — milch cows; शिशुं न (*śiśuṃ na*) — as (they lick) their calves; रिहंति (*rihaṃti*) — lick (praise Indra with affection); तं ईं (*taṃ īṃ*) — that same Indra; नरां (*narāṃ*) — of men who perform the sacrifice; सुरभिष्टमं (*surabhiṣṭamaṃ*) — fruit joined with exceeding fragrance; जनयः (*janayaḥ*) — producing; गिरः (*giraḥ*) — words of praise; (जनयः (*janayaḥ*) — having the power to beget sons); पत्नीः न (*patnīḥ na*) — as wives join their husbands; नसंत (*nasaṃta*) — pervade.

**Bhāvārtha.** Our minds, yoked together like horses, pervade and praise with affection this ever-young Indra, as milch cows lick their calves. The words of praise of men, producing fruit joined with exceeding fragrance, pervade that same Indra, as wives who have the power to beget sons join their husbands.

**English Translation (as printed):**

For our minds, yoked together like horses, tend to the ever youthful Indra, as cows to their calves : and the praises of men, (addressed) to him, are generating most fragrant (fruit), as wives bear (children to their husbands)·

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

अश्वयोगाः (*aśvayogāḥ*) — As horses are yoked to a chariot and stay together, so may our minds dwell in Indra with attachment, or praise him: this is the main intention … *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 154 (PDF 172)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 7, continued and concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā begins.)*

*(The aśvayogāḥ note ended at the foot of p. 153; this page opens with the next headword.)*

गावः शिशुं न रिहंति (*gāvaḥ śiśuṃ na rihaṃti*) — The simile is stated: in the way milch cows lick their calves with love, in that same way may our minds serve Indra.

तरुणं (*taruṇaṃ*) — नित्ययुवानमिंद्रं (*nityayuvānamiṃdraṃ*): Indra who is always like a youth, or who is ever young. On Indra being young —

> पुरां भिंदुर्युवा कविरमितौजा अजायत ।

> *purāṃ bhiṃduryuvā kaviramitaujā ajāyata |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-11-4, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The breaker of forts, young, a sage, of boundless might, was born.")

— in such ṛks it is said that Indra is young and exceedingly lustrous.

ईं (*īṃ*) — The mitākṣara words कं (*kaṃ*), ईं (*īṃ*), इत् (*it*), उ (*u*) are used to fill out a pāda. On this Yāska —

> अथ ये प्रवृत्तेऽर्थेऽमिताक्षरेषु ग्रंथेषु वाक्यपूरणा आगच्छंति पदपूरणास्ते मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमीमिद्विति ॥

> *atha ye pravṛtte 'rthe 'mitākṣareṣu graṃtheṣu vākyapūraṇā āgacchaṃti padapūraṇāste mitākṣareṣvanarthakāḥ kamīmidviti ‖*

(Ni. 1-9, zoomed)

The words कं (*kaṃ*), ईं (*īṃ*), इत् (*it*), उ (*u*) are used in sentences not bound by metre (amitākṣara) to fill out the sentence, and in ṛks or mantras bound by metre (mitākṣara) to fill out the pāda. Therefore he has explained that these words need have no definite meaning.

In this ṛk Indra is praised.

गिरः (*giraḥ*) — words, that is, words in the form of praise. Yāska, giving the derivation of the word गिरः (*giraḥ*) as स्तुतयः गिरो गृणातेः (*stutayaḥ giro gṛṇāteḥ*) (Ni. 1-10, zoomed), has said that गिरः (*giraḥ*) means praises.

जनयः (*janayaḥ*) — नोत्पादयित्र्यः (*notpādayitryaḥ*): the meaning is women who have not yet had children but have the power to bear children, that is, young women. The simile is stated: in the way such wives join their husbands with the heart's desire, in that same way may our praises join Indra.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** अश्वयोगाः (*aśvayogāḥ*) — अश्वस्य योग इव योगः यासां ताः अश्वयोगाः (*aśvasya yoga iva yogaḥ yāsāṃ tāḥ aśvayogāḥ*); the prior member keeps its own accent by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā*). तरुणम् (*taruṇam*) (headword printed like तरु म (*taru ma*), broken print, zoomed) — root तॄ प्लवनतरणयोः (*tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ*); suffix उनन् (*unan*) by त्रोरश्च लो वा (*troraśca lo vā*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-334, per numeral file); when guṇa with r following comes to the root, conditioned by it, optionally for the r … *(continues on the next page)*

*(Header printed "Va. 1 A. 2. A. 5" (order reversed and Varga numeral 1, as printed, zoomed; Varga 5 runs on). Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Ṛk 7 concluded; Ṛk 8 begins.)*

… substitution of l. ṇatva for the n by the sūtra अट्कुप्वाङ् (*aṭkupvāṅ*); ādyudātta because the suffix is nit. रिहंति (*rihaṃti*) — root लिह आस्वादने (*liha āsvādane*), adādi; laṭ, third person plural; "by vyatyaya l is substituted for the r of the root" (so printed; the root has l); nighāta accent because it stands after a non-tiṅanta. जनयः (*janayaḥ*) — root जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*); suffix इन् (*in*) by सर्वधातुभ्य इन् (*sarvadhātubhya in*); ādyudātta because it is nit. सुरभिष्टमम् (*surabhiṣṭamam*) — suffix तमप् (*tamap*) by अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ (*atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau*); it is anudātta because it is pit. नसंत (*nasaṃta*) — root णस कौटिल्ये (*ṇasa kauṭilye*), bhvādi; n for the initial by णो नः (*ṇo naḥ*); laṅ in the sense of the present by छंदसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः (*chaṃdasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-6, zoomed); third person plural; no aṭ augment by बहुलं छंद(सि) (*bahulaṃ chaṃda(si)*) (so printed, ending cut short); tiṅanta-nighāta.

## Sūkta 186, Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उत न ईं मरुतो वृद्धसेनाः स्मद्रोदसी समनसः सदंतु ।
> पृषदश्वासोऽवनयो न रथा रिशादसो मित्रयुजो न देवाः ॥ ८ ॥

> *uta na īṃ maruto vṛddhasenāḥ smadrodasī samanasaḥ sadaṃtu |*
> *pṛṣadaśvāso 'vanayo na rathā riśādaso mitrayujo na devāḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उत । नः । ईं । मरुतः । वृद्धऽसेनाः । स्मत् । रोदसी इति । सऽमनसः । सदंतु ।
> पृषत्ऽअश्वासः । अवनयः । न । रथाः । रिशादसः । मित्रऽयुजः । न । देवाः ॥ ८ ॥

> *uta | naḥ | īṃ | marutaḥ | vṛddha 'senāḥ | smat | rodasī iti | sa 'manasaḥ | sadaṃtu |*
> *pṛṣat 'aśvāsaḥ | avanayaḥ | na | rathāḥ | riśādasaḥ | mitra 'yujaḥ | na | devāḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(p. 155; the bhāṣya runs on to p. 156)*

*(Zoomed: 'gacchatāṃ' with a partly broken ta; 'yathaiva namanasvabhāvā' with a stray dot after yathaiva, as printed.)*

> उतापि च नोऽस्मदीयमीमिदानीमेनं यागं वा मरुतः स्मत् सहापि सदंतु । गच्छंतु । कुतो देशात् । रोदसी रोदस्योर्द्यावापृथिव्योः सकाशात् । यद्वा । रोदस्यावपि गच्छतां । कीदृशास्ते मरुतः । वृद्धसेनाः प्रवृद्धबलाः समनसः समानमनस्काः पृषदश्वासः पृषद्वर्णाश्वाः । पृषत्यो मरुतामिति यास्कः । अवनयो न यथैव नमनस्वभावा रथा रंहणस्वभावा रथवंतो वा ॥ मत्वर्थो लुप्यते ॥

> *utāpi ca no 'smadīyamīmidānīmenaṃ yāgaṃ vā marutaḥ smat sahāpi sadaṃtu | gacchaṃtu | kuto deśāt | rodasī rodasyordyāvāpṛthivyoḥ sakāśāt | yadvā | rodasyāvapi gacchatāṃ | kīdṛśāste marutaḥ | vṛddhasenāḥ pravṛddhabalāḥ samanasaḥ samānamanaskāḥ pṛṣadaśvāsaḥ pṛṣadvarṇāśvāḥ | pṛṣatyo marutāmiti yāskaḥ | avanayo na yathaiva namanasvabhāvā rathā raṃhaṇasvabhāvā rathavaṃto vā ‖ matvartho lupyate ‖*

### Printed p. 156 (PDF 174)

*(Header printed "Maṃ. 1 A. 23 Sū. 186" (Anuvāka 23 as printed for 24, zoomed). Ṛk 8: bhāṣya concluded, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics.)*

> यद्वा । अवनयो रक्षका रथा इव स्थिताः । रिशादसः । रिशाः शत्रवः । तेषामत्तारो मित्रयुजो देवा न मैत्रीयुक्ता व्यवहर्तार ऋत्विज इव । यद्वा । मैत्रीयुक्ता अन्ये देवा यथा गच्छंति तद्वत् ॥

> *yadvā | avanayo rakṣakā rathā iva sthitāḥ | riśādasaḥ | riśāḥ śatravaḥ | teṣāmattāro mitrayujo devā na maitrīyuktā vyavahartāra ṛtvija iva | yadvā | maitrīyuktā anye devā yathā gacchaṃti tadvat ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** उत (*uta*) — and; वृद्धसेनाः (*vṛddhasenāḥ*) — having grown strength; समनसः (*samanasaḥ*) — of one mind; पृषदश्वासः (*pṛṣadaśvāsaḥ*) — having horses of variegated colour; अवनयः रथाः न (*avanayaḥ rathāḥ na*) — like protecting chariots, or possessing chariots; रिशादसः (*riśādasaḥ*) — devourers of enemies; मरुतः स्मत् (*marutaḥ smat*) — the Marut deities, together; मित्रयुजः (*mitrayujaḥ*) — joined with friends; देवाः न (*devāḥ na*) — like the other deities; रोदसी (*rodasī*) — from the earth and the atmosphere; नः (*naḥ*) — our; ईं (*īṃ*) — to this sacrifice; सदंतु (*sadaṃtu*) — may they come (रोदसी सदंतु (*rodasī sadaṃtu*) — may Heaven and Earth also come).

**Bhāvārtha.** May the Marut deities — of grown strength, of one mind, with horses of variegated colour, possessing protecting chariots, devourers of enemies — come together from the earth and the atmosphere to this our sacrifice, like the other deities joined with friends. With them may Heaven and Earth also come.

**English Translation (as printed):**

Or may the Maruts, being of one mind, come from heaven and earth (to the sacrifice) ; they who are a mighty host, who have parti-coloured steeds, who are like protecting chariots, and who are devourers of foes, may they come like friendly deities·

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

In this ṛk the Marut deities and Heaven and Earth are praised.

पृषदश्वासः (*pṛṣadaśvāsaḥ*) — पृषद्वर्णाश्वाः (*pṛṣadvarṇāśvāḥ*): the meaning is "having horses called pṛṣatī, of many kinds of colour". On the vehicles of the various deities Yāska —

> हरी इंद्रस्य । रोहितोऽग्नेः । हरित आदित्यस्य । रासभावश्विनोः । अजाः पूष्णः । पृषत्यो मरुतां । अरुण्यो गाव उषसः । श्यावाः सवितुः । विश्वरूपा बृहस्पतेः । नियुतो वायोः ।

> *harī iṃdrasya | rohito 'gneḥ | harita ādityasya | rāsabhāvaśvinoḥ | ajāḥ pūṣṇaḥ | pṛṣatyo marutāṃ | aruṇyo gāva uṣasaḥ | śyāvāḥ savituḥ | viśvarūpā bṛhaspateḥ | niyuto vāyoḥ |*

(Ni. 2-28, as printed, zoomed) *('harita' as printed.)*

— since it is said so, it is well known that the deer of variegated colour called pṛṣatī are the vehicles of the Marut deities.

— in these and other ṛks the matter of yoking to the chariot of the Marut deities the deer called pṛṣatī, which have spots (Spotted deer — in English in the source), is mentioned.

रिशादसः (*riśādasaḥ*) — रिशाः शत्रवः । तेषामत्तारो मरुतः । (*riśāḥ śatravaḥ | teṣāmattāro marutaḥ |*) "Riśaḥ" means enemies; "devourers of them" means those who crush and destroy them: the meaning is destroyers of enemies. The word रिशादसः (*riśādasaḥ*) has been used of many deities in the sense "destroyers of enemies".

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** वृद्धसेनाः (*vṛddhasenāḥ*) — वृद्धा सेना येषां ते वृद्धसेनाः (*vṛddhā senā yeṣāṃ te vṛddhasenāḥ*); the prior member keeps its own accent by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā*). समनसः (*samanasaḥ*) — समानं मनः येषां ते समनसः (*samānaṃ manaḥ yeṣāṃ te samanasaḥ*); sa for samāna by the sūtra समानस्य छंदस्यमूर्ध- (*samānasya chaṃdasyamūrdha-*); in the bahuvrīhi the prior member keeps its own accent. सदंतु (*sadaṃtu*) — root षद्ॢ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु (*ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*); s for the initial by धात्वादेः षः सः (*dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64, split over a line break, zoomed); loṭ, third person plural, अंत (*aṃta*) for jh; u by एरुः (*eruḥ*); luk of the vikaraṇa by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*), so the root does not take the सीद (*sīda*) substitute; tiṅanta-nighāta. पृषदश्वासः (*pṛṣadaśvāsaḥ*) — the augment असुक् (*asuk*) by आज्जसेरसुक् (*ājjaserasuk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50, zoomed). अवनयः (*avanayaḥ*) — root अव रक्षणे (*ava rakṣaṇe*); suffix अनि (*ani*) by अर्तिसृधृधम्य- (*artisṛdhṛdhamya-*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-254, as read, zoomed); ādyudātta of the suffix. रथाः (*rathāḥ*) — when matup comes in the sense "possessing that", luk of the matup as a chāndasa form. रिशादसः (*riśādasaḥ*) — रिशान् अदंति इति रिशादसः (*riśān adaṃti iti riśādasaḥ*); root अद भक्षणे (*ada bhakṣaṇe*); suffix असुन् (*asun*) by सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन् (*sarvadhātubhyo 'sun*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-628, as read, zoomed); ādyudātta by ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ñnityādirnityam*); in the compound the kṛt final member keeps its own accent. *(The page ends here; the Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Ṛk 8 may continue on p. 158.)*

## Sūkta 186, Ṛk 9

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> प्र नु यदेषां महिना चिकित्रे प्र युंजते प्रयुजस्ते सुवृक्ति ।
> अध यदेषां सुदिने न शरुर्विश्वमेरिणं प्रुषायंत सेनाः ॥ ९ ॥

> *pra nu yadeṣāṃ mahinā cikitre pra yuṃjate prayujaste suvṛkti |*
> *adha yadeṣāṃ sudine na śarurviśvameriṇaṃ pruṣāyaṃta senāḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्र । नु । यत् । एषां । महिना । चिकित्रे । प्र । युंजते । प्रऽयुजः । ते । सुऽवृक्ति ।
> अध । यत् । एषां । सुऽदिने । न । शरुः । विश्वं । आ । इरिणं । प्रुषायंत । सेनाः ॥ ९ ॥

> *pra | nu | yat | eṣāṃ | mahinā | cikitre | pra | yuṃjate | pra 'yujaḥ | te | su 'vṛkti |*
> *adha | yat | eṣāṃ | su 'dine | na | śaruḥ | viśvaṃ | ā | iriṇaṃ | pruṣāyaṃta | senāḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*(Zoomed: 'adhātha', 'utpādayaṃti', 'sarvamūṣaraṃ karoti' as printed; 'satyāṃ' with the subscript under ta partly unclear.)*

> एषां मरुतां महिना महिमा वृष्टिलक्षणो यद्यस्मात्प्र चिकित्रे प्रज्ञायते । यद्वा । एषां महत्त्वेन युक्ता नराश्चिकित्रे जानंत्यनुष्ठेयं । न्विति पूरणः । ततस्ते ज्ञातारः सुवृक्ति ॥ सुपो लुक् ॥ सुष्टुतीनां प्रयुजः प्रयोगान्प्र युंजते । अधाथ प्रयोगानंतरं यद्यस्मादेषां सेना वृष्ट्युत्पादका विश्वं सर्वं भुवनमिरिणमूषरप्रदेशं यथा तथा सर्वतः प्रुषायंत उत्पादयंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । सुदिने मेघावरणादिरहिते दिने शरुरंधकारहिंसकः प्रकाश इव । स यथा सर्वमावृणोति तथा मरुत्सेना वृष्ट्या सर्वमूषरं करोति । यद्वा । मरुन्महिमा वृष्टिर्भवति । तदा सस्यादिसमृद्ध्या सत्यां प्रयोगं कुर्वंति । यदा यजंति तदा मरुत्सेनाः सर्वां महीमुंदंतीत्येवं महानुभावा मरुत इति तेषां स्तुतिः ।

> *eṣāṃ marutāṃ mahinā mahimā vṛṣṭilakṣaṇo yadyasmātpra cikitre prajñāyate | yadvā | eṣāṃ mahattvena yuktā narāścikitre jānaṃtyanuṣṭheyaṃ | nviti pūraṇaḥ | tataste jñātāraḥ suvṛkti ‖ supo luk ‖ suṣṭutīnāṃ prayujaḥ prayogānpra yuṃjate | adhātha prayogānaṃtaraṃ yadyasmādeṣāṃ senā vṛṣṭyutpādakā viśvaṃ sarvaṃ bhuvanamiriṇamūṣarapradeśaṃ yathā tathā sarvataḥ pruṣāyaṃta utpādayaṃti | tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | sudine meghāvaraṇādirahite dine śaruraṃdhakārahiṃsakaḥ prakāśa iva | sa yathā sarvamāvṛṇoti tathā marutsenā vṛṣṭyā sarvamūṣaraṃ karoti | yadvā | marunmahimā vṛṣṭirbhavati | tadā sasyādisamṛddhyā satyāṃ prayogaṃ kurvaṃti | yadā yajaṃti tadā marutsenāḥ sarvāṃ mahīmuṃdaṃtītyevaṃ mahānubhāvā maruta iti teṣāṃ stutiḥ |*

*Gist: The Maruts' greatness (rain) is well known; the knowing priests then perform their rites; the Maruts' hosts drench the whole land, even barren ground, as light pervades a clear day.*

**Pratipadārtha.** अध (*adha*) — afterwards; सुदिने (*sudine*) — on fine days free of the covering of clouds; शरुः न (*śaruḥ na*) — as light pervades everywhere; यत् (*yat*) — for which reason; एषां (*eṣāṃ*) — of these Marut deities; सेनाः (*senāḥ*) — the rain-producing forces; इरिणं (*iriṇaṃ*) — making the barren (ūṣara) ground wetted with water; विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*) — the whole world; आ प्रुषायंत (*ā pruṣāyaṃta*) — fill with water (and); यत् (*yat*) — for which reason; एषां (*eṣāṃ*) — of these Marut deities; महिना (*mahinā*) — the greatness in the form of rain; प्र चिकित्रे (*pra cikitre*) — becomes well known; [or: यत् (*yat*) — for which reason; एषां (*eṣāṃ*) — of these Marut deities; महिना (*mahinā*) — by the greatness; प्र चिकित्रे नु (*pra cikitre nu*) — the rites to be performed become well known — for that reason;] ते (*te*) — those sacrificers who know; सुवृक्ति (*suvṛkti*) — joined with excellent praises; प्रयुजां (*prayujāṃ*) (so printed; Pada प्रयुजः (*prayujaḥ*)) — those rites; प्र युंजते (*pra yuṃjate*) — perform (carry out).

### Printed p. 159 (PDF 177)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 5". Ṛk 9: Pratipadārtha concluded, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics.)*

**Bhāvārtha.** As light pervades everywhere on fine days free of the covering of clouds, the rain-producing forces of these Marut deities fill the whole world with water, making even barren ground wet with water. And by this their greatness in the form of rain becomes well known. For this reason the performers of sacrifice, knowing well their duties, carry out the various prescribed rites joined with excellent praises.

**English Translation (as printed):**

For, verily, their greatness is well known, (as) they diligently discharge their functions ; by which their sport pours rain upon every arid soil, as light spreads (universally) on a fine day.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

नु (*nu*) — Yāska's explanation of the word nu is thus —

> नु इत्येषोऽनेककर्मा । इदं नु करिष्यतीति हेत्वपदेशे । कथं नु करिष्यतीत्यनुपृष्टे । नन्वेतदकार्षीदिति च । अथाप्युपमार्थे भवति ।

> *nu ityeṣo 'nekakarmā | idaṃ nu kariṣyatīti hetvapadeśe | kathaṃ nu kariṣyatītyanupṛṣṭe | nanvetadakārṣīditi ca | athāpyupamārthe bhavati |*

(Ni. 1-4, zoomed)

The word nu is used in many senses; and, having said that it is used also when stating a reason and in the sense of comparison, (Yāska) quotes the ṛk —

> वृक्षस्य नु ते पुरुहूत वया व्यू३तयो रुरुहुरिंद्र पूर्वीः ।

> *vṛkṣasya nu te puruhūta vayā vyū3tayo ruruhuriṃdra pūrvīḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-24-3, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Like the branches of a tree, O much-invoked Indra, your many aids have grown forth.")

— and establishes that in the words वृक्षस्य नु (*vṛkṣasya nu*) in it there is the sense of comparison: वृक्षस्य इव (*vṛkṣasya iva*), "like a tree".

सुदिने (*sudine*) — मेघावरणादिरहिते दिने (*meghāvaraṇādirahite dine*) । The bhāṣyakāra has called a day without clouds, with clear sunlight, "sudina". In common usage too it is the same: मेघच्छ- (*meghaccha-*) …

### Printed p. 160 (PDF 178)

*(Header printed "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 9, continued.)*

*(The page opens with the end of the word begun on p. 159; read, zoomed, as "hne 'hni" — the first akṣara looks like the ha of the following word; मेघच्छन्नेऽह्नि (*meghacchanne 'hni*) would be expected.)*

… ह्नेऽह्नि दुर्दिनम् (*hne 'hni durdinam*) — the Kośa explains that a day on which clouds cover (the sky) and the sun's rays are not seen is called durdina. Therefore sudina means a day without clouds, joined with the light of the sun.

शरुः (*śaruḥ*) — Yāska has said that शरुमान् (*śarumān*) means हिंसावान् (*hiṃsāvān*), "one who injures" (Ni. 5-12, zoomed). In the present ṛk the bhāṣyakāra has explained अंधकारहिंसकः प्रकाशकः (*aṃdhakārahiṃsakaḥ prakāśakaḥ*) as the sun, who injures, that is destroys, darkness and produces light. Here, by way of illustration, the greatness of the Marut deities is described thus: as on a day without clouds the sun drives away darkness and spreads his light in every quarter, so the Marut deities pour rain, wet with water every region, even barren (ūṣara) land, and make it favourable to the abundance of crops.

इरिणं (*iriṇaṃ*) — ऊषरप्रदेशं (*ūṣarapradeśaṃ*) । The bhāṣyakāra's explanation is "barren land where nothing grows". On this Yāska in his Nirukta —

> प्रावेपा मा बृहतो मादयंति प्रवातेजा इरिणे वर्वृतानाः ।
> सोमस्येव मौजवतस्य भक्षो विभीदको जागृविर्मह्यमच्छान् ॥

> *prāvepā mā bṛhato mādayaṃti pravātejā iriṇe varvṛtānāḥ |*
> *somasyeva maujavatasya bhakṣo vibhīdako jāgṛvirmahyamacchān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-34-1, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The dangling (dice), born in a windy place, rolling on the playing-ground, gladden me; like a draught of Soma from Mūjavat, the wakeful vibhīdaka has pleased me.")

— quoting this ṛk, he has given the explanation of the word इरिणे (*iriṇe*) in it —

> इरिणं निर्ऋणं ऋणातेरपार्णं भवति । अपरता अस्मादोषधय इति वा ॥

> *iriṇaṃ nirṛṇaṃ ṛṇāterapārṇaṃ bhavati | aparatā asmādoṣadhaya iti vā ‖*

(Ni. 9-8, zoomed)

That is: iriṇa or apārṇa means "without ṛṇa, or debt"; or, since there is no water in this region (arṇa means water, apārṇa land without water), herbs and trees do not grow there. Therefore he has explained it as a waterless region or desert.

What is chiefly to be noted here is that making abundant rain (vṛṣṭi) even in a desert where nothing grows for want of water, and making crops and the like grow abundantly there, is described as one of the greatnesses of the Marut deities.

> दिवा चित्तमः कृण्वंति पर्जन्येनोदवाहेन । यत्पृथिवीं व्युंदंति ॥

> *divā cittamaḥ kṛṇvaṃti parjanyenodavāhena | yatpṛthivīṃ vyuṃdaṃti ‖*

(Ṛ. Suṃ. 1-38-9, as printed, zoomed)

In this ṛk it is said that these Marut deities, covering even the daytime with clouds so that it becomes dark, pour rain, make streams of water flow, and make the whole earth wet.

*('vithatheṣv' as read [?], two dha/tha-like letters; विदथेष्व् (*vidatheṣv*) expected.)*

> पिन्वंत्यपो मरुतः सुदानवः पयो घृतवद्विथथेष्वाभुवः ।

> *pinvaṃtyapo marutaḥ sudānavaḥ payo ghṛtavadvithatheṣvābhuvaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-6, zoomed)

### Printed p. 161 (PDF 179)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 5". Special Topics of Ṛk 9 concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā. The page ends with a separator and the signature mark "[11]" / "Vol. 14".)*

> ये द्रप्सा इव रोदसी धमंत्यनु वृष्टिभिः । उत्सं दुहंतो अक्षितम् ॥

> *ye drapsā iva rodasī dhamaṃtyanu vṛṣṭibhiḥ | utsaṃ duhaṃto akṣitam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-7-16, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Who, like drops, blow along both worlds with rains, milking the unfailing spring.")

— in these and many other ṛks it is described that the Marut deities pour rain and blow in both worlds.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** महिना (*mahinā*) — the word mahat, of the pṛthvādi group, takes इमनिच् (*imanic*); ṭi-lopa by टेः (*ṭeḥ*); su replaced by ā by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*); by vyatyaya the bha-saṃjñā, so the a of an is dropped; the m dropped as a chāndasa form. चिकित्रे (*cikitre*) — root कित ज्ञाने (*kita jñāne*); liṭ in the passive as a chāndasa form; इरेच् (*irec*) by लिटस्तझयोरेशिरेच् (*liṭastajhayoreśirec*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-81, zoomed), रे (*re*) by इरयो रे (*irayo re*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-66, zoomed); no nighāta because of yad; antodātta by the suffix accent. युंजते (*yuṃjate*) — root युजिर् योगे (*yujir yoge*), laṭ third person plural; tiṅanta-nighāta. सुवृक्ति (*suvṛkti*) — luk of the genitive plural by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*). शरुः (*śaruḥ*) — root शॄ हिंसायां (*śṝ hiṃsāyāṃ*); suffix उन् (*un*) by शॄस्वृस्निहित्रपि- (*śṝsvṛsnihitrapi-*) (Uṇ. Sū. 1-10, zoomed); guṇa by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*); ādyudātta because nit. इरिणम् (*iriṇam*) — root ऋ गतौ (*ṛ gatau*); suffix इनन् (*inan*) by अर्तेः किदिच्च (*arteḥ kidicca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 2-209 [?], digits undecided between 2 and 7); being kit, i for the root, with r; ṇatva by अट्कुप्वाङ्- (*aṭkupvāṅ-*); ādyudātta by ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ñnityādirnityam*). प्रुषायंत (*pruṣāyaṃta*) — root प्रुष स्नेहनसेचनपूरणेषु (*pruṣa snehanasecanapūraṇeṣu*), kryādi; laṅ as a chāndasa form; शायच् (*śāyac*) for the vikaraṇa śnā by छंदसि शायजपि (*chaṃdasi śāyajapi*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-84, zoomed); no laghūpadha guṇa because the suffix is treated as ṅit; third person plural; no nighāta because of yad; antodātta because śāyac is cit; no aṭ augment as a chāndasa form.

## Sūkta 186, Ṛk 10

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(After कृणुध्वं (*kṛṇudhvaṃ*) the Saṃhitā prints an extra akṣara like sa (or pa), not in the Pada; zoomed twice, written sa[?].)*

> प्रो अश्विनाववसे कृणुध्वं स[?] प्र पूषणं स्वतवसो हि संति ।
> अद्वेषो विष्णुर्वात ऋभुक्षा अच्छा सुम्नाय ववृतीय देवान् ॥ १० ॥

> *pro aśvināvavase kṛṇudhvaṃ sa[?] pra pūṣaṇaṃ svatavaso hi saṃti |*
> *adveṣo viṣṇurvāta ṛbhukṣā acchā sumnāya vavṛtīya devān ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्रो इति । अश्विना । अवसे । कृणुध्वं । प्र । पूषणं । स्वऽतवसः । हि । संति ।
> अद्वेषः । विष्णुः । वातः । ऋभुक्षाः । अच्छ । सुम्नाय । ववृतीय । देवान् ॥ १० ॥

> *pro iti | aśvinā | avase | kṛṇudhvaṃ | pra | pūṣaṇaṃ | sva 'tavasaḥ | hi | saṃti |*
> *adveṣaḥ | viṣṇuḥ | vātaḥ | ṛbhukṣāḥ | accha | sumnāya | vavṛtīya | devān ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे ऋत्विजः अश्विनावेतन्नामकौ देवावुद्दिश्यावसेऽस्मद्रक्षणाय प्रो कृणुध्वं स्तुतिं प्रकर्षेण कृणुध्वं । पूषणं पोषकमेतन्नामकं देवमप्यवसे प्रकर्षेण स्तुतिं कृणुध्वं । किंच ये स्वतवसः स्वायत्तबलाः संति तानपि प्र कृणुध्वं । के ते । अद्वेषो द्वेषरहितो विष्णुर्व्याप्त एतन्नामको देवः । प्रथममनाहूतोऽपि न कुप्यतीति वक्तुमद्वेष इत्युक्तं । तथा वातः सर्वत्र संचारी वायुरृभुक्षाः पतिरिंद्रश्च । एतानपि प्र कृणुध्वं । अतोऽहं स्वायत्तबलान् सर्वानपि देवान् सुम्नाय सुखायाच्छाभिमुख्येन ववृतीय । स्तोत्रैरभिवर्तयेयं ॥

> *he ṛtvijaḥ aśvināvetannāmakau devāvuddiśyāvase 'smadrakṣaṇāya pro kṛṇudhvaṃ stutiṃ prakarṣeṇa kṛṇudhvaṃ | pūṣaṇaṃ poṣakametannāmakaṃ devamapyavase prakarṣeṇa stutiṃ kṛṇudhvaṃ | kiṃca ye svatavasaḥ svāyattabalāḥ saṃti tānapi pra kṛṇudhvaṃ | ke te | adveṣo dveṣarahito viṣṇurvyāpta etannāmako devaḥ | prathamamanāhūto 'pi na kupyatīti vaktumadveṣa ityuktaṃ | tathā vātaḥ sarvatra saṃcārī vāyurṛbhukṣāḥ patiriṃdraśca | etānapi pra kṛṇudhvaṃ | ato 'haṃ svāyattabalān sarvānapi devān sumnāya sukhāyācchābhimukhyena vavṛtīya | stotrairabhivartayeyaṃ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** (O ṛtviks!) अश्विना (*aśvinā*) — the Aśvin deities; पूषणं (*pūṣaṇaṃ*) — and the Pūṣan deity, the nourisher (aiming at them); अवसे (*avase*) — for our protection; प्रो कृणुध्वं (*pro kṛṇudhvaṃ*) — praise fully; अद्वेषः (*adveṣaḥ*) — free from hatred; विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*) — Viṣṇu, the pervader; वातः (*vātaḥ*) — the Vāyu deity who moves everywhere; ऋभुक्षाः (*ṛbhukṣāḥ*) — Indra, the lord; स्वतवसः (*svatavasaḥ*) — the other deities of independent strength; संति हि (*saṃti hi*) — who are there; (तानपि (*tānapi*) — aiming at them too) प्र (कृणुध्वं) (*pra (kṛṇudhvaṃ)*) — praise fully; (I too) देवान् (*devān*) — all the deities; सुम्नाय (*sumnāya*) — for happiness; अच्छ (*accha*) — so that they face me; ववृतीय (*vavṛtīya*) — make (by praises) to turn toward me.

**Bhāvārtha** *(begun on p. 162, continued on p. 163)*. O ṛtviks, praise the Aśvin deities and the nourishing Pūṣan deity for our protection. Viṣṇu, free from hatred and pervading, Vāyu who moves everywhere …

### Printed p. 163 (PDF 181)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 5". Ṛk 10: Bhāvārtha concluded, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

… the Vāyu deity, the lord Indra, and the other deities of independent strength — praise them all together. I too, in order to obtain my happiness, praise them so that all the deities may remain facing toward me.

**English Translation (as printed):**

Propitiate the Ashwins and Pushan, for my protection ; (propitiate) those (deities), who are of independent powers, as Vishnu, devoid of hatred, Vayu, and Ribhukshin, and may I influence the gods to be present for my felicity.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

In this ṛk the Aśvin deities, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, Vāta, Indra and other deities are praised.

ऋभुक्षाः (*ṛbhukṣāḥ*) — The Niruktakāra has given two meanings for this word: उरुक्षयणः इंद्रः (*urukṣayaṇaḥ iṃdraḥ*) — "he who dwells in the wide atmosphere", as an epithet of Indra; or ऋभूणां राजा (*ṛbhūṇāṃ rājā*) — "king of the Ṛbhus, or of the shining deities" — he has said it may mean (Ni. 9-3, zoomed). Or, as Sāyaṇa has explained, since this word is read among the names for "great" (mahannāmas) (Ni. 3-13, zoomed), it may also be Indra, the great one.

वातः (*vātaḥ*) — For this word Yāska's Nirukta: वातो वातीति सतः (*vāto vātīti sataḥ*) — because it blows, this deity (the wind) is named Vāta (Ni. 10-34, zoomed). The two words vāyu and vāta are both used in a sense denoting both the Vāyu deity and the wind. But Vāyu is the deity, Vāta the wind. There are two sūktas with Vāta as deity (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-168 and 10-186; 10-168 zoomed, 10-186 read from the strip), some portions in other sūktas, and about twelve sūktas (of Vāyu) together with Indra. The two words vāyu and vāta also occur in one and the same ṛk —

> ते नो रुद्रः सरस्वती सजोषा मीळ्हुष्मंतो विष्णुर्मृळंतु वायुः ।
> ऋभुक्षा वाजो दैव्यो विधाता पर्जन्यावाता पिप्यतामिषं नः ॥

> *te no rudraḥ sarasvatī sajoṣā mīḷhuṣmaṃto viṣṇurmṛḷaṃtu vāyuḥ |*
> *ṛbhukṣā vājo daivyo vidhātā parjanyāvātā pipyatāmiṣaṃ naḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-50-12, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "May Rudra, Sarasvatī of one accord, the bountiful ones, Viṣṇu and Vāyu be gracious to us; Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, the divine Disposer, Parjanya and Vāta swell for us refreshment.")

> प्र नः पूषा चरथं विश्वदेव्योऽपां नपादवतु वायुरिष्टये ।
> आत्मानं वस्यो अभि वातमर्चत तदश्विना सुहवा यामनि श्रुतं ॥

> *pra naḥ pūṣā carathaṃ viśvadevyo 'pāṃ napādavatu vāyuriṣṭaye |*
> *ātmānaṃ vasyo abhi vātamarcata tadaśvinā suhavā yāmani śrutaṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-92-13, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "May Pūṣan, dear to all gods, further our moving herds, may Apāṃ Napāt and Vāyu help us to our desire; praise Vāta, the breath, for a better state; hear that, O Aśvins, easy to call, on your course.")
