### Printed p. 194 (PDF 212)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 187". Ṛk 3: Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā concluded; end of Ṛk 3. Ṛk 4: Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha.)*

सुशेवः (*suśevaḥ*) — root शीङ् स्वप्ने (*śīṅ svapne*); suffix वन् (*van*) by इण्शीङ्भ्यां वन् (*iṇśīṅbhyāṃ van*) (U. Sū. 1-150, zoomed; middle digit read as 5); guṇa by सार्वधातुकार्ध (*sārvadhātukārdha*)— (no number printed); being *nit*, initial acute. In the bahuvrīhi compound, overriding the accent of सु (*su*), the second member takes initial acute by आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच् छन्दसि (*ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-119, zoomed). अद्वयाः (*advayāḥ*) — by तत्पुरुषे तुल्या (*tatpuruṣe tulyā*)— (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2, zoomed) the first member नञ् (*nañ*) keeps its own accent.

*(A short rule: end of Ṛk 3.)*

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तव त्ये पितो रसा रजांस्यनु विष्ठिताः ।
> दिवि वाता इव श्रिताः ॥ ४ ॥

> *tava tye pito rasā rajāṃsyanu viṣṭhitāḥ |*
> *divi vātā iva śritāḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तव । त्ये । पितो इति । रसाः । रजांसि । अनु । विऽस्थिताः ।
> दिवि । वाताःऽइव । श्रिताः ॥ ४ ॥

> *tava | tye | pito iti | rasāḥ | rajāṃsi | anu | vi 'sthitāḥ |*
> *divi | vātāḥ 'iva | śritāḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; one place zoomed.)*

> हे पितो तव त्वत्संबंधिनस्त्ये ते स्वाद्वम्लादिषड्रसा रजांसि लोकाँल्लोके-स्थानार्थानन्वानुकूल्येन विष्ठिताः । विविधं स्थिताः । विविधस्थितौ दृष्टांतः । दिवि द्युलोकेऽंतरिक्षे श्रिता वाता वायवः ते यथा व्याप्तास्तद्वत् ॥

> *he pito tava tvatsaṃbaṃdhinastye te svādvamlādiṣaḍrasā rajāṃsi lokā~lloke-sthānārthānanvānukūlyena viṣṭhitāḥ | vividhaṃ sthitāḥ | vividhasthitau dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | divi dyuloke 'ṃtarikṣe śritā vātā vāyavaḥ te yathā vyāptāstadvat ‖*

*Gist:* Your six tastes, sweet, sour and the rest, pervade the worlds favourably, as the winds resting in the sky pervade it.

**Pratipadārtha.** पितो (*pito*) — O food; दिवि (*divi*) — in the antarikṣa; श्रिताः (*śritāḥ*) — having taken shelter and spreading; वाताः इव (*vātāḥ iva*) — as the winds are pervading everywhere; ते (*te*) — your; त्ये रसाः (*tye rasāḥ*) — the renowned six tastes beginning with sour too; रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*) — all the worlds; अनुविष्ठिताः (*anuviṣṭhitāḥ*) — have spread and pervaded in various ways, so as to be favourable to the world.

**Bhāvārtha.** O food, just as the winds spreading in the antarikṣa pervade everywhere, so your six tastes beginning with sour too pervade all the worlds in various ways and are favourable to the world.

### Printed p. 195 (PDF 213)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 6". Ṛk 4: printed English; Special Topics.)*

**English Translation (as printed).**

Your flavours, Pitu, are diffused through the regions, as the winds are spread through the sky.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**त्ये—ते (*tye—te*)** — wherever the word त्य (*tya*) occurs in the Ṛgveda, it has the meaning of the word तत् (*tat*) ("that") itself. The Niruktakāra —

> त्यमू षु वाजिनं देवजूतं सहावानं तरुतारं रथानां ।

> *tyamū ṣu vājinaṃ devajūtaṃ sahāvānaṃ tarutāraṃ rathānāṃ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-178-1, zoomed)

> प्रति त्यं चारुमध्वरं गोपीथाय प्र हूयसे । मरुद्भिरग्न आ गहि ॥

> *prati tyaṃ cārumadhvaraṃ gopīthāya pra hūyase | marudbhiragna ā gahi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-19-1, zoomed)

— has explained the meaning of the word त्यम् (*tyam*) in ṛks such as these as तम् (*tam*) (Ni. 10-29, 37, zoomed).

**रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*)** — the word रजः (*rajaḥ*) is read among the thirty names of night beginning with श्यावी (*śyāvī*), क्षपा (*kṣapā*) (Ni. 2-18, zoomed). And Yāska, explaining the meaning of the word रजः (*rajaḥ*) —

> रजः । रजो रजतेर्ज्योती रज उच्यते । उदकं रज उच्यते । लोका रजांस्युच्यंते ॥

> *rajaḥ | rajo rajaterjyotī raja ucyate | udakaṃ raja ucyate | lokā rajāṃsyucyaṃte ‖*

(Ni. 4-19, zoomed; 'jyotī' as read)

— having stated in his etymology that, being derived from the root रजति (*rajati*), which gives the meaning "to shine", रजः (*rajaḥ*) means light, brightness; that रजः (*rajaḥ*) also means water; and that the word रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*) (the plural of रजः (*rajaḥ*)) means the worlds — has shown, as examples, that in the ṛk

> भुवो यज्ञस्य रजसश्च नेता यत्रा नियुद्भिः सचसे शिवाभिः ।
> दिवि मूर्धानं दधिषे स्वर्षां जिह्वामग्ने चकृषे हव्यवाहं ॥

> *bhuvo yajñasya rajasaśca netā yatrā niyudbhiḥ sacase śivābhiḥ |*
> *divi mūrdhānaṃ dadhiṣe svarṣāṃ jihvāmagne cakṛṣe havyavāhaṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-8-6, zoomed)

the word रजसः (*rajasaḥ*) means water, and that in ṛks such as

*(no reference printed for the next line)*

> रजांसि चित्रा विचरंति तान्यवः ।

> *rajāṃsi citrā vicaraṃti tānyavaḥ |*

> अद्या चिन्नू चित्तदपो नदीनां यदाभ्यो अरदो गातुमिंद्र ।
> नि पर्वता अद्मसदो न सेदुस्त्वया दृळ्हानि सुक्रतो रजांसि ॥

> *adyā cinnū cittadapo nadīnāṃ yadābhyo arado gātumiṃdra |*
> *ni parvatā admasado na sedustvayā dṛḷhāni sukrato rajāṃsi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-30-3, zoomed)

the word रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*) means the worlds. In the present ṛk the meaning is "the worlds".

**रसाः दिवि वाता इव श्रिताः (*rasāḥ divi vātā iva śritāḥ*)** — just as the wind pervades everywhere in the antarikṣa evenly, so the six tastes beginning with sweet pervade the food and produce various kinds of relish: this is the example the ṛṣi has set out here.

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तव त्ये पितो ददतस्तव स्वादिष्ठ ते पितो ।
> प्र स्वाद्मानो रसानां तुविग्रीवा इवेरते ॥ ५ ॥

> *tava tye pito dadatastava svādiṣṭha te pito |*
> *pra svādmāno rasānāṃ tuvigrīvā iverate ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

*(Pada: 'tuvigrīvāḥ' printed without an internal division mark.)*

> तव । त्ये । पितो इति । ददतः । तव । स्वादिष्ठ । ते । पितो इति ।
> प्र । स्वाद्मानः । रसानां । तुविग्रीवाःऽइव । ईरते ॥ ५ ॥

> *tava | tye | pito iti | dadataḥ | tava | svādiṣṭha | te | pito iti |*
> *pra | svādmānaḥ | rasānāṃ | tuvigrīvāḥ 'iva | īrate ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed.)*

> हे पितो पालकान्न त्ये ते त्वदर्थिनो नरास्तव भोक्तारो भवंतीति शेषः । के ते नराः । हे स्वादिष्ठ स्वादुतम पितो पालक तव त्वदनुग्रहात्ते त्वां ददतः प्रयच्छंतो भवंति । यद्वा । ते पितो इत्यादरार्थं । अभ्यासे हि भूयांसमर्थं मन्यंते । किंच तव रसानां स्वाद्वम्लादीनां षण्णां स्वाद्मानः स्वादयितारो भक्षयितार एव तुविग्रीवा इव । तुवीति बहुनाम । प्रवृद्धग्रीवा एव प्रेरते । प्रकर्षेण गच्छंति । संचरंति । इवशब्द एवकारार्थः पूरणो वा । भूलोकेऽत्तार एव दृढांगा भवंतीति प्रसिद्धं । अनशने हि ग्रीवा अधो लंबंते । यद्वा । तव रसानामत्तारोऽसंख्यातग्रीवा इव भवंति रसानां बाहुल्यादिति भावः । एवं बहुरसोपेतमन्नमिति तस्य स्तुतिः ॥

> *he pito pālakānna tye te tvadarthino narāstava bhoktāro bhavaṃtīti śeṣaḥ | ke te narāḥ | he svādiṣṭha svādutama pito pālaka tava tvadanugrahātte tvāṃ dadataḥ prayacchaṃto bhavaṃti | yadvā | te pito ityādarārthaṃ | abhyāse hi bhūyāṃsamarthaṃ manyaṃte | kiṃca tava rasānāṃ svādvamlādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ svādmānaḥ svādayitāro bhakṣayitāra eva tuvigrīvā iva | tuvīti bahunāma | pravṛddhagrīvā eva prerate | prakarṣeṇa gacchaṃti | saṃcaraṃti | ivaśabda evakārārthaḥ pūraṇo vā | bhūloke 'ttāra eva dṛḍhāṃgā bhavaṃtīti prasiddhaṃ | anaśane hi grīvā adho laṃbaṃte | yadvā | tava rasānāmattāro 'saṃkhyātagrīvā iva bhavaṃti rasānāṃ bāhulyāditi bhāvaḥ | evaṃ bahurasopetamannamiti tasya stutiḥ ‖*

*Gist:* Those who give food are its enjoyers by its grace; those who relish its six tastes move about with strong, raised necks (the starving droop theirs); so food rich in tastes is praised.

### Printed p. 197 (PDF 215)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 6". Ṛk 5: Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** स्वादिष्ठ (*svādiṣṭha*) — exceedingly tasty; पितो (*pito*) — O food, the protector; त्ये (*tye*) — the men who seek you; तव (*tava*) — partaking of you, are happy. पितो (*pito*) — O food, the protector; तव (*tava*) — by your grace; ते (*te*) — they (the performers of sacrifice); ददतः (*dadataḥ*) — share you (with others too); रसानाम् (*rasānām*) — your six tastes; स्वाद्मानः (*svādmānaḥ*) — the enjoyers (those who relish your tastes and are happy); तुविग्रीवाः इव (*tuvigrīvāḥ iva*) — like those who have grown and have well-nourished necks; प्र ईरते (*pra īrate*) — move about showing their joy.

**Bhāvārtha.** O food, exceedingly tasty and protecting, the sacrificers who eat you partake of you and are happy. Not only that: they share that happiness with others too. All who relish your six tastes and enjoy happiness move about showing their joy, like those who have grown and have well-nourished necks.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Those (men), Pitu, (are the enjoyers of yonr [sic] bounty), who are your distributors, most sweet Pitu, (to others): they who are relishers, of your flavours, are as if they had stiff necks·

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**त्ये—ते (*tye—te*)** — the meaning of this word we have explained in the preceding ṛk. Here ते (*te*) means men who desire food (or living beings?); the sense is that they eat food.

**तव (*tava*)** — since the word तव (*tava*) is read twice in this ṛk, in accordance with the Niruktakāra's saying अभ्यासे हि भूयांसमर्थं मन्यंते (*abhyāse hi bhūyāṃsamarthaṃ manyaṃte*) (no reference printed) the repetition indicates the esteem, love and regard for food.

**ददतः तव (*dadataḥ tava*)** — those who give (your) food to others (by your grace), who make gifts; and

**स्वाद्मानः रसानाम् (*svādmānaḥ rasānām*)** — those who relish the various tastes in the food, or those who eat food of this kind: these are attributes of the word त्ये (*tye*) (नराः (*narāḥ*)), men. That is, the principal sense is that men who themselves eat food endowed with the six tastes and also give it to others (become well-nourished).

### Printed p. 198 (PDF 216)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 187". Ṛk 5: Special Topics concluded (with Wilson's note); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā.)*

**तुविग्रीवा इव (*tuvigrīvā iva*)** — तुवि (*tuvi*) means "much" (Ni. 3-13 as printed, zoomed); ग्रीव (*grīva*) means the neck, the throat. For this word तुविग्रीवाः (*tuvigrīvāḥ*) Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of meaning. प्रवृद्धग्रीवाः (*pravṛddhagrīvāḥ*) — "as having necks that are well-fed, stout and firm": this is one kind of meaning. Those having stout necks means simply those of firm limbs. It is well known in the world that by partaking of good food not only the neck (throat) becomes stout, but the whole body becomes stout. Though here only the word ग्रीव (*grīva*), neck, is used, it indicates the other limbs of the body too, or the whole body. Therefore he has explained तुविग्रीवा इव (*tuvigrīvā iva*) to mean those who move about with firm limbs. The Bhāṣyakāra has explained that here the word इव (*iva*) has the meaning of the word एव (*eva*), or that the word इव (*iva*) has no definite meaning and is used here merely to fill out the pāda. And explaining a second meaning of the word तुविग्रीवाइव (*tuvigrīvāiva*) —

> तव रसानामत्तारोऽसंख्यातग्रीवा इव भवंति रसानां बाहुल्यादिति भावः ।

> *tava rasānāmattāro 'saṃkhyātagrīvā iva bhavaṃti rasānāṃ bāhulyāditi bhāvaḥ |*

— he has given another kind of meaning: those who eat the manifold tastes of food, that is, food endowed with manifold tastes, are like those who eat with many throats (mouths), that is, they become great eaters. On this matter the English scholar Wilson has explained Sāyaṇa's view in this way —

तुविग्रीवा इवेरते—तुवि is ordinarily, a synonyme [sic] of बहु much, many; Sayana explains it by प्रवृद्ध, enlarged; becuuse [sic], he says, when people eat, they are दृढांग, firm ; and when they are without food, the neck is bent, bends down ; or it may mean that they are great eaters, as if they had many throats·

*(The Sanskrit words in Wilson's note are printed in Kannada script: तुविग्रीवा इवेरते (*tuvigrīvā iverate*), तुवि (*tuvi*), बहु (*bahu*), प्रवृद्ध (*pravṛddha*), दृढांग (*dṛḍhāṃga*).)*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** ददतः (*dadataḥ*) — root डुदाञ् दाने (*ḍudāñ dāne*); शतृ (*śatṛ*) substituted for laṭ; श्लु (*ślu*) vikaraṇa; reduplication of the root etc.; loss of the root's *ā* by श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः (*śnābhyastayorātaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-112, zoomed); in the nominative plural no augment नुम् (*num*) by नाभ्यस्ताच्छतुः (*nābhyastācchatuḥ*) (no number printed); initial acute by अभ्यस्तानामादिः (*abhyastānāmādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-189, zoomed). स्वादिष्ठ (*svādiṣṭha*) — after the word स्वादु (*svādu*) in the sense of excellence by अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ (*atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau*) (no number printed); loss of the टि (*ṭi*) (*u*) of स्वादु (*svādu*) by the sūtra टेः (*ṭeḥ*); in the vocative, the āmantrita-nighāta accent. स्वाद्मानः (*svādmānaḥ*) — root स्वाद आस्वादने (*svāda āsvādane*); suffix मनिन् (*manin*) by अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यंते (*anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyaṃte*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-75, zoomed); being *nit*, initial acute; nominative plural form. ईरते (*īrate*) — root ईर गतौ प्रेरणे च (*īra gatau preraṇe ca*), adādi; laṭ, third person plural form; tiṅanta nighāta accent.

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वे पितो महानां देवानां मनो हितं ।
> अकारि चारु केतुना तवाहिमवसावधीत् ॥ ६ ॥

> *tve pito mahānāṃ devānāṃ mano hitaṃ |*
> *akāri cāru ketunā tavāhimavasāvadhīt ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वे इति । पितो इति । महानां । देवानां । मनः । हितं ।
> अकारि । चारु । केतुना । तव । अहिं । अवसा । अवधीत् ॥ ६ ॥

> *tve iti | pito iti | mahānāṃ | devānāṃ | manaḥ | hitaṃ |*
> *akāri | cāru | ketunā | tava | ahiṃ | avasā | avadhīt ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; two places zoomed.)*

*Gist:* The minds of the great gods are set on food (the mind is made of food, Chāndogya); by food's protection Indra slew the serpent, Vṛtra, for the world's protection.

> हे पितो महानां पूज्यानां महतां वा देवानामिंद्रादीनां मनस्त्वे त्वयि हितं निहितमकारि । कृतं । अन्यृतमपि विहाय त्वय्येव वर्तते । हे पितो तव चारु समीचीनेन केतुना त्वत्कृतेन प्रज्ञानलक्षणेनावसा रक्षणेनाहिं मेघं वृत्रं वावधीत् । हतवानिंद्रः । अन्नमयं हि सोम्य मनः । छां. ६ ५-४ । इति श्रुतेः । अथवा त्वत्केतुना जगद्रक्षणेन निमित्तेनेति योज्यं । जगद्रक्षणार्थं हींद्रेणाहिर्वध्यते ॥

> *he pito mahānāṃ pūjyānāṃ mahatāṃ vā devānāmiṃdrādīnāṃ manastve tvayi hitaṃ nihitamakāri | kṛtaṃ | anyṛtamapi vihāya tvayyeva vartate | he pito tava cāru samīcīnena ketunā tvatkṛtena prajñānalakṣaṇenāvasā rakṣaṇenāhiṃ meghaṃ vṛtraṃ vāvadhīt | hatavāniṃdraḥ | annamayaṃ hi somya manaḥ | chāṃ. 6 5-4 | iti śruteḥ | athavā tvatketunā jagadrakṣaṇena nimitteneti yojyaṃ | jagadrakṣaṇārthaṃ hīṃdreṇāhirvadhyate ‖*

*('anyṛtamapi' as printed; 'vāvadhīt' = vā avadhīt; reference Chāṃ. 6 5-4 as printed, zoomed.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** पितो (*pito*) — O food; महानाम् (*mahānām*) — venerable; देवानाम् (*devānām*) — of the gods Indra and the rest; मनः (*manaḥ*) — the mind; त्वे (*tve*) — in you alone; हितम् अकारि (*hitam akāri*) — has been placed; तव (*tava*) — your; चारु (*cāru*) — which is beautiful; केतुना (*ketunā*) — and which is of the form of knowledge; अवसा (*avasā*) — by the protection; अहिम् (*ahim*) — the cloud (or Vṛtra); अवधीत् (*avadhīt*) — Indra slew.

**Bhāvārtha.** O food, the venerable gods Indra and the rest too have their minds fixed on you alone. By your protection, beautiful and of the form of knowledge, Indra slew Vṛtra.

**English Translation (as printed).**

The thoughts of the mighty gods are fixed. [sic] Pitu, upon you, by your kind and intelligent assistance, (Indra) slew Ahi·

### Printed p. 200 (PDF 218)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 187" (zoomed). Ṛk 6: Special Topics; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā begins.)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**महानाम् (*mahānām*)** — of the noble-minded, or of the venerable. The words महत् (*mahat*) and महः (*mahaḥ*) are also read among the names of water (Ni. 2-24 as printed, zoomed). And Yāska, giving the nirvacana of the first ṛk of this sūkta, पितुं नु स्तोषं (*pituṃ nu stoṣaṃ*), has explained the word महः (*mahaḥ*) in it as meaning महतः (*mahataḥ*). Therefore in the present ṛk the meaning "having greatness, of great glory, great, that is, venerable" for the word महानाम् (*mahānām*) is appropriate. Here the use of the word महानाम् (*mahānām*) serves to heighten the excellence of food. Thus महानां देवानां मनः त्वे हितम् (*mahānāṃ devānāṃ manaḥ tve hitam*) — it is said that the mind of the gods of great glory, not counting for so much even amṛta, their natural food, is set on you (on food). That is, even the gods of great glory desire food. The use of the word महानाम् (*mahānām*) emphatically states the greatness of food, so that it need not even be said how great the need of food is for men and other living beings.

**केतुना (*ketunā*)** — the word केतु (*ketu*) means prajñāna, knowledge (Ni. 3-13 as printed, zoomed). The Bhāṣyakāra's explanation is "(protection) endowed with the character of prajñāna". That is, the intended sense is the excellent knowledge or intelligence that arises in those who partake of food.

**अहिं अवधीत् (*ahiṃ avadhīt*)** — though the word अहि (*ahi*) has various meanings, here it means Vṛtra. Though in this sentence there is no noun denoting the agent, it must be supplied. Since the one who destroyed Vṛtra is Indra, the intention is that here the word इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*) must be supplied as the agent. The very meaning stated in the first ṛk of this sūkta — namely, that Indra destroyed the asura Vṛtra by the excellent (abundant) strength of food — is stated in the latter half of this ṛk.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** महानाम् (*mahānām*) — root मह पूजायाम् (*maha pūjāyām*); suffix अच् (*ac*) by नंदिग्रहिपचादिभ्य (*naṃdigrahipacādibhya*) (visarga not printed) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-134, zoomed); being *cit*, end-acute; genitive plural form. हितम् (*hitam*) — root डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*); suffix क्त (*kta*) by निष्ठा (*niṣṭhā*); हि (*hi*) substituted when the suffix follows by दधातेर्हिः (*dadhāterhiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-42, zoomed); end-acute by the suffix accent. अकारि (*akāri*) — root डुकृञ् करणे (*ḍukṛñ karaṇe*); luṅ in the passive; चिण् (*ciṇ*) for च्लि (*cli*) by चिण् भावकर्मणोः (*ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-66, zoomed); vṛddhi of the root's *ṛ* by the sūtra अचो ञ्णिति (*aco ñṇiti*) …

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यददो पितो अजगन्विवस्व पर्वतानां ।
> अत्रा चिन्नो मधो पितोऽरं भक्षाय गम्याः ॥ ७ ॥

> *yadado pito ajaganvivasva parvatānāṃ |*
> *atrā cinno madho pito 'raṃ bhakṣāya gamyāḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यत् । अदः । पितो इति । अजगन् । विवस्व । पर्वतानां ।
> अत्र । चित् । नः । मधो इति । पितो इति । अरं । भक्षाय । गम्याः ॥ ७ ॥

> *yat | adaḥ | pito iti | ajagan | vivasva | parvatānāṃ |*
> *atra | cit | naḥ | madho iti | pito iti | araṃ | bhakṣāya | gamyāḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; first two lines zoomed.)*

*('supo luk', the double daṇḍas and 'vivo dhanam' as printed, zoomed.)*

*Gist:* When that well-known water of the clouds, rich in lightning-light, comes to you, O food, then, sweet food, come to us fully for eating.

> हे पितो अन्न त्वां यद्यदा विवस्व ॥ सुपो लुक् । अंत्यलोपश्छांदसः ॥ विवासनवतां विद्युद्रूपप्रकाशनवतां । विवो धनमुदकलक्षणं । धनवतां वा पर्वतानां मेघानां संबंध्यदः प्रसिद्धं तदुदकमजगन् अगमत् गच्छेत् । अत्र चिदस्मिन्काले नोऽस्मान् हे मधो हे पितो माधुर्योपेतान्न त्वं नोऽस्मानरमलं संपूर्णं भक्षाय भक्षणाय गम्याः । गच्छ । संनिहितो भव ॥

> *he pito anna tvāṃ yadyadā vivasva ‖ supo luk | aṃtyalopaśchāṃdasaḥ ‖ vivāsanavatāṃ vidyudrūpaprakāśanavatāṃ | vivo dhanamudakalakṣaṇaṃ | dhanavatāṃ vā parvatānāṃ meghānāṃ saṃbaṃdhyadaḥ prasiddhaṃ tadudakamajagan agamat gacchet | atra cidasminkāle no 'smān he madho he pito mādhuryopetānna tvaṃ no 'smānaramalaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ bhakṣāya bhakṣaṇāya gamyāḥ | gaccha | saṃnihito bhava ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** पितो (*pito*) — O food, the protector; यत् (*yat*) — when; विवस्व (*vivasva*) — endowed with wealth (in the form of water), or with brightness in the form of lightning; पर्वतानाम् (*parvatānām*) — of the clouds; अदः (*adaḥ*) — that well-known water; अजगन् (*ajagan*) — reaches (you); अत्र चित् (*atra cit*) — at that time; मधो (*madho*) — endowed with sweetness; पितो (*pito*) — O food, the protector; नः (*naḥ*) — to us; अरम् (*aram*) — full; भक्षाय (*bhakṣāya*) — fit for eating; गम्याः (*gamyāḥ*) — be present.

**Bhāvārtha.** O food, the protector, when the abundant water of the clouds, endowed with brightness in the form of lightning, reaches you, at that time, O food endowed with sweetness, be present with us so as to be fit for ample eating.

### Printed p. 202 (PDF 220)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 187" (zoomed). Ṛk 7: printed English, Special Topics, Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā.)*

**English Translation (as printed).**

When, Pitu, this (product) of the water-wealthy clouds, (the rain), arrives ; then do you, sweet Pitu, be at hand with sufficiency for our eating·

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**विवस्व (*vivasva*)** — here there should be the word विवस्वताम् (*vivasvatām*), the genitive plural of the word विवस्वत् (*vivasvat*). Since the final syllable ताम् (*tām*) has been dropped as a Vedic usage, only विवस्व (*vivasva*) remains. For the word विवस्वत् (*vivasvat*) Yāska has given विवस्वान् विवासनवान् (*vivasvān vivāsanavān*) (Ni. 7-26, zoomed) विवासनक्रियया तमसाम् (*vivāsanakriyayā tamasām*) — the sense "causing the darkness to go away"; it is just this that the Bhāṣyakāra has explained here. The meaning is "having the light of lightning (*miñcu*), which drives the darkness away". This word is an attribute of the word पर्वतानाम् (*parvatānām*) (मेघानाम् (*meghānām*)).

**पर्वतानाम् (*parvatānām*)** — the word *parvata* is read among the thirty names of the cloud beginning with अद्रिः (*adriḥ*), ग्राव (*grāva*) (Ni. 2-21, zoomed). For the word *parvata* Yāska has given the nirvacana पर्ववान् पर्वतः । पर्व पुनः पृणातेः प्रीणातेर्वा (*parvavān parvataḥ | parva punaḥ pṛṇāteḥ prīṇātervā*) (Ni. 1-20, zoomed). That is, the word *parva* is formed either from the root पृ (*pṛ*), which gives the meaning "to fill", or from the root प्रीञ् (*prīñ*), which gives the meaning "to satisfy". That which has such *parvas* is named *parvata*. If the word *parvata* is formed from the root पृ (*pṛ*), it then means "filling the empty regions". What fills the empty regions of the earth is the hill (the mountain); what fill the empty regions of the sky are the clouds (*parvatas*). And if it is formed from the root प्रीञ् (*prīñ*), the meaning then is "that which produces satisfaction for the whole world by the release of rain". In this meaning too the word *parvata* means the cloud.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** अजगन् (*ajagan*) — root गम्लृ गतौ (*gamlṛ gatau*); as a Vedic usage लङ् in the sense of लिङ्; तिप् (*tip*) in the third person singular; loss of the final *i* by इतश्च (*itaśca*); श्लु (*ślu*) for शप् (*śap*) by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*); reduplication etc. of the root on that account; in the form जगम्-त् (*jagam-t*), loss of the suffix by the sūtra printed हल्ङाभ्यो (*halṅābhyo*) (as printed, zoomed); न (*na*) for the root-final म (*ma*) by मो नो धातोः (*mo no dhātoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-64, zoomed); augment अट् (*aṭ*) to the aṅga; since यत् (*yat*) is connected, the nighāta accent is prohibited; since the augment अट् (*aṭ*) is udātta, initial acute. विवस्व (*vivasva*) — विवः धनं । अस्य अस्ति इति विवस्वान् (*vivaḥ dhanaṃ | asya asti iti vivasvān*); suffix मतुप् (*matup*) by the sūtra तदस्यास्ति (*tadasyāsti*); by तसौ मत्वर्थे (*tasau matvarthe*) (Pā. Sū. 1-1-19 as printed, zoomed), since it has the designation *bha*, *ru* and visarga for the *s* …

… do not come. When the genitive plural follows, its *luk* by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (Pā. #### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यदपामोषधीनां परिंशमारिशामहे ।
> वातापे पीव इद्भव ॥ ८ ॥

> *yadapāmoṣadhīnāṃ pariṃśamāriśāmahe |*
> *vātāpe pīva idbhava ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यत् । अपां । ओषधीनां । परिंशं । आऽरिशामहे ।
> वातापे । पीवः । इत् । भव ॥ ८ ॥

> *yat | apāṃ | oṣadhīnāṃ | pariṃśaṃ | ā 'riśāmahe |*
> *vātāpe | pīvaḥ | it | bhava ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; 'āsvādhayāmaḥ' at its second occurrence as printed, zoomed.)*

*Gist:* Since we eat the gladdening portion of waters and plants, O body (*vātāpi*, sustained by breath), grow stout; or, O all-pervading food, though we taste little of you, be ample.

> यद्येनापामोषधीनां संबंधि परिंशं परिलेशं परितः सुखकरमन्नमारिशामहे आस्वादयामः भक्षयामः तेनान्नोदकसारेण हे वातापे । वातेन प्राणेनाप्नोति स्वनिर्वाहमिति वातेनाप्यायत इति वा वातापि शरीरं । हे शरीर त्वं पीव इदाप्यायित एव भव । अन्नोदकाभ्यां शरीरवृद्धिः प्रसिद्धा । यद्वा । यद्यप्यपामोषधीनां परिंशं लेशमास्वाधयामः तथापि हे वातापे वातवत्सर्वव्यापक पितो त्वमल्पमपि पीवः पीवानेव भव ॥

> *yadyenāpāmoṣadhīnāṃ saṃbaṃdhi pariṃśaṃ parileśaṃ paritaḥ sukhakaramannamāriśāmahe āsvādayāmaḥ bhakṣayāmaḥ tenānnodakasāreṇa he vātāpe | vātena prāṇenāpnoti svanirvāhamiti vātenāpyāyata iti vā vātāpi śarīraṃ | he śarīra tvaṃ pīva idāpyāyita eva bhava | annodakābhyāṃ śarīravṛddhiḥ prasiddhā | yadvā | yadyapyapāmoṣadhīnāṃ pariṃśaṃ leśamāsvādhayāmaḥ tathāpi he vātāpe vātavatsarvavyāpaka pito tvamalpamapi pīvaḥ pīvāneva bhava ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** यत् (*yat*) — for which reason; अपाम् (*apām*) — of the waters too; ओषधीनाम् (*oṣadhīnām*) — and belonging to the plants; परिंशम् (*pariṃśam*) — the food that produces happiness fully; आरिशामहे (*āriśāmahe*) — we eat (therefore); वातापे (*vātāpe*) — O body; पीव इत् भव (*pīva it bhava*) — …

… grow exceedingly stout. [Or: यत् (*yat*) — if; अपाम् (*apām*) — of the waters too; ओषधीनाम् (*oṣadhīnām*) — and in the food belonging to the plants; परिंशम् (*pariṃśam*) — only a small portion; आरिशामहे (*āriśāmahe*) — even though we eat; वातापे (*vātāpe*) — O food, all-pervading like the wind; पीव इत् भव (*pīva it bhava*) — (even though small) be indeed nourishing. *(The closing bracket is not printed.)*

**Bhāvārtha.** O body, by eating food that belongs to the waters and the plants and produces happiness fully, grow exceedingly stout.

**English Translation (as printed).**

And since we enjoy, the abundance of the waters and the plants ; therefore, Body, do you grow fat·

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).** *(The heading is printed garbled, "Viṣaśeṣaviyagaḷu".)*

**यत् अपां ओषधीनाम् (*yat apāṃ oṣadhīnām*)** — *oṣadhis* means crops and the like, or the grains and the like obtained from crops. Here they are attribute-words to food: "connected with water and with plants". Since plants are obtained from water, grains from plants, and food from grains, food is said to be connected with plants and water.

**वातापे (*vātāpe*)** — वातेन प्राणेनाप्नोति स्वनिर्वाहमिति वातेनाप्यायत इति वा वातापि शरीरम् (*vātena prāṇenāpnoti svanirvāhamiti vātenāpyāyata iti vā vātāpi śarīram*) — that is, since all its (the body's) activities are carried on by the vital air, *vātāpi* means the body; or, since it is satisfied by the air, *vātāpi* means the body: so the Bhāṣyakāra has given two kinds of meaning for the word *vātāpi*.

**पीवः आप्यायितः (*pīvaḥ āpyāyitaḥ*)** — Sāyaṇa's explanation is "that which produces satisfaction". In Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-91-3 (zoomed) —

> पीवोअन्ना रयिवृधः सुमेधाः श्वेतः सिषक्ति नियुतामभिश्रीः ।

> *pīvoannā rayivṛdhaḥ sumedhāḥ śvetaḥ siṣakti niyutāmabhiśrīḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-91-3, zoomed)

— when explaining the word पीवोअन्नान् (*pīvoannān*) in that ṛk the Bhāṣyakāra has given पीवोअन्नान् पीवांसि स्थूलानि प्रभूतान्यन्नानि येषां तान् (*pīvoannān pīvāṃsi sthūlāni prabhūtānyannāni yeṣāṃ tān*) — for the word *pīva* the meaning *sthūla*, that is, very abundant.

> उताहमद्मि पीव इदुभा कुक्षी पृणंति मे विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ।

> *utāhamadmi pīva idubhā kukṣī pṛṇaṃti me viśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-86-14, zoomed)

— in that ṛk पीव इत् (*pīva it*) is स्थूल एव (*sthūla eva*), that is, *sthūla*; and

— in that ṛk the Bhāṣyakāra has explained पीवः (*pīvaḥ*) as प्रवृद्धम् (*pravṛddham*), that is, "producing growth". Since it is a matter of common knowledge that by eating excellent food the body is satisfied and grows and increases, there is no need to explain anything more on that matter.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** अपाम् (*apām*) — udātta accent on the genitive plural ending by ऊडिदंपदादि (*ūḍidaṃpadādi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198, zoomed). पीवः (*pīvaḥ*) — root प्यैङ् वृद्धौ (*pyaiṅ vṛddhau*); auṇādika suffix वन् (*van*); samprasāraṇa of the root; parapūrva form; since the suffix is *nit*, initial acute.

#### Ṛk 9

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यत्ते सोम गवाशिरो यवाशिरो भजामहे ।
> वातापे पीव इद्भव ॥ ९ ॥

> *yatte soma gavāśiro yavāśiro bhajāmahe |*
> *vātāpe pīva idbhava ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥** *(No daṇḍa is printed between इत् (*it*) and भव (*bhava*).)*

> वातापे । पीवः । इत् भव ॥ ९ ॥

> *yat | te | soma | go 'āśiraḥ | yava 'āśiraḥ | bhajāmahe |*
> *vātāpe | pīvaḥ | it bhava ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed.)*

*Gist:* Having praised food in general, he now praises food in the form of Soma: by the Soma we partake of, mixed with milk or barley, O body, grow stout.

### Printed p. 206 (PDF 225)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 187". Ṛk 9: Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** सोम (*soma*) — O Soma juice; ते (*te*) — your; गवाशिरः (*gavāśiraḥ*) — joined with milk and the like; यवाशिरः (*yavāśiraḥ*) — mixed with barley and other grains; यत् (*yat*) — whatever portion of yours; भजामहे (*bhajāmahe*) — we partake of (therefore); वातापे (*vātāpe*) — O body; पीवः इत् भव (*pīvaḥ it bhava*) — grow indeed stout. *(The headword is printed प्रीवः (*prīvaḥ*), with a ra-subscript, zoomed.)*

**Bhāvārtha.** O body, since we drink the portion of Soma juice which is गवाशिर (*gavāśira*) and यवाशिर (*yavāśira*), therefore do you grow stout.

**English Translation (as printed).**

And since we enjoy Soma, your mixture with boiled milk or boiled barley ; therefore body do you grow fat·

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

Up to this point food in general has been praised. Now, in this ṛk and in the ṛks that follow it, it is not the food ordinarily in use that is praised; rather food in the form of Soma, and the foods called गवाशिर (*gavāśira*) and यवाशिर (*yavāśira*) mixed with Soma, are praised.

On the subject of Soma we have given detailed explanations many times before. Still, it is necessary now to give a brief explanation of it. In the Veda there are many mantras dealing with Soma. The whole of the ninth Maṇḍala is nothing but the praise of Soma. When many deities are invoked, they are called to come to this sacrifice for the drinking of Soma. There are many sacrifices connected with Soma. Among them the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice is the chief. In this sacrifice, with the recitation of mantras such as the स्तोत्र (*stotra*)s and शस्त्र (*śastra*)s, Soma is pressed out as enjoined at the three pressings (सवन (*savana*)s) (morning, midday and evening), prepared, and the sacrificer (यजमान (*yajamāna*)) and the priests (ऋत्विज् (*ṛtvij*)s) drink it. In the other Soma sacrifices too this same order is followed, with some differences.

Now it must be considered what Soma is. Soma is a particular kind of creeper. This Soma creeper is not now found anywhere in India. It grows especially in open lands, on river banks and on hills. The higher the place where it grows, the more juice it gives. It grows even at a height of about 2000 feet. Therefore descriptions of this Soma being brought from the mountains are found in many places in the Ṛgveda (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-93-6; 3-48-2; 5-43-4 etc., zoomed). The mountain called मौजवत (*maujavata*) (as printed) is famous for the Soma creeper.
### Printed p. 207 (PDF 226)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 7" (zoomed). Special Topics of Ṛk 9, continued.)*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-34-1; Vā. Saṃ. 3-61; Ni. 9-8 etc., zoomed). It is said here and there in the Ṛgveda (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-7-29, 8-64-11, 9-65-22 etc., zoomed) that the Soma creeper is found on the banks of the lake called शर्यणावत् (*śaryaṇāvat*). And it is said that Soma is found in the place called आर्जीक (*ārjīka*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-7-29, 8-64-11 etc., zoomed), in the country called पस्त्य (*pastya*) (as printed) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-65-23, zoomed), in the place where the five groups called the पंचजन (*paṃcajana*)s live (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-65-23, 9-92-3 etc., zoomed), and in the regions round about the river called सुषोम (*suṣoma*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-7-29, 8-64-11 etc., zoomed). As for the last, सुषोम (*suṣoma*) means su + soma: since it is a place where good Soma is obtained, this region may have come to be named सुषोम (*suṣoma*). It therefore becomes known that in the Ṛgvedic period the Soma creeper grew in plenty in the plains and on the river banks of the present Punjab country. Since the creeper growing in the plains did not yield as much juice as the creeper growing on the mountains, they used the creeper of the plains after soaking it well in water (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-63-4, 9-74-9, 9-79-4 etc., zoomed).

The stalk of this creeper grows to a height of about 4 feet. Its stalk is round, soft, and of a red colour mixed with white; and it is about a finger's breadth thick. The leaves are very few, and white and small. Generally the leaves fall off. At the tip of the plant there is a cluster (looking like *joḷa*, millet) joined with some seeds. Its juice is white mixed with green. Though it is somewhat sweet in taste, it turns sour if kept for some days. When it grows near a large tree, it spreads round the tree like a creeper and grows. Here and there it has joints. It can be broken easily.

We describe here briefly the procedure to be followed in preparing the Soma juice — the Soma creeper growing on river banks and on the mountains they brought with much effort, or acquired by purchase from those who brought it, and used in the sacrifices. Even now the rite called सोमविक्रयण (*somavikrayaṇa*) (as printed) is performed in the sacrifices. After the Soma creeper has been brought, it is the custom to crush and pound it with stones (ग्राव (*grāva*), अद्रि (*adri*)), strain it through a cloth, mix with it curd, milk and flour according to the occasion, offer it to the deities, and afterwards for the sacrificer and the priests to drink it. This preparing of the Soma juice takes place in the morning, at midday and in the evening of the chief day of the sacrifice. It is called अभिषवण (*abhiṣavaṇa*) or सवन (*savana*) (pressing out the juice). The rite of the morning is called प्रातःसवन (*prātaḥsavana*), the pressing done at midday माध्यंदिनसवन (*mādhyaṃdinasavana*), and the pressing done in the evening तृतीयसवन (*tṛtīyasavana*).

The Soma creeper (its creepers) is of a बभ्रु (*babhru*), अरुण (*aruṇa*) (dull red) or yellow-mixed red colour. The creeper grown at a great height on the mountains is (held to be) the best, and from it more … *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 208 (PDF 227)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 187". Special Topics of Ṛk 9, continued.)*

… juice can be drawn, it has been said; therefore, wherever possible, they brought the Soma creeper from the mountains themselves. Among such mountains the mountain called मूजवत (*mūjavata*) (so printed here; p. 206 has मौजवत (*maujavata*)) was famous. The shoot of this Soma creeper is called by the name अंश (*aṃśa*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-168-3; 3-48-2 etc., zoomed); the shoot together with its tender leaves वक्षणा (*vakṣaṇā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-1-17, zoomed) and वाणी (*vāṇī*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-28-9; 9-50-1, zoomed); the Soma juice अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-28-7; 3-48-1; 4-16-1, zoomed); and the stalk (stem) of the Soma creeper पर्वन् (*parvan*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-9-0, zoomed): such is the usage.

The procedure for preparing the Soma juice: they removed the leaves on the Soma creeper or on its stems, put it in a mortar and pounded it with a stone. If the creeper was not fresh, they soaked it in water for a day or two and drew the juice after it had become soft. The mortar in which the Soma creeper is pounded is called उलूखल (*ulūkhala*). It is generally made of stone itself; making it of wood is also known. The stone with which it is struck from above in the mortar has the names ग्रावा (*grāvā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-83-6; 1-135-7, zoomed) and अद्रि (*adri*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-130-2; 1-135-5; 1-136-1, zoomed). It may be guessed that the उलूखल (*ulūkhala*) was not like the mortar we use now, but was only a small hollow in the middle of a stone. This mortar called उलूखल (*ulūkhala*) was used for pounding grain with the मुसल (*musala*) (pestle).

The vessel in which Soma is placed for offering to the deities is called चमू (*camū*). The vessels the priests use for drinking the Soma are called कलश (*kalaśa*) and चमस (*camasa*). In some contexts the word चमू (*camū*) is also used to denote the उलूखल (*ulūkhala*) and the ग्रावा (*grāvā*) (mortar and pounding stone; printed in English "mortar and pestle") (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-28-9; 4-18-3; 6-5 7 [?], zoomed; the last reference printed with a gap and no hyphen).

When the Soma creepers are pounded, it is the custom to keep them on hides. This hide is called त्वक् (*tvak*). For this they used cow-hide (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-94-9; 10-116-4, zoomed). The vessels in which the Soma is collected and kept have names such as कोश (*kośa*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-101-4; 8-20-8), सधस्थ (*sadhastha*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-62-15; 9-1-2; 9-17-8), द्रु (*dru*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-1-2; 9-65-6; 9-98-2), वन (*vana*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-9; 9-66-9) and द्रोण (*droṇa*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-15-7; 9-33-2) (all zoomed). स्रुव (*sruva*) means a ladle (printed "ladle·" [sic]; Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-24, zoomed). The cloth or strainer through which the Soma juice is filtered is called पवित्र (*pavitra*). In some contexts they filtered the Soma even through the gaps between the fingers.

For the use of the Soma juice without admixture of other substances they say शुक्र (*śukra*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-136-1 : 3-32-2; 8-2-10, colon as printed) and शुचि (*śuci*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-5-5; 1-30-2; 8-2-9) (zoomed).
### Printed p. 209 (PDF 228)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 7" (zoomed). Special Topics of Ṛk 9, continued.)*

There are descriptions of many kinds saying that the colour of this juice is of various sorts — बभ्रु (*babhru*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-33-2; 9-63-4 & 6), हरित (*harita*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-3-9 : 9-7-6; 9-65-8), अरुण (*aruṇa*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-40-2; 9-45-3), अरुष (*aruṣa*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-61-21), शोण (*śoṇa*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-97-13) — and that it is endowed with a good fragrance (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-97-9, 9-107-2) (all zoomed).

To give the Soma juice a taste they mix some substances with it. This admixture is called the आशिर (*āśira*)-substances. Soma juice mixed with milk is called गवाशिर (*gavāśira*), Soma juice mixed with curd दध्याशिर (*dadhyāśira*), and Soma juice mixed with flour यवाशिर (*yavāśira*). The Soma juice is sometimes called तीव्र (*tīvra*). It is then to be understood as having a sharp smell or taste (printed in English "pungent flavour"). The fibrous part left over after the Soma juice has been drawn is called ऋजीष (*ṛjīṣa*).

ग्रावा (*grāvā*) — the stone with which the Soma juice is pounded out. As the word पृथुबुध्नः (*pṛthubudhnaḥ*) explains, this stone is a round stone broad at the bottom and shaped like a handle at the top; a stone shaped like the grinding stone in a stone hand-mill (*kalbatti*). Generally in the Ṛgveda the stones used for pounding the Soma creeper are called by the words ग्रावा (*grāvā*) and अद्रि (*adri*).

दध्याशिरः (*dadhyāśiraḥ*) — for this word the Bhāṣyakāra has given the meaning अवनीयमानं दध्याशीर्दोषघातकं येषां सोमानां ते दध्याशिरः (*avanīyamānaṃ dadhyāśīrdoṣaghātakaṃ yeṣāṃ somānāṃ te dadhyāśiraḥ*), that is, since curd is mixed with the Soma juice to remove the defect in it, it is called दध्याशिरः (*dadhyāśiraḥ*). It was the custom to use the Soma juice after mixing with it (for taste) not only curd but also other substances such as milk and flour. On this matter we have written at length in Part 1 of this Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, page 676. The word दध्याशिरः (*dadhyāśiraḥ*) occurs not only in this ṛk but also in the other ṛks given below —

(1)

> इम आयातमिंदवः सोमासो दध्याशिरः सुतासो दध्याशिरः ।

> *ima āyātamiṃdavaḥ somāso dadhyāśiraḥ sutāso dadhyāśiraḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-137-2, zoomed; "āyāta" printed as one word)

(2)

> सुता इंद्राय वायवे सोमासो दध्याशिरः ।

> *sutā iṃdrāya vāyave somāso dadhyāśiraḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-51-7, zoomed)

(3)

> इम इंद्राय सुन्विरे सोमासो दध्याशिरः ॥

> *ima iṃdrāya sunvire somāso dadhyāśiraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-32-4, zoomed)

(4)

> एते पूता विपश्चितः सोमासो दध्याशिरः ॥

> *ete pūtā vipaścitaḥ somāso dadhyāśiraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-22-3, zoomed)

(5)

> सुता इंद्राय वज्रिणे सोमासो दध्याशिरः ।

> *sutā iṃdrāya vajriṇe somāso dadhyāśiraḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-63-15, zoomed)

*(Foot of the page: signature mark "[14]" and "Vol. 14".)*

### Printed p. 210 (PDF 229)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 187". Special Topics of Ṛk 9, continued.)*

(6)

> एते पूता विपश्चितः सोमासो दध्याशिरः ॥

> *ete pūtā vipaścitaḥ somāso dadhyāśiraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-101-12, zoomed)

Besides this word दध्याशिर (*dadhyāśira*), Soma juices mixed with other substances, such as गवाशिर (*gavāśira*) and यवाशिर (*yavāśira*), are mentioned in these ṛks —

(1)

> तीव्राः सोमास आ गह्याशीर्वंतः सुता इमे ॥

> *tīvrāḥ somāsa ā gahyāśīrvaṃtaḥ sutā ime ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-23-1, zoomed)

Since in this ṛk it is said आशीर्वंतः सोमासः (*āśīrvaṃtaḥ somāsaḥ*), it is stated in general that some kind of आशिर (*āśira*)-substance, such as milk or curd, has been mixed with the Soma juice.

(2)

> शतं वा यः शुचीनां सहस्रं वा समाशिरां ॥

> *śataṃ vā yaḥ śucīnāṃ sahasraṃ vā samāśirāṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-30-2, zoomed)

Here समाशिरां (*samāśirāṃ*) states in general that आशिर (*āśira*)-substances have been well mixed with the Soma juice. No substance is named specifically.

(3)

> सुषुमा यातमद्रिभिर्गोश्रीता मत्सरा इमे सोमासो मत्सरा
> इमे ।
> आ राजाना दिविस्पृशास्मत्रा गंतमुप नः ॥
> इमे वां मित्रावरुणा गवाशिरः सोमाः शुक्रा गवाशिरः ॥

> *suṣumā yātamadribhirgośrītā matsarā ime somāso matsarā*
> *ime |*
> *ā rājānā divispṛśāsmatrā gaṃtamupa naḥ ‖*
> *ime vāṃ mitrāvaruṇā gavāśiraḥ somāḥ śukrā gavāśiraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-137-1, zoomed)

Here गोश्रीताः (*gośrītāḥ*) means गवां पयोभिर्मिश्रिताः (*gavāṃ payobhirmiśritāḥ*), that is, mixed with cow's milk. For the word गवाशिरः (*gavāśiraḥ*) in the last pāda of this same ṛk too the meaning is just Soma mixed with cow's milk.

(4)

> शुचिरसि पुरुनिःष्ठाः क्षीरैर्मध्यतः आशीर्तः । दध्ना मंदिष्ठः शूरस्य ॥

> *śucirasi puruniḥṣṭhāḥ kṣīrairmadhyataḥ āśīrtaḥ | dadhnā maṃdiṣṭhaḥ śūrasya ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-2-9, zoomed; 'puruniḥṣṭhāḥ' and 'madhyataḥ āśīrtaḥ' as printed)

Here it is said that there are two separate juices, with milk and with curd mixed in; that is, it is to be understood that there are both kinds, Soma juice mixed with milk and Soma juice mixed with curd.

(5)

> सं शुक्रासः शुचयः सं गवाशिरः सोमा इंद्रममंदिषुः ॥

> *saṃ śukrāsaḥ śucayaḥ saṃ gavāśiraḥ somā iṃdramamaṃdiṣuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-52-10, zoomed)

Here it is said clearly that गवाशिर (*gavāśira*) means Soma mixed with milk.

> सुतं यथावशत् ॥

> *trikadrukeṣu mahiṣo yavāśiraṃ tuviśuṣmastṛpatsomamapibadviṣṇunā*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-48-0, zoomed)

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** गवाशिरः (*gavāśiraḥ*) — गोभिः आशिरः गवाशिरः (*gobhiḥ āśiraḥ gavāśiraḥ*); here the word *go* denotes milk and the like, the products of the cow; root अश भोजने (*aśa bhojane*); suffix किरच् (*kirac*) by अशेर्णित् (*aśerṇit*) (U. Sū. 1-52, zoomed); since it is declared णित् (*ṇit*), initial vṛddhi by अत उपधायाः (*ata upadhāyāḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116, zoomed); in the compound the original accent of the prior member. भजामहे (*bhajāmahe*) — root भज सेवायाम् (*bhaja sevāyām*); bhvādi; laṭ, first person plural form; since यत् (*yat*) is connected, no nighāta accent; by तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186, zoomed) the lasārvadhātuka is unaccented, so the root accent remains.

*(A short rule: end of Ṛk 9.)*

#### Ṛk 10

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> करंभ ओषधे भव पीवो वृक्क उदारथिः ।
> वातापे पीव इद्भव ॥ १० ॥

> *karaṃbha oṣadhe bhava pīvo vṛkka udārathiḥ |*
> *vātāpe pīva idbhava ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> करंभः । ओषधे । भव । पीवः । वृक्कः । उदारथिः ।
> वातापे । पीवः । इत् । भव ॥ १० ॥

> *karaṃbhaḥ | oṣadhe | bhava | pīvaḥ | vṛkkaḥ | udārathiḥ |*
> *vātāpe | pīvaḥ | it | bhava ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; "ūrdhvagama" zoomed: the hooked glyph is ma.)*

*Gist:* O plant, you who are the lump of meal, be stout, a remover of disease and an enkindler of the senses.

> करंभो यः करंभादिरूपः सक्तुपिंडोऽस्ति तदात्मक हे ओषधे त्वं पीवः स्थौल्यवान् वृक्को व्याधेर्वर्जयिता भव । उदारथिरूर्ध्वगम इंद्रियाणामुद्दीपयिता भव । शिष्टो गतः ॥

> *karaṃbho yaḥ karaṃbhādirūpaḥ saktupiṃḍo 'sti tadātmaka he oṣadhe tvaṃ pīvaḥ sthaulyavān vṛkko vyādhervarjayitā bhava | udārathirūrdhvagama iṃdriyāṇāmuddīpayitā bhava | śiṣṭo gataḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** करंभ (*karaṃbha*) — having the form of करंभ (*karaṃbha*); ओषधे (*oṣadhe*) — O plant (you); पीवः (*pīvaḥ*) — being one who gives nourishment; वृक्कः (*vṛkkaḥ*) — being one who promotes health free from disease; उदारथिः (*udārathiḥ*) — being one who gives consciousness (to the senses), be; वातापे (*vātāpe*) — O body; पीव इत् भव (*pīva it bhava*) — grow indeed stout.

**Bhāvārtha.** O plant having the form of करंभ (*karaṃbha*), be you the giver of nourishment, the promoter of health free from disease, and the giver of consciousness to the senses. O body, do you grow indeed stout.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Vegetable cake of fried meal, be substantial, wholesome, and invigorating ; and, Body, do you grow fat· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

In this ṛk the plant (the crop), which is the cause of food, is praised.

**करंभ (*karaṃbha*)** — for this word the Bhāṣyakāra has said करंभो यः करंभादिरूपः सक्तुपिंडोऽस्ति तदात्मक (*karaṃbho yaḥ karaṃbhādirūpaḥ saktupiṃḍo 'sti tadātmaka*) |, that is, that what is made into balls by mixing (grain) flour is called करंभ (*karaṃbha*), and that the plant … *(continued on p. 213)*

### Printed p. 213 (PDF 232)

… present in that करंभ (*karaṃbha*) form is the plant: so the plant has been addressed. Yāska has said nothing about the word करंभ (*karaṃbha*). The Bhāṣyakāra —

> पूषण्वते ते चकृमा करंभं हरिवते हर्यश्वाय धानाः ।

> *pūṣaṇvate te cakṛmā karaṃbhaṃ harivate haryaśvāya dhānāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-52-7, zoomed)

— for the word करंभ (*karaṃbha*) in this ṛk, करंभं दधिमिश्रं सक्तुं (*karaṃbhaṃ dadhimiśraṃ saktuṃ*), a ball of flour mixed with curd; and

> य एनमादिदेशति करंभादिति पूषणं । न तेन देव आदिशे ॥

> *ya enamādideśati karaṃbhāditi pūṣaṇaṃ | na tena deva ādiśe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-56-1, zoomed)

— in the bhāṣya of this ṛk, करंभात् करंभाणां घृतमिश्राणां यवसक्तूनां (*karaṃbhāt karaṃbhāṇāṃ ghṛtamiśrāṇāṃ yavasaktūnāṃ*), made by mixing wheat flour (as printed in the Kannada) and ghee and tying them into balls; and

> सोममन्य उपासदत्पातवे चम्वोः सुतं । करंभमन्य इच्छति ॥

> *somamanya upāsadatpātave camvoḥ sutaṃ | karaṃbhamanya icchati ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-57 2, as printed: a gap, no hyphen; zoomed)

— for the word करंभम् (*karaṃbham*) in this ṛk, करंभं घृतसिक्तं सक्त्वात्मकं हविः (*karaṃbhaṃ ghṛtasiktaṃ saktvātmakaṃ haviḥ*), an oblation (हविस् (*havis*)) in the form of flour mixed with ghee: so he has explained the meaning. Therefore करंभ (*karaṃbha*) may be taken to mean the oblation prepared in the form of a ball by combining ghee, curd and the like with flour, to be offered to the deities. The English scholar called Wilson has said of this word — करंभ ओषधे (*karaṃbha oṣadhe*) —

The first is explained, a lump or cake of parched meal, सक्तुपिंड idendified [sic] with an herb or vegetable तदात्मक ओषधिः

— and the scholar called Griffith —

करंभ is some soft food, a sort of gruel, offered especially to पूषन्.

*(The Sanskrit words in these notes are printed in Kannada script: सक्तुपिंड (*saktupiṃḍa*), तदात्मक ओषधिः (*tadātmaka oṣadhiḥ*), करंभ (*karaṃbha*), पूषन् (*pūṣan*).)*

**ओषधे (*oṣadhe*)** — the meaning of the word ओषधि (*oṣadhi*) is a tree (वनस्पति (*vanaspati*)) or a plant (सस्य (*sasya*)). Yāska, stating the etymology of the word ओषधि (*oṣadhi*), cites the ṛk

> या ओषधीः पूर्वा जाता देवेभ्यस्त्रियुगं पुरा ।
> मन्ये नु बभ्रूणामहं शतं धामानि सप्त च ॥

> *yā oṣadhīḥ pūrvā jātā devebhyastriyugaṃ purā |*
> *manye nu babhrūṇāmahaṃ śataṃ dhāmāni sapta ca ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-97-1, zoomed)

— and has said

> ओषधयः । ओषधय ओषद्धयंतीति वा ।
> ओषत्येना धयंतीति वा ॥
> दोषं धयंतीति वा ॥

> *oṣadhayaḥ | oṣadhaya oṣaddhayaṃtīti vā |*
> *oṣatyenā dhayaṃtīti vā ‖*
> *doṣaṃ dhayaṃtīti vā ‖*

(Ni. 9-27, zoomed)

That is, because it destroys (धयंति (*dhayaṃti*)) the diseases such as consumption (ओषत् (*oṣat*)) in the body, it has the name ओषधि (*oṣadhi*). Or, for the allaying of the burning that arises in the parts of the body such as the stomach … *(continued on p. 214)*

> *devebhyastvā sadhamādamasmabhyaṃ tvā sadhamādaṃ ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥** *(The Pada prints सुसूदिम (*susūdima*), the Saṃhitā सुषूदिम (*suṣūdima*).)*

> तं । त्वा । वयं । पितो इति । वचःऽभिः । गावः । न । हव्या । सुसूदिम ।
> देवेभ्यः । त्वा । सधऽमादं । अस्मभ्यं । त्वा । सधऽमादं ॥ ११ ॥

> *taṃ | tvā | vayaṃ | pito iti | vacaḥ 'bhiḥ | gāvaḥ | na | havyā | susūdima |*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed.)*

*Gist:* O food in Soma form, with words of praise we press out your juices, as cows yield milk for oblations, to gladden the gods and ourselves.

> हे पितो अन्न सोमरूप तं तादृशं स्तुतं त्वा त्वां महानुभावं वचोभिः स्तुतिवाग्भिर्वयं सुषूदिम । क्षारयामो रसान् । तत्र दृष्टांतः । गावो न हव्या । गाव इव हवींष्युत्पादयंति तथा त्वत्सकाशात्सोमं सुषूदिम । किमर्थं कीदृशं चेति चेत् उच्यते । देवेभ्य इंद्रादिभ्यस्तदर्थं सधमादं तेषां सह मादयितारं । न केवलं देवेभ्य एव किंतु सधमादमस्माभिः सह मादयितारं हुतशेषरूपं त्वा त्वामस्मभ्यमस्मदर्थमपि ॥

> *he pito anna somarūpa taṃ tādṛśaṃ stutaṃ tvā tvāṃ mahānubhāvaṃ vacobhiḥ stutivāgbhirvayaṃ suṣūdima | kṣārayāmo rasān | tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | gāvo na havyā | gāva iva havīṃṣyutpādayaṃti tathā tvatsakāśātsomaṃ suṣūdima | kimarthaṃ kīdṛśaṃ ceti cet ucyate | devebhya iṃdrādibhyastadarthaṃ sadhamādaṃ teṣāṃ saha mādayitāraṃ | na kevalaṃ devebhya eva kiṃtu sadhamādamasmābhiḥ saha mādayitāraṃ hutaśeṣarūpaṃ tvā tvāmasmabhyamasmadarthamapi ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** पितो (*pito*) — O food in the form of Soma; तं त्वा (*taṃ tvā*) — you, possessed of the qualities described before; देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*) — for the deities; सधमादं (*sadhamādaṃ*) — giving satisfaction; त्वा (*tvā*) — you also; अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*) — for us … *(continued on p. 215)*

… too; सधमादं (*sadhamādaṃ*) — causing satisfaction; त्वा (*tvā*) — you; वयं (*vayaṃ*) — we; वचोभिः (*vacobhiḥ*) — with words in the form of praise; गावो न हव्या (*gāvo na havyā*) — as cows yield milk and the like needed for the oblation; सुषूदिम (*suṣūdima*) — we draw out your juice.

**Bhāvārtha.** O food in the form of Soma, possessed of the qualities described before, giving satisfaction to the deities and to us: with our words in the form of praise we draw out your juice, so that you may give satisfaction to us as well, just as cows yield milk and the like needed for the oblation.

**English Translation (as printed).**

We extract from you, Pitu, by our praises, (the sacrificial food), as cows yield butter· [sic] for oblation ; from you, who are exhilarating to the gods ; exhilarating also to us· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

In this ṛk food in the form of Soma is praised. Here an illustration, गावो न हव्या (*gāvo na havyā*), is given. The chief intended meaning is: as cows yield the milk needed for the oblation, so we, with words in the form of praise, obtain the six tastes such as sweetness that are in you (in the food); and by such food, that is, by food in the form of Soma, satisfaction (joy) arises for the deities and for us as well.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly; the heading is printed "Vyākara prakriyā").** वचोभिः (*vacobhiḥ*) — root वच परिभाषणे (*vaca paribhāṣaṇe*); suffix असुन् (*asun*), applicable to all roots; since it is *nit*, initial acute. हव्या (*havyā*) — by शेश्छंदसि बहुलम् (*śeśchaṃdasi bahulam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-7, as printed, zoomed) elision of *śi* in the neuter plural. सुषूदिम (*suṣūdima*) — root षूद क्षरणे (*ṣūda kṣaraṇe*); *s* for the initial by धात्वादेः षः सः (*dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ*); by छंदसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः (*chaṃdasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-26, per numeral file) liṭ in the sense of the present; *ma* substituted for the first person plural; by आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः (*ārdhadhātukasyeḍvalādeḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-3-5, as printed, zoomed) the augment *iṭ*; reduplication and the rest for the root; standing after a word that is not a finite verb, nighāta accent. सधमादम् (*sadhamādam*) — सह मादयति इति सधमादः (*saha mādayati iti sadhamādaḥ*); root मद तृप्तियोगे (*mada tṛptiyoge*), curādi; suffix अच् (*ac*) by नंदिग्रहपचादिभ्यः (*naṃdigrahapacādibhyaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-134, as printed, zoomed); सधमादस्थयोश्छंदसि (*sadhamādasthayośchaṃdasi*) … *(continued on p. 216)*

## Sūkta 188 — introductory matter (Pīṭhike)

**The Hundred and Eighty-eighth Sūkta.** *(Half-title, in Kannada: "Nūra embhattentaneya sūktavu".)*

**Pīṭhike (Introduction).**

We have given the explanation of the Āprī sūktas in Ṛgveda Saṃhitā Bhāga 2, pages 73–74 and 528. In the Ṛgveda there are in all 10 (zoomed) Āprī sūktas. In them there are mantras whose deities are इध्मः (*idhmaḥ*) (समिद्धोऽग्निर्वा (*samiddho 'gnirvā*)), नराशंसः (*narāśaṃsaḥ*), तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*), इळः (*iḷaḥ*), बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*), देवीर्द्वारः (*devīrdvāraḥ*), उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*), दैव्यौ होतारौ प्रचेतसौ (*daivyau hotārau pracetasau*), तिस्रो देव्यः सरस्वतीळाभारत्यः (*tisro devyaḥ sarasvatīḷābhāratyaḥ*), त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*), वनस्पतिः (*vanaspatiḥ*), स्वाहाकृतयः (*svāhākṛtayaḥ*). But concerning the deities called Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt: in some sūktas the single deity called Narāśaṃsa, in some sūktas the single deity called Tanūnapāt, and in some sūktas both deities, Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt, are praised. In accordance with this they have divided these Āprī sūktas in three ways. Namely, the Āprī sūktas composed by the ṛṣis Vasiṣṭha, Atri, Vādhryaśva and Gṛtsamada —

*(Reference numerals zoomed. Item 3 is printed with आ (*ā*): आग्ने (*āgne*).)*

1) जुषस्व नः समिधमग्ने (*juṣasva naḥ samidhamagne*) — Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2 (मैत्रावरुणिर्वसिष्ठः (*maitrāvaruṇirvasiṣṭhaḥ*))

2) सुसमिद्धाय शोचिषे (*susamiddhāya śociṣe*) — Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-5 (वसुश्रुत आत्रेयः (*vasuśruta ātreyaḥ*))

3) इमां मे आग्ने समिधं (*imāṃ me āgne samidhaṃ*) — Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-70 (सुमित्रो वाध्र्यश्वः (*sumitro vādhryaśvaḥ*))

4) समिद्धो अग्निर्निहितः (*samiddho agnirnihitaḥ*) — Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3 (गृत्समदः (*gṛtsamadaḥ*))

— these four sūktas belong to one group. In them there is one ṛk each whose deity is Narāśaṃsa. Therefore these four sūktas have the name नराशंसवंति सूक्तानि (*narāśaṃsavaṃti sūktāni*) — Āprī sūktas that praise only the deity Narāśaṃsa.

1) सुसमिद्धो न आ वह (*susamiddho na ā vaha*) — Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13 (मेधातिथिः काण्वः (*medhātithiḥ kāṇvaḥ*))

2) समिद्धो अग्न आ वह (*samiddho agna ā vaha*) — Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-142 (दीर्घतमा औचथ्यः (*dīrghatamā aucathyaḥ*))

— these two Āprī sūktas belong to the second group. In them there is one ṛk each relating to both deities, Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt. Therefore these Āprī sūktas are well known as sūktas having both kinds of deity, Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt. In these sūktas both deities … *(continued on p. 217)*

### Printed p. 217 (PDF 236)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 8" (zoomed). Pīṭhike of Sūkta 188, continued.)*

… being present (in the 1-142nd sūkta (zoomed), leaving out Indra), instead of eleven प्रयाज (*prayāja*) homas it came to be that there are twelve homas.

*(Reference numerals zoomed.)*

1) समिद्धो अद्य राजसि (*samiddho adya rājasi*) — Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188 (अगस्त्यो मैत्रावरुणिः (*agastyo maitrāvaruṇiḥ*))

2) समित्समित्सुमना (*samitsamitsumanā*) — Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4 (गाधिनो विश्वामित्रः (*gādhino viśvāmitraḥ*))

3) समिद्धो विश्वतस्पतिः (*samiddho viśvataspatiḥ*) — Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5 (काश्यपोऽसितो देवलो वा (*kāśyapo 'sito devalo vā*))

4) समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो (*samiddho adya manuṣo*) — Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110 (जमदग्निर्भार्गवः (*jamadagnirbhārgavaḥ*))

— these sūktas belong to the third group. In them there are only ṛks whose deity is Tanūnapāt. (There are no ṛks whose deity is Narāśaṃsa.) Therefore they have the name तनूनपात्वंति सूक्तानि (*tanūnapātvaṃti sūktāni*), that is, Āprī sūktas containing the mantra whose deity is Tanūnapāt.

These Āprī sūktas are recited, when the animal sacrifice (पशुहोम (*paśuhoma*)) is performed, for performing the eleven (एकादश (*ekādaśa*)) प्रयाज (*prayāja*) homas. There is the Taittirīya Saṃhitā statement एकादशावदानान्यवद्यति दश वै पशोः प्राणा आत्मैकादशः (*ekādaśāvadānānyavadyati daśa vai paśoḥ prāṇā ātmaikādaśaḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-3-10-3, zoomed; a stray mark is printed in आत्मैकादशः (*ātmaikādaśaḥ*)). When these Āprī sūktas are recited and the animal sacrifice is performed there is a special rule: sacrificers born in the respective gotras must, when performing the sacrifice, recite the Āprī sūktas composed by the respective ṛṣis — such is the rule (Ā. 3-2, zoomed). The present Āprī sūkta is to be recited by those born in the gotra of the ṛṣi Agastya.

If one wishes to know the nature of the Āprī sūktas and the places they hold in ritual practice, the sources we have are of two kinds: first, the Śruti statements of the Brāhmaṇas and the like; second, the etymological statements of the Nirukta and the like. Of these two kinds of sources, the etymological statements of the Nirukta and the like are more reasoned and are furnished with scientific explanations.

If one notes the derivation of the word आप्री (*āprī*) stated in the Brāhmaṇas such as the Aitareya, it may be said that they have all explained this word by understanding it from the standpoint of ritual practice such as sacrifice. For example —

> तद्यदा प्रीणाति तस्मादाप्रियो नाम ।

> *tadyadā prīṇāti tasmādāpriyo nāma |*

(Kau. Brā. 10-3, zoomed)

— in the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa, that they have this name because they are the means of giving satisfaction; and

> आप्रीभिराप्नुवन् । तदाप्रीणामाप्रित्वं ।

> *āprībhirāpnuvan | tadāprīṇāmāpritvaṃ |*

(Tai. Brā. 2-2-8-6, zoomed)

— in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, stating the same view; and … *(continues on p. 218)*

### Printed p. 218 (PDF 237)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188". Pīṭhike of Sūkta 188, continued.)*

*(Reference numerals zoomed. "evettair" is printed with a ta-subscript, as printed.)*

> यदेतान्याप्रिय आज्यानि भवंति । आत्मानमेवेत्तैराप्रीणाति ।

> *yadetānyāpriya ājyāni bhavaṃti | ātmānamevettairāprīṇāti |*

(Tā. Brā. 15-8-2)

— thus in the Tāṇḍya Brāhmaṇa too the nature of the word आप्री (*āprī*) is made known.

In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, when the duties the Hotṛ must perform at the time of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice are set out, the explanation of the Āprīs is given. After the description of the animal to be offered to Agni and Soma (2-3), the eleven प्रयाज (*prayāja*) mantras are stated (2-4). In that context —

> आप्रीभिराप्रीणाति । तेजो वै ब्रह्मवर्चसमाप्रियस्तेजसैवेनं तद्ब्रह्मवर्चसेन समर्धयति ।

> *āprībhirāprīṇāti | tejo vai brahmavarcasamāpriyastejasaivenaṃ tadbrahmavarcasena samardhayati |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-4)

— the Āprī ṛks are full of splendour and joined with *brahmavarcas*; by such ṛks (the Hotṛ) becomes a cause of satisfaction: so there too it is shown that they are a means to the satisfaction of the self. Further, the deities समिध् (*samidh*), तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) and the rest are shown to be identical with the principles such as *prāṇa*.

In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa itself, before anything else, it is stated, while giving these sūktas found in the different maṇḍalas of the Ṛksaṃhitā and their fruit, about the ṛṣis who recited them —

> ताभिर्यथऋष्याप्रीणीयाद्यद्यथऋष्या प्रीणाति यजमानमेव तद्बंधुताया नोत्सृजति ।

> *tābhiryathaṛṣyāprīṇīyādyadyathaṛṣyā prīṇāti yajamānameva tadbaṃdhutāyā notsṛjati |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-4)

— by the recitation of these ṛks composed by the ṛṣis he protects the sacrificer without letting him go from the bond of the sacrifice: thus the fruit of reciting these ṛks is shown. These sūktas were not seen by one single ṛṣi. Different ṛṣis saw these sūktas on their own individual occasions. Even so, the nature of these sūktas and the fruit of their recitation appear the same everywhere.

That about these Āprī sūktas, and about the deities of these sūktas, there has been difference of opinion from the ancient time of the Brāhmaṇas and the like is known from the Niruktakāra's explanation.

> अथात आप्रियः । आप्रियः कस्मादाप्नोतेः प्रीणातेर्वा । आप्रीभिराप्रीणातीति च ब्राह्मणं ।

> *athāta āpriyaḥ | āpriyaḥ kasmādāpnoteḥ prīṇātervā | āprībhirāprīṇātīti ca brāhmaṇaṃ |*

(Ni. 8-4)

— thus the Niruktakāra has shown that, concerning the Āprī sūktas, the view of the Brāhmaṇas and the like differs from his own. Besides, the view of the ṛṣis Kātthakya, Śākapūṇi, Mādhyamika and others … *(continued on p. 219)*

… they have quoted from time to time. Though Kātthakya and the others are ritualists (*yājñika*), it is noted in the Special Topics of the respective ṛks that on many occasions they do not accept the etymologies given in the Brāhmaṇas and the like. Having made known all these views, Yāska has at the end made known his own definite view. For example, he has first collected all of them, (to show) what the views stated in the Brāhmaṇas and the like concerning the Āprī deities are —

> इतीमा आप्रीदेवता अनुक्रांताः । अथ किं देवताः प्रयाजानुयाजाः । आग्नेया इत्येके । आग्नेया वै प्रयाजा आग्नेया अनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणं । छंदोदेवता इत्यपरं । छंदांसि वै प्रयाजाश्छंदांस्यनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणं । ऋतुदेवता इत्यपरं । ऋतवो वै स्रयाजा ऋतवोऽनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणं । पशुदेवता इत्यपरं । पशवो वै प्रयाजाः पशवोऽनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणं । प्राणदेवता इत्यपरं । प्राणा वै प्रयाजा प्राणा वा अनुयाजाः इति च ब्राह्मणं । आत्मदेवता इत्यपरं । आत्मा वै प्रयाजाः आत्मा वा अनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणं । आग्नेया इति तु स्थितिः । भक्तिमात्रमितरं ।

> तवाग्ने यज्ञोऽयमस्तु सर्वस्तुभ्यं नमंतां प्रदिशश्चतस्रः ।

Of these, this same view is supported by the Brāhmaṇa statement. But some (say) that they are directed to the deities of the metres (*chandodevatā*) (Śa. Brā. 1-3-2-9); some others that they are directed to deities in the form of the seasons (Śa. Brā. 1-3-2-8); others that they are directed to the sacrificial animal (Kau. Brā. 3-4); some that they are directed to a deity in the form of *prāṇa* (Ai. Brā. 1-11, Śa. Brā. 11-2-7-27); and still others that they are directed to the self (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-5-4). Having collected and stated all that has been said, he then stated his own definite view, that the right view is to say they are directed to Agni. *(References zoomed.)*

Speaking on how many Āprī sūktas there are, the Niruktakāra —

> इतीमान्येकादशाप्रीसूक्तानि । तेषां वासिष्ठमात्रेयं वाध्र्यश्वं गार्त्समदमिति नाराशंसवंति ; मैधातिथं दैर्घतमसं प्रैषिकमित्युभयवंत्यतोऽन्यानि तनूनपात्वंति तनूनपात्वंति ।

> *itīmānyekādaśāprīsūktāni | teṣāṃ vāsiṣṭhamātreyaṃ vādhryaśvaṃ gārtsamadamiti nārāśaṃsavaṃti ; maidhātithaṃ dairghatamasaṃ praiṣikamityubhayavaṃtyato 'nyāni tanūnapātvaṃti tanūnapātvaṃti |*

(Ni. 8-22, zoomed)

Of these sūktas, the praises seen by Vasiṣṭha, Atri, Vadhryaśva and Gṛtsamada are directed to Narāśaṃsa; those seen by the ṛṣis Medhātithi and Dīrghatamas, and the Praiṣa sūkta as well, are directed to both deities, Tanūpāt (as printed) and Narāśaṃsa; the remaining four sūktas are directed only to the deity called Tanūnapāt. Altogether (if the Praiṣa sūkta is included) there are eleven Āprī sūktas. The same view in the Bṛhaddevatā too —

*("daśyaitānītarāṇi" as printed, zoomed.)*

> सौत्रामण्यानि तु त्रीणि प्राजापत्याश्च मेधिके ।

> *praiṣaiḥ sahāprīsūktāni tānyekādaśa saṃti ca |*

> *sautrāmaṇyāni tu trīṇi prājāpatyāśca medhike |*

(Bṛ. De. 2-152 to 157)

In these statements it is said that if the Praiṣa sūkta is included there are altogether eleven Āprī sūktas, and if not, ten sūktas. And, following the Nirukta statement itself, the order is given of the sūktas directed to the deities Narāśaṃsa, Tanūnapāt and the rest and composed by the ṛṣis Medhātithi and the rest.

The Praiṣa sūkta is ordered, and it gathers the essence of all the Āprī sūktas together and gives a definite picture. Joining together all the individual epithets of the deities addressed in the Āprī sūktas, it makes known, dividing them, the nature and the function of each deity. When addressing each deity it first utters a fixed portion of mantra, होता यक्षत् (*hotā yakṣat*) |, and then names the respective deity. If one first examines the deity, the deity's epithets and the function explained in the Praiṣa sūkta, one can then know the agreement, or else the differing views, on the questions what the purpose of such Āprī sūktas made up of deities is, what their characteristics are, and what benefit comes from reciting them.

2. अग्निः (तनूनपात्) (*agniḥ (tanūnapāt)*) — अदितेः गर्भं भुवनस्य गोपां (*aditeḥ garbhaṃ bhuvanasya gopāṃ*)

7. उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) — बृहती, सुपेशसा पतिभ्यः योनिं (*bṛhatī, supeśasā patibhyaḥ yoniṃ*) कृणवान्ते (*kṛṇavānte*) [?] संस्मयमाने (*saṃsmayamāne*)
8. दैव्या होतारा (*daivyā hotārā*) — मंद्रा, पोतारा, कवी, प्रचेतसा (*maṃdrā, potārā, kavī, pracetasā*)
9. तिस्रो देवीः (*tisro devīḥ*) — अपसां अपस्तमाः देवीः (*apasāṃ apastamāḥ devīḥ*)
10. त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*) — अचिष्टः, अपाकः, रेतोधाः, विश्रवस्, यशोधाः, पुरुरूपः, अकामकर्शन (*aciṣṭaḥ, apākaḥ, retodhāḥ, viśravas, yaśodhāḥ, pururūpaḥ, akāmakarśana*)
11. वनस्पतिः (*vanaspatiḥ*) — धियो ज्येष्ठा, स्वदान् स्वधितिः, देवेभ्यः ऋतुथा हव्यवाट्, यज्ञस्य, आयुः कल्पमानः (*dhiyo jyeṣṭhā, svadān svadhitiḥ, devebhyaḥ ṛtuthā havyavāṭ, yajñasya, āyuḥ kalpamānaḥ*)
12. अग्निः (स्वाहा) (*agniḥ (svāhā)*) — आज्यस्य मेदसः स्वाहा (*ājyasya medasaḥ svāhā*)

In this way the Praiṣa sūkta, collecting the principal parts of all the Āprī sūktas, has given an ordered picture. The order of composition of these Āprī sūktas, their styles, their uses in the work of sacrifice, and besides their poetic nature, and also the views stated about them by modern scholars, are told at the end.

Concerning the need and purposes of the Āprī sūktas, the scholar called Max Muller first said that they are a means of reconciling either the gods or kinsmen, and then said thus that it is laborious to understand their secret meanings fully:

"It is possible that Apri hymns may have been the songs of reconciliation and that they were called Apri, i.e., appeasing hymns, not because of their appeasing the anger of Gods but the enmities of the members of the same or different families· [sic] However it may be, they indeed prove an active intercourse between the ancient families of India long before the final collection of the ten books....................... ...The original purpose of the Apri hymns and the motive for allowing the priests to choose, are difficult to discover".

(Ancient Sanskrit Literature p. 246-7)

Although even among the ancient Vedic scholars there was a difference of view about the place the Āprī sūktas hold in sacrifices and other rites and about their deities, since there are many common features in all the Āprī sūktas, and a definite pattern and refinement in their composition and in their subjects, it cannot be said either that all were composed together or that they have no relation to one another. Leaving out the ṛṣis of the fourth and sixth maṇḍalas, all the ṛṣis of the remaining maṇḍalas have Āprī sūktas traditional to their own families. Though there is no separate Āprī sūkta for the Kāṇva lineage of the eighth maṇḍala, even so they — the 1-16th (zoomed; faint) … *(continued on p. 223)*

… are well known to use (that) sūkta itself. But the reason why the ṛṣis who are the seers of the fourth and sixth maṇḍalas had no need of it cannot be told. Or else the Vāmadeva and Bhāradvāja lineages may have been reciting some other mantras in this place (the Bhāradvājas, being born in the Āṅgirasa gotra, the sūkta that applies to that gotra itself).

The mantras indicated by the designations Āprī and Āpra —

Kātyāyana in the Sarvānukramaṇikā has said, एतदाप्रीसूक्तं एतेनान्यान्युक्तदैवतानि एकादशकानि तु नाराशंसानि आप्रशब्दोक्तानि अतनूनपात्वंति (*etadāprīsūktaṃ etenānyānyuktadaivatāni ekādaśakāni tu nārāśaṃsāni āpraśabdoktāni atanūnapātvaṃti*) |, that the mantras recited directed to the deity Narāśaṃsa are well known by the name Āpra, and the mantras recited directed to the deity Tanūnapāt by the name Āprī. But in the Nirukta and the like there are no statements at all showing this difference.

Whether the name Āprī refers to the deities or refers to the sūkta is also a natural question. Looked at minutely, it may be said that it first referred to the sūkta and afterwards may have come to be mantras indicating the deities.

The nature of the rite — it may be said that the sacrificial rite indicated by the Āprī sūkta did not hold a secondary place, as indicated by the Brāhmaṇas and the like, but held the place of a principal sacrifice. The difference between the प्रयाज (*prayāja*) oblations and the oblations specified in this rite is seen in many places. In the ṛks 1-13-8, 1-188-6, 1-142-8, 3-4-8, 5-5-7, 9-5-8 the mantra इमं यज्ञं (*imaṃ yajñaṃ*); in the ṛks 5-5-2, 3-4-5 नः यज्ञं (*naḥ yajñaṃ*); and in the ṛks 1-13-2, 7-2-7, 10-110-8 अस्मिन् यज्ञे (*asmin yajñe*) — these too show only a principal place in the sacrificial rite, whether in the sacrifice or in the offering of oblations; they do not show a secondary place like that of the prayāja oblations. *(References zoomed.)*

By the mantras त्रिर्दिवा आमिमिक्षति (*trirdivā āmimikṣati*) (1-142-3) and त्रिरहन्नायजंते (*trirahannāyajaṃte*) (3-4-2) it is known that this rite is to be performed at three times in the day; and by समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो दुरोणे (*samiddho adya manuṣo duroṇe*) (10-110-1) that there is no separate sacrificial house for it, and that the fire may be established in an ordinary house itself. *(References zoomed.)*

> जुषस्व नः समिधमग्ने अद्य शोचा बृहद्यजतं धूममृण्वन् ।

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2-1, zoomed)

— by this ṛk, the description too of the rays of Agni and the rays of the sun spreading forth joined together shows the poetic nature of the mantras. These same descriptions show that this rite is to be begun in the morning.

पूर्व्यं तंतुं तनुष्व (*pūrvyaṃ taṃtuṃ tanuṣva*) (1-142-1, zoomed) — this mantra shows that this rite is ancient. Since the help of Agni, who is the divine Hotṛ, is needed for this sacrifice to be accomplished without hindrance, the oblation of ājya must first be offered to Agni. Thereby, after Agni is satisfied, Agni spreads towards the mid-region (7-2-1); then he brings the deities. Because Agni is the friend of men (3-4-1), he does this service.

**Skill of composition (kṛtikauśalya)** — Although the Āprī sūktas were composed differently one from another, at different times, and though they belong to different lineages of ṛṣis, yet, because in all these sūktas there is one kind of word-arrangement and aim, a harmony and charm greater than in all other kinds of sūktas shows their distinctiveness.

That in all the sūktas (leaving out two sūktas) the number of ṛks is eleven, and that the sūkta begins with the word समिद् (*samid*) and ends with स्वाहा (*svāhā*), shows a fixed rule both from the poetic and from the artistic point of view.

In the matter of metre there is no such restriction. The sūktas 1-13, 1-188, 5-5, 9-5 are composed in the *gāyatrī* metre, the sūkta 1-142 in the *anuṣṭubh* metre, and the sūktas 2-3, 3-4, 7-2, 10-70 in the *triṣṭubh* metre. *(Both lists zoomed.)*

Many mantra-portions such as देवान् आवह (*devān āvaha*), देवान् वक्षि (*devān vakṣi*), विप्रा यज्ञेषु मानुषेषु कारुः (*viprā yajñeṣu mānuṣeṣu kāruḥ*) are repeated.

## Sūkta 188 — *samiddho adya* (Anuvāka 24, ninth Sūkta; 11 ṛks)

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; introduction to the sūkta, continued on p. 225.)*

> समिद्धो अद्येत्येकादशर्चं नवमं सूक्तमागस्त्यं सर्वं गायत्रं । समिद्धाग्नितनूनपादादय एकादश प्रत्यृचं देवता यास्केन किंदेवताः प्रयाजा इत्युपक्रम्याग्नेयाः प्रयाजा ऋतुदेवताश्छंदोदेवताः पशुदेवताः प्राणदेवता आत्म-

> *samiddho adyetyekādaśarcaṃ navamaṃ sūktamāgastyaṃ sarvaṃ gāyatraṃ | samiddhāgnitanūnapādādaya ekādaśa pratyṛcaṃ devatā yāskena kiṃdevatāḥ prayājā ityupakramyāgneyāḥ prayājā ṛtudevatāśchaṃdodevatāḥ paśudevatāḥ prāṇadevatā ātma-*

### Printed p. 225 (PDF 244)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 8". Introduction of Sūkta 188, concluded; the sūkta's heading block.)*

*(Bhāṣya lines zoomed; "Ni. 8-22" and "samiddha āpriya" (no visarga) as printed.)*

*Gist:* eleven-ṛk ninth sūkta of Agastya, all *gāyatrī*; deities Samiddha Agni, Tanūnapāt and the rest, one per ṛk; Yāska, after weighing many views, concludes the prayājas belong to Agni; used as the eleven prayājas in the animal sacrifice of the Agastyas.

> देवता इत्यादिना बहून्पक्षानुपन्यस्य ब्राह्मणानि च प्रदर्श्याग्नेया एवेति सिद्धांतितं । नि. ८-२२ । समिद्ध आप्रिय इत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ पशावगस्त्यानामेकादशप्रयाजरूपमिदमाप्रीसूक्तं ॥

> *devatā ityādinā bahūnpakṣānupanyasya brāhmaṇāni ca pradarśyāgneyā eveti siddhāṃtitaṃ | ni. 8-22 | samiddha āpriya ityanukrāṃtaṃ ‖ paśāvagastyānāmekādaśaprayājarūpamidamāprīsūktaṃ ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, समिद्धो अद्य (*samiddho adya*), is the ninth sūkta in the twenty-fourth anuvāka. There are eleven ṛks in it. Of this sūkta Agastya is the ṛṣi; *gāyatrī* the metre; the eleven deities of the Āprī sūkta, beginning with Samiddha Agni and Tanūnapāt, belong to the eleven ṛks of this sūkta. Yāska, having asked who the deities of the Āprī sūkta are, began his answer with प्रयाजाः (*prayājāḥ*) and, after examining many conflicting views — that the prayāja mantras relate to Agni; that their mantras have the seasons as deities, the metres as deities, the animals as deities, the breaths as deities, the self as deity, and so on — and giving Brāhmaṇa statements by way of example as their resolution, has finally concluded that all these mantras are rightly those relating to Agni (Ni. 8-22). In the Anukramaṇikā too it is said समिद्ध आप्रियः (*samiddha āpriyaḥ*). The use (*viniyoga*) of this Āprī sūkta is for the eleven prayāja oblations to be employed by the descendants of the ṛṣi Agastya in the animal sacrifice (*paśuhoma*).

*(A short rule.)*

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> समिद्धो अद्य राजसि देवो देवैः सहस्रजित् ।
> दूतो हव्या कविर्वह ॥ १ ॥

> *samiddho adya rājasi devo devaiḥ sahasrajit |*
> *dūto havyā kavirvaha ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सम्ऽइद्धः । अद्य । राजसि । देवः । देवैः । सहस्रऽजित् ।
> दूतः । हव्या । कविः । वह ॥ १ ॥

> *sam 'iddhaḥ | adya | rājasi | devaḥ | devaiḥ | sahasra 'jit |*
> *dūtaḥ | havyā | kaviḥ | vaha ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; the first two lines zoomed, "devo 'ta dīpyamānaḥ" as printed.)*

> हे अग्ने देवैर्व्यवहर्तृभिर्ऋत्विग्भिः समिद्धः सम्यग्दीपितो देवोऽत दीप्यमानः समिद्धैर्वा देवैः सहितः समिद्धः सन्नद्यास्मिन्यागदिने राजसि । ईशिषे । हे सहस्रजित् सहस्रस्य धनस्यैतत्संख्याकानां शत्रूणां वा जेतः ततो दूतो देवानां दूतस्तद्यज्ञादिवार्ताहर आह्वाता वा । अग्निर्देवानां दूत आसीदिति श्रुतेः । कविः क्रांतदर्शी ईदृशस्त्वं हव्यास्मदीयानि हवींषि वह । देवेभ्यः प्रापय ॥

> *he agne devairvyavahartṛbhirṛtvigbhiḥ samiddhaḥ samyagdīpito devo 'ta dīpyamānaḥ samiddhairvā devaiḥ sahitaḥ samiddhaḥ sannadyāsminyāgadine rājasi | īśiṣe | he sahasrajit sahasrasya dhanasyaitatsaṃkhyākānāṃ śatrūṇāṃ vā jetaḥ tato dūto devānāṃ dūtastadyajñādivārtāhara āhvātā vā | agnirdevānāṃ dūta āsīditi śruteḥ | kaviḥ krāṃtadarśī īdṛśastvaṃ havyāsmadīyāni havīṃṣi vaha | devebhyaḥ prāpaya ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** (O Agni!) *devaiḥ* — by the ṛtviks devoted to the sacrifice; *samiddhaḥ* — being kindled; *devaḥ* — you who are shining; *adya* — on this day of sacrifice; *rājasi* — are lord; *sahasrajit* — you who possess wealth numbering a thousand, or who have conquered enemies numbering a thousand; *dūtaḥ* — who are the messenger of the gods; *kaviḥ* — who are far-seeing — such are you; *havyā* — the oblations given by us; *vaha* — convey to the gods.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, you, kindled by the ṛtviks devoted to the sacrifice and shining, are lord on this day of sacrifice. You who possess wealth numbering a thousand, who have conquered enemies, who are the messenger of the gods and far-seeing — convey to the gods the oblations given by us.

**English Translation (as printed).**

You shine to-day, divine conqueror of thousands, kindled by the priests: do you, who are the sapient messenger (of the gods), convey (to them) our oblation· [sic]

### Printed p. 227 (PDF 246)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 8". Ṛk 1, continued.)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**देवैः—व्यवहर्तृभिर्ऋत्विग्भिः (*devaiḥ—vyavahartṛbhirṛtvigbhiḥ*)** — the Bhāṣyakāra has explained the meaning of this word as: by the ṛtvik people taking part in the sacrificial rite.

**सहस्रजित्—सहस्रस्य धनस्य, एतावत्संख्याकानां शत्रूणां वा जेता (*sahasrajit—sahasrasya dhanasya, etāvatsaṃkhyākānāṃ śatrūṇāṃ vā jetā*)** — the owner, lord, of thousands of riches, or he who conquers thousands of enemy people. Here the word *sahasra* does not mean a definite number, a thousand; the word *sahasra* is used in the sense "many, much".

**दूतः (*dūtaḥ*)** — Agni conveys to the gods what men have offered as oblation in Agni, and brings the gods to the place of sacrifice. Therefore Agni has the epithets हव्यवाट् (*havyavāṭ*) and दूत (*dūta*).

*(References on this page zoomed; "agni" printed without anusvara.)*

> अग्नि दूतं वृणीमहे होतारं विश्ववेदसं ।

> *agni dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe hotāraṃ viśvavedasaṃ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-1)

— in this ṛk he is prayed to as the messenger who brings the gods to the place of sacrifice and invites them.

> अग्निमग्निं हवीमभिः सदा हवंत विश्पतिं । हव्यवाहं पुरुप्रियं ॥

> *agnimagniṃ havīmabhiḥ sadā havaṃta viśpatiṃ | havyavāhaṃ purupriyaṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-2)

> अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते कविर्गृहपतिर्युवा । हव्यवाट् जुह्वास्यः ॥

> *agnināgniḥ samidhyate kavirgṛhapatiryuvā | havyavāṭ juhvāsyaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-6)

In these and other ṛks it is said that Agni is the messenger who conveys the oblation to the gods. Therefore in the present ṛk too Agni is addressed: दूतो हव्या कविर्वह (*dūto havyā kavirvaha*) |.

**कविः (*kaviḥ*)** — Yāska has given the etymology of the word *kavi*: मेधावी कविः क्रांतदर्शनो भवति, कवतेर्वा (*medhāvī kaviḥ krāṃtadarśano bhavati, kavatervā*) (Ni. 12-13). For the word *kavi* the Bhāṣyakāra has said in many contexts *kaviḥ* — अतींद्रियज्ञः (*atīṃdriyajñaḥ*), that is, a person who by the power of his own capacity knows matters not perceptible, that is, not known, to ordinary men. What the nature of the *kavi* is and what his power is, and to make known what nature and powers the word *kavi* is used in the Ṛksaṃhitā, has also been subtly shown earlier. The word *kavi* is used in the sense of a person having the capacity to know, by his inner vision, even the parts hidden away and not perceptible to the sight of the world, and to make them known to the sight of the world too.

**समिद्धः—सम्यग्दीपितः एतन्नामकः त्वं (*samiddhaḥ—samyagdīpitaḥ etannāmakaḥ tvaṃ*)** — Sāyaṇa has explained: (you) who are renowned by the name *samiddha*. It refers to Samiddha Agni, who holds the first place in the Āprī sūkta.
