### Printed p. 228 (PDF 247)

*(Header: "Maṃ. . A. 24. Sū. 188" (the Maṇḍala numeral is not printed). Ṛk 1, Special Topics continued.)*

*(Bṛ. De. 2-188 zoomed.)*

> इध्मो यः सर्वमेवाग्निरयं हीध्मः समिध्यते ।
> ध्मातेर्वैतत्कृतं रूपं ध्मातो हीध्मः समिध्यते ॥

> *idhmo yaḥ sarvamevāgnirayaṃ hīdhmaḥ samidhyate |*
> *dhmātervaitatkṛtaṃ rūpaṃ dhmāto hīdhmaḥ samidhyate ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-188)

Here the identity of the *idhma*, which is of the form of wood, with the all-pervading Agni is stated. The word *idhma* is formed from the root *dhmā*. The author of the Bṛhaddevatā has stated the etymology of the words *idhma* and *samiddha*: this name, because it blazes up after it is blown upon. This etymology follows the Niruktakāra's explanation. In the Nirukta too,

> तासामिध्मः प्रथमागामी भवति । इध्मः समिंधनात् ।

> *tāsāmidhmaḥ prathamāgāmī bhavati | idhmaḥ samiṃdhanāt |*

(Ni. 8-5)

— so he has said concerning the first deity of the Āprī sūkta. In the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa too, at the beginning of the Praiṣa sūkta,

*(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-1 zoomed; "prathivyāḥ" (ra-subscript) as printed.)*

> होता यक्षदग्निग्ं समिधा समिद्धं सुषमिधा नाभा प्रथिव्याः संगथे वामस्य ।

> *hotā yakṣadagnigṃ samidhā samiddhaṃ suṣamidhā nābhā prathivyāḥ saṃgathe vāmasya |*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-1)

— thus it is addressed: perform the sacrifice directed to Agni, who is called *samidh* and is joined with the deity of the first prayāja.

Here one more matter has to be noted. The proper name *idhma* does not occur in the Āprī sūktas. In the Praiṣa sūkta too this name is not there. Only in the Sarvānukramaṇī —

> सुसमिद्ध इतीध्म समिद्धो वा अग्नि.......... इति प्रत्यृचं देवताः ।

> *susamiddha itīdhma samiddho vā agni.......... iti pratyṛcaṃ devatāḥ |*

— is it indicated. While in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa too this word is not used in this context, it is known that Śaunaka and Kātyāyana, in using it, have followed the Niruktakāra. Besides, the epithet *samiddha* or *susamiddha* is used in seven sūktas, and the epithet समिध् (*samidh*) in the remaining three sūktas, Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-1; 7-2-1; 10-70-1. *(Zoomed.)*

The first duty of this Agni called *samiddha* is to invite the gods. In the opening ṛks of the sūktas 1-13-1, 1-142-1, 3-4-1, 10-110-1 *(zoomed)* the duty of Agni is indicated by the prayer सुसमिद्धो न आ वह देवाँ अग्ने हविष्मते (*susamiddho na ā vaha devā~ agne haviṣmate*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-1). Not only this — he is also prayed to convey the oblations and the like.

On whether this deity is Agni or not, there has been a difference of opinion from the beginning. The Niruktakāra too, citing this difference of opinion, afterwards states his own opinion.

Having made known the views of the respective ṛṣis — यज्ञेध्म इति कात्थक्यः (*yajñedhma iti kātthakyaḥ*) (Ni. 8-5), अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः (*agniriti śākapūṇiḥ*) (8-5) — he has then stated his own opinion too: आग्नेय इति तु स्थितिः (*āgneya iti tu sthitiḥ*) (Ni. 8-22). *(Zoomed; a stray mark after the first akṣara of "yajñedhma" as printed.)* In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa — *(continued on p. 229)*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** राजसि (*rājasi*) — root राजृ दीप्तौ (*rājṛ dīptau*); laṭ, second person singular; nighāta accent because it follows a non-finite word. सहस्रजित् (*sahasrajit*) — सहस्रं जयतीति (*sahasraṃ jayatīti*); root जि जये (*ji jaye*); suffix *kvip* by क्विप् च (*kvip ca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-76), *tuk* augment by ह्रस्वस्य पिति कृति तुक् (*hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-71), accent by गतिकारकोपपदात् (*gatikārakopapadāt*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139); here vocative, all-anudātta by आमंत्रितस्य च (*āmaṃtritasya ca*). दूतः (*dūtaḥ*) — root दु गतौ (*du gatau*); suffix *kta* with lengthening by दुतनिभ्यां दीर्घश्च (*dutanibhyāṃ dīrghaśca*) (U. Sū. 3-370, as read); end-acute. वह (*vaha*) — root वह प्रापणे (*vaha prāpaṇe*); loṭ, second person singular; nighāta accent. *(Sūtra numbers zoomed.)*

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तनूनपादृतं यते मध्वा यज्ञः समज्यते ।
> दधत्सहस्रिणीरिषः ॥ २ ॥

> *tanūnapādṛtaṃ yate madhvā yajñaḥ samajyate |*
> *dadhatsahasriṇīriṣaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तनूऽनपात् । ऋतं । यते । मध्वा । यज्ञः । सं । अज्यते ।
> दधत् । सहस्रिणीः । इषः ॥ २ ॥

> *tanū 'napāt | ṛtaṃ | yate | madhvā | yajñaḥ | saṃ | ajyate |*
> *dadhat | sahasriṇīḥ | iṣaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; "adbhya oṣadhayaḥ" as printed; continued on p. 230.)*

> तनूनपाद्यज्ञशरीरस्य नपातयिता । यद्वा । आपोऽत्र तन्व उच्यंत इत्युक्तत्वादपां नपातयिता तासां नप्ता वा । अद्भ्य ओषधयः ओषधीभ्योऽग्निरिति नप्तृत्वं ।

> *tanūnapādyajñaśarīrasya napātayitā | yadvā | āpo 'tra tanva ucyaṃta ityuktatvādapāṃ napātayitā tāsāṃ naptā vā | adbhya oṣadhayaḥ oṣadhībhyo 'gniriti naptṛtvaṃ |*

### Printed p. 230 (PDF 249)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188" (zoomed). Ṛk 2, continued: the bhāṣya of p. 229 concluded.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(continued from p. 229.)*

> यज्ञः पूज्यः । यज्ञनिर्वाहकत्वाद्वा यज्ञः । ईदृशोऽग्निर्ऋतं यज्ञं यते । गच्छते । अनुतिष्ठते । यजमानाय तदभिमतार्थं । मध्वा मधुरेणाज्यसोमादिद्रव्येण समज्यते । किं कुर्वन्नयं । सहस्रिणीरेतत्संख्याकानीषोऽन्नानि दधद्यजमानेभ्यो धारयन् ॥

> *yajñaḥ pūjyaḥ | yajñanirvāhakatvādvā yajñaḥ | īdṛśo 'gnirṛtaṃ yajñaṃ yate | gacchate | anutiṣṭhate | yajamānāya tadabhimatārthaṃ | madhvā madhureṇājyasomādidravyeṇa samajyate | kiṃ kurvannayaṃ | sahasriṇīretatsaṃkhyākānīṣo 'nnāni dadhadyajamānebhyo dhārayan ‖*

*Gist:* Tanūnapāt — the preserver of the sacrifice's body, or the grandson of the waters (waters → plants → Agni) — is united with sweet ājya for the sacrificer, bringing him thousandfold food.

**Pratipadārtha.** *tanūnapāt* — he who is renowned by the name Tanūnapāt; *yajñaḥ* — the adorable one — (that is,) Agni; *sahasriṇīḥ* — numbering a thousand; *iṣaḥ* — food; *dadhat* — bearing; *ṛtaṃ* — the sacrifice; *yate* — for the yajamāna who performs; *madhvā* — with sweet substances such as ājya; *samajyate* — combines (the oblation).

**Bhāvārtha.** Agni, renowned by the name Tanūnapāt and adorable, bearing food numbering a thousand, combines the oblation with sweet substances such as ājya for the yajamāna who performs the sacrifice.

**English Translation (as printed).**

The adorable Tanunapat proceeds to the rite, and combines with the oblation, bearing (for the sacrificer) infinite (abundance of) food· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)** — here the Bhāṣyakāra has taken the meaning "sacrifice" for the word ऋत (*ṛta*). Yāska in his Nirukta, citing the ṛk

> न यातव इंद्र जूजुवुर्नो न वंदना शविष्ठ वेद्याभिः ।
> स शर्धदर्यो विषुणस्य जंतोर्मा शिश्नदेवा अपि गुर्ऋतं नः ॥

> *na yātava iṃdra jūjuvurno na vaṃdanā śaviṣṭha vedyābhiḥ |*
> *sa śardhadaryo viṣuṇasya jaṃtormā śiśnadevā api gurṛtaṃ naḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-21-5) *(zoomed)*

— has explained the meaning of the word ऋत (*ṛta*) as सत्यं वा यज्ञं वा (*satyaṃ vā yajñaṃ vā*) (Ni. 4-19) *(zoomed)*. The word ऋत (*ṛta*) has many meanings. In the present ṛk the meaning "sacrifice" is fitting.

**तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*)** — यज्ञशरीरस्य नपातयिता (*yajñaśarīrasya napātayitā*), that is, he who does not let the (तनु (*tanu*)) body of the sacrifice perish, that is, the protector of the sacrifice — this is one kind of meaning; यद्वा । आपोऽत्र तन्व उच्यंत इत्युक्तत्वादपां नपातयिता तासां नप्ता वा । अद्भ्यः ओषधयः ओषधीभ्योऽग्निरिति नप्तृत्वं । (*yadvā | āpo 'tra tanva ucyaṃta ityuktatvādapāṃ napātayitā tāsāṃ naptā vā | adbhyaḥ oṣadhayaḥ oṣadhībhyo 'gniriti naptṛtvaṃ |*) *(here "adbhyaḥ" with visarga; p. 229 bhāṣya "adbhya")* Or else, आपः (*āpaḥ*) here must be taken in the sense "body". That is, आपः (*āpaḥ*) — of the waters, the grandson — *(continued on p. 231)*

### Printed p. 231 (PDF 250)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 8" (zoomed). Ṛk 2, Special Topics continued.)*

(grandson) is the meaning. How is that? From the waters (from waters such as rain) plants and trees are born. From those plants and trees (from the pieces of wood called *araṇi*) Agni is born. Therefore the intent is that Agni is the grandson of अपां (*apāṃ*), the waters. That the two words तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) and अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*) have one and the same meaning we have explained at length on pages 144–146.

**तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*)** — for this word Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of meaning on the basis of the Nirukta. First:

> तनूनपात् आज्यं इति कात्थक्यपक्षे तन्वो गावो भोगानां तासु जायमानत्वात् । ताभ्यः उत्पन्नं क्षीरं क्षीरात्सर्पिः इति आज्यस्य नप्तृत्वं । तद्वान् यज्ञः ।

> *tanūnapāt ājyaṃ iti kātthakyapakṣe tanvo gāvo bhogānāṃ tāsu jāyamānatvāt | tābhyaḥ utpannaṃ kṣīraṃ kṣīrātsarpiḥ iti ājyasya naptṛtvaṃ | tadvān yajñaḥ |*

If Kātthakya's meaning, that तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) means ājya, is accepted, then the word तनु (*tanu*) means "cows", and since ājya is produced from the milk born of them, तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) means ājya; or else they have taken it to mean the sacrifice joined with ājya. In this context, by the Niruktakāra's statement नपादित्यनंतरायाः प्रजाया नामधेयं निर्णततमा भवति (*napādityanaṃtarāyāḥ prajāyā nāmadheyaṃ nirṇatatamā bhavati*) (Ni. 8-5) *(zoomed)*, the word नपात् (*napāt*) means grandson; so here too the meaning is ājya, produced from the milk born of cows. Second:

> अग्निपक्षे आपस्तन्व उच्यंते । ताभ्यः ओषधिवनस्पतयः, तेभ्योऽग्निरिति नप्तृत्वं । अरणीभ्यां इति भावः ।

> *agnipakṣe āpastanva ucyaṃte | tābhyaḥ oṣadhivanaspatayaḥ, tebhyo 'gniriti naptṛtvaṃ | araṇībhyāṃ iti bhāvaḥ |*

— the word तनु (*tanu*) means water; from it the plants and trees (the araṇis) are born, and from them Agni is born; hence the name तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*). Thus he has given two kinds of meaning. In the Bṛhaddevatā,

*("kṛpaṇyavaḥ" and "napādamuṣya" (hooked ma) as printed.)*

> अयं तनूनपादग्निरसौ हि तननात्तनुः ।
> ततस्तु मध्यमो जज्ञे स्थानेऽयं मध्यमात्ततः ॥
> अनंतरां प्रजामाहुर्नपादिति कृपण्यवः ।
> नपादमुष्य चैवायं अग्निस्तेन तनूनपात् ।

> *ayaṃ tanūnapādagnirasau hi tananāttanuḥ |*
> *tatastu madhyamo jajñe sthāne 'yaṃ madhyamāttataḥ ‖*
> *anaṃtarāṃ prajāmāhurnapāditi kṛpaṇyavaḥ |*
> *napādamuṣya caivāyaṃ agnistena tanūnapāt |*

(Bṛ. De. 2-26 [?] to 27) *(zoomed at 600 and 1000 dpi; the second numeral's first digit is drawn unlike the other 2-glyphs)*

*("yacchatvasau tanuṃ" (anusvara) as printed; zoomed.)*

> तनूनपादयं त्वेव नाम्ना यच्छत्वसौ तनुं ।
> नपादिति प्रजा माहुरमुतोऽस्य च संभवं ।

> *tanūnapādayaṃ tveva nāmnā yacchatvasau tanuṃ |*
> *napāditi prajā māhuramuto 'sya ca saṃbhavaṃ |*

(Bṛ. De. 3-1) *(zoomed)*

This earthly Agni is the नपात् (*napāt*), the grandson, of the Agni of the heavenly world; how? The heavenly Agni, being endowed with the power of spreading (तननात् (*tananāt*)), is called by the synonym तनु (*tanu*). From him the Agni in the form of lightning, abiding in the mid-region, is born, and from him this earthly Agni; therefore to the earthly Agni — *(continued on p. 232)*

— the name तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*). It is explained that, because he spread out of his own body and was born in this form, he too has the name तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*).

**सहस्रिणीः इषः (*sahasriṇīḥ iṣaḥ*)** — the intent is: foods, or nourishments, of many kinds.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) — तनुं नपातयति इति तनूनपात् (*tanuṃ napātayati iti tanūnapāt*); initial-acute accent by its inclusion in the पृषादि (*pṛṣādi*) list (as printed). यते (*yate*) — root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*); *śatṛ* for laṭ; *yaṇ* substitute by इणो यण् (*iṇo yaṇ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-81); acute on the dative by शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी (*śaturanumo nadyajādī*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-173). मध्वा (*madhvā*) — no ना (*nā*)-substitution by the vārttika जसादिषु छंदसि वा वचनम् (*jasādiṣu chaṃdasi vā vacanam*); *yaṇ* substitute. अज्यते (*ajyate*) — root अंजू व्यक्तिम्रक्षणकांतिगतिषु (*aṃjū vyaktimrakṣaṇakāṃtigatiṣu*); passive laṭ; *yak* by सार्वधातुके यक् (*sārvadhātuke yak*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-67), elision of the penultimate nasal by अनिदितां हल उपधा (*aniditāṃ hala upadhā*)— sūtra (so printed, the sūtra only begun); nighāta accent because it follows a non-finite word. दधत् (*dadhat*) — root डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*); *śatṛ*; initial acute by अभ्यस्तानामादिः (*abhyastānāmādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-189). सहस्रिणीः (*sahasriṇīḥ*) — सहस्रं आसां अस्ति इति सहस्रिण्यः (*sahasraṃ āsāṃ asti iti sahasriṇyaḥ*); *ini* in the possessive sense by अत इनिठनौ (*ata iniṭhanau*); *ṅīp* by ऋन्नेभ्यो ङीप् (*ṛnnebhyo ṅīp*); accusative plural. *(Sūtra numbers zoomed.)*

*(Bhāṣya: "iḷnāmakastvaṃ" (hooked ma) and "devānā vakṣi" as printed.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे अग्ने आजुह्वानोऽस्माभिराहूयमानः सन्नीड्योऽस्माभिः स्तुत्य इळ्नामकस्त्वं नोऽस्मदर्थं यज्ञियान् यज्ञभाजो देवाना वक्षि । आवह । हे अग्ने त्वं सहस्रसा असि । अपरिमितधनस्य दातासि ॥

> *he agne ājuhvāno 'smābhirāhūyamānaḥ sannīḍyo 'smābhiḥ stutya iḷnāmakastvaṃ no 'smadarthaṃ yajñiyān yajñabhājo devānā vakṣi | āvaha | he agne tvaṃ sahasrasā asi | aparimitadhanasya dātāsi ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** *agne* — O Agni; *ājuhvānaḥ* — being invoked by us; *īḍyaḥ* — and being praiseworthy, you; *naḥ* — for us; *yajñiyān* — worthy of the sacrifice; *devān* — the gods; *ā vakṣi* — bring hither; *tvaṃ* — you; *sahasrasā asi* — are the giver of boundless wealth.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, you who are invoked by us and are praiseworthy, bring hither for us the gods who are worthy of the sacrifice. You are the giver of boundless wealth.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Agni, who are to be glorified, bring hither, being invoked by us, the adorable gods, for you are for the donor of thousands· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**देवान् आ वक्षि यज्ञियान् (*devān ā vakṣi yajñiyān*)** — the meaning is: bring (to our place of sacrifice) the gods who are worthy of the sacrifice, that is, whom we desire to come to the sacrifice. The prayer that Agni should bring the gods —

> अग्निः पूर्वेभिर्ऋषिभिरीड्यो नूतनैरुत । स देवाँ एह वक्षति ॥

> *agniḥ pūrvebhirṛṣibhirīḍyo nūtanairuta | sa devā~ eha vakṣati ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-2)

> अग्ने देवाँ इहा वह जज्ञानो वृक्तबर्हिषे । असि होता न ईड्यः ।

> *agne devā~ ihā vaha jajñāno vṛktabarhiṣe | asi hotā na īḍyaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-3) *(zoomed)*

— is set out in these and other ṛks.

**ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*)** — सर्वैः स्तुत्यः इळ् नामकः त्वं (*sarvaiḥ stutyaḥ iḷ nāmakaḥ tvaṃ*) | It has been taken to mean Agni, who is to be praised by all and is renowned by the name इडः (*iḍaḥ*) *(so printed in the Kannada)*. With ईळ ईट्टेः स्तुतिकर्मणः ; इंधतेर्वा (*īḷa īṭṭeḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ ; iṃdhatervā*) *(as printed; zoomed)* — it may be derived either from the root ईड् (*īḍ*), meaning praise, or from the root इंध् (*iṃdh*), meaning blazing (Ni. 8-8) *(zoomed)* — thus showing the etymology of this word, the Niruktakāra, quoting the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-3 *(zoomed)*, has explained the correct meaning of this word.

### Printed p. 234 (PDF 253)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū 188". Ṛk 3, Special Topics continued.)*

First, like the word समिध् (*samidh*), this word too appears to have been used only as an epithet of Agni, without designating a separate deity. At the time the sacrifice is carried out, Agni's help and assistance has to be complete; therefore he is by his very nature one to be praised. At the beginning Agni must be (1) kindled (समिद्ध (*samiddha*)). Next, (2) under the name तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) or नराशंस (*narāśaṃsa*), he must make the oblations of the sacrifice filled with honey. Next he must bring the gods to the sacrifice. For this task he must be ईड्य (*īḍya*) (one to be praised). Therefore in this context he is (3) ईड्य (*īḍya*) to the yajamāna (he is prayed to).

In the Āprī sūktas this word, derived from the root ईड् (*īḍ*), has been used of Agni in nine places in all: in eight places as an epithet, "praised" or "to be praised", and in one place as an epithet showing Agni's office of messenger. And in the Āprī sūkta made by Viśvāmitra,

> प्र दीधितिर्विश्ववारा जिगाति होतारमिळः प्रथमं यजध्यै ।
> अच्छा नमोभिर्वृषभं वंदध्यै स देवान्यक्षदिषितो यजीयान् ।

> *pra dīdhitirviśvavārā jigāti hotāramiḷaḥ prathamaṃ yajadhyai |*
> *acchā namobhirvṛṣabhaṃ vaṃdadhyai sa devānyakṣadiṣito yajīyān |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-3) *(zoomed)*

— only in this ṛk of the Āprī sūkta does it mean food in the form of the oblation. Even so, it is connected with Agni, the chief deity of that ṛk. This meaning differs from the tradition of the Āprī sūkta. But in the Praiṣa sūkta it is purely a synonym of Agni:

*("agnimiḍa" as printed.)*

> होता यक्षदग्निमिड ईडितो देवो देवाग्ं आवक्षद्दूतो हव्यवाडमूरः ।
> उपेमं यज्ञमुपेमां देवो देवहूतिमवतु वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ।

> *hotā yakṣadagnimiḍa īḍito devo devāgṃ āvakṣaddūto havyavāḍamūraḥ |*
> *upemaṃ yajñamupemāṃ devo devahūtimavatu vetvājyasya hotaryaja |*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-1) *(zoomed)*

— for this statement the Bhāṣyakāra has said इडेत्येतन्नामकमग्निं तृतीयप्रयाजदेवं (*iḍetyetannāmakamagniṃ tṛtīyaprayājadevaṃ*), that is, that it is a synonym-name of Agni. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa —

*("tatprīṇāti" printed with a broken ra-sign.)*

> इळो यजत्यन्नं वा इळोऽन्नमेव तत्प्रीणात्यन्नं यजमाने दधाति ।

> *iḷo yajatyannaṃ vā iḷo 'nnameva tatprīṇātyannaṃ yajamāne dadhāti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-4) *(zoomed)*

— it is said that इळः (*iḷaḥ*) means the food, in the form of the oblation, to be offered in the sacrifice, and that as the fruit of offering this food the yajamāna too obtains food.

As explained above, Yāska's showing a connection of this word with the root इंध् (*iṃdh*) as well is not properly intelligible. Here Yāska has not stated Kātthakya's opinion. In the Bṛhaddevatā,

*("iḷestvṛṣikṛtaṃ" and "vokto" as printed.)*

> इळेस्त्वृषिकृतं रूपं ईडेश्च स्तुतिकर्मणः ।
> इळावांस्तेन वोक्तोऽग्निरिडिना वृद्धिकर्मणा ॥

> *iḷestvṛṣikṛtaṃ rūpaṃ īḍeśca stutikarmaṇaḥ |*
> *iḷāvāṃstena vokto 'gniriḍinā vṛddhikarmaṇā ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-4) *(zoomed)*

### Printed p. 235 (PDF 254)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 8". Ṛk 3: Special Topics concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; end of Ṛk 3.)*

— by these statements it is shown that this word is of ṛṣi origin (आर्षेय (*ārṣeya*)) and a synonym-name of Agni; and the word इळावान् (*iḷāvān*) is an epithet of Agni.

> गोमाँ अग्नेऽविमाँ अश्वी यज्ञो नृवत्सखा सदमिदप्रमृष्यः ।
> इळावाँ एषो असुर प्रजावान्दीर्घो रयिः पृथुबुध्नः सभावान् ।

> *gomā~ agne 'vimā~ aśvī yajño nṛvatsakhā sadamidapramṛṣyaḥ |*
> *iḷāvā~ eṣo asura prajāvāndīrgho rayiḥ pṛthubudhnaḥ sabhāvān |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-2-5) *(zoomed)*

— since in this ṛk the word इळावान् (*iḷāvān*) is an epithet of Agni, the Bṛhaddevatā has pointed to that aspect.

Although such differences of tradition are found in the explanations, it may be said in sum that it is a synonym-name of the deity Agni, who holds the fourth place in the sūkta. *("fourth" as printed.)*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** आजुह्वानः (*ājuhvānaḥ*) — root हु दानादनयोः (*hu dānādanayoḥ*); *śānac* for laṭ; *ślu* vikaraṇa, and reduplication on that account; initial acute by अभ्यस्तानामादिः (*abhyastānāmādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-189); in the *prādi* compound the kṛt final member keeps its own accent. ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*) — root ईड स्तुतौ (*īḍa stutau*); suffix *yat*; initial acute by यतोऽनावः (*yato 'nāvaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-213). वक्षि (*vakṣi*) — root वह प्रापणे (*vaha prāpaṇe*); laṭ, second person singular *sip*; *luk* of the vikaraṇa by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*); *ḍha* for the root's *h* by हो ढः (*ho ḍhaḥ*), *ka* for that *ḍha* before *s* by the sūtra षढोः कः सि (*ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si*), then *ṣa* for the suffix's *s*; nighāta accent of a finite verb. यज्ञियान् (*yajñiyān*) — यज्ञमर्हंति इति यज्ञियाः (*yajñamarhaṃti iti yajñiyāḥ*); suffix *gha* by यज्ञर्त्विग्भ्यां घखञौ (*yajñartvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau*) (Pā. Sū. 5-1-71); *iya* substitute by आयनेयीनी— (*āyaneyīnī—*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-2) *(so printed, the sūtra only begun)*; elision of the preceding *a* by यस्येति च (*yasyeti ca*); initial acute of the suffix. सहस्रसाः (*sahasrasāḥ*) — सहस्रं सनोति इति सहस्रसाः (*sahasraṃ sanoti iti sahasrasāḥ*); root षणु दाने (*ṣaṇu dāne*); *kvip*; *ā* for the root by जनसनखनां— (*janasanakhanāṃ—*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-42); the kṛt final member keeps its accent by गतिकारकोपपदात् (*gatikārakopapadāt*). *(Sūtra numbers zoomed.)*

*(Rule — end of Ṛk 3.)*

#### Ṛk 4

### Printed p. 236 (PDF 255)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188". Ṛk 4.)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> प्राचीनं बर्हिरोजसा सहस्रवीरमस्तृणन् ।
> यत्रादित्या विराजथ ॥ ४ ॥

> *prācīnaṃ barhirojasā sahasravīramastṛṇan |*
> *yatrādityā virājatha ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्राचीनं । बर्हिः । ओजसा । सहस्रऽवीरं । अस्तृणन् ।
> यत्र । आदित्याः । विऽराजथ ॥ ४ ॥

> *prācīnaṃ | barhiḥ | ojasā | sahasra 'vīraṃ | astṛṇan |*
> *yatra | ādityāḥ | vi 'rājatha ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> प्राचीनं प्रागग्रं सहस्रवीरं सहस्रसंख्याका वीराः शत्रूणां विशेषेणेरयितारो देवा यस्य तत्तादृक् । यद्वा । अपरिमितवीराः पुत्रादयो येन तादृक् । बर्हिरोजसा मंत्रलक्षणबलेनोपेता ऋत्विजोऽस्तृणन् । आच्छादयन् । यत्र यस्मिन्बर्हिष्यादित्या अदितेः पुत्राः यूयं विराजथ विविधं राजध्वे तद्बर्हिरस्तृणन् ॥

> *prācīnaṃ prāgagraṃ sahasravīraṃ sahasrasaṃkhyākā vīrāḥ śatrūṇāṃ viśeṣeṇerayitāro devā yasya tattādṛk | yadvā | aparimitavīrāḥ putrādayo yena tādṛk | barhirojasā maṃtralakṣaṇabalenopetā ṛtvijo 'stṛṇan | ācchādayan | yatra yasminbarhiṣyādityā aditeḥ putrāḥ yūyaṃ virājatha vividhaṃ rājadhve tadbarhirastṛṇan ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** *prācīnam* — having its tips turned to the east; *sahasravīram* — and having (attended by) heroes numbering a thousand; *yatra* — on which; *ādityāḥ* — you, the sons of Aditi (being gods); *virājatha* — shine, such; *barhiḥ* — the darbha seat (the ṛtviks); *ojasā* — by the power in the form of mantras; *astṛṇan* — have spread out and made ready.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Ādityas, the darbha seat on which you sit and shine, which has its tips turned to the east and has heroes numbering a thousand, the ṛtviks, endowed with the power in the form of mantras, have spread out and made ready.

**English Translation (as printed).**

By the power (of their prayers) they have strewn the sacred grass, the seat of numerous heroes, pointing to the east, on which Adityas, you are manifest *(no full stop printed)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**सहस्रवीरम् (*sahasravīram*)** — for this word the Bhāṣyakāra has given three kinds of meaning:

> सहस्रवीरं सहस्रसंख्याका वीराः शत्रूणां विशेषेणेरयितारो देवा यस्य तादृक् ।

> *sahasravīraṃ sahasrasaṃkhyākā vīrāḥ śatrūṇāṃ viśeṣeṇerayitāro devā yasya tādṛk |*

---

### Printed p. 237 (PDF 256)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 8". Ṛk 4, Special Topics continued.)*

> यद्वा । अपरिमितवीराः पुत्रादयो येन तादृक् ।

> *yadvā | aparimitavīrāḥ putrādayo yena tādṛk |*

— that is, having a thousand (many) heroes; or having gods who destroy a thousand enemy heroes; or having heroes, sons, grandsons and the like, many in number.

**बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)** — compared with the notions इध्म (*idhma*) and ईळः (*īḷaḥ*), this means has a more concrete form. बर्हि (*barhi*) means simply the darbha seat. Unlike देवीः द्वारः (*devīḥ dvāraḥ*), where a divine aspect is ascribed to the doors, this has not been done for barhis; only the sense "seat of the gods" is indicated. Moreover, it is prayed that the doors, for the coming of the gods, should open of themselves without other help and make the way. Insentient doors cannot open of their own accord and make a wide passage unless they have divine power. But in the case of barhis alone this power is not ascribed: the ṛtviks must spread it. Not only in this ṛk, but in the other ṛks of the Āprī sūktas too, it is clearly said that barhis is to be spread only with the help of the ṛtviks and others. For example —

> प्राचीनं बर्हिरोजसा सहस्रवीरमस्तृणन् । यत्रादित्या विराजथ ।

> *prācīnaṃ barhirojasā sahasravīramastṛṇan | yatrādityā virājatha |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188-4) *(zoomed)*

— in this ṛk; and likewise in Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5-4 *(zoomed)*, बर्हिः प्राचीनमोजसा पवमानः स्तृणन् हरिः । (*barhiḥ prācīnamojasā pavamānaḥ stṛṇan hariḥ |*) — there is the description that the ṛtviks spread the barhis. Likewise in the ṛks of the other Āprī sūktas too, barhis, though earthly and insentient, is said to be a place in the form of a seat holy to the gods. Only in the Praiṣa sūkta,

*("suṣṭarīnorṇaṃmradā" (na, not ma), "vicapraca" (no spaces), "prathatāgṃ" and "emonadadya" as printed; zoomed.)*

> होता यक्षद्बर्हिः सुष्टरीनोर्णंम्रदा अस्मिन्यज्ञे विचप्रच प्रथताग्ं स्वासस्थं देवेभ्यः । एमोनदद्य वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याः सदंतु प्रियमिंद्रस्यास्तु वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥

> *hotā yakṣadbarhiḥ suṣṭarīnorṇaṃmradā asminyajñe vicapraca prathatāgṃ svāsasthaṃ devebhyaḥ | emonadadya vasavo rudrā ādityāḥ sadaṃtu priyamiṃdrasyāstu vetvājyasya hotaryaja ‖*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-1) *(zoomed)*

— here (the Bhāṣyakāra's) बर्हिर्नामकं चतुर्थप्रयाजदेवमग्निं (*barhirnāmakaṃ caturthaprayājadevamagniṃ*) says that it is a synonym-name of Agni and a seat of divine nature. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa,

> बर्हिर्यजति, पशवो वै बर्हिः पशूनेव तत्प्रीणाति पशून्यजमाने दधाति ।

> *barhiryajati, paśavo vai barhiḥ paśūneva tatprīṇāti paśūnyajamāne dadhāti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-4) *(zoomed)*

— it is explained as the cattle that graze grass and are united with grass. But it appears that there is no room at all for this meaning.

The Niruktakāra has said बर्हिः परिबर्हणात् । (*barhiḥ paribarhaṇāt |*): because it grows fast, darbha has the name barhis (Ni. 8-8) *(zoomed)*. In the Bṛhaddevatā,
---

### Printed p. 238 (PDF 257)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188". Ṛk 4: Special Topics concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; end of Ṛk 4; Ṛk 5 begins.)*

> बर्हिरेवायमग्निस्तु सर्वं हि परिबृंहितं ।
> अन्नेन यद्धुतो वा सन्निध्मेन परिबृंहितः ॥

> *barhirevāyamagnistu sarvaṃ hi paribṛṃhitaṃ |*
> *annena yaddhuto vā sannidhmena paribṛṃhitaḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-5) *(zoomed)*

— since all food is pervaded by it, and since after the oblation it is filled out by the idhma, Agni himself is in the form of barhis: so the identity is stated.

Though in many matters the author of the Bṛhaddevatā has followed the statements of the Nirukta, in this context he shows some difference: what the Niruktakāra called merely barhis, the seat of the gods, he has interpreted as a seat that is of divine nature and a synonym of Agni.

**आदित्याः (*ādityāḥ*)** — who the Ādityas are has been examined on p. 120 of this same part.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** सहस्रवीरम् (*sahasravīram*) — सहस्रसंख्याकाः वीराः यस्य तत् (*sahasrasaṃkhyākāḥ vīrāḥ yasya tat*); in the bahuvrīhi the prior member keeps its own accent by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*). अस्तृणन् (*astṛṇan*) — root स्तृञ् आच्छादने (*stṛñ ācchādane*), kryādi class; laṅ, third person plural; *anta* for *jha*, elision of *i*, *śnā* vikaraṇa; elision of the vikaraṇa's *ā* by श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः (*śnābhyastayorātaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-112); *ṇa* after *ṛ*; *aṭ* augment; nighāta accent because it follows a non-finite word. आदित्याः (*ādityāḥ*) — अदितेः अपत्यानि पुमांसः आदित्याः (*aditeḥ apatyāni pumāṃsaḥ ādityāḥ*); suffix *ṇya* by दित्यदित्यादि— (*dityadityādi—*) (Pā. Sū. 4-1-85) *(as printed, the sūtra only begun)*; initial vṛddhi by तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (*taddhiteṣvacāmādeḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-117); elision of *i* by यस्येति च (*yasyeti ca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-148); all-grave accent as a Vedic usage. *(Sūtra numbers zoomed.)*

*(Rule — end of Ṛk 4.)*

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> विराट् सम्राड्विभ्वीः प्रभ्वीर्बह्वीश्च भूयसीश्च याः ।
> दुरो घृतान्यक्षरन् ॥ ५ ॥

> *virāṭ samrāḍvibhvīḥ prabhvīrbahvīśca bhūyasīśca yāḥ |*
> *duro ghṛtānyakṣaran ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> विऽराट् । संऽराट् । विऽभ्वीः । प्रऽभ्वीः । बह्वीः । च । भूयसीः । च । याः ।
> दुरः । घृतानि । अक्षरन् ॥ ५ ॥

> *vi 'rāṭ | saṃ 'rāṭ | vi 'bhvīḥ | pra 'bhvīḥ | bahvīḥ | ca | bhūyasīḥ | ca | yāḥ |*
> *duraḥ | ghṛtāni | akṣaran ‖ 5 ‖*

### Printed p. 239 (PDF 258)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 8". Ṛk 5, continued.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> विराट् ॥ विशेषेण राजंते इति व्यत्ययेनैकवचनं ॥ सम्राट् सम्यगिति पूज्यतरं राजमानाः ॥ अत्रापि व्यत्ययेनैकवचनं ॥ विभ्वीर्विभ्व्यो विविधं भवित्र्यः प्रभ्वीः प्रभ्व्यः प्रकर्षेण भवित्र्यो बह्वीर्बह्व्यो भूयसीर्लोकप्रसिद्धसंख्याभिश्च भूयस्यश्च या दुरो यज्ञगृहद्वारः संति ता घृतान्युदकानि प्राण्युपकारार्थमक्षरन् । क्षरंति । यद्वा । बह्वीर्भूयसीरित्येते संख्यावचने । शिष्टानि तासां नामधेयानि ॥

> *virāṭ ‖ viśeṣeṇa rājaṃte iti vyatyayenaikavacanaṃ ‖ samrāṭ samyagiti pūjyataraṃ rājamānāḥ ‖ atrāpi vyatyayenaikavacanaṃ ‖ vibhvīrvibhvyo vividhaṃ bhavitryaḥ prabhvīḥ prabhvyaḥ prakarṣeṇa bhavitryo bahvīrbahvyo bhūyasīrlokaprasiddhasaṃkhyābhiśca bhūyasyaśca yā duro yajñagṛhadvāraḥ saṃti tā ghṛtānyudakāni prāṇyupakārārthamakṣaran | kṣaraṃti | yadvā | bahvīrbhūyasīrityete saṃkhyāvacane | śiṣṭāni tāsāṃ nāmadheyāni ‖*

*Gist:* the singulars virāṭ and samrāṭ stand for plurals (vyatyaya); alternatively bahvīḥ and bhūyasīḥ are number-words and the other four are names of the doors.

**Pratipadārtha.** *virāṭ* — shining in a special manner; *samrāṭ* — shining as more worthy of honour; *vibhvīḥ* — splendid in many ways; *prabhvīḥ* — endowed with greatness; *bahvīḥ* — many in number; *bhūyasīśca* — and having abundance; *yāḥ duraḥ* — whichever doors of the sacrificial hall there are, at them; *ghṛtāni* — waters; *akṣaran* — are sprinkled.

**Bhāvārtha.** At whichever doors of the sacrificial hall there are, which shine in a special manner, shine as more worthy of honour, are splendid in many ways, are endowed with greatness, are many in number and have abundance — at them waters are sprinkled.

**English Translation (as printed).**

They have sprinkled water on the doors (of the hall of sacrifice), which are variously and perfectly radiant, manifold, excellent, many, and numerous- *(so printed, ending in a dash; "hall" and "sacrifice" faint, zoomed)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

In this ṛk the door-deities of the sacrificial hall, called देवीर्द्वारः (*devīrdvāraḥ*) (दुरः (*duraḥ*)), are prayed to. A further special point of this ṛk is that the names of the four doors in the four quarters of the sacrificial hall are indicated here; in the other Āprī sūktas there are no such names. Still, it is equally fitting to imagine etymological meanings for विराट् (*virāṭ*) and the other words and take them as adjectives of the word दुरः (*duraḥ*). The Bhāṣyakāra has made both these kinds of attempt.

**दुरः (*duraḥ*)** — द्वारः (*dvāraḥ*): the door-deities of the sacrificial hall. On who these are, Yāska says —

> द्वारः । द्वारो जवतेर्वा द्रवतेर्वा वारयतेर्वा । गृहद्वार इति कात्थक्यः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥

> *dvāraḥ | dvāro javatervā dravatervā vārayatervā | gṛhadvāra iti kātthakyaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*

(Ni. 8-10)

### Printed p. 240 (PDF 259)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 23. Sū. 188" — the Anuvāka numeral is printed as 23 here, not 24 (zoomed). Ṛk 5, Special Topics continued.)*

— so they have given the etymology. A door (द्वार (*dvāra*)) is so called because it is for entering, for going in, or for preventing going in. That द्वार (*dvāra*) means the house-door (*bāgilu*) is the view of Kātthakya; that it is Agni is the view of Śākapūṇi, they have said. They say that the homa-house where the homa is performed is itself a form of Agni, and therefore its doors too are special forms of Agni (अग्निविशेषमूर्तयः (*agniviśeṣamūrtayaḥ*)). The doors of the chamber in which the oblation is offered said to be personification of Agni· [sic]

Sāyaṇa has explained them as the deities presiding over the doors of the sacrificial hall. There is a difference of opinion whether these doors are the actual doors of the sacrificial hall or whether this is merely a figurative usage. If here the word does not mean house-doors, then in the matter of the deities of the Āprī sūktas too, aspects different from those stated so far would have to be considered.

Seen from the standpoint of the ritual procedure, for two things only, barhis and svāhākṛti, no divinity is ascribed: qualities are stated of them, that they are merely earthly but, being connected with the sacrifice, have a supernatural purity. In तिस्रो देवीः (*tisro devīḥ*), because Sarasvatī has a pure divine element, and because the two other rivers are named together with that river, all of them together are called deities. In the same way in दैव्या होतारा (*daivyā hotārā*) too, since Agni, whose self is divine, is with them, the earthly office of hotṛ is also meant as a deity. But in देवीः द्वारः (*devīḥ dvāraḥ*) alone there is no room for this. If these doors are simply the doors of the sacrificial hall, a question arises: why should they have a special place that barhis and svāhākṛti do not have? If only some of the implements and materials that are parts of the sacrifice were to be viewed as divine, then the name of the vedi, the most important of all, is missing.

Not only this: another point to be noted here is that the doors are in the plural.

*("abhīimaṃ" as printed; zoomed.)*

> सप्त होत्राणि मनसा वृणाना इन्वंतो विश्वं प्रति यन्नृतेन ।
> नृपेशसो विदथेषु प्र जाता अभीइमं यज्ञं वि चरंत पूर्वीः ॥

> *sapta hotrāṇi manasā vṛṇānā invaṃto viśvaṃ prati yannṛtena |*
> *nṛpeśaso vidatheṣu pra jātā abhīimaṃ yajñaṃ vi caraṃta pūrvīḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-5) *(zoomed)*

— in this ṛk of an Āprī sūkta the adjective पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*) too is in the plural. And if the office of these door-deities is examined:

1) वि श्रयंतामृतावृधो द्वारो देवीरसश्चतः (*vi śrayaṃtāmṛtāvṛdho dvāro devīrasaścataḥ*) — "open separately for the furtherance of the sacrificial work", in the ṛk 1-13-6 *(zoomed)*;

2) दुरो घृतान्यक्षरन् । (*duro ghṛtānyakṣaran |*) — "they poured waters", in the present ṛk;
---

### Printed p. 241 (PDF 260)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 8". Ṛk 5, Special Topics continued.)*

3) प्र प्र यज्ञं प्रणीत न । (*pra pra yajñaṃ praṇīta na |*) *(so printed)* — "they fill the sacrifice with fruit", in 5-5-5 *(zoomed)*;

4) इन्वंतो विश्वं प्रति यन्नृतेन । (*invaṃto viśvaṃ prati yannṛtena |*) — "they make the whole universe endowed with life by water", in 3-4-5 *(zoomed)*; in these and many other ways their office is indicated. Some hold that in these offices many actions are merely ornamental and figurative, ascribed to them, and that there is no truth in them.

*("asya" (for the expected adya) as printed; zoomed.)*

> समिद्धो अस्य मनुषो दुरोणे देवो देवान् यजसि जातवेदः ।
> आ च वह मित्रमहश्चिकित्वान्त्वं दूतः कविरसि प्रचेताः ॥

> *samiddho asya manuṣo duroṇe devo devān yajasi jātavedaḥ |*
> *ā ca vaha mitramahaścikitvāntvaṃ dūtaḥ kavirasi pracetāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-1) *(zoomed)*

— in this ṛk, since it says मनुषो दुरोणे । (*manuṣo duroṇe |*), "in the sacrificial house of man", this figurative language applied to these ordinary house-doors may also be seen as an exaggeration. Some critics hold that adjectives such as नृपेशसः (*nṛpeśasaḥ*), ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*), पावका (*pāvakā*) and the like are not appropriate. In the present context it is good to know the opinions of the Vedic scholars, who are the mainstay of the preservation of the Vedic tradition, whether to support or to refute these views.

*("svādhyo3" (a 3-like sign after -dhyo) as printed; zoomed.)*

> स्वाध्यो३ वि दुरो देवयंतोऽशिश्रयू रथयुर्देवताता ।
> पूर्वी शिशुं न मातरा रिहाणे समग्रुवो न समनेष्वंजन् ।

> *svādhyo3 vi duro devayaṃto 'śiśrayū rathayurdevatātā |*
> *pūrvī śiśuṃ na mātarā rihāṇe samagruvo na samaneṣvaṃjan |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2-5) *(zoomed)*

— in this ṛk of an Āprī sūkta, यज्ञगृहद्वाराणि इत्यर्थः । (*yajñagṛhadvārāṇi ityarthaḥ |*) — they make clear that the meaning is "the doors of the sacrificial hall". In the same way some other scholars have explained that for the verb व्यशिश्रयुः (*vyaśiśrayuḥ*) the agent is यजमानाः (*yajamānāḥ*), and the construction is that they stood resorting to the doors of the sacrificial hall. The English (Western) scholars Oldenberg, Grassman *(so printed)* and Ludwig too endorse this same explanation, and in

*("virāṭsaṃmrāḍvibhrīḥ" (ra-subscript) as printed; zoomed.)*

> विराट्संम्राड्विभ्रीः प्रभ्वीर्बह्वीश्च भूयसीश्च याः । दुरो घृतान्यक्षरन् ।

> *virāṭsaṃmrāḍvibhrīḥ prabhvīrbahvīśca bhūyasīśca yāḥ | duro ghṛtānyakṣaran |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188-5) *(zoomed)*

— in this ṛk they say the words विराट् (*virāṭ*) and सम्राट् (*samrāṭ*) are the names of two doors. The scholar Max Muller says these are the heavenly doors by which the gods come down from heaven. (History of Ancient Sanskrit Literature· p· 245)· [sic] In the Praiṣa sūkta,

> होतायक्षद्दुर ऋष्वाः कवष्योऽकोषधावनीरुदाताभिर्जिहतां वि पक्षोभिः श्रयंतां । सुप्रायणा अस्मिन्यज्ञे विश्रयंतामृतावृधो वियंत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ।

> *hotāyakṣaddura ṛṣvāḥ kavaṣyo 'koṣadhāvanīrudātābhirjihatāṃ vi pakṣobhiḥ śrayaṃtāṃ | suprāyaṇā asminyajñe viśrayaṃtāmṛtāvṛdho viyaṃtvājyasya hotaryaja |*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-2) *(zoomed)*

*(Ṛk 5, Special Topics continue on p. 242. The printed page ends with the signature "[16]" and "Vol. 14".)*

### Printed p. 242 (PDF 261)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188". Ṛk 5, Special Topics continued.)*

— what is said in these sentences the Bhāṣyakāra has explained as दुरो द्वारसंज्ञकाः पंचमप्रयाजदेवतास्तद्रूपमग्निं दैव्यो होता यजतु (*duro dvārasaṃjñakāḥ paṃcamaprayājadevatāstadrūpamagniṃ daivyo hotā yajatu*) ("the Durs, called the doors, deities of the fifth prayāja: may the divine Hotṛ worship Agni in their form"). In these sentences the words आताभिः उज्जिहतां (*ātābhiḥ ujjihatāṃ*) are the important ones. This somewhat opposes the view above. From this it is one view that the doors being the doors of the sacrificial house may be called figurative. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa,

> दुरो यजति वृष्टिर्वै दुरो वृष्टिमेव तत्प्रीणाति वृष्टिमन्नाद्यं यजमाने दधाति ।

> *duro yajati vṛṣṭirvai duro vṛṣṭimeva tatprīṇāti vṛṣṭimannādyaṃ yajamāne dadhāti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-4) *(zoomed)*

— so, instead of the meaning "door", the meaning "rain" has been given ("he worships the Durs; the Durs are rain; so he pleases rain, and places rain and food in the sacrificer"). How this meaning comes about has not been made clear. The Niruktakāra,

द्वारो जवतेर्वा द्रवतेर्वा वारयतेर्वा । (*dvāro javatervā dravatervā vārayatervā |*) — has said that it is formed either from the root जु (*ju*), meaning "to push forward", or from the root द्रु (*dru*), meaning "to run forward", or from the root वृ (*vṛ*), meaning "to keep apart"; and,

> व्यचस्वतीरुर्विया वि श्रयंतां पतिभ्यो न जनयः शुंभमानाः ।
> देवीर्द्वारो बृहतीर्विश्वमिन्वा देवेभ्यो भवत सुप्रायणाः ।

> *vyacasvatīrurviyā vi śrayaṃtāṃ patibhyo na janayaḥ śuṃbhamānāḥ |*
> *devīrdvāro bṛhatīrviśvaminvā devebhyo bhavata suprāyaṇāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-5) *(zoomed)*

— citing this ṛk and explaining the meaning of the word द्वार (*dvāra*), गृहद्वार इति कात्थक्यः । (*gṛhadvāra iti kātthakyaḥ |*) — according to the view of Kātthakya, house-doors; अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः । (*agniriti śākapūṇiḥ |*) — according to the view of Śākapūṇi, Agni: so they have set out the difference of opinion too (Ni. 8-10) *(zoomed)*. In the Bṛhaddevatā,

> द्वारस्तु देव्यो याः प्रोक्ता विश्वेषां तास्तु पत्नयः ।
> अग्नायीमनुवर्तंते तथाग्नाय्यग्निमेव च ॥
> अग्नौ ध्रुवं स्थितास्तास्तु संस्तूयंतेऽग्निना सह ।
> प्राधान्यं तासु चैवाग्नेः स्तुतिष्वेव हविष्षु च ॥

> *dvārastu devyo yāḥ proktā viśveṣāṃ tāstu patnayaḥ |*
> *agnāyīmanuvartaṃte tathāgnāyyagnimeva ca ‖*
> *agnau dhruvaṃ sthitāstāstu saṃstūyaṃte 'gninā saha |*
> *prādhānyaṃ tāsu caivāgneḥ stutiṣveva haviṣṣu ca ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-6 to 7) *(zoomed)*

— it is said that these doors are the wives of the gods; that they follow Agnāyī, who follows Agni; and that, being firmly settled in Agni himself, they are praised together with Agni. This explanation is reasonable.

On consecrating the four doors of the sacrificial house, the Taittirīya Saṃhitā describes it thus —

### Printed p. 243 (PDF 262)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 8" (zoomed). Ṛk 5, Special Topics concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā begins.)*

> प्राचीनवग्ंशं करोति देवमनुष्या दिशो व्यभजंत प्राचीं देवा दक्षिणा पितरः प्रतीचीं मनुष्या उदीचीग्ं रुद्राः ॥

> *prācīnavagṃśaṃ karoti devamanuṣyā diśo vyabhajaṃta prācīṃ devā dakṣiṇā pitaraḥ pratīcīṃ manuṣyā udīcīgṃ rudrāḥ ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-1-1) *(zoomed; two tries)*

— that is, it says that the gods took the eastern door of the sacrificial house, the Pitṛ-deities the southern door, men the western door and the (eleven) Rudras the northern door, dividing them among themselves.

The names of the doors of this sacrificial house, as stated in this ṛk, are as follows. विराट् (*virāṭ*) may be said to be the eastern door, सम्राट् (*samrāṭ*) the southern door, विभ्वीः (*vibhvīḥ*) the western door and प्रभ्वीः (*prabhvīḥ*) the northern door. Sāyaṇa has explained the etymological meanings of these words.

**विराट् (*virāṭ*)** — विशेषेण राजंत इति । व्यत्ययेनैकवचनं । (*viśeṣeṇa rājaṃta iti | vyatyayenaikavacanaṃ |*) Because it shines in a special manner, this door (the eastern door) has the name विराट् (*virāṭ*). The singular is used as a Vedic usage.

**सम्राट् (*samrāṭ*)** — सम्यगिति पूज्यतरं राजमानाः । अत्रापि व्यत्ययेनैकवचनं । (*samyagiti pūjyataraṃ rājamānāḥ | atrāpi vyatyayenaikavacanaṃ |*) Because it is well made, this door is worthy of honour and shining. Here too the singular is used for the reason stated above.

**विभ्वीः (*vibhvīḥ*)** — विभ्व्यः विविधं भवित्र्यः । (*vibhvyaḥ vividhaṃ bhavitryaḥ |*) Being in various ways, that is, the meaning is doors that are decorated.

**प्रभ्वीः (*prabhvīḥ*)** — प्रकर्षेण भवित्र्यः । (*prakarṣeṇa bhavitryaḥ |*) The meaning is doors that are very well decorated.

**बह्वीश्च भूयसीश्च (*bahvīśca bhūyasīśca*)** — लोकप्रसिद्धसंख्याभिश्च भूयस्यश्च । (*lokaprasiddhasaṃkhyābhiśca bhūyasyaśca |*) That is, the four doors in the four directions, as is well known in the world. From the word भूयसीश्च (*bhūyasīśca*) it becomes clear that, because these doors are large, they are well known as great doors.

**घृतानि (*ghṛtāni*)** — since the word घृत (*ghṛta*) is read among the hundred-and-one names of water beginning with अर्णः क्षोदः (*arṇaḥ kṣodaḥ*) (Ni. 2-24-) *(zoomed; so printed, with a trailing hyphen)*, here घृतानि (*ghṛtāni*) means waters.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** विराट् (*virāṭ*) — विशेषेण राजंते इति विराजः (*viśeṣeṇa rājaṃte iti virājaḥ*); root राजृ दीप्तौ (*rājṛ dīptau*), suffix *kvip*; by व्यत्ययो बहुलम् (*vyatyayo bahulam*) a singular ending for the plural; at the end of the word *ṣa* for the root's *ja* by व्रश्चभृस्ज— (*vraścabhṛsja—*) *(as printed, the sūtra only begun)*; by the sūtra गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत् (*gatikārakopapadātkṛt*) the final member, a kṛt-formation, keeps its own accent. In सम्राट् (*samrāṭ*) likewise the singular comes by vyatyaya. *(No sūtra numbers printed on this page.)*

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Ṛk numeral zoomed.)*

> सुरुक्मे हि सुपेशसाधि श्रिया विराजतः ।
> उषासावेह सीदतां ॥ ६ ॥

> *surukme hi supeśasādhi śriyā virājataḥ |*
> *uṣāsāveha sīdatāṃ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सुरुक्मे इति सुऽरुक्मे । हि । सुऽपेशसा । अधि । श्रिया । विऽराजतः ।
> उषसौ । आ । इह । सीदतां ॥ ६ ॥

> *surukme iti su 'rukme | hi | su 'peśasā | adhi | śriyā | vi 'rājataḥ |*
> *uṣasau | ā | iha | sīdatāṃ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* the deities of Day and Night, of fair ornament and form, shine greatly with beauty; "uṣas" stands for night as well as day (by implication); may both come and sit here today.

> सुरुक्मे शोभनदीप्त्याभरणे प्रसिद्धे सुपेशसा शोभनरूपे ईदृश्यावहोरात्रदेवते अध्यधिकं श्रिया सौंदर्येण विराजतः । विशेषेण दीप्येते ॥ हियोगादनिघातः ॥ तादृश्यावुषसौ । एतद्रात्रेरप्युपलक्षणं । उषःशब्दो दिवसस्योपलक्षकः । रात्रिरुषाश्चोभे इहास्मिन्दिन आ सीदतां । आगत्य तिष्ठतां । आगच्छतां वा ॥

> *surukme śobhanadīptyābharaṇe prasiddhe supeśasā śobhanarūpe īdṛśyāvahorātradevate adhyadhikaṃ śriyā sauṃdaryeṇa virājataḥ | viśeṣeṇa dīpyete ‖ hiyogādanighātaḥ ‖ tādṛśyāvuṣasau | etadrātrerapyupalakṣaṇaṃ | uṣaḥśabdo divasasyopalakṣakaḥ | rātriruṣāścobhe ihāsmindina ā sīdatāṃ | āgatya tiṣṭhatāṃ | āgacchatāṃ vā ‖*


**Pratipadārtha.** सुरुक्मे (*surukme*) — who have radiance itself as their ornament; सुपेशसा (*supeśasā*) — and who have an attractive form, the deities of Day and Night; अधि (*adhi*) — exceeding; श्रिया (*śriyā*) — with beauty; विराजतः (*virājataḥ*) — shine; उषसौ (*uṣasau*) — the Day-and-Night deities of such beauty; इह (*iha*) — today (on the darbha seat); आ सीदतां (*ā sīdatāṃ*) — may they come and sit.

**Bhāvārtha.** The deities of Day and Night, who have radiance itself as their ornament and who have an attractive form, shine with exceeding beauty. May the Day-and-Night deities of such beauty come and sit on the darbha seat.

### Printed p. 245 (PDF 264)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 9" (zoomed) — the Varga changes to 9 with Ṛk 6; no Varga-closing line is printed at the end of Ṛk 5. Ṛk 6, continued.)*

**English Translation (as printed).**

Let the brilliant and beautiful Day and Night, who shine with surpassing lustre, sit down here (upon the sacred grass)· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**सुपेशसा (*supeśasā*)** — since the word पेशः (*peśaḥ*) is read among the 16 words meaning "form", beginning with निर्णिक् (*nirṇik*), वव्रिः (*vavriḥ*) *(zoomed)*, (Ni. 8-11) *(zoomed)*, पेशः (*peśaḥ*) means form. Therefore सुपेशसा (*supeśasā*) — शोभनरूपयुक्ते (*śobhanarūpayukte*) — means endowed with a fair form, beautiful.

**उषसौ (*uṣasau*)** — since in this ṛk the dual उषसौ (*uṣasau*) is used, it should be understood that the two deities called उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) or नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*) are meant. Who is this deity called नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*)? What is their nature? Such matters must be examined closely.

In this ṛk the presiding deities of night and of early morning, called नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*), are invoked. Yāska's explanation of the word नक्तोषसा (*naktoṣasā*) *(so printed here)* is as follows —

> उषासानक्ता । उषासानक्तोषाश्च नक्ता चोषा व्याख्याता । नक्तेति रात्रिनामानक्ति भूतान्यवश्यायेनापि वा नक्ताऽव्यक्तवर्णा ॥

> *uṣāsānaktā | uṣāsānaktoṣāśca naktā coṣā vyākhyātā | nakteti rātrināmānakti bhūtānyavaśyāyenāpi vā naktā 'vyaktavarṇā ‖*

— though it is read in two ways, नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*) and उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*), the meaning is one and the same. The explanation of the word उषाः (*uṣāḥ*) has been given earlier, he says. नक्ता (*naktā*) is a name of night, because नक्ता (*naktā*) means अव्यक्तवर्णा (*avyaktavarṇā*): since it is darkness, things are unmanifest, that is, they are not seen well. Therefore night, joined with darkness, has the name नक्ता (*naktā*); and in this night-time living beings are unable to do their various activities. अनक्ति क्लेदयति भूतानि अवश्यायेन । अपि वानक्ता अव्यक्तवर्णा । यथा अहः सर्वमभिव्यक्तरूपं भवति न तथा रात्रिः ॥ (*anakti kledayati bhūtāni avaśyāyena | api vānaktā avyaktavarṇā | yathā ahaḥ sarvamabhivyaktarūpaṃ bhavati na tathā rātriḥ ‖*) Because darkness gives trouble to living beings, so that there is no room for their activities to go on properly, night joined with such darkness has the name नक्ता (*naktā*). Or, because nothing is seen well and everything is unmanifest, it has the name नक्ता (*naktā*). In the daytime the forms of all things are seen clearly; at night they are not seen so. Therefore night-time has the name नक्ता (*naktā*): so they have explained the meaning (Ni. 8-11) *(zoomed)*.

He has merely said that the meaning of the word उषाः (*uṣāḥ*) has been explained earlier. That explanation is as follows —

### Printed p. 246 (PDF 265)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188". Ṛk 6, Special Topics continued.)*

विभावरी (*vibhāvarī*), सूनरी (*sūnarī*) and the rest — sixteen words — are names of Uṣas (2-19) *(zoomed at 600 and 1000 dpi; so printed)*; and

> उषाः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः ॥

> *uṣāḥ kasmāducchatīti satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ ‖*

— because it removes the darkness (*tamas*) of the night-time, it has the name उषाः (*uṣāḥ*); that is, the later time of the night, its last part. To support this meaning they have given an example.

*("jotir-" (without the ya-subscript) in the first line as printed.)*

> इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां जोतिरागाच्चित्रः प्रकेतो अजनिष्ट विभ्वा ।
> यथा प्रसूता सवितुः सवायँ एवा रात्र्युषसे योनिमारैक् ॥

> *idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jotirāgāccitraḥ praketo ajaniṣṭa vibhvā |*
> *yathā prasūtā savituḥ savāya~ evā rātryuṣase yonimāraik ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-1) *(zoomed; three tries)*

The Nirukta of this ṛk —

> इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागमत् । चित्रं प्रकेतनं प्रज्ञाततममजनिष्ट विभूततमं यथा प्रसूता सवितुः प्रसवाय रात्रिरादित्यस्य । एवं रात्र्युषसे योनिमरिचत् स्थानं । स्त्रीयोनिरभियुत एनां गर्भः ॥

> *idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāgamat | citraṃ praketanaṃ prajñātatamamajaniṣṭa vibhūtatamaṃ yathā prasūtā savituḥ prasavāya rātrirādityasya | evaṃ rātryuṣase yonimaricat sthānaṃ | strīyonirabhiyuta enāṃ garbhaḥ ‖*

— the excellent and exceedingly brilliant light of the sun is rising. The dawn-time, which precedes such light of the sun, appears before the daylight like the banner (*niketana*, like a flag) of that light. That is: just as the light of the sun, having shone all day, at the time of setting becomes the source (*yoni*), that is, the cause, of night, so night in its final period becomes the source, that is, the cause, of the dawn-time. *Yoni* means the place of birth. The main intent is that at the end of the day night, and at the end of night the dawn-time, come about in the form of a cycle of change. Therefore उषः (*uṣaḥ*) means the light, the brightness, that spreads over all the quarters and appears before sunrise, after the night has passed.

The Bhāṣyakāra's (Sāyaṇa's) explanation of the meaning — नक्तशब्द उषश्शब्दश्च लोके कालविशेषवाचिनौ । इह तु तत्कालाभिमानिवह्निमूर्तिद्वये प्रयुज्येते । नक्तोषासा नक्तोषोनामिके वह्निमूर्ती (*naktaśabda uṣaśśabdaśca loke kālaviśeṣavācinau | iha tu tatkālābhimānivahnimūrtidvaye prayujyete | naktoṣāsā naktoṣonāmike vahnimūrtī*) — that is: these two words, नक्त (*nakta*) (night) and उषः (*uṣaḥ*) (morning), have in worldly usage the meaning of denoting the particular times night and morning. Here, that is in this ṛk or in the Ṛgveda, these words convey the meaning of the deities presiding over night and the morning-time. Therefore the words नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*) or उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*), in the sense of the two forms (*mūrti*, shapes) of Agni that are the deities presiding over night and the dawn-time,

---

### Printed p. 247 (PDF 266)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 9" (zoomed). Ṛk 6, Special Topics continued.)*

— are used. The word सुपेशसा (*supeśasā*) (having a good form or shape) used in this ṛk supports this meaning. For night and morning, being divisions of time, have neither form nor shape. In the view that they are the deities presiding over those times, a form can be ascribed to those deities. Since there is such an ascription in this ṛk, it should be understood that here the deities presiding over those times are meant. The *ṣa* in the word नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*) is long for the convenience of the metre.

In the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-142-6 *(zoomed; three tries)* the epithet ऋतस्य मातरा (*ṛtasya mātarā*) is very important.

> प्रवतां त उषसा वाजयंती अग्ने वातस्य पथ्याभिरच्छ ।
> यत्सीमंजंति पूर्व्यं हविर्भिरा वंधुरेव तस्थतुर्दुरोणे ॥

> *pravatāṃ ta uṣasā vājayaṃtī agne vātasya pathyābhiraccha |*
> *yatsīmaṃjaṃti pūrvyaṃ havirbhirā vaṃdhureva tasthaturduroṇe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-14-3) *(zoomed)*

— in this ṛk their eternal connection with the sacrifice is described. In all the ṛks that invoke them (there are about twenty such ṛks) they are prayed to come together with the other deities and sit on the darbha seat. Among them, they have a very close connection with Agni, which is kindled at the dawn-time and at evening. Hence also the figurative description that they hold Agni between them,

> नक्तोषासा वर्णमामेम्याने धापयेते शिशुमेकं समीची ।
> द्यावाक्षामा रुक्मो अंतर्वि भाति देवा अग्निं धारयन्द्रविणोदां ।

> *naktoṣāsā varṇamāmemyāne dhāpayete śiśumekaṃ samīcī |*
> *dyāvākṣāmā rukmo aṃtarvi bhāti devā agniṃ dhārayandraviṇodāṃ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-5) *(zoomed)*

— in such ṛks it is made known that they help Agni, who is in the form of an infant, to drink the havis. Because of this connection they are said to be near to the performers of the sacrifice. Generally in the Āprī sūktas too the description of this aspect is repeated. For example —

*("sakupiśaṃ" (for the expected śukrapiśaṃ) as printed; zoomed.)*

> आ सुष्वयंती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योनौ ।
> दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं सकुपिशं दधाने ॥

> *ā suṣvayaṃtī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ ni yonau |*
> *divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṃ sakupiśaṃ dadhāne ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-6) *(zoomed)*

— in this ṛk of an Āprī sūkta too the same matter is stated.

From this aspect it is known that the Uṣāsānaktā deities obtain in sacrificial work not a secondary place but a most important place. This chief place,

*(Ṛk 6, Special Topics continue on p. 248.)*

### Printed p. 248 (PDF 267)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188". Ṛk 6, Special Topics continued.)*

*("न्राग्ः" in the first line as the Kannada letters stand; "सग्ं" as printed.)*

> होता यक्षदुषासानक्ता बृहती सुपेशसा न्राग्ः पतिभ्यो योनिं कृण्वाने ।
> सग्ं स्मयमाने इंद्रेण देवैरेदं बर्हिः सीदतां वीतामाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥

> *hotā yakṣaduṣāsānaktā bṛhatī supeśasā nrāgḥ patibhyo yoniṃ kṛṇvāne |*
> *sagṃ smayamāne iṃdreṇa devairedaṃ barhiḥ sīdatāṃ vītāmājyasya hotaryaja ‖*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-1) *(zoomed)*

— as indicated in this mantra of the Praiṣa sūkta, there is the prayer that the Uṣānaktās should sit on the darbha seat not only together with Agni but also together with Indra and the other deities. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa they are addressed as अहोरात्रे (*ahorātre*). The Niruktakāra has also explained the nature of these deities in 8-11. It has been made known earlier that the Niruktakāra has stated the derivation of the two words उषस् (*uṣas*) and नक्त (*nakta*) and the nature of these deities. In the Bṛhaddevatā too they are described in this way.

> नक्तोषासौ च ये देव्यावाग्नेय्यावेव ते स्मृते ।
> श्याव्याग्नेयी हि कालस्य तस्यैवोषाः कलेव तु ॥

> *naktoṣāsau ca ye devyāvāgneyyāveva te smṛte |*
> *śyāvyāgneyī hi kālasya tasyaivoṣāḥ kaleva tu ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-8)

Both these deities, Uṣas and Nakta, are well known as connected with Agni. Of them, it is a known matter that श्यावी (*śyāvī*) (the night-deity, 1-71-1 *(so printed; zoomed at 1000 dpi)*) has a close connection with Agni, and, from the Nirukta sentence उषः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः (*uṣaḥ kasmāducchatīti satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ*) (Ni. 2-18) *(zoomed; "uṣaḥ" here, "uṣāḥ" on p. 246)*, that Uṣas is the later time of that night.

*("नञद् पूर्वाञ्जेरिदं" as printed; zoomed.)*

> तम उच्छत्युषा नक्तानक्तीमां हिमबिंदुभिः ।
> अपि वाव्यक्तवर्णेति नञद् पूर्वाञ्जेरिदं भवेत् ॥

> *tama ucchatyuṣā naktānaktīmāṃ himabiṃdubhiḥ |*
> *api vāvyaktavarṇeti nañad pūrvāñjeridaṃ bhavet ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-9)

Of these two, Uṣas drives away the darkness. Night makes everything wet with dew-drops and pervaded by them. Or, since it has no definite colour, the root अञ्ज्न् (*añjn*) *(so printed; zoomed)* joined with the word नञ् (*nañ*) gives the meaning "of unmanifest colour".

> सा हि दोषा भवत्यादौ निशीथे सा तमस्वती ।
> नाम्ना भवत्युषाश्चैव सैषा प्रागुदयाद्रवेः ॥

> *sā hi doṣā bhavatyādau niśīthe sā tamasvatī |*
> *nāmnā bhavatyuṣāścaiva saiṣā prāgudayādraveḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-10)

At the beginning this deity has the name (प्र (*pra*))दोषा (*doṣā*), at midnight तमस्वती (*tamasvatī*), and before sunrise उषस् (*uṣas*). दोषा (*doṣā*), तमस्वती (*tamasvatī*), श्यावी (*śyāvī*), नक्ता (*naktā*) — all these are read in the Nighaṇṭu as names of night (Nighaṇṭu 1-7) *(zoomed)*.

In other places of the Ṛksaṃhitā the help of the Uṣāsānaktās in extending the sacrifice is described with epithets such as तंतुं ततं संवयंती (*taṃtuṃ tataṃ saṃvayaṃtī*) (2-3-6) *(zoomed; three tries)*.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly).* सुरुक्मे (*surukme*) — शोभनं रुक्मं ययोस्ते (*śobhanaṃ rukmaṃ yayoste*); final udātta of the second member by नञ्सुभ्याम् (*nañsubhyām*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) *(zoomed)*; dual. सुपेशसा (*supeśasā*) — initial udātta of the second member by आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छंदसि (*ādyudāttaṃ dvyacchaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-1[?]9) *(so printed; the fourth digit is broken; zoomed, two tries)*, overriding the accent of सु (*su*); *ā* for the dual by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*). विराजतः (*virājataḥ*) — root राजृ दीप्तौ (*rājṛ dīptau*), *laṭ*, third person dual; no nighāta by हि च (*hi ca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-34) *(zoomed)*; the root accent stays by तास्यनुदात्तेत्— (*tāsyanudāttet—*); the gati वि (*vi*) is anudātta by तिङ्ङ् चोदात्तवति (*tiṅṅ codāttavati*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71) *(zoomed)*. सीदतां (*sīdatāṃ*) — root षद्लृ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु (*ṣadlṛ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*); *loṭ* third person dual, ताम् (*tām*) by तस्थस्थ— (*tasthastha—*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-101), सीद (*sīda*) by पाघ्रा— (*pāghrā—*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-78) *(both zoomed)*; nighāta, being after a non-finite word.

*(Rule — end of Ṛk 6.)*

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Ṛk numeral zoomed.)*

> प्रथमा हि सुवाचसा होतारा दैव्या कवी ।
> यज्ञं नो यक्षतामिमं ॥ ७ ॥

> *prathamā hi suvācasā hotārā daivyā kavī |*
> *yajñaṃ no yakṣatāmimaṃ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्रथमा । हि । सुऽवाचसा । होतारा । दैव्या । कवी इति ।
> यज्ञं । नः । यक्षतां । इमं ॥ ७ ॥

> *prathamā | hi | su 'vācasā | hotārā | daivyā | kavī iti |*
> *yajñaṃ | naḥ | yakṣatāṃ | imaṃ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*("प्रतमौ" and "हिः" as printed.)*

> प्रथमा । मुख्यनामैतत् । प्रतमौ प्रकृष्टतमौ । हिः प्रसिद्धौ । सुवाचसा प्रियवचनौ दैव्या देवार्हौ होतारा देवानामाह्वातारौ होमनिष्पादकौ वा कवी मेधाविनावेतौ नोऽस्मदीयमिमं यज्ञं यक्षतां । यजतां । गच्छतां वा ॥

> *prathamā | mukhyanāmaitat | pratamau prakṛṣṭatamau | hiḥ prasiddhau | suvācasā priyavacanau daivyā devārhau hotārā devānāmāhvātārau homaniṣpādakau vā kavī medhāvināvetau no 'smadīyamimaṃ yajñaṃ yakṣatāṃ | yajatāṃ | gacchatāṃ vā ‖*


**Pratipadārtha.** प्रथमा हि (*prathamā hi*) — renowned and pre-eminent; सुवाचसा (*suvācasā*) — having pleasing speech;

*(Ṛk 7, Pratipadārtha continues on p. 250.)*

### Printed p. 250 (PDF 269)

*(Header: "Maṃ. . A. 24. Sū. 188" (the Maṇḍala numeral is not printed). Ṛk 7, continued.)*

*(Pratipadārtha, continued.)* दैव्या (*daivyā*) — of divine nature; होतारा (*hotārā*) — who give the invitation to the deities; कवी (*kavī*) — and wise, these two; नः (*naḥ*) — our; इमं यज्ञं (*imaṃ yajñaṃ*) — this sacrifice; यक्षतां (*yakṣatāṃ*) — may they accomplish.

**Bhāvārtha.** May these two — renowned, pre-eminent, of most pleasing speech, of divine nature, who give the invitation to the deities, and wise — together accomplish this our sacrifice.

**English Translation (as printed; heading printed "English Translatin" [sic]).**

Let these two chief, well-spoken, divine sages, the invokers (of the gods), perform this our sacrifice· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**दैव्या होतारा (*daivyā hotārā*)** — देवसंबंधिनौ होतारौ । अयं च मध्यमस्थानश्च इत्युभौ (*devasaṃbaṃdhinau hotārau | ayaṃ ca madhyamasthānaśca ityubhau*) — Sāyaṇa has interpreted them as the two forms of Agni, both connected with the gods and both hotṛs: the terrestrial Agni and the Agni that is in the mid-region. Some modern scholars have given a different meaning for this and have shown differences of opinion among themselves. The scholar Geldner has interpreted it as the hotṛ who performs the sacrifice and his Agni; Haug as the hotṛ and the adhvaryu; Oldenberg as the hotṛ and his assistant, the Maitrāvaruṇa. None of these is fitting.

That accomplishing the sacrifice is the chief duty of these hotṛs is stated in ṛks 1-13-8 and 1-188-7 with यज्ञं नो यक्षतामिमं (*yajñaṃ no yakṣatāmimaṃ*), and in ṛk 2-3-7 with देवान्यजंतावृतुथा (*devānyajaṃtāvṛtuthā*) *(refs zoomed)*. This statement of duty is applicable to the human hotṛ, and it addresses Agni figuratively.

Yāska's explanation concerning the word दैवा होतारा (*daivā hotārā*) *(so printed, without the ya-subscript)* —

> दैव्या होतारा दैव्यौ होतारावयं चाग्निरसौ च मध्यमः ॥

> *daivyā hotārā daivyau hotārāvayaṃ cāgnirasau ca madhyamaḥ ‖*

— that is, this word indicates Agni alone. Since Agni invites the deities, Agni stands in the middle between the deities and men; on this matter they have given an example.

> दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै ।
> प्रचोदयंता विदथेषु कारू प्राचीनं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशंता ॥

> *daivyā hotārā prathamā suvācā mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai |*
> *pracodayaṃtā vidatheṣu kārū prācīnaṃ jyotiḥ pradiśā diśaṃtā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-7) *(zoomed)*

### Printed p. 251 (PDF 270)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 9" (zoomed). Ṛk 7, Special Topics continued.)*

Durgācārya's commentary on it —

> यावेतौ दैव्यौ होतारौ । देवेषु भवौ दैव्यौ देवावेव दैव्यौ । स्वार्थे एव तद्धितः । मनुष्यहोतारौ अपेक्ष्य । दैव्यौ होतारौ होतृमैत्रावरुणौ इति विशेषणं । होतारा होतारौ आह्वातारौ देवानां वाय्वग्नी । प्रथमा प्रथमौ मुख्यौ मनुष्यहोतारावपेक्ष्य । सुवाचा । सुवाचौ, प्रशस्तवाचौ, सुस्तुतौ । मिमाना यज्ञं यज्ञनिर्मातारौ नित्यं । मनुषः मनुष्यस्य यजध्यै यजनाय । प्रचोदयंता प्रचोदयमानौ । विदथेषु यज्ञेषु । कारू कर्तारौ । इत्यादि ।

> *yāvetau daivyau hotārau | deveṣu bhavau daivyau devāveva daivyau | svārthe eva taddhitaḥ | manuṣyahotārau apekṣya | daivyau hotārau hotṛmaitrāvaruṇau iti viśeṣaṇaṃ | hotārā hotārau āhvātārau devānāṃ vāyvagnī | prathamā prathamau mukhyau manuṣyahotārāvapekṣya | suvācā | suvācau, praśastavācau, sustutau | mimānā yajñaṃ yajñanirmātārau nityaṃ | manuṣaḥ manuṣyasya yajadhyai yajanāya | pracodayaṃtā pracodayamānau | vidatheṣu yajñeṣu | kārū kartārau | ityādi |*

Its main intent is this: for the deities, Agni and Vāyu are known as the hotṛs; for men, the ṛtvijs called the Hotṛ and the Maitrāvaruṇa are known as the hotṛs. Since Agni, or Agni and Vāyu, stand in the middle between the deities and men and establish the connection between them, Agni is called the *madhyama* (the one in the middle). The name of the deities दैव्या होतारा (*daivyā hotārā*), apart from the Āprī sūktas, —

> त्वष्टारं वायुमृभवो य ओहते दैव्या होतारा उषसं स्वस्तये ।

> *tvaṣṭāraṃ vāyumṛbhavo ya ohate daivyā hotārā uṣasaṃ svastaye |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-65-10) *(zoomed)*

> दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा पुरोहित ऋतस्य पंथामन्वेमि साधुया ।

> *daivyā hotārā prathamā purohita ṛtasya paṃthāmanvemi sādhuyā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-66-13) *(zoomed)*

— is read only in these two ṛks. In ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2-7 they are called जातावेदसा (*jātāvedasā*), and in ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-70-7 पुरोहितौ (*purohitau*) *(both refs zoomed)*. And since the words in the ṛks quoted above — मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै (*mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai*), यज्ञेषु मानुषेषु कारू (*yajñeṣu mānuṣeṣu kārū*) and प्रचोदयंता विदथेषु कारू (*pracodayaṃtā vidatheṣu kārū*) — say that these deities conduct the sacrifices performed by men, it is natural that they are called *purohitas*. Among the deities the hotṛs are Agni and Vāyu, while among men the Hotṛ and his assistant ṛtvij, the Maitrāvaruṇa, are called the hotṛs. This Maitrāvaruṇa, by the praiṣa mantras, commands the other ṛtvijs to do their respective tasks. In the Yajurveda (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1- ) *(so printed, with a blank; zoomed)* it is said: मैत्रावरुणो हि पुरस्तादृत्विग्भ्यो वाचं विभजति (*maitrāvaruṇo hi purastādṛtvigbhyo vācaṃ vibhajati*).

Thus, just as some epithets, though common to both hotṛs, indicate the duty of the human hotṛ alone, so some other epithets too, though common to both, describe only the duties of Agni, who is the divine hotṛ. For example —

*(Ṛk 7, Special Topics continue on p. 252.)*

### Printed p. 252 (PDF 271)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188". Ṛk 7, Special Topics concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā begun.)*

> दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा न्यृंजे सप्त पृक्षासः स्वधया मदंति ।
> ऋतं शंसंत ऋतमित्त आहुरनु व्रतं व्रतपा दीध्यानाः ॥

> *daivyā hotārā prathamā nyṛṃje sapta pṛkṣāsaḥ svadhayā madaṃti |*
> *ṛtaṃ śaṃsaṃta ṛtamitta āhuranu vrataṃ vratapā dīdhyānāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-7) *(zoomed)*

That in this ṛk the epithet प्रथमा (*prathamā*) refers to Agni, the divine hotṛ, alone, there is no doubt. In 1-13-4 *(zoomed)* too, होता मनुर्हितः (*hotā manurhitaḥ*) is an epithet of Agni. The definite difference between these two hotṛs is stated in the Praiṣa sūkta in this way.

*("पोतारा" as printed.)*

> होता यक्षद्दैव्या होतारा मंद्रा पोतारा कवी प्रचेतसा । स्विष्टमद्यान्यः करदिषा स्वभिगूर्तमन्य ऊर्जा सतवसेमं यज्ञं दिवि देवेषु धत्तां वीतामाज्यस्य होतर्यज ।

> *hotā yakṣaddaivyā hotārā maṃdrā potārā kavī pracetasā | sviṣṭamadyānyaḥ karadiṣā svabhigūrtamanya ūrjā satavasemaṃ yajñaṃ divi deveṣu dhattāṃ vītāmājyasya hotaryaja |*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-2) *(zoomed)*

In this sentence it is indicated that one hotṛ should make the sacrifice acceptable by the havis in the form of food, and that the other should establish this sacrifice in heaven among the deities. This division of work makes known the difference between the human hotṛ and Agni, the divine hotṛ. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa,

> दैव्या होतारा यजति प्राणापानौ वै दैव्या होतारा प्राणापानावेव तत्प्रीणाति प्राणापानौ यजमाने दधाति ।

> *daivyā hotārā yajati prāṇāpānau vai daivyā hotārā prāṇāpānāveva tatprīṇāti prāṇāpānau yajamāne dadhāti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-4) *(zoomed)*

— thus, stating the identity of these hotṛs with prāṇa and apāna, it says that the one who recites this mantra procures for the sacrificer the well-being of prāṇa and apāna. In the Nirukta,

> दैव्या होतारा दैव्यौ होतारावयं चाग्निरसौ च मध्यमः ।

> *daivyā hotārā daivyau hotārāvayaṃ cāgnirasau ca madhyamaḥ |*

(Ni. 8-12) *(zoomed)*

— thus, by supporting statements that confirm Sāyaṇa's meaning, it is said that they are the terrestrial Agni and the Agni in the mid-region. In the Bṛhaddevatā too, approving this same opinion,

> दैव्याविति तु होतारावग्नी पार्थिवमध्यमौ ।
> दिव्यादग्नेर्हि जज्ञाते दैव्यौ तेनेह जन्मना ॥

> *daivyāviti tu hotārāvagnī pārthivamadhyamau |*
> *divyādagnerhi jajñāte daivyau teneha janmanā ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-11) *(zoomed)*

— these two hotṛs are said to be the terrestrial and the middle (in the mid-region) Agnis.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly).* प्रथमा (*prathamā*) — *ā* substituted for the dual case-ending by सुपां सुलुक्— (*supāṃ suluk—*) (Pā. Sū. 7-[?]-39) *(the middle digit is broken; zoomed, two tries)*.

*(Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Ṛk 7, continued.)* सुवाचसा (*suvācasā*) — शोभनं वाचः ययोस्ते (*śobhanaṃ vācaḥ yayoste*); by आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छंदसि (*ādyudāttaṃ dvyacchaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-119) *(so printed; zoomed, three tries)* the accent of the second member is *antodātta* *(so printed)*; *ā* for the dual as before. दैव्या (*daivyā*) — देवमर्हत इति दैव्यौ (*devamarhata iti daivyau*); the suffix यञ् (*yañ*) by देवाद्यञञौ (*devādyañañau*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-59) *(read from the strip)*; thus the form यक्षताम् (*yakṣatām*); nighāta, being after a non-finite word.

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Ṛk numeral zoomed.)*

> भारतीळे सरस्वति या वः सर्वा उपब्रुवे ।
> ता नश्चोदयत श्रिये ॥ ८ ॥

> *bhāratīḷe sarasvati yā vaḥ sarvā upabruve |*
> *tā naścodayata śriye ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> भारति । इळे । सरस्वति । याः । वः । सर्वाः । उपऽब्रुवे ।
> ताः । नः । चोदयत । श्रिये ॥ ८ ॥

> *bhārati | iḷe | sarasvati | yāḥ | vaḥ | sarvāḥ | upa 'bruve |*
> *tāḥ | naḥ | codayata | śriye ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Bhāratī (of the sun, *bharata*), the heaven-deity; Iḷā, the earth-goddess; Sarasvatī, the mid-region deity (*saras* = speech or water) — said to be forms of the sun's power; I praise you all: urge us to prosperity.

> हे भारति । भरत आदित्यः । तस्य संबंधिनी भारती । तादृशि द्युलोकदेवते हे इळे भूदेवि हे सरस्वति । सरो वागुदकं वा । तद्वत्यंतरिक्षदेवते तादृशि देवि । एताः क्षित्यादिदेवताः । एतास्तिस्र आदित्यप्रभावविशेषरूपा इत्याहुः । यास्तिस्रः सर्वा वो युष्मानुपब्रुवे उपेत्य स्तौमि ता यूयं नोऽस्माञ्छ्रिये संपदे चोदयत । प्रेरयत ॥

> *he bhārati | bharata ādityaḥ | tasya saṃbaṃdhinī bhāratī | tādṛśi dyulokadevate he iḷe bhūdevi he sarasvati | saro vāgudakaṃ vā | tadvatyaṃtarikṣadevate tādṛśi devi | etāḥ kṣityādidevatāḥ | etāstisra ādityaprabhāvaviśeṣarūpā ityāhuḥ | yāstisraḥ sarvā vo yuṣmānupabruve upetya staumi tā yūyaṃ no 'smāñchriye saṃpade codayata | prerayata ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** भारति (*bhārati*) — O deity presiding over the heavenly world; इळे (*iḷe*) — O earth-deity; सरस्वति (*sarasvati*) — O deity of the mid-region; याः (*yāḥ*) — you three deities who are; वः सर्वाः (*vaḥ sarvāḥ*) — all of you;

*(Ṛk 8, Pratipadārtha continues on p. 254.)*

### Printed p. 254 (PDF 273)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188". Ṛk 8, continued.)*

*(Pratipadārtha, continued.)* उपब्रुवे (*upabruve*) — approaching, I praise; ताः (*tāḥ*) — you three deities; नः (*naḥ*) — us; श्रिये (*śriye*) — for obtaining wealth; चोदयत (*codayata*) — urge on.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Bhāratī, Iḷā and Sarasvatī, presiding deities of the three worlds, approaching all of you, I praise you. All of you together, urge us on to obtain wealth.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Bharati, Ila, Saraswati, I invoke you all, that you may direct us to prosperity· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

In this ṛk a group of three deities is addressed and they are prayed to be gracious to the sacrifice. Leaving out the present sūkta and sūkta 1-142, in all the other Āprī sūktas too these deities are put together and designated collectively as तिस्रो देवीः (*tisro devīḥ*). Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī are these three. Concerning what the nature of these deities is, there is much difference of opinion. In 1-142 the deity Bhāratī has the epithets होत्रा (*hotrā*), शुचिः (*śuciḥ*), (मरुत्सु (*marutsu*), देवेषु (*deveṣu*)) अर्पिता (*arpitā*), and the deity Sarasvatī the epithet मही (*mahī*). In some sūktas the word मही (*mahī*) is used not as an epithet but as a synonym of the deity Bhāratī. Whether the nature of these deities can be known definitively in the present context may be examined by taking the statements of Śruti and the rest as authority.

On the subject of तिस्रो देवीः (*tisro devīḥ*), Yāska —

> तिस्रो देवीः । तिस्रो देवीस्तिस्रो देव्यः ॥

> *tisro devīḥ | tisro devīstisro devyaḥ ‖*

— saying only this, in the ṛk he has given as an example —

*(Verse line 1 zoomed: "तूयमेत्विळा".)*

> आ नो यज्ञं भारती तूयमेत्विळा मनुष्वदिह चेतयंती ।
> तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदं स्योनं सरस्वती स्वपसः सदंतु ॥

> *ā no yajñaṃ bhāratī tūyametviḷā manuṣvadiha cetayaṃtī |*
> *tisro devīrbarhiredaṃ syonaṃ sarasvatī svapasaḥ sadaṃtu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-8)

*(Nirukta's explanation zoomed: printed "ऐतु" (for एतु) and "सक-र्माण" (for सुकर्माण); p. 255 prints both correctly.)*

> ऐतु नो यज्ञं भारती क्षिप्रं । भरत आदित्यस्तस्य भा इळा च मनुष्वदिह चेतयमाना तिस्रो देव्यो बर्हिरिदं सुखं सरस्वती च सकर्माण आसीदंतु ॥

> *aitu no yajñaṃ bhāratī kṣipraṃ | bharata ādityastasya bhā iḷā ca manuṣvadiha cetayamānā tisro devyo barhiridaṃ sukhaṃ sarasvatī ca sakarmāṇa āsīdaṃtu ‖*

— so he has explained. That is —

**Bhāratī** — *Bharata* is one among the twelve Ādityas; the radiance of the Āditya is called भा (*bhā*). Therefore Bhāratī means the light of the sun, or the Agni that is in the solar orb in the form of light.

---

### Printed p. 255 (PDF 274)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 9". Ṛk 8, Special Topics continued.)*

**Iḷā** — Iḷā means the earth. मनुष्वत् चेतयंती (*manuṣvat cetayaṃtī*) — having the power that urges on as men do; that is, since she gives food and other nourishment and wealth and the like to the men who are on the earth, Iḷā is a particular form of the Agni that is in the earthly region.

**Sarasvatī** — Since she is the presiding deity of the thunder and lightning that are in the mid-region, Sarasvatī is said to be the form of Agni that is in the mid-region.

Therefore there is a convention of calling the three goddesses Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī the three forms of Agni that are in heaven, the mid-region and on the earth.

If one examines the mantra designating these deities in the Praiṣa sūkta, which collects the chief portions of the Āprī sūktas —

*(Reference and "वियंत्वाजस्य" (ja without ya-subscript, as printed) zoomed, two tries.)*

> होता यक्षत्तिस्रो देवीरपसामपस्तमा अच्छिद्रमद्येदमपस्तन्वतां । देवेभ्यो देवीर्देवमपो वियंत्वाजस्य होतर्यज ॥

> *hotā yakṣattisro devīrapasāmapastamā acchidramadyedamapastanvatāṃ | devebhyo devīrdevamapo viyaṃtvājasya hotaryaja ‖*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-2)

— in the original there is only तिस्रो देवीः (*tisro devīḥ*). In the bhāṣya, explaining this,

> इडा सरस्वती भारतीत्येवंरूपास्तिस्रोऽष्टमप्रयाजदेव्यस्तद्रूपमग्निं दैव्यो होता यजतु ।

> *iḍā sarasvatī bhāratītyevaṃrūpāstisro 'ṣṭamaprayājadevyastadrūpamagniṃ daivyo hotā yajatu |*

— it is said that the three, Iḍā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī, the deities of the eighth prayāja, are deities who reflect Agni. Moreover,

> अपसां अपस्तमाः । कर्मवतीनां मध्येऽतिशयेन कर्मवत्यः ।

> *apasāṃ apastamāḥ | karmavatīnāṃ madhye 'tiśayena karmavatyaḥ |*

— by this epithet it makes known that they are the most excellent among those active in rites. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa,

> तिस्रो देवीर्यजति प्राणो वा अपानो व्यानस्तिस्रो देव्यस्ता एव तत्प्रीणाति ता यजमाने दधाति ।

> *tisro devīryajati prāṇo vā apāno vyānastisro devyastā eva tatprīṇāti tā yajamāne dadhāti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-4)

— thus it states the identity of these three deities with the life-principles called prāṇa, apāna and vyāna. The author of the Nirukta, citing the ṛk 10-110-8 आ नो यज्ञं (*ā no yajñaṃ*), has given its explanation in this way:

*(Ni. reference zoomed, second try.)*

> एतु नो यज्ञं भारती क्षिप्रं । भरत आदित्यस्तस्य भा इळा च मनुष्यवदिह चेतयमाना तिस्रो देव्यः बर्हिरिदं सुखं सरस्वती च सुकर्माण आसीदंतु ।

> *etu no yajñaṃ bhāratī kṣipraṃ | bharata ādityastasya bhā iḷā ca manuṣyavadiha cetayamānā tisro devyaḥ barhiridaṃ sukhaṃ sarasvatī ca sukarmāṇa āsīdaṃtu |*

(Ni. 8-13)

— may the deity who is the radiance of Bharata (the sun), and Iḷā, and Sarasvatī adorn the sacrificial grass. In the Bṛhaddevatā,

> तिस्रस्तु देव्यो याः प्रोक्तास्त्रिस्थानैवेह सा तु वाक् ।
> त्रिविधेनोच्यते नाम्ना ज्योतिःषु त्रिषु वर्तिनी ॥

> *tisrastu devyo yāḥ proktāstristhānaiveha sā tu vāk |*
> *trividhenocyate nāmnā jyotiḥṣu triṣu vartinī ‖*

*(Ṛk 8, Special Topics continue on p. 256.)*

### Printed p. 256 (PDF 275)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188". Ṛk 8, Special Topics continued: the Bṛhaddevatā verses of p. 255, concluded.)*

*(Verses zoomed: "अमू" (no anusvara) as printed; "वाग्स्यै" with [?] as the glyph looks (UNDECIDED); "चैव" read as this font's cai.)*

> अग्निमेवानुगेळा तु मध्यं प्राप्ता सरस्वती ।
> अमू स्थिताधि लोकं तु भारती भवति ह्यसौ ॥
> स्यैषा तु त्रिविधा वाग्स्यै [?] दिवि च व्योम्नि चेह च ।
> व्यस्ता चैव समस्ता च भजत्यग्नीनिमानपि ॥

> *agnimevānugeḷā tu madhyaṃ prāptā sarasvatī |*
> *amū sthitādhi lokaṃ tu bhāratī bhavati hyasau ‖*
> *syaiṣā tu trividhā vāgsyai [?] divi ca vyomni ceha ca |*
> *vyastā caiva samastā ca bhajatyagnīnimānapi ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-12 to 14) *(zoomed)*

तिस्रो देव्यः (*tisro devyaḥ*) means the presiding deities of speech that are in the three worlds. (The three forms of speech are explained in Bṛ. De. 2-72 to 82 ślokas *(zoomed; the abbreviation is printed "Bṛ. Pe.")*.)

> अयं प्रयोगस्त्वेतेषां ज्योतिषां त्रिषु वर्तताम् ।

> *ayaṃ prayogastveteṣāṃ jyotiṣāṃ triṣu vartatām |*

(Bṛ. De. 1-90) *(abbreviation printed "Ḍe."; zoomed, second try)*

— as it is said there, the different deities that are in the three worlds are transformations of the one presiding deity of speech. Among them Iḷā has followed the terrestrial Agni; Sarasvatī has passed through the middle world, and Bhāratī is one who stands in the heavenly world. Even so,

> देव्यस्तिस्रः श्रिताश्चैनं त्वष्टा चैवैतदाश्रयः ।

> *devyastisraḥ śritāścainaṃ tvaṣṭā caivaitadāśrayaḥ |*

(Bṛ. De. 1-108) *(zoomed)*

— as stated in this sentence, the deities of these three worlds too serve the terrestrial Agni alone; thus at the end it has concluded everything with reference to Agni.

> इळा सरस्वती मही तिस्रो देवीर्मयोभुवः । बर्हिः सीदंत्वस्रिधः ॥

> *iḷā sarasvatī mahī tisro devīrmayobhuvaḥ | barhiḥ sīdaṃtvasridhaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-9) *(zoomed)*

— in this ṛk, and also in Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-5-8 *(zoomed, three tries)*, which has the same wording, there is no mention of Bhāratī; therefore Sāyaṇa has said that मही (*mahī*) is a synonym of the deity Bhāratī. In the present ṛk and also in

> भारती पवमानस्य सरस्वतीळा मही ।
> इमं नो यज्ञमा गमंतिस्रो देवीः सुपेशसः ॥

> *bhāratī pavamānasya sarasvatīḷā mahī |*
> *imaṃ no yajñamā gamaṃtisro devīḥ supeśasaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5-8) *(zoomed)*

— in this ṛk too it is an epithet.

**Iḷā** — because in the Bṛhaddevatā it is said अग्निमेवानुगेळा (*agnimevānugeḷā*) (3-13) *(zoomed, second try)*, that Iḷā followed the terrestrial Agni, and also because of

> प्र दीधितिर्विश्ववारा जिगाति होतारमिळः प्रथमं यजध्यै ।
> अच्छा नमोभिर्वृषभं वंदध्यै स देवान्यक्षदिषितो यजीयान् ।

> *pra dīdhitirviśvavārā jigāti hotāramiḷaḥ prathamaṃ yajadhyai |*
> *acchā namobhirvṛṣabhaṃ vaṃdadhyai sa devānyakṣadiṣito yajīyān |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-3) *(zoomed)*

*(Ṛk 8, Special Topics continue on p. 257.)*

### Printed p. 257 (PDF 276)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 9". Ṛk 8, Special Topics continued.)*

— because in this ṛk the word *iḷe* (Iḷā) has been explained as food in the form of havis, and because in ṛk 7-16-8 *(zoomed)* there is the epithet घृतहस्ता (*ghṛtahastā*) and in 10-70-8 *(read from the strip)* the epithet घृतपदी (*ghṛtapadī*), it appears that Iḷā may be taken to mean havis. Probably for this reason,

> उत्तानायामव भरा चिकित्वान्त्सद्यः प्रवीता वृषणं जजान ।
> अरुषस्तूपो रुशदस्य पाज इळायास्पुत्रो वयुनेऽजनिष्ट ॥

> *uttānāyāmava bharā cikitvāntsadyaḥ pravītā vṛṣaṇaṃ jajāna |*
> *aruṣastūpo ruśadasya pāja iḷāyāsputro vayune 'janiṣṭa ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-29-3) *(zoomed)*

— in this ṛk he (Agni) is called the son of Iḷā.

**Bhāratī** — in the Nirukta it is said to be the radiance of the Āditya (भरतः आदित्यः तस्य भाः (*bharataḥ ādityaḥ tasya bhāḥ*)). The scholar Macdonell, in his book Vedic Mythology, has taken it as the havis offered by those of the Bharata lineage (p. 87), and Grassmann as the goddess of speech. Or it may be taken as related to Agni.

> तस्मा अग्निर्भारतः शर्म यंसज्ज्योक्पश्यात्सूर्यमुच्चरंतं ।
> य इंद्राय सुनवामेत्याह नरे नर्याय नृतमाय नृणां ।

> *tasmā agnirbhārataḥ śarma yaṃsajjyokpaśyātsūryamuccaraṃtaṃ |*
> *ya iṃdrāya sunavāmetyāha nare naryāya nṛtamāya nṛṇāṃ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-25-4) *(zoomed)*

— since in this ṛk भारतः (*bhārataḥ*) is an epithet of Agni, the deity related to him may be named Bhāratī; this is the opinion of some others.

**Sarasvatī** — सर इत्युदकनाम । तद्वतीस्तनितादिरूपा माध्यमिका च वाक् (*sara ityudakanāma | tadvatīstanitādirūpā mādhyamikā ca vāk*) — the word *sara* means water. Sāyaṇa has explained her as a transformation of the goddess of speech in the mid-region, who has water and has sound such as thunder. Some hold that Sarasvatī is a river of divine nature. Or, because it is said देव्यस्तिस्रः श्रिताश्चैनं (*devyastisraḥ śritāścainaṃ*) (Bṛ. De. 1-108) *(read from the strip; zoom missed twice)* — that these three have resorted to Agni; because Agni is in three forms in the earth, the mid-region and the heavenly world; because Bhāratī is said to be the radiance of the sun; because Sarasvatī is said to be the deity of thunder and lightning; and because Iḷā too has a direct connection with Agni — some hold that these three are transformations of Agni. That in the explanation of the Praiṣa sūkta it is said तद्रूपमग्निं (*tadrūpamagniṃ*) has been stated above.

Since Sarasvatī is described in many places as the presiding deity of thunder and lightning, this Sarasvatī is the form of Agni that is in the mid-region. Since the goddess Iḷā gives wealth and the like and long life to the creatures (people) on the earth, this deity is the form of Agni that is on the earth — this is the significance of Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī. The ṛṣis have praised these three deities that they should come to the sacrificial altar and sit on the strewn barhis (the spread darbha grass).

*(Foot of page: signature "[17]" and "Vol. 14". Ṛk 8, Special Topics continue on p. 258.)*
