### Printed p. 258 (PDF 277)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188". Ṛk 8, Special Topics continued.)*

We give some examples in which the ṛṣis have praised Sarasvatī, conceiving her as a deity other than the river.

(1)

> तान्पूर्वया निविदा हूमहे वयं भगं मित्रमदितिं दक्षमस्रिधं ।
> अर्यमणं वरुणं सोममश्विना सरस्वती नः सुभगा मयस्करत् ।

> *tānpūrvayā nividā hūmahe vayaṃ bhagaṃ mitramaditiṃ dakṣamasridhaṃ |*
> *aryamaṇaṃ varuṇaṃ somamaśvinā sarasvatī naḥ subhagā mayaskarat |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-89-3) *(zoomed, three tries)*

In this ṛk Sarasvatī is the goddess of speech, or the presiding deity of thunder and lightning.

(2)

> सरस्वति त्वमस्माँ अविड्ढि मरुत्वती धृषती जेषि शत्रून् ।

> *sarasvati tvamasmā~ aviḍḍhi marutvatī dhṛṣatī jeṣi śatrūn |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-30-8) *(zoomed, two tries)*

(3)

> सरस्वती शृणवन् यज्ञियासो धाता रयिं सहवीरं तुरासः ।

> *sarasvatī śṛṇavan yajñiyāso dhātā rayiṃ sahavīraṃ turāsaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-54-13) *(zoomed, three tries)*

In these ṛks Sarasvatī has been conceived either as a river or as the presiding deity of thunder and lightning.

(4) *(First word "पमूनसो" as printed; zoomed.)*

> पमूनसो अपसो ये सुहस्ता वृष्णः पत्नीर्नद्यो विभ्वतष्टाः ।
> सरस्वती बृहद्दिवोत राका दशस्यंतीर्वरिवस्यंतु शुभ्राः ।

> *pamūnaso apaso ye suhastā vṛṣṇaḥ patnīrnadyo vibhvataṣṭāḥ |*
> *sarasvatī bṛhaddivota rākā daśasyaṃtīrvarivasyaṃtu śubhrāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-42-12) *(zoomed)*

(5)

> आ नो दिवो बृहतः पर्वतादा सरस्वती यजता गंतु यज्ञं ।

> *ā no divo bṛhataḥ parvatādā sarasvatī yajatā gaṃtu yajñaṃ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-43-11) *(zoomed)*

(6)

> उभा नासत्या रुद्रो अध ग्नाः पूषा भगः सरस्वती जुषंत ।

> *ubhā nāsatyā rudro adha gnāḥ pūṣā bhagaḥ sarasvatī juṣaṃta |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-46-2) *(zoomed)*

In these three ṛks too Sarasvatī is the presiding deity of thunder and lightning. Griffith is of the opinion that of these three ṛks, in the first Sarasvatī appears as a river, either the Sindhu or the Sarasvatī, and in the 2nd–3rd ṛks *(zoomed)* as a deity. K. C. Chattopadhyaya says that the 1st–2nd ṛks apply to the river Sindhu. These three ṛks are all uttered by those of the lineage of the ṛṣi Atri. Of the first ṛk the ṛṣi is Atri or Bhauma, the son of Atri; of the second Atri; and of the third Pratikṣatra, of Atri's lineage. In the second ṛk Sarasvatī is invoked from heaven (दिवः (*divaḥ*)) and from the cloud region (पर्वतादा (*parvatādā*)). In the first ṛk, since the word पत्नीः (*patnīḥ*) is present, the bhāṣyakāra has conceived Sarasvatī and the other rivers as the wives of Indra.

(7)

> अग्निरिंद्रो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा वायुः पूषा सरस्वती सजोषसः ।

Here it is fitting to call Sarasvatī the goddess of speech itself.

We shall explain briefly, as far as is known, the question of where the river Sarasvatī flowed at that time. This explanation is written following the works (1) R. D. Oldham in Journal of Asiatic Society Bengal 1886 page 322 (2) C. F. Oldham, Journal of Royal Asiatic Society 1893, page 51 (3) Maps of the Cambridge History of India Vol. I. Ancient India (4) Maps of Punjab published by the Surveyor-Genleral [sic] of India (5) Ancient India as describd [sic] by Magastheneses [sic] and Arrian *(the English titles as printed)*. The river Sarasvatī was at that time a large river. Rising in the Sirmūr (printed "(Sismur)") range in the Himālaya mountains, it flows from there somewhat to the west and to the south. At its source five small streams (small brooks in which water flows) may have joined to flow on as this river; therefore it must have got the name पंचाजाता (*paṃcājātā*) *(as printed)*. After it has flowed a short distance, the river named Dṛṣadvatī (the modren [sic] Chitrang) comes flowing from the east and joins it. The Āpayā is a tributary of the Dṛṣadvatī. The Sarasvatī of that time was to the south of the present river Sarasuti. (Rivers that flow in desert lands often change their beds.) The small rivers named Mārkaṇḍā (Markand) and Gaggar (Ghaggar) join the present river Sarasuti. Afterwards the Sarasvatī flows in the southern and western directions and at last joins the sea. The bed of the dried-up river named the present Hākra (Hakra) must have been the bed of the Sarasvatī river of that time. It may have joined the river named (Sutlej) of today and merged in the river Sindhu, or it may have gone straight and joined the river Sindhu itself. At that time the river Sindhu was much further to the east than it is now, and it joined the sea near the gulf named (Rann of Kach). The scholar Max Muller (Max Muller), on the basis of the word आसमुद्रात् (*āsamudrāt*) said in ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-95-2 *(zoomed, two tries)*, holds the opinion that this river Sarasvatī went straight and joined the sea. Since this river, before joining the sea, flowed in the region of the desert,

*(Ṛk 8, Special Topics continue on p. 260.)*

### Printed p. 260 (PDF 279)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188". Ṛk 8, Special Topics concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; end of Ṛk 8; Ṛk 9 begins.)*

*(Special Topics, continued.)* … the river may have sunk away (dried up) in the desert before joining the sea (See Muir's Sanskrit Texts Vol· II page 393) *(as printed)*. The account of the river sinking away in the desert in this manner is given in the Mahābhārata too (Vanaparva — the description of the tīrtha-yātrā) and in the Manusaṃhitā (1-21) *(so printed; zoomed)*. For all these reasons it may be said that the present river Sarasuti itself must have been the former river Sarasvatī.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly).* भारति (*bhārati*) — being included in the *śārṅgaravādi* group, the suffix ञीन् (*ñīn*) by शार्ङ्गरवादिभ्यो ञीन् (*śārṅgaravādibhyo ñīn*) *(so the sūtra name reads in the print)* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-73) *(zoomed, two tries)*; standing at the beginning of the pāda, it takes no vocative nighāta; initial udātta by आमंत्रितस्य (*āmaṃtritasya*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198) *(zoomed, two tries)*. इळे (*iḷe*) — by आमंत्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवत् (*āmaṃtritaṃ pūrvamavidyamānavat*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-72) *(zoomed, two tries)* the preceding vocative counts as non-existent, so the word is not treated as following a pada and is not wholly anudātta; initial udātta as before; for the following सरस्वति (*sarasvati*) too both preceding words count as absent, so it too has initial udātta by the former sūtra. उपब्रुवे (*upabruve*) — root ब्रूञ् व्यक्तायां वाचि (*brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*); *laṭ*, *uttama-puruṣa* singular; nighāta barred by यद्वृत्तान्नित्यम् (*yadvṛttānnityam*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66) *(zoomed)*, so antodātta by the suffix accent; the gati उप (*upa*) wholly anudātta by तिङ्ङ् चोदात्तवति (*tiṅṅ codāttavati*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71) *(zoomed)*. चोदयत (*codayata*) — root चुद प्रेरणे (*cuda preraṇe*); *loṭ*, *madhyama-puruṣa* plural; nighāta of a finite verb, standing after a non-finite word. श्रिये (*śriye*) — dative singular; udātta on the case-ending by सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिः (*sāvekācastṛtīyādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168) *(zoomed, two tries)*.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Tvaṣṭṛ, deity of the sacrificial vessels, is able to give form to the seed laid in the womb (so Śruti); he has made all our cattle distinct; directly addressed: bring about their increase for us.

> त्वष्टा यज्ञसाधनपात्राभिमानी देवो रूपाणि योनौ सृष्टानि रेतांसि रूपाणि कर्तुं प्रभुर्हि । हिशब्दः श्रुत्यंतरप्रसिद्धिद्योतनार्थः । यावच्छो वै रेतसः सिक्तस्य त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोति । तै. सं. १-५-९-१ । इति श्रुतेः । स देवो विश्वान् सर्वानपि पशूनस्मदीयान् गवादिकान् समानजे । सम्यगनक्ति । व्यक्तीकरोति ॥ संपूर्वादनक्तेर्लिटि तस्मान्नुडिति नुट् ॥ अथ प्रत्यक्षः । तेषामुक्तानां पशूनां स्फातिं वृद्धिं नोऽस्मदर्थमा यज । सर्वतः पूजय । कुर्वित्यर्थः ॥

> *tvaṣṭā yajñasādhanapātrābhimānī devo rūpāṇi yonau sṛṣṭāni retāṃsi rūpāṇi kartuṃ prabhurhi | hiśabdaḥ śrutyaṃtaraprasiddhidyotanārthaḥ | yāvaccho vai retasaḥ siktasya tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi vikaroti | tai. saṃ. 1-5-9-1 | iti śruteḥ | sa devo viśvān sarvānapi paśūnasmadīyān gavādikān samānaje | samyaganakti | vyaktīkaroti ‖ saṃpūrvādanakterliṭi tasmānnuḍiti nuṭ ‖ atha pratyakṣaḥ | teṣāmuktānāṃ paśūnāṃ sphātiṃ vṛddhiṃ no 'smadarthamā yaja | sarvataḥ pūjaya | kurvityarthaḥ ‖*


*(Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-9-1 and "यावच्छो वै" zoomed (1000 dpi, three tries). "पूजय" is printed with a stray mark under the प; "तस्मान्नुडिति नुट्" as printed.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*) — Tvaṣṭṛ; रूपाणि (*rūpāṇi*) — to give forms to the created seeds and perfect them; प्रभुः हि (*prabhuḥ hi*) — is able; (he) विश्वान् पशून् (*viśvān paśūn*) — all the cattle and the like belonging to us; समानजे (*samānaje*) — perfected, giving them individual form; (O Tvaṣṭṛ!) तेषां (*teṣāṃ*) — of those cattle and the like; स्फातिं (*sphātiṃ*) — increase; नः (*naḥ*) — for us; आ यज (*ā yaja*) — make.

**Bhāvārtha.** Tvaṣṭṛ is able to give forms to the created seeds and perfect them. He has perfected all the cattle and the like belonging to us, giving them individual form. O Tvaṣṭṛ, creating those cattle and the like for us, increase their number.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Twashtri, who is the master (in fashioning) the forms (of beings), has made all animals distinct; grant us, (Twashtri), their increase· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**Tvaṣṭā** — Yāska's explanation:

> त्वष्टा । त्वष्टा तूर्णमश्नुत इति नैरुक्ताः । त्विषेर्वा स्याद्दीप्तिकर्मणस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात्करोतिकर्मणः ॥ माध्यमिकस्त्वष्टेत्याहुर्मध्यमे च स्थाने समाम्नातः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥

> *tvaṣṭā | tvaṣṭā tūrṇamaśnuta iti nairuktāḥ | tviṣervā syāddīptikarmaṇastvakṣatervā syātkarotikarmaṇaḥ ‖ mādhyamikastvaṣṭetyāhurmadhyame ca sthāne samāmnātaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*

(Ni. 8-14) *(zoomed, two tries)*

That is, the Nairuktas say the word *tvaṣṭā* means one who pervades quickly, or one who is shining, or one who does works (works of craft); some say he is the *mādhyamika*, that is, one who is in the middle between heaven and earth; Śākapūṇi says he is Agni.

### Printed p. 262 (PDF 281)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188" ("Sū" without its dot). Ṛk 9, Special Topics continued.)*

Some also say that Tvaṣṭṛ, like Viśvakarman, is the craftsman of the gods. For in the ṛk Yāska has given as an example,

> य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भुवनानि विश्वा ।
> तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान् देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् ॥

> *ya ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpairapiṃśadbhuvanāni viśvā |*
> *tamadya hotariṣito yajīyān devaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yakṣi vidvān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-9) *(zoomed, three tries)*

— it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ is the maker of heaven and earth and the causal agent of the form, beauty, growth, increase and the like suited to each of the creatures in all the worlds. Besides this, Śruti (Yajurveda) sentences such as त्वष्टा वै पशूनां मिथुनानां रूपकृत् (*tvaṣṭā vai paśūnāṃ mithunānāṃ rūpakṛt*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-8-5) *(zoomed, 600 and 1000 dpi)*, त्वष्टा रूपाणामधिपतिः (*tvaṣṭā rūpāṇāmadhipatiḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-3) *(so printed; zoomed)*, त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोति (*tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi vikaroti*) set forth Tvaṣṭṛ's skill in fashioning things. And

> मह्यं त्वष्टा वज्रमतक्षदायसं मयि देवासोऽवृजन्नपि क्रतुं ॥

> *mahyaṃ tvaṣṭā vajramatakṣadāyasaṃ mayi devāso 'vṛjannapi kratuṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-48-3) *(zoomed)*

— Indra has said that Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for him the vajra weapon of steel. That he has made and given to the deities the materials of sacrifice they need and many other things is said in many mantras of the Ṛgveda.

Tvaṣṭṛ is well known as one of the twelve Ādityas. For that very reason Yāska has explained the meaning as "one who is shining".

Among the Śruti sentences that convey individual views about the deity Tvaṣṭṛ, the ones cited below indicate only the deity connected with the Āprī sūktas.

*(Praiṣa read with a zoom: "अचिष्टुम्" and "सुपोषः पोषैः" as they look.)*

> होता यक्षत्त्वष्टारमचिष्टुमपाकग्ं रेतोधां विश्रवसं यशोधां ।
> पुरुरूपमकामकर्शनग्ं सुपोषः पोषैः स्यात्सुवीरो वीरैर्वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ।

> *hotā yakṣattvaṣṭāramaciṣṭumapākagṃ retodhāṃ viśravasaṃ yaśodhāṃ |*
> *pururūpamakāmakarśanagṃ supoṣaḥ poṣaiḥ syātsuvīro vīrairvetvājyasya hotaryaja |*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-2) *(zoomed, 600 and 1000 dpi)*

In this mantra there are the epithets अचिष्टुं (*aciṣṭuṃ*), अपाकं (*apākaṃ*), रेतोधां (*retodhāṃ*), विश्रवसं (*viśravasaṃ*), यशोधां (*yaśodhāṃ*), पुरुरूपं (*pururūpaṃ*), अकामकर्शनं (*akāmakarśanaṃ*). Among these —

**अचिष्टं (*aciṣṭaṃ*)** *(so printed in this heading, beside "अचिष्टुं" in the list; zoomed)* — that is, चेष्टनरहितं, चांचल्यरहितं, स्थिरं (*ceṣṭanarahitaṃ, cāṃcalyarahitaṃ, sthiraṃ*): one who is not restless but remains steady;

**अपाकं (*apākaṃ*)** — that is, अबालं, प्राज्ञं (*abālaṃ, prājñaṃ*): one who is not a child but wise;

### Printed p. 263 (PDF 282)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 9". Ṛk 9, Special Topics continued.)*

**रेतोधां (*retodhāṃ*)** — for this, पुत्रादिबीजस्य यजमाने धारयितारं (*putrādibījasya yajamāne dhārayitāraṃ*): one who sows in the sacrificer the seed of sons and the like;

**विश्रवसं (*viśravasaṃ*)** — for this, विविधकीर्तियुक्तं (*vividhakīrtiyuktaṃ*): one endowed with fame of many kinds;

**यशोधां (*yaśodhāṃ*)** — that is, यजमाने यशसः धारयितारं (*yajamāne yaśasaḥ dhārayitāraṃ*): one who makes the sacrificer a sharer of glory;

**पुरुरूपं (*pururūpaṃ*)** — for this, बहुरूपं (*bahurūpaṃ*): one having forms of many kinds;

**अकामकर्शनं (*akāmakarśanaṃ*)** — that is, कामानां अनाशयितारं (*kāmānāṃ anāśayitāraṃ*): one who fulfils the desired objects of the sacrificer — so it is explained.

These epithets make known the individual nature of Tvaṣṭṛ. The author of the Nirukta, showing the derivation of the word *tvaṣṭṛ* (8-14) *(zoomed)* —

*("दीप्तिकमणस्" without the repha, as printed.)*

> त्वष्टा तूर्णमश्नुत इति नैरुक्ताः । त्विषेर्वा स्याद्दीप्तिकमणस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात् करोतिकर्मणः ।

> *tvaṣṭā tūrṇamaśnuta iti nairuktāḥ | tviṣervā syāddīptikamaṇastvakṣatervā syāt karotikarmaṇaḥ |*

— has said that the word may be formed according to the Nairuktas' view that the name is from pervading quickly, or from the root त्विष् (*tviṣ*) meaning "to shine", or from the root त्वक्ष् (*tvakṣ*) with the sense of making. By these derivations Tvaṣṭṛ means one who pervades quickly, one who shines, and one who fashions. To show to which world this deity belongs —

> माध्यमिकस्त्वष्टेत्याहुर्मध्यमे च स्थाने समाम्नातः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ।

> *mādhyamikastvaṣṭetyāhurmadhyame ca sthāne samāmnātaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ |*

— he has made known the views that some say he belongs to the group of deities of the mid-region, and Śākapūṇi that he is Agni. In the Bṛhaddevatā, approving the first view,

*(Verse zoomed: "सूक्तं स्य तेन" as printed.)*

> त्वष्टा रूपविकर्ता च योऽसौ माध्यमिके गणे ।
> स्तुतः स च निपातेन सूक्तं स्य तेन विद्यते ।

> *tvaṣṭā rūpavikartā ca yo 'sau mādhyamike gaṇe |*
> *stutaḥ sa ca nipātena sūktaṃ sya tena vidyate |*

(Bṛ. De. 3-[?]) *(UNDECIDED: after "3-" a round 2-like loop fused with a 5-like glyph with a dot above; zoomed at 500 and 1000 dpi)*

— in this śloka it is said that he belongs to the group of deities of the middle world. Before this,

*(Verses zoomed: "वर्चः" as it looks, "यन्मथु" as printed.)*

> त्वष्टा तु यस्त्वयमेव पार्थिवोऽग्निरिति स्तुतिः ।
> पार्थिवस्यास्य वर्चः स्युः कस्याप्यृक् चार्तवेषु च ॥
> त्विषितस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात् तूर्णमश्नुत एव वा ।
> कर्मसूत्पारणो वेति तेन नाम्नैतदश्नुते ॥
> यः सहस्रतमो रश्मी रवेश्चंद्रमुपाश्रितः ।
> सोऽपि त्वष्टारमेवाग्निं परं चेह च यन्मथु ॥

> *tvaṣṭā tu yastvayameva pārthivo 'gniriti stutiḥ |*
> *pārthivasyāsya varcaḥ syuḥ kasyāpyṛk cārtaveṣu ca ‖*
> *tviṣitastvakṣatervā syāt tūrṇamaśnuta eva vā |*
> *karmasūtpāraṇo veti tena nāmnaitadaśnute ‖*
> *yaḥ sahasratamo raśmī raveścaṃdramupāśritaḥ |*
> *so 'pi tvaṣṭāramevāgniṃ paraṃ ceha ca yanmathu ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-25 to 16) *(zoomed)*

— there are indications in some places that the praise belonging to the terrestrial Agni is itself addressed to Tvaṣṭṛ too, and that he is a deity connected with the earth. In the sūktas concerning the seasons too he is described as a portion of Agni.

### Printed p. 264 (PDF 283)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188". Ṛk 9, Special Topics continued.)*

— in these verses the very derivation of the word *tvaṣṭṛ* found in the Nirukta is then given. It is also described that, just as the thousandth ray of the sun which pervades the moon pervades the *madhu*, the other world and the earth, so it is in Tvaṣṭṛ too *(the Kannada reads the printed "यन्मथु" as madhu)*. Chiefly, the author of the Bṛhaddevatā has approved in this matter the view of Śākapūṇi stated in the Nirukta. In the Nighaṇṭu Tvaṣṭṛ is placed first together with the Āprī deities (5-2), then with the deities of the mid-region (5-5), and first among the deities of the heavenly world (5-6) *(all three zoomed)*.

The story of Tvaṣṭṛ and the ṛṣi Dadhīci has been told in the Special Topics of sūkta 1-139 *(so printed; zoomed, three tries)*. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa,

*(Zoomed at 800 dpi: after "त्वाष्टि" the next word has lost its base letter; only a ra-subscript and the ī-sign with anusvara are printed.)*

> त्वष्टारं यजति वाग्वै त्वष्टा वाग्घीदं सर्वं । त्वाष्टि [?] वाचमेव तत्प्रीणाति वाचं यजमाने दधाति ।

> *tvaṣṭāraṃ yajati vāgvai tvaṣṭā vāgghīdaṃ sarvaṃ | tvāṣṭi [?] vācameva tatprīṇāti vācaṃ yajamāne dadhāti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-4) *(zoomed)*

— by this sentence the identity of Tvaṣṭṛ with speech has been stated; this too is one view.

> य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भुवनानि विश्वा ।
> तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान् देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् ।

> *ya ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpairapiṃśadbhuvanāni viśvā |*
> *tamadya hotariṣito yajīyān devaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yakṣi vidvān |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-9) *(zoomed)*

— in this ṛk he is praised as having a divine birth, and therefore as showing his primacy even at the times of creation. The view that Tvaṣṭṛ is most ancient —

> इह त्वष्टारमग्रियं विश्वरूपमुपह्वये । अस्माकमस्तु केवलः ॥

> *iha tvaṣṭāramagriyaṃ viśvarūpamupahvaye | asmākamastu kevalaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-10) *(zoomed, two tries)*

> त्वष्टारमग्रजां गोपां पुरोयावानमा हुवे ।
> इंदुरिंद्रो वृषा हरिः पवमानः प्रजापतिः ॥

> *tvaṣṭāramagrajāṃ gopāṃ puroyāvānamā huve |*
> *iṃduriṃdro vṛṣā hariḥ pavamānaḥ prajāpatiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5-9) *(zoomed, two tries)*

— is made known in ṛks such as these by the epithets अग्रिय (*agriya*) and अग्रज (*agraja*) *(so printed)*.

> त्वष्टा रूपाणि हि प्रभुः पशून्विश्वान्त्समानजे । तेषां नः स्फातिमा यज ।

> *tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi hi prabhuḥ paśūnviśvāntsamānaje | teṣāṃ naḥ sphātimā yaja |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188-9) *(zoomed, two tries)*

> त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोति ।

> *tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi vikaroti |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-9-2) *(zoomed, two tries)*

— sentences such as these praise Tvaṣṭṛ's work of fashioning. Moreover, he has the epithet *viśvarūpa* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-10) *(zoomed)*.

### Printed p. 265 (PDF 284)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 9". Ṛk 9: the Special Topics ended on p. 264; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; end of Ṛk 9; Ṛk 10 begins.)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly).* समानजे (*samānaje*) — prefix सम् (*sam*); root अंजू व्यक्तिम्रक्षणकांतिगतिषु (*aṃjū vyaktimrakṣaṇakāṃtigatiṣu*); *liṭ* in Vedic usage; ए (*e*) for त (*ta*) by लिटस्तझयोरेशिरेच् (*liṭastajhayoreśirec*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-81) *(zoomed)*; loss of *n*, the suffix being treated as *kit*; on reduplication, the augment नुट् (*nuṭ*) by तस्मान्नुट् द्विहलः (*tasmānnuṭ dvihalaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-71) *(zoomed)*; nighāta barred by हि च (*hi ca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-34) *(zoomed)*, so antodātta by the suffix accent; अनुदात्त for सम् (*sam*) by तिङ्ङ् चोदात्तवति (*tiṅṅ codāttavati*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71) *(zoomed)*. स्फातिम् (*sphātim*) — root स्फायी वृद्धौ (*sphāyī vṛddhau*); suffix क्तिच् (*ktic*) by क्तिच्क्तौ च— (*kticktau ca—*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-174) *(zoomed, two tries)*; loss of *ya* by लोपो व्योः— (*lopo vyoḥ—*); antodātta, being *cit*. यज (*yaja*) — root यज देवपूजादिषु (*yaja devapūjādiṣu*); *loṭ*, *madhyama-puruṣa* singular; nighāta of a finite verb.

*(Rule with ":o:" — end of Ṛk 9.)*

#### Ṛk 10

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Ṛk numeral zoomed.)*

> उप त्मन्या वनस्पते पाथो देवेभ्यः सृज ।
> अग्निर्हव्यानि सिष्वदत् ॥ १० ॥

> *upa tmanyā vanaspate pātho devebhyaḥ sṛja |*
> *agnirhavyāni siṣvadat ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उप । त्मन्या । वनस्पते । पाथः । देवेभ्यः । सृज ।
> अग्निः । हव्यानि । सिस्वदत् ॥ १० ॥

> *upa | tmanyā | vanaspate | pāthaḥ | devebhyaḥ | sṛja |*
> *agniḥ | havyāni | sisvadat ‖ 10 ‖*

*(Pada "सिस्वदत्" (dental s) beside Saṃhitā "सिष्वदत्", as printed.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* O Vanaspati, deity of the sacrificial post, of yourself send forth food in the form of the animal to the gods (without the post no animal is bound, so no oblation); then may Agni sweeten the oblations.

*(Bhāṣya "त्मन्यात्मन्यैव" as printed; zoomed.)*

> हे वनस्पते यूपाभिमानि देव त्मन्यात्मन्यैव देवेभ्योऽग्न्यादिभ्यः पाथः पशुरूपमन्नमुप सृज । उत्पादय । यूपाभावे पशुनियोजनाभावेन हविषोऽभावात् । त्वय्येवं कृतवति सत्यग्निर्हव्यानि हवींषि सिष्वदत् । स्वदयतु । स्वादूकरोतु ॥

> *he vanaspate yūpābhimāni deva tmanyātmanyaiva devebhyo 'gnyādibhyaḥ pāthaḥ paśurūpamannamupa sṛja | utpādaya | yūpābhāve paśuniyojanābhāvena haviṣo 'bhāvāt | tvayyevaṃ kṛtavati satyagnirhavyāni havīṃṣi siṣvadat | svadayatu | svādūkarotu ‖*


**Pratipadārtha.** वनस्पते (*vanaspate*) — O deity presiding over the sacrificial post; त्मन्या (*tmanyā*) — by your own nature; देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*) — for the deities Agni and the rest; पाथः (*pāthaḥ*) — food in the form of the animal; उप सृज (*upa sṛja*) — create; (then) अग्निः (*agniḥ*) — Agni; हव्यानि (*havyāni*) — the oblations; सिस्वदत् (*sisvadat*) — may he taste *(headword with dental s, as printed)*.

*(Ṛk 10, Bhāvārtha follows on p. 266.)*

### Printed p. 266 (PDF 285)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188". Ṛk 10: Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

**Bhāvārtha.** O deity presiding over the sacrificial post, by your own nature create food in the form of the animal for the deities Agni and the rest. Then may Agni taste the oblations.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Vanaspati, deliver of yourself the victim to the gods, so that Agni may taste the oblation· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**Vanaspate** — Yāska's explanation of the word *vanaspati*:

*(Ni. 8-3 and 8-18 zoomed; "इत्येनमाह्यैष (*ityenamāhyaiṣa*)" (ha with ya-subscript) and "कात्थक्यः (*kātthakyaḥ*)" as printed.)*

> वनस्पत इत्येनमाह्यैष हि वनानां पाता वा पालयिता वा । वनं वनोतेः ॥

> *vanaspata ityenamāhyaiṣa hi vanānāṃ pātā vā pālayitā vā | vanaṃ vanoteḥ ‖*

(Ni. 8-3)

> तत्को वनस्पतिः । यूप इति कात्थक्यः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥

> *tatko vanaspatiḥ | yūpa iti kātthakyaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*

(Ni. 8-18)

That is, they call Agni himself Vanaspati. For Agni is the protector or the guardian of the forests. Though Agni is contained within the tree, since he does not burn it he is called its guardian. Or else, because (the wood) is useful for the means of sacrifice such as the wooden vessels, it has the name *vana*. *Vanaspati* means the king of trees, a great tree. Who is the deity called Vanaspati? The opinion of Kātthakya is that it is the wooden pillar set up in the sacrifice for tying the animal. The opinion of Śākapūṇi is that Vanaspati means Agni.

To support Kātthakya's opinion Yāska has given a ṛk as an example —

> अंजंति त्वामध्वरे देवयंतो वनस्पते मधुना दैव्येन ॥

> *aṃjaṃti tvāmadhvare devayaṃto vanaspate madhunā daivyena ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-1) *(zoomed)*

That is, "O Vanaspati (O sacrificial pillar), in the sacrifice the ṛtviks and the sacrificer anoint you with ghee (*tuppa*) consecrated by mantras" — so the pillar to which the animal is tied is addressed. And in the 3rd, 6th and 11th *(zoomed)* ṛks of this same sūkta too, besides Vanaspati being addressed as the sacrificial pillar, it is well known that the pillar itself is the deity of this sūkta. In the eleventh ṛk of this sūkta — "वनस्पते शतवल्शो विरोह सहस्रवल्शा वि वयं रुहेम (*vanaspate śatavalśo viroha sahasravalśā vi vayaṃ ruhema*)" *(so printed)*, that is, "O Vanaspati, grow with shoots in hundreds and thousands (of places)" — what is said fits the tree that is Vanaspati. In the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-70-10 *(zoomed)*, "वनस्पते रशनया नियूय (*vanaspate raśanayā niyūya*)" — "O Vanaspati, tie (the animal) with the rope that ties the animal" — what is said confirms the meaning 'sacrificial pillar' for the word *vanaspati*. Therefore the meaning of *vanaspati* is the sacrificial pillar itself; 'Agni' is the indirect (*parokṣa*) meaning.

### Printed p. 267 (PDF 286)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 9" (zoomed). Ṛk 10, Special Topics continued.)*

The nature of **Vanaspati** must be known by much enquiry. On the basis of this word some modern Western scholars have come to the conclusion that in the Vedic period the animal sacrifice involving killing was predominant, and that the Āprī sūktas are prayāja mantras connected with such a sacrifice.

Looked at from a gross point of view, **Vanaspati** means the sacrificial pillar to which the sacrificial animal is tied. But on the question whether it is or is not the very pillar to which the sacrificial animal is tied, one may first note the Śruti statements and then, on their basis, determine the nature of **Vanaspati**.

In the Praiṣa-sūkta:

*(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-2 zoomed; "जोष्टारग्ं" (ṭa) as printed; the line-end "स्वदात्स्व-" has a stray mark (zoomed).)*

> होता यक्षद्वनस्पतिमुपावस्रक्षद्धियो जोष्टारग्ं शशमं नरः । स्वदात्स्वधितिर्ऋतुथाद्य देवो देवेभ्यो हव्यावाड्वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ।

> *hotā yakṣadvanaspatimupāvasrakṣaddhiyo joṣṭāragṃ śaśamaṃ naraḥ | svadātsvadhitirṛtuthādya devo devebhyo havyāvāḍvetvājyasya hotaryaja |*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-2)

The bhāṣya on this mantra is as follows. **वनस्पतिं यूपाधारभूतं दशमप्रयाजदेवतात्मकमग्निं दैव्यो होता यजतु (*vanaspatiṃ yūpādhārabhūtaṃ daśamaprayājadevatātmakamagniṃ daivyo hotā yajatu*)** — may the divine Hotṛ perform sacrifice for Vanaspati, which is the support of the sacrificial post, and for Agni, who has the nature of the deity of the tenth prayāja. For **Vanaspati** there are the epithets **धियो जोष्टा, स्वदात् स्वधितिः, देवेभ्यः ऋतुथा हव्यवाट्, यज्ञस्य आयुः कल्पमानः (*dhiyo joṣṭā, svadāt svadhitiḥ, devebhyaḥ ṛtuthā havyavāṭ, yajñasya āyuḥ kalpamānaḥ*)**. Among these epithets, for **धियो जोष्टा (*dhiyo joṣṭā*)** (the bhāṣya says) **बुद्धेः प्रीणयितारं (*buddheḥ prīṇayitāraṃ*)** — the one who gives joy to the intellect; **स्वदितिः (*svaditiḥ*)** *(so printed)* — consecrated by the *svaditi* (the thunderbolt-weapon, or) a divine weapon; **ऋतुथा (*ṛtuthā*)** — **ऋतौ विहिते कालविशेषे अद्य अस्मिन्कर्मणि स्वदादस्माभिर्दीयमानं हविः स्वदयतु । किंच देवो वनस्पतिर्देवेभ्यो देवार्थं हव्या हवींष्यवाड्वहतु (*ṛtau vihite kālaviśeṣe adya asminkarmaṇi svadādasmābhirdīyamānaṃ haviḥ svadayatu | kiṃca devo vanaspatirdevebhyo devārthaṃ havyā havīṃṣyavāḍvahatu*)** *(so printed)* — the meaning of the mantra is: may he offer to the deities the oblations offered by us at this time of sacrifice. And by the epithet **यज्ञस्य आयुः कल्पमानः (*yajñasya āyuḥ kalpamānaḥ*)** the meaning is: he who makes the life of the sacrifice grow. By epithets of this kind the Praiṣa-sūkta states the identity of Agni and Vanaspati. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa it is indicated by the statement **प्राणो वै वनस्पतिः (*prāṇo vai vanaspatiḥ*)** (2-4) *(zoomed, two tries)*. The Niruktakāra first gives the derivation of the word *vanaspati* and then makes known in the **Āprī sūkta** what the nature of Vanaspati is. While explaining the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-37-3 *(so printed; zoomed)*, showing the derivation of the word *vanaspati* in it — (Ni. 8-3) *(zoomed)* **वनानां पाता वा पालयिता वा । वनं वनोतेः (*vanānāṃ pātā vā pālayitā vā | vanaṃ vanoteḥ*)** — (Agni) is well known as Vanaspati either because he is lord of the forests or because he is their guardian; and having said that (*vana*) is formed from the root **वन् (*van*)**, which gives the meaning **'to obtain'**, then, when discussing the nature of the deities of the Āprī sūkta (8-18) *(zoomed)*, he states two opinions — **तत् को वनस्पतिः, यूप इति कात्थक्यः अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः (*tat ko vanaspatiḥ, yūpa iti kātthakyaḥ agniriti śākapūṇiḥ*)** — and in order to support Kātthakya's view … *(continued on p. 268)*

### Printed p. 268 (PDF 287)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188". Ṛk 10, Special Topics continued.)*

… (the Niruktakāra) has cited the ṛk

> अंजंति त्वामध्वरे देवयंतो वनस्पते मधुना दैव्येन ।
> यदूर्ध्वस्तिष्ठा द्रविणेह धत्ताद्यद्वा क्षयो मातुरस्या उपस्थे ॥

> *aṃjaṃti tvāmadhvare devayaṃto vanaspate madhunā daivyena |*
> *yadūrdhvastiṣṭhā draviṇeha dhattādyadvā kṣayo māturasyā upasthe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-1) *(zoomed)*

In this ṛk Sāyaṇa has addressed the word *vanaspati* as the sacrificial post itself. Then the Niruktakāra, to support Śākapūṇi's view, has cited the ṛk —

> वनस्पते रशनया नियूया देवानां पाथ उप वक्षि विद्वान् ।
> स्वदाति देवः कृणवद्धवींष्यवतां द्यावापृथिवी हवं मे ॥

> *vanaspate raśanayā niyūyā devānāṃ pātha upa vakṣi vidvān |*
> *svadāti devaḥ kṛṇavaddhavīṃṣyavatāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī havaṃ me ‖*

(10-70-10) *(zoomed)*

Here too Sāyaṇa has taken the meaning as the sacrificial post itself. But the Niruktakāra's view is that it is Agni contained within the post. Durgācārya, explaining this ṛk in (his commentary on) the Nirukta, says:

*("अग्निरेनासौ (*agnirenāsau*)" (na) as printed; zoomed.)*

> एवमग्निर्वनस्पतिः । यत् पुनरेतदुक्तं यूपांजनीयायां ‘यूपे वनस्पतिशब्दः’ इति । अत्र ब्रूमः—अग्निरेनासौ यूपांतर्गतो यूपात्मना वर्तमानो यूपांजनीयायां वनस्पतिशब्देनोच्यते ।

> *evamagnirvanaspatiḥ | yat punaretaduktaṃ yūpāṃjanīyāyāṃ ‘yūpe vanaspatiśabdaḥ’ iti | atra brūmaḥ—agnirenāsau yūpāṃtargato yūpātmanā vartamāno yūpāṃjanīyāyāṃ vanaspatiśabdenocyate |*

Here he has settled that Vanaspati means none other than Agni contained within the sacrificial post. The author of the Bṛhaddevatā, by the statements

*("वनस्पतिरितीळितः (*vanaspatiritīḷitaḥ*)" (ḷa) as printed; zoomed.)*

> वनस्पतिं तु यं प्राहुरयं सोऽग्निर्वनस्पतिः ।
> अयं वनानां हि पतिः पाता पालयितीति वा ॥
> अग्निर्गृत्समदेनायं वनस्पतिरितीळितः ।
> मंदस्वेत्यस्य सूक्तस्य षळृचस्य तृतीयया ॥
> यूपवत्तरुवच्चैव स्तुतिर्यास्य प्रसंगजा ।
> सर्वेणांजति सूक्तेन तृतीये सा तु मंडले ॥

> *vanaspatiṃ tu yaṃ prāhurayaṃ so 'gnirvanaspatiḥ |*
> *ayaṃ vanānāṃ hi patiḥ pātā pālayitīti vā ‖*
> *agnirgṛtsamadenāyaṃ vanaspatiritīḷitaḥ |*
> *maṃdasvetyasya sūktasya ṣaḷṛcasya tṛtīyayā ‖*
> *yūpavattaruvaccaiva stutiryāsya prasaṃgajā |*
> *sarveṇāṃjati sūktena tṛtīye sā tu maṃḍale ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-26 to 28) *(zoomed)*

discusses the nature of the Āprī deity referred to in the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-11 *(zoomed)*, and makes known that here *vanaspati* means the terrestrial Agni (**pārthivāgni**); that in the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-37-2 *(so printed; zoomed)* **Gṛtsamada** too refers to this same terrestrial Agni by the word *vanaspati*; that only in some ṛks of the third Maṇḍala the meaning is **sacrificial post** or **tree**; and that this too is **incidental (prasaṃgaja)**. Besides this,

> *ihyaiṣa pavamāno 'gnirmadhyamo 'gnirvanaspatiḥ |*

### Printed p. 270 (PDF 289)

*(Header: "Maṃ. . A. 24. Sū. 188" (zoomed; the Maṇḍala numeral is not printed). Ṛk 11: bhāṣya concluded, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

*Gist:* Agni goes before the gods in the battle with the Asuras, or in the sacrifice (hence his name, Ni. 6-14); he is honoured with the gāyatrī mantra and shines when oblations are offered with svāhā; these prayāja deities preside over parts of the sacrifice (so some), or are other names of Agni (so others).

*("सम्यग्लक्ष्यते (*samyaglakṣyate*)" zoomed.)*

> समज्यते सम्यग्लक्ष्यते । स्वाहाकृतीषु स्वाहाकारेषु सत्सु हविःषु दीयमानेषु रोचते । अत्यर्थं दीप्यते । एताः प्रयाजदेवता यज्ञावयवाभिमानिन्यः । तद्द्वारा यज्ञ एव स्तूयत इति केषांचिन्मतं । अग्निरेव नामांतरमित्यन्ये ॥

> *samajyate samyaglakṣyate | svāhākṛtīṣu svāhākāreṣu satsu haviḥṣu dīyamāneṣu rocate | atyarthaṃ dīpyate | etāḥ prayājadevatā yajñāvayavābhimāninyaḥ | taddvārā yajña eva stūyata iti keṣāṃcinmataṃ | agnireva nāmāṃtaramityanye ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** अग्निः (*agniḥ*) — Agni; देवानां (*devānāṃ*) — of all the deities; पुरोगाः (*purogāḥ*) — (this Agni) is the leader, whether at the time of battle or at the time of sacrifice; गायत्रेण (*gāyatreṇa*) — by the mantra in the form of the gāyatrī; समज्यते (*samajyate*) — he is described; स्वाहाकृतीषु (*svāhākṛtīṣu*) — when the oblation is offered with the utterance *svāhā*; रोचते (*rocate*) — he shines.

**Bhāvārtha.** Whether at the time of battle or at the time of sacrifice, Agni alone goes in front of all the deities. This Agni is described by the mantra in the form of the gāyatrī. When the oblation is offered with the utterance *svāhā*, he shines.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Agni, the preceder of the gods, is characterized by the Gayatri measure, (metre) ; he blazes when the oblations are offered· [sic]

*(A stray mark stands beside the comma after "measure", as printed.)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**Purogāḥ** — "अयमग्निर्देवानां पुरोगा असुरयुद्धं प्रति पुरोगामी । यद्वा । देवानां मध्ये यज्ञं प्रत्यग्निरेव पुरोगामी (*ayamagnirdevānāṃ purogā asurayuddhaṃ prati purogāmī | yadvā | devānāṃ madhye yajñaṃ pratyagnireva purogāmī*)" — that is, when (the gods) fight with the Asuras, this Agni is in front of both the gods and men, he is the leader (Leader); or, in the sacrifice, when the various deities are invoked and praised, the first place among them all belongs to Agni, that is, Agni is praised first. The word **purohita** too has more or less this same meaning. In sacrifices (on the sacrificial altar) he is established in front of the sacrificer, and therefore Agni is called *purohita*. From whatever point of view one looks, it must be said that in sacrifices and the like the first place (the chief place) belongs to Agni. Yāska on this subject — **अग्निः कस्मात् अग्रणीर्भवतीति (*agniḥ kasmāt agraṇīrbhavatīti*)** (Ni. 6-14) *(zoomed, two tries)* — explaining the formation of the word *agni*, has said that he has the name Agni because he is the leader in front of all. Therefore here Agni is described by the word **purogāḥ**.

**Gāyatreṇa saṃ ajyate** — the sense is: we offer this mantra called *svāhākṛti* to Agni with the gāyatrī metre, or with the Sāman mantra called *gāyatra*. The word **गायत्रवेपसे (*gāyatravepase*)** in the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-142-12 *(zoomed)* also supports this same meaning.

### Printed p. 271 (PDF 290)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 9" (zoomed). Ṛk 11, Special Topics continued.)*

**Svāhākṛtīṣu** — Yāska's explanation:

*(Ni. 8-21 zoomed; the second word is printed "साहाकृतयः (*sāhākṛtayaḥ*)" (without va), as printed; zoomed.)*

> स्वाहाकृतयः । साहाकृतयः स्वाहेत्येतत् सु आहेति वा । स्वा वागाहेति वा । स्वं प्राहेति वा । स्वाहुतं हविर्जुहोतीति वा ॥

> *svāhākṛtayaḥ | sāhākṛtayaḥ svāhetyetat su āheti vā | svā vāgāheti vā | svaṃ prāheti vā | svāhutaṃ havirjuhotīti vā ‖*

(Ni. 8-21)

The word *svāhā* has four kinds of etymological meaning.

(1) सु आहेति वा (*su āheti vā*) — *su* = well, *āha* = says. Because it is uttered well, or clearly, it has the name *svāhā*.

(2) स्वा वागाहेति वा (*svā vāgāheti vā*) — *svā* = one's own, *vāk* = speech. There is the Śruti statement (Brāhmaṇa) **तं स्वा वागभ्यवदज्जुहुधीति तत्स्वाहाकारस्य जन्म (*taṃ svā vāgabhyavadajjuhudhīti tatsvāhākārasya janma*)** *(zoomed, two tries)*. That is, when performing the homa, because (the one performing the homa) himself adds and utters the word *svāhā* at the end of the ṛk, the Vedic mantra, it has the name *svāhā*.

(3) स्वं प्राहेति वा (*svaṃ prāheti vā*) — here *svaṃ* = his own oblation; *āha* — he says, "I make the homa (of it)". Therefore it has the name *svāhā*.

(4) स्वाहुतं हविर्जुहोतीति वा (*svāhutaṃ havirjuhotīti vā*) — because one makes the homa of the oblation by means of uttering the word *svāhā*, that is, because one gives the oblation into Agni, it has the name **svāhā**.

For the meaning of *svāhākāra* Yāska has given this ṛk as an example —

> सद्यो जातो व्यमिमीत यज्ञमग्निर्देवानामभवत्पुरोगाः ।
> अस्य होतुः प्रदिश्यृतस्य वाचि स्वाहाकृतं हविरदंतु देवाः ॥

> *sadyo jāto vyamimīta yajñamagnirdevānāmabhavatpurogāḥ |*
> *asya hotuḥ pradiśyṛtasya vāci svāhākṛtaṃ haviradaṃtu devāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-11) *(zoomed)*

Its chief meaning is: Agni, just now born (that is, just now established in the sacrifice), sits in front of the deities and, performing the duty of the Hotṛ, that is, the work of invoking the deities, carries the sacrifice through. May the deities eat the oblation offered with the utterance of the word *svāhā*, which this Hotṛ, being in the eastern quarter, offers. Therefore the sense is that *svāhā* is the name of the word uttered at the end of the mantra when the oblation is offered, according to rule, into Agni established for the sacrifice, for the pleasure of the deities.

In some Āprī sūktas the plural usage **svāhākṛtayaḥ** is found. The eleven prayāja mantras used when making the homa to the eleven deities in this sūkta … *(continued on p. 272)*

### Printed p. 272 (PDF 291)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188" (zoomed). Ṛk 11, Special Topics continued.)*

… (since) they are recited with the *svāhākāra* added to them as well, the plural **svāhākṛtayaḥ** has been used.

In the Purāṇas and the like the word **svāhā** is used in another sense. In the Mahābhārata Svāhā is said to be the daughter of Bṛhaspati, the son of the ṛṣi Aṅgiras. In the Purāṇas Svāhādevī is said to be the daughter of Dakṣa Prajāpati and the wife of Agni.

*(Zoomed.)*

> स्वाहा इत्येवंपूर्वा कृतिः करणमुच्चारणं यक्ष्यमाणदेवतानां ताः स्वाहाकृतयः । तद्वंति हव्यानि ।

> *svāhā ityevaṃpūrvā kṛtiḥ karaṇamuccāraṇaṃ yakṣyamāṇadevatānāṃ tāḥ svāhākṛtayaḥ | tadvaṃti havyāni |*

— that is, it is an epithet of the word **havyāni**, meaning the oblations joined with the mantra *svāhā* that is recited for offering the oblation. It is a word recited chiefly in the last ṛks of the Āprī sūktas. In some ṛks it is also an adverb: that is, in 1-13-12 as **स्वाहा कृणोतन (*svāhā kṛṇotana*)**, and in 1-142-12 as **स्वाहा कर्तन (*svāhā kartana*)**; in the ṛks 3-4-11, 7-2-11 and 10-70-11 in the instrumental sense; in 2-3-11 as an epithet of the oblation (*havya*); and in 10-110-11 as an epithet of the word **haviḥ**. *(All references zoomed.)*

In explaining this word, some have held that by this word the *svāhākṛti* in the form of a deity is indicated, and some that by this word Agni is indicated. In the Praiṣa sūkta it is recited:

*(Zoomed; the end of "agni-" is printed as ga with a halant and a ga-subscript, as it looks.)*

> होता यक्षदग्निग्ग् स्वाहाज्यस्य……….वियंतु होतर्यज ।

> *hotā yakṣadagnigg svāhājyasya……….viyaṃtu hotaryaja |*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-2, zoomed)

On this Sāyaṇa —

> योऽयं स्वाहाशब्दोदितः उत्तमप्रयाजदेवः अग्निः तं दैव्यो होता यजतु ।

> *yo 'yaṃ svāhāśabdoditaḥ uttamaprayājadevaḥ agniḥ taṃ daivyo hotā yajatu |*

— has explained that by the word *svāhā* Agni, the deity of the eleventh prayāja, is meant. The Niruktakāra —

*(First word printed "ಸಾಹಾ" (without va), as on p. 271.)*

> साहाकृतयः । स्वाहेत्येतत् सु आहेति वा, स्वा वागाहेति वा स्वं प्राहेति वा, स्वाहुतं हविर्जुहोतीति वा ।

> *sāhākṛtayaḥ | svāhetyetat su āheti vā, svā vāgāheti vā svaṃ prāheti vā, svāhutaṃ havirjuhotīti vā |*

(Ni. 8-21, zoomed)

— having explained that it is known as *svāhākṛti* because one recites (it) well, or because speech itself said "it is well", or because one offers the oblation purified by the mantra *svāhā*, has made this idea clear by citing the ṛk 10-110-11 *(zoomed)*. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa —

> स्वाहाकृतीर्यजति प्रतिष्ठा वै स्वाहाकृतयः प्रतिष्ठायामेव तद्यज्ञमंततः प्रतिष्ठापयति ।

> *svāhākṛtīryajati pratiṣṭhā vai svāhākṛtayaḥ pratiṣṭhāyāmeva tadyajñamaṃtataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-4, zoomed)

— it is explained that, because the offering is completed by the *svāhākṛti*, that alone is the support of the whole sacrifice, and that it sets the sacrifice on a proper foundation. In the Bṛhaddevatā —

(Bṛ. De. 3-29 to 30, zoomed)

The opinions of the learned on the *svāhākṛti* are not of one kind. Even so, the whole idea indicated by this word refers to this earthly Agni. Because this Agni is the maker of the *svāhā*, and because he himself is also its making, the earthly Agni is called in this way: so the author of the Bṛhaddevatā has made his opinion known, following the view of the Niruktakāra, आग्नेयी इति तु स्थितिः (*āgneyī iti tu sthitiḥ*) (Ni. 8-22, zoomed).

In the last ṛks of the Āprī sūktas, which consist of the *svāhākāra*, deities such as Pūṣan, the Maruts, Vāyu, Sūrya, Indra, Varuṇa are all addressed; but more than all of them —

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** पुरोगाः (*purogāḥ*) — root गमॢ गतौ (*gamḷ gatau*); suffix *viṭ* by जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट् (*janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-67, zoomed); विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् (*viḍvanoranunāsikasyāt*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-41, zoomed) gives *ā* for the nasal; the suffix is wholly elided; in the compound the accent of the kṛt-final member. गायत्रेण (*gāyatreṇa*) — suffix *aṇ* by तस्येदम् (*tasyedam*) (Pā. Sū. 4-3-122, as printed, zoomed), *ī* elided by यस्येति च (*yasyeti ca*), end-acute; instrumental singular. अज्यते (*ajyate*) — root अंजू व्यक्तिम्रक्षणकांतिगतिषु (*aṃjū vyaktimrakṣaṇakāṃtigatiṣu*); passive *laṭ* third person singular; nighāta accent. रोचते (*rocate*) — root रुच दीप्तौ (*ruca dīptau*), bhvādi; *laṭ* third person singular; nighāta by तिङ्ङतिङः (*tiṅṅatiṅaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28, zoomed).

## Sūkta 189 — *agne naya* (Anuvāka 24, tenth Sūkta; 8 ṛks)

**The Hundred and Eighty-ninth Sūkta.** *(Half-title, in Kannada: "Nūra embhattombhattaneya sūktavu"; a short double rule follows. No Pīṭhike precedes the sūkta.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; introduction to the sūkta; its Kannada rendering follows on p. 275.)*

*(Zoomed: "traiṣṭubhaśchaṃdasi", "aṣṭānāmuttamāduttamāstisra uddharet", "Ā, 4-13" (comma), "Ṛgvi. 1-27", "Ā. Gṛ. 2-1-4", "Ā 3-7", "Ā. 4-3", as printed.)*

*Gist:* eight-ṛk tenth sūkta of Agastya, triṣṭubh, to Agni; its uses: Prātaranuvāka and Āśvina-śastra; Śaunaka prescribes it (oblations of ghee, japa) for one who has strayed from the path or done a blameworthy act; the first four ṛks in the Śravaṇā rite, and single ṛks as anuvākyā and yājyā in the animal sacrifice to Agni and in the Prāyaṇīya and Udayanīya iṣṭis.

> अग्ने नयेति दशमं सूक्तमष्टर्चमागस्त्यं त्रैष्टुभमाग्नेयं । अग्ने नयाष्टावाग्नेयमित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोस्त्रैष्टुभश्छंदसि विनियोगः । अथैतस्या इत्यत्राग्ने नयाग्ने बृहन्नित्यष्टानामुत्तमादुत्तमास्तिस्र उद्धरेत् । आ, ४-१३ । इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥ अत्र शौनकः । उत्पथप्रतिपन्नो यो भ्रष्टो वापि पथः क्वचित् । पंथानं प्रतिपद्येत कृत्वा वा कर्म गर्हितं ॥ अग्ने नयेति सूक्तेन प्रत्यृचं जुहुयाद्घृतं । जपेच्च प्रयतो नित्यमुपतिष्ठेत वाऽनलं । ऋग्वि १-२७ । इति ॥ आद्याश्चतस्रः श्रवणाकर्मणि विनियुक्ताः । श्रावण्यां पौर्णमास्यामित्यत्र सूत्रितं । अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मानिति चतसृभिः प्रत्यृचं हुत्वा । आ. गृ. २-१-४ । इति ॥ आग्नेये पशौ वपापुरोडाशयोराद्ये द्वे अनुवाक्ये । तथा च सूत्रितं । अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान् पाहि नो अग्ने पायुभिरजस्रैः । आ ३-७ । इति ॥ आद्या प्रायणीयेष्टावाग्नेयस्यानुवाक्या । सैवोदयनीये याज्या । तदहः प्रायणीयेष्टिरित्यत्र सूत्रितं । अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान्देवानामपि पंथामगन्म । आ. ४-३ । इति ॥ विपरीताश्च याज्यानुवाक्या इति च ॥

> *agne nayeti daśamaṃ sūktamaṣṭarcamāgastyaṃ traiṣṭubhamāgneyaṃ | agne nayāṣṭāvāgneyamityanukramaṇikā ‖ prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayostraiṣṭubhaśchaṃdasi viniyogaḥ | athaitasyā ityatrāgne nayāgne bṛhannityaṣṭānāmuttamāduttamāstisra uddharet | ā, 4-13 | iti sūtritatvāt ‖ atra śaunakaḥ | utpathapratipanno yo bhraṣṭo vāpi pathaḥ kvacit | paṃthānaṃ pratipadyeta kṛtvā vā karma garhitaṃ ‖ agne nayeti sūktena pratyṛcaṃ juhuyādghṛtaṃ | japecca prayato nityamupatiṣṭheta vā 'nalaṃ | ṛgvi 1-27 | iti ‖ ādyāścatasraḥ śravaṇākarmaṇi viniyuktāḥ | śrāvaṇyāṃ paurṇamāsyāmityatra sūtritaṃ | agne naya supathā rāye asmāniti catasṛbhiḥ pratyṛcaṃ hutvā | ā. gṛ. 2-1-4 | iti ‖ āgneye paśau vapāpuroḍāśayorādye dve anuvākye | tathā ca sūtritaṃ | agne naya supathā rāye asmān pāhi no agne pāyubhirajasraiḥ | ā 3-7 | iti ‖ ādyā prāyaṇīyeṣṭāvāgneyasyānuvākyā | saivodayanīye yājyā | tadahaḥ prāyaṇīyeṣṭirityatra sūtritaṃ | agne naya supathā rāye asmāndevānāmapi paṃthāmaganma | ā. 4-3 | iti ‖ viparītāśca yājyānuvākyā iti ca ‖*

### Printed p. 275 (PDF 294)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 9" (zoomed). Sūkta 189: Kannada rendering (Anuvāda) of the bhāṣya introduction.)*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, अग्ने नय (*agne naya*), is the tenth in the twenty-fourth anuvāka *(the text prints "anuvākavu" for "sūktavu")*. There are eight ṛks in it. Of this sūkta Agastya is the ṛṣi; Agni the deity; *triṣṭubh* the metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated beginning with अग्ने नयाष्टावाग्नेयं (*agne nayāṣṭāvāgneyaṃ*). That this sūkta is used for the Āśvina-śastra mantras of the *triṣṭubh* metre at the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अथैतस्या इत्यत्राग्ने नयाग्ने बृहन्नित्यष्टानामुत्तमादुत्तमास्तिस्र उद्धरेत् (*athaitasyā ityatrāgne nayāgne bṛhannityaṣṭānāmuttamāduttamāstisra uddharet*) (Ā 4-13, zoomed). And on the use of this sūkta the great sage Śaunaka has said this in the work called Ṛgvidhāna —

> उत्पथप्रतिपन्नो यो भ्रष्टो वापि पथः क्वचित् ।
> पंथानं प्रतिपद्येत कृत्वा वा कर्म गर्हितं ॥
> अग्ने नयेति सूक्तेन प्रत्यृचं जुहुयाद्घृतं ।
> जपेच्च प्रयतो नित्यमुपतिष्ठेत वाऽनलं ॥

> *utpathapratipanno yo bhraṣṭo vāpi pathaḥ kvacit |*
> *paṃthānaṃ pratipadyeta kṛtvā vā karma garhitaṃ ‖*
> *agne nayeti sūktena pratyṛcaṃ juhuyādghṛtaṃ |*
> *japecca prayato nityamupatiṣṭheta vā 'nalaṃ ‖*

(Ṛgvidhāna 1-27, zoomed)

That is: if a man, while climbing a hill or travelling to a distant country, somewhere in the middle loses his way, or if he unknowingly does a blameworthy act, such a man should make homa in the fire with ghee with each ṛk of this sūkta अग्ने नय (*agne naya*), and, having become pure, should recite this sūkta daily and worship Agni (*agnyupasthāna*). If he does so, he will find the right path: so he has said. Besides this, that the first four ṛks of this sūkta are to be used for homa, one with each ṛk, in the rite called Upākarma on the full-moon day joined with the Śravaṇa nakṣatra, is set out by the sūtra अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मानिति चतसृभिः प्रत्यृचं हुत्वा (*agne naya supathā rāye asmāniti catasṛbhiḥ pratyṛcaṃ hutvā*) of the section श्रावण्यां पौर्णमास्यां (*śrāvaṇyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ*) of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 2-1-4, zoomed). And that in the animal sacrifice relating to Agni, when making the homa of the omentum (*vapā*) and the puroḍāśa, the first two ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited as *puronuvākyā* mantras, is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान् पाहि नो अग्ने पायुभिरजस्रैः (*agne naya supathā rāye asmān pāhi no agne pāyubhirajasraiḥ*) (Ā. 3-7, zoomed). And that in the Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi (the first day of the sacrifice) the first ṛk of this sūkta is to be used as the *puronuvākyā* mantra relating to Agni, and in the Udayanīyeṣṭi (the last day of the sacrifice) the same ṛk as the *yājyā* mantra, is set out by the sūtra अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान्देवानामपि पंथामगन्म (*agne naya supathā rāye asmāndevānāmapi paṃthāmaganma*) of the section तदहः प्रायणीयेष्टि (*tadahaḥ prāyaṇīyeṣṭi*) of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, and also by the sūtra विपरीताश्च याज्यानुवाक्या (*viparītāśca yājyānuvākyā*) (Ā. 4-3, zoomed).

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(A small accent numeral "1" (the kampa sign) is printed after "yuyodhy-"; accents are not reproduced.)*

> अग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान्विश्वानि देव वयुनानि विद्वान् ।
> युयोध्यस्मज्जुहुराणमेनो भूयिष्ठां ते नमउक्तिं विधेम ॥ १ ॥

> *agne naya supathā rāye asmānviśvāni deva vayunāni vidvān |*
> *yuyodhyasmajjuhurāṇameno bhūyiṣṭhāṃ te namauktiṃ vidhema ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अग्ने । नय । सुऽपथा । राये । अस्मान् । विश्वानि । देव । वयुनानि । विद्वान् ।
> युयोधि । अस्मत् । जुहुराणं । एनः । भूयिष्ठां । ते । नमःऽउक्तिं । विधेम ॥

> *agne | naya | su 'pathā | rāye | asmān | viśvāni | deva | vayunāni | vidvān |*
> *yuyodhi | asmat | juhurāṇaṃ | enaḥ | bhūyiṣṭhāṃ | te | namaḥ 'uktiṃ | vidhema ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; lines zoomed.)*

> हे अग्नेऽगनादिगुणविशिष्ट देव द्योतमान विश्वानि वयुनानि सर्वाणि प्रज्ञानानि । अनेनैतदनुष्ठितमिदं प्रायणीयमिति यदेतज्ज्ञानमस्ति तद्विद्वानित्यर्थः । यतो विद्वान् अतस्त्वमस्मान् सुपथा शोभनेन मार्गेण राये गंतव्याय स्वर्गादिधनाय । द्वितीयार्थे वा चतुर्थी । प्रापणीयं रयिं प्रति नय । तदर्थं जुहुराणं कुटिलकार्येनः पापं फलप्रतिबंधरूपमस्मदस्मत्तो युयोधि । पृथक्कुरु । ते तव वयं भूयिष्ठामतिप्रवृद्धां नमउक्तिं नमस्कारोक्तिं स्तुतिं विधेम । परिचरेम । कुर्मः ॥

> *he agne 'ganādiguṇaviśiṣṭa deva dyotamāna viśvāni vayunāni sarvāṇi prajñānāni | anenaitadanuṣṭhitamidaṃ prāyaṇīyamiti yadetajjñānamasti tadvidvānityarthaḥ | yato vidvān atastvamasmān supathā śobhanena mārgeṇa rāye gaṃtavyāya svargādidhanāya | dvitīyārthe vā caturthī | prāpaṇīyaṃ rayiṃ prati naya | tadarthaṃ juhurāṇaṃ kuṭilakāryenaḥ pāpaṃ phalapratibaṃdharūpamasmadasmatto yuyodhi | pṛthakkuru | te tava vayaṃ bhūyiṣṭhāmatipravṛddhāṃ namauktiṃ namaskāroktiṃ stutiṃ vidhema | paricarema | kurmaḥ ‖*

### Printed p. 277 (PDF 296)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 10" (zoomed). Ṛk 1: Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** देव (*deva*) — who are of the nature of a deity; अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; विश्वानि वयुनानि (*viśvāni vayunāni*) — all knowledges; विद्वान् (*vidvān*) — you who know; अस्मान् (*asmān*) — us; सुपथा (*supathā*) — by the excellent path; राये (*rāye*) — to obtain wealth in the form of heaven and the like; नय (*naya*) — lead; जुहुराणं (*juhurāṇaṃ*) — that drags (us) into a crooked path; एनः (*enaḥ*) — sin; अस्मत् (*asmat*) — from us; युयोधि (*yuyodhi*) — separate; ते (*te*) — to you; भूयिष्ठां (*bhūyiṣṭhāṃ*) — exceedingly; नमउक्तिं (*namauktiṃ*) — the utterance of salutation; विधेम (*vidhema*) — we recite.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, who are of the nature of a deity, you who know all knowledges, lead us by the excellent path to obtain wealth in the form of heaven and the like. Remove from us the sin that drags us into a crooked path. We recite to you an abundant utterance of salutation.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Agni, knowing all kinds of knowledge, lead us by good ways to wealth, remove far from us the sin that would force us astry [sic], that we may offer to you most ample adoration· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**राये (*rāye*)** — the word *rayi* is read among the names of water (Ni. 2-24, as printed; zoomed) and among the names of wealth (3-9, zoomed). Besides this, Yāska —

> रयिरिति धननाम रातेर्दानकर्मणः ।

> *rayiriti dhananāma rāterdānakarmaṇaḥ |*

(Ni. 4-17, zoomed)

— has given the word *rayi* the meaning "wealth". He has explained that this word is formed from the root *rā*, "to give, to make a gift", and has the meaning "wealth". In the present ṛk too it has the same meaning.

**देव (*deva*)** — Yāska's Nirukta for the word *deva* is thus —

> देवो दानाद्वा, दीपनाद्वा, द्योतनाद्वा, द्युस्थानो भवतीति वा, यो देवः सा देवता ।

> *devo dānādvā, dīpanādvā, dyotanādvā, dyusthāno bhavatīti vā, yo devaḥ sā devatā |*

(Ni. 7-15, zoomed)

That is: because this deity gives prosperity and the like (दानाद्वा (*dānādvā*)), he has the name *deva*; because he illumines everything with his splendour (with light) (दीपनात् (*dīpanāt*), द्योतनाद्वा (*dyotanādvā*) — both words have the same meaning), he has the name *deva*. Or, the one who is in the heavenly region (in svarga) … *(continued on p. 278)*

### Printed p. 278 (PDF 297)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189" (zoomed). Ṛk 1: Special Topics continued and concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā begun.)*

… is (*dyusthāna*), therefore he has the name *deva*: thus he has stated various meanings for the word *deva*. Here, since the word *deva* is an epithet of the word अग्ने (*agne*), all the explanations stated above fit.

**वयुनानि (*vayunāni*)** — the word *vayunam* is read among the ten names of the praiseworthy (*praśasya*) beginning with अस्रेमाः अनेमाः (*asremāḥ anemāḥ*), and among the eleven names of knowledge (*prajñā*) beginning with केतः केतुः (*ketaḥ ketuḥ*) (Ni. [?]-13, as printed; first digit broken; zoomed). Besides this, for this word Yāska —

> वयुनं वेतेः कांतिर्वा प्रज्ञा वा ।

> *vayunaṃ veteḥ kāṃtirvā prajñā vā |*

(Ni. 5-95, zoomed) — having said that the word *vayunam* is formed from the root *veti* and has the meaning "splendour" or "knowledge", in support of this —

> अहिरिव भोगैः पर्येति बाहुं ज्याया हेतिं परिबाधमानः ।
> हस्तघ्नो विश्वा वयुनानि विद्वान् पुमान्पुमांसं परि पातु विश्वतः ॥

> *ahiriva bhogaiḥ paryeti bāhuṃ jyāyā hetiṃ paribādhamānaḥ |*
> *hastaghno viśvā vayunāni vidvān pumānpumāṃsaṃ pari pātu viśvataḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-75-14, zoomed)

— has given this ṛk as an example. Here too [Sāyaṇa], saying वयुनानि प्रज्ञानानि (*vayunāni prajñānāni*), has stated for the word *vayuna* the very meaning "knowledge" (*prajñāna*).

**नमउक्तिं (*namauktiṃ*)** — नमस्कारोक्तिं स्तुतिं (*namaskāroktiṃ stutiṃ*) | The intention is: "we recite a hymn preceded by salutation." *(A stray mark stands before "stutiṃ".)*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** नय (*naya*) — root णीञ् प्रापणे (*ṇīñ prāpaṇe*); *loṭ* second person singular; by आमन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवत् (*āmantritaṃ pūrvamavidyamānavat*) the preceding vocative अग्ने (*agne*) counts as absent, so no nighāta; *śap* being anudātta, the root accent remains. राये (*rāye*) — dative in the sense of the accusative by the dictum सुपां सुपो भवन्ति (*supāṃ supo bhavanti*); by ऊडिदंपदादि (*ūḍidaṃpadādi*) (Pā. Sū. 1-171, as printed, zoomed) the case ending is udātta. वयुनानि (*vayunāni*) — root अज गतिक्षेपणयोः (*aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ*); suffix *unan* by अजियमिशीङ्भ्यश्च (*ajiyamiśīṅbhyaśca*) (U. Sū. 3-441, as printed, zoomed); वी (*vī*) for the root by अजेर्व्यघञपोः (*ajervyaghañapoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-56, zoomed); guṇa, *ay*-substitution; by *vyatyaya* the suffix is initial-acute. युयोधि (*yuyodhi*) — at the head of the pāda, so no nighāta; *apit* treatment gives the udātta, hence end-acute. जुहुराणम् (*juhurāṇam*) — root हुर्छा कौटिल्ये (*hurchā kauṭilye*); by हुर्छेः सनो लुक् छलोपश्च (*hurcheḥ sano luk chalopaśca*) (U. Sū. 2-284, as printed, zoomed) suffix *ānac* after the desiderative, *luk* of *san*; to the *cha* of the root … *(continues on p. 279)*

… elision; by अट्कुप्वाङ् (*aṭkupvāṅ*)— *ṇa* for the *na* of the suffix; the suffix being *cit*, end-acute. नमउक्तिम् (*namauktim*) — by तादौ च निति (*tādau ca niti*)— (Pā. Sū. 6-2-50, zoomed) the *gati* keeps its own accent. विधेम (*vidhema*) — root विध विधाने (*vidha vidhāne*), tudādi; *liṅ* first person plural; nighāta by तिङ्ङतिङः (*tiṅṅatiṅaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28, zoomed).

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अग्ने त्वं पारया नव्यो अस्मान्त्स्वस्तिभिरति दुर्गाणि विश्वा ।
> पूश्च पृथ्वी बहुला न उर्वी भवा तोकाय तनयाय शं योः ॥ २ ॥

> *agne tvaṃ pārayā navyo asmāntsvastibhirati durgāṇi viśvā |*
> *pūśca pṛthvī bahulā na urvī bhavā tokāya tanayāya śaṃ yoḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥** *(The Pada prints "duḥ'gāni" (with *ga*-*na*) where the Saṃhitā has "durgāṇi".)*

> अग्ने । त्वं । पारय । नव्यः । अस्मान् । स्वस्तिऽभिः । अति । दुःऽगानि । विश्वा ।
> पूः । च । पृथ्वी । बहुला । नः । उर्वी । भव । तोकाय । तनयाय । शं । योः ॥ २ ॥

> *agne | tvaṃ | pāraya | navyaḥ | asmān | svasti 'bhiḥ | ati | duḥ 'gāni | viśvā |*
> *pūḥ | ca | pṛthvī | bahulā | naḥ | urvī | bhava | tokāya | tanayāya | śaṃ | yoḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; "Ā. 2-10", "yormiśrayitā" and "yāgānuṣṭhātṝnati" zoomed; "astirabhipūjitaḥ" as printed.)*

*Gist:* uses — in the iṣṭi for long life this and the next ṛk are the Sviṣṭakṛt yājyās, with ṛk 4 (*pāhi naḥ*) as anuvākyā; Ā. 2-10 gives ṛks 4 and 2 as saṃyājyās, also in the Svastyayanī; *pūḥ* (class singular) = towns; *śaṃ yoḥ* = happiness and mixing (or allaying of diseases and warding off of fears).

> आयुष्कामेष्ट्यामग्ने त्वं पारयेति द्वे स्विष्टकृतो याज्ये पाहि न इति चतुर्थ्यनुवाक्या । पाहि नो अग्ने पायुभिरजस्रैरग्ने त्वं पारया नव्यो अस्मानिति संयाज्ये । आ. २-१० । इति सूत्रितं ॥ एते एव स्वस्त्ययन्यामपि संयाज्ये इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥
> हे अग्ने त्वं नव्यो नवतरः स्तुत्यो वा त्वमस्मान्यागानुष्ठातॄनति पारय । कर्म समापयातिपारय । अतिक्रामय । केन साधनेन । स्वस्तिभिः । अस्तिरभिपूजितः । सुशब्दः शोभनवचनः । अत्यंतं पूजितैर्यज्ञादिसाधनैः । कानि । दुर्गाणि दुर्गमनानि पापानि । अनतिक्रमणीयानि दुरिताख्यान्यतिपारय । किंच नोऽस्माकं पृथ्वी पृथुतरा पूश्च पुर्यपि भवत्विति शेषः । चशब्दो वक्ष्यमाणेन सह समुच्चयार्थः । पूरिति जात्येकवचनं । पुराण्यपि भवंत्वित्यर्थः । तथा नोऽस्माकमुर्वी पृथ्व्यपि बहुतरा भवतु । त्वं तु तोकायापत्याय तनयाय पुत्राय । तोकशब्दोऽपत्यसामान्यवचनः । तनयशब्दः पुत्रवचनः । शं सुखं योर्मिश्रयिता भव । यद्वा । रोगाणां शमनं भयानां यावनं च भव । कुर्वित्यर्थः ॥

> *āyuṣkāmeṣṭyāmagne tvaṃ pārayeti dve sviṣṭakṛto yājye pāhi na iti caturthyanuvākyā | pāhi no agne pāyubhirajasrairagne tvaṃ pārayā navyo asmāniti saṃyājye | ā. 2-10 | iti sūtritaṃ ‖ ete eva svastyayanyāmapi saṃyājye iti sūtritatvāt ‖*
> *he agne tvaṃ navyo navataraḥ stutyo vā tvamasmānyāgānuṣṭhātṝnati pāraya | karma samāpayātipāraya | atikrāmaya | kena sādhanena | svastibhiḥ | astirabhipūjitaḥ | suśabdaḥ śobhanavacanaḥ | atyaṃtaṃ pūjitairyajñādisādhanaiḥ | kāni | durgāṇi durgamanāni pāpāni | anatikramaṇīyāni duritākhyānyatipāraya | kiṃca no 'smākaṃ pṛthvī pṛthutarā pūśca puryapi bhavatviti śeṣaḥ | caśabdo vakṣyamāṇena saha samuccayārthaḥ | pūriti jātyekavacanaṃ | purāṇyapi bhavaṃtvityarthaḥ | tathā no 'smākamurvī pṛthvyapi bahutarā bhavatu | tvaṃ tu tokāyāpatyāya tanayāya putrāya | tokaśabdo 'patyasāmānyavacanaḥ | tanayaśabdaḥ putravacanaḥ | śaṃ sukhaṃ yormiśrayitā bhava | yadvā | rogāṇāṃ śamanaṃ bhayānāṃ yāvanaṃ ca bhava | kurvityarthaḥ ‖*

### Printed p. 280 (PDF 299)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189". Ṛk 2: Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; नव्यः (*navyaḥ*) — being praiseworthy; अस्मान् (*asmān*) — us; स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*) — by the means, sacrifice and the like, that are exceedingly auspicious; दुर्गाणि (*durgāṇi*) — (from) the sins that cannot be crossed (by ordinary means); अति पारय (*ati pāraya*) — make cross; नः (*naḥ*) — our; पूः (*pūḥ*) — town; पृथ्वी (*pṛthvī*) — being exceedingly extensive; उर्वी च (*urvī ca*) — and the extensive land too; बहुला (*bahulā*) — being many in number, may it be; तोकाय (*tokāya*) — for our grandsons and the rest; तनयाय (*tanayāya*) — for sons; शंयोः (*śaṃyoḥ*) — as one who brings about happiness; or शंयोः (*śaṃyoḥ*) — as one who brings about the allaying of disease and freedom from fear; भव (*bhava*) — be.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, being praiseworthy, take us away from hard sins by the means, sacrifice and the like, that are exceedingly auspicious. May our town be exceedingly extensive, and the extensive land too be many in number. For all our sons, grandsons and the rest be the one who brings about the allaying of disease and freedom from fear.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Adorable Agni, convey us by the sacred acts (of worship), beyond all evil ways : may our city be spacious ; our land be extensive ; be the bestower of happiness upon our offspring, upon our sons *(no closing stop printed)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**अग्ने त्वं पारय (*agne tvaṃ pāraya*)** — that this ṛk and the next ṛk are to be recited as *yājyā* mantras when making the Sviṣṭakṛt homa in the Āyuṣkāmeṣṭi, and the fourth ṛk of this sūkta, पाहि नो अग्ने (*pāhi no agne*), as the *puronuvākyā* mantra, and, by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra पाहि नो अग्ने पायुभिरजस्रैरग्ने त्वं पाराया नव्यो अस्मानिति संयाज्ये (*pāhi no agne pāyubhirajasrairagne tvaṃ pārāyā navyo asmāniti saṃyājye*) *(as printed, for "pārayā")*, that in the Svastyayana too these ṛks are to be recited as *yājyā* mantras, is stated there (Ā. 2-10).

**नव्यः (*navyaḥ*)** — नवतरः स्तुत्यो वा (*navataraḥ stutyo vā*) | Yāska's derivation (*nirvacana*) for the word *navya* is "newer" (*navatara*) (Ni. 6-9, zoomed). Since fuel-sticks and the like are put into Agni, he grows and is ever new: there are such descriptions in many places. Sāyaṇa has given along with this the meaning स्तुत्यः (*stutyaḥ*) — "one who is praised". The word *navya* has been used with reference to Agni in many ṛks.

### Printed p. 281 (PDF 300)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 10". Ṛk 2: Special Topics concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; Ṛk 3: Saṃhitā.)*

**स्वस्तिभिः (*svastibhiḥ*)** — अस्तिरभिपूजितः । सुशब्दः शोभनवचनः । अत्यंतं पूजितैर्यज्ञादिसाधनैः (*astirabhipūjitaḥ | suśabdaḥ śobhanavacanaḥ | atyaṃtaṃ pūjitairyajñādisādhanaiḥ*) | The meaning is "by the means, sacrifice and the like, that are worthy of worship". Yāska's derivation is स्वस्तीत्यविनाशिनाम । अस्तिरभिपूजतः सु अस्तीति (*svastītyavināśināma | astirabhipūjataḥ su astīti*) *("abhipūjataḥ", as printed)* (Ni. 3-21, zoomed). The intention is: because it is that which is not destroyed, it is worthy of worship. The prefix *su* indicates the meaning "exceedingly, good, of auspicious form".

**पूः (*pūḥ*)** — the city, the town in which we live. The bhāṣyakāra has said that this word is a singular of the class (*jātyekavacana*); that is, though used in the singular, a plural sense may be given to it.

**बहुला (*bahulā*)** — बहुतरा (*bahutarā*) — the intention is: may it become such as to furnish happiness and wealth of many kinds, and sons, grandsons and the rest.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** पारय (*pāraya*) — root पार तीरसमाप्तौ (*pāra tīrasamāptau*); *loṭ* second person singular of the *ṇic*-form; standing after a verb-free word (*atiṅanta*), nighāta. दुर्गाणि (*durgāṇi*) — root गम्ऌ गतौ (*gamḷ gatau*); suffix *ḍa* by सुदुरोरधिकरणे (*suduroradhikaraṇe*); by force of the *ḍit*, elision of the root's *ṭi*; accent of the kṛt-final member. विश्वा (*viśvā*) — elision of *śi* by शेश्छंदसि बहुलम् (*śeśchaṃdasi bahulam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70, zoomed). पृथ्वी (*pṛthvī*) — read in the *gaurādi* group, suffix *ṅīṣ*; end-acute by the suffix accent. भवा (*bhavā*) — root भू सत्तायां (*bhū sattāyāṃ*); *loṭ* second person singular; at the head of the pāda, so no nighāta; the root accent remains; lengthening in the Saṃhitā by द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङः (*dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-135, zoomed). तनयाय (*tanayāya*) — root तनु विस्तारे (*tanu vistāre*); suffix *kayan* by वलिमलितनिभ्यः कयन् (*valimalitanibhyaḥ kayan*) (U. Sū. 4-239, as printed, zoomed), giving *tanaya*; the suffix being *nit*, initial-acute by ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ñnityādirnityam*).

*(A short rule closes Ṛk 2.)*

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अग्ने त्वमस्मद्युयोध्यमीवा अनग्नित्रा अभ्यमंत कृष्टीः ।
> पुनरस्मभ्यं सुविताय देव क्षां विश्वेभिरमृतेभिर्यजत्र ॥ ३ ॥

> *agne tvamasmadyuyodhyamīvā anagnitrā abhyamaṃta kṛṣṭīḥ |*
> *punarasmabhyaṃ suvitāya deva kṣāṃ viśvebhiramṛtebhiryajatra ‖ 3 ‖*

### Printed p. 282 (PDF 301)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189". Ṛk 3: Pada, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English.)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अग्ने । त्वं । अस्मत् । युयोधि । अमीवाः । अनग्निऽत्राः । अभि । अमंत । कृष्टीः ।
> पुनः । अस्मभ्यं । सुविताय । देव । क्षां । विश्वेभिः । अमृतेभिः । यजत्र ॥ ३ ॥

> *agne | tvaṃ | asmat | yuyodhi | amīvāḥ | anagni 'trāḥ | abhi | amaṃta | kṛṣṭīḥ |*
> *punaḥ | asmabhyaṃ | suvitāya | deva | kṣāṃ | viśvebhiḥ | amṛtebhiḥ | yajatra ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed.)*

*Gist:* the relative *yāḥ* is supplied, hence no nighāta of *abhyamanta*; alternatively the sinful people unprotected by Agni deserve to be afflicted by you with diseases, "we are not such"; *kṣām* = the earth as place of sacrifice, "come" supplied.

> हे अग्ने त्वममीवा रोगानस्मदस्मत्तो युयोधि । व्यावर्तय । या अनग्नित्रा अग्निनापालिताः कृष्टीः प्रजा अभ्यमंत अभिमिमतेऽस्मान् ॥ यच्छब्दाध्याहारादनिघातः ॥ ता युयोधि । यद्वा । ता अनग्नित्राः पापिन्यः कृष्टयः प्रजा अभ्यमंत । त्वयाभ्यमितुमभितो रोगैः प्रापयितुमर्हंति । वयं तु न तादृशाः । अतोऽस्मत्तो वियोजयेत्यर्थः । न केवलं वियोगमात्रं अपि तु पुनःपुनरिदं कर्तव्यं । अस्मभ्यमस्मदर्थं सुविताय शोभनफलाय हे यजत्र यष्टव्य देव द्योतमानाग्ने विश्वेभिरमृतेभिः सर्वैरमरणधर्मभिरन्यैर्यष्टव्यैर्देवैः सह क्षां पृथिवीं देवयजनलक्षणामागच्छेति शेषः ॥

> *he agne tvamamīvā rogānasmadasmatto yuyodhi | vyāvartaya | yā anagnitrā agnināpālitāḥ kṛṣṭīḥ prajā abhyamaṃta abhimimate 'smān ‖ yacchabdādhyāhārādanighātaḥ ‖ tā yuyodhi | yadvā | tā anagnitrāḥ pāpinyaḥ kṛṣṭayaḥ prajā abhyamaṃta | tvayābhyamitumabhito rogaiḥ prāpayitumarhaṃti | vayaṃ tu na tādṛśāḥ | ato 'smatto viyojayetyarthaḥ | na kevalaṃ viyogamātraṃ api tu punaḥpunaridaṃ kartavyaṃ | asmabhyamasmadarthaṃ suvitāya śobhanaphalāya he yajatra yaṣṭavya deva dyotamānāgne viśvebhiramṛtebhiḥ sarvairamaraṇadharmabhiranyairyaṣṭavyairdevaiḥ saha kṣāṃ pṛthivīṃ devayajanalakṣaṇāmāgaccheti śeṣaḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; अमीवाः (*amīvāḥ*) — diseases (and); अनग्नित्राः (*anagnitrāḥ*) — those who are unprotected by Agni; याः कृष्टीः (*yāḥ kṛṣṭīḥ*) — whatever people, being of the form of our enemies; अभ्यमंत (*abhyamaṃta*) — who confront us and hate us, them too; पुनः (*punaḥ*) — again and again; अस्मत् (*asmat*) — from us; युयोधि (*yuyodhi*) — remove and destroy; अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*) — for us; सुविताय (*suvitāya*) — in order to furnish excellent fruit; यजत्र (*yajatra*) — you who are worthy of sacrifice; देव (*deva*) — and shining, O Agni; विश्वेभिरमृतेभिः (*viśvebhiramṛtebhiḥ*) — together with all the deities who are free from the property of death; क्षां (*kṣāṃ*) — show favour to the sacrificial ground.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, remove from us again and again and destroy our diseases and the enemies who, not coming under your protection, harm us. O Agni, worthy of sacrifice and shining, in order to furnish us excellent fruit, together with all the deities who are free from the property of death, show favour to the sacrificial ground.

**English Translatin [sic] (as printed).**

Agni, remove from us disease, and those men who, unprotected by Agni, are adverse to us ; and, adorable divinity, (visit) the earth, with the all immortals, rfo [sic] our welfare· [sic]

### Printed p. 283 (PDF 302)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 10" (zoomed). Ṛk 3: Special Topics; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; end of Ṛk 3.)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).** *(No heading is printed on this page; the topics follow the printed English of p. 282.)*

**अमीवाः (*amīvāḥ*)** — diseases. This word, formed from the root अम रोगे (*ama roge*) (curādi, parasmaipadī), indicates the meaning "disease" or "injury". Yāska —

> यस्ते गर्भममीवा दुर्णामा योनिमाशये ।
> अग्निष्टं ब्रह्मणा सह निष्क्रव्यादमनीनशत् ॥

> *yaste garbhamamīvā durṇāmā yonimāśaye |*
> *agniṣṭaṃ brahmaṇā saha niṣkravyādamanīnaśat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-162-2, zoomed)

— quoting this ṛk, has stated for the word अमीवा (*amīvā*) in it the meaning रोगभूतः (*rogabhūtaḥ*) (Ni. 6-12, zoomed).

**अनग्नित्राः (*anagnitrāḥ*)** — those not protected by Agni, that is, those who do sinful deeds, rākṣasas.

**अमृतेभिः (*amṛtebhiḥ*)** — अमरणधर्मभिरन्यैर्यष्टव्यैर्देवैः (*amaraṇadharmabhiranyairyaṣṭavyairdevaiḥ*) | By the other deities, free from death and worthy of worship.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** अनग्नित्रा (*anagnitrā*) — अग्निना त्राताः अग्नित्राः न अग्नित्राः अनग्नित्राः (*agninā trātāḥ agnitrāḥ na agnitrāḥ anagnitrāḥ*); by तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ (*tatpuruṣe tulyārtha*)— (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1, zoomed) the prior member with *nañ* keeps its own accent. अमंत (*amaṃta*) — root माङ् माने शब्दे च (*māṅ māne śabde ca*); Vedic *laṅ* in the sense of the present; by *vyatyaya*, *luk* of the vikaraṇa; third person plural; since *yat* is supplied, nighāta is barred by यद्वृत्तान्नित्यम् (*yadvṛttānnityam*); the augment *aṭ* being udātta, initial-acute. कृष्टीः (*kṛṣṭīḥ*) — root कृष विलेखने (*kṛṣa vilekhane*); suffix *ktic* by क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायाम् (*kticktau ca saṃjñāyām*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-174, zoomed); *ṣṭutva* through the *ṣa*; *cit*, hence end-acute. सुविताय (*suvitāya*) — सुष्ठु इतः सुवितः तस्मै (*suṣṭhu itaḥ suvitaḥ tasmai*); root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*), suffix *kta*; *uvaṅ* for the *u* by तन्वादीनां छंदसि बहुलमुपसंख्यानम् (*tanvādīnāṃ chaṃdasi bahulamupasaṃkhyānam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-77-1, zoomed); end-acute by the suffix accent. अमृतेभिः (*amṛtebhiḥ*) — by नञो जरमर (*naño jaramara*)— (Pā. Sū. 6-2-116, zoomed) the latter member is initial-acute; in the Veda the *ais* for *bhis* being optional, *e* by बहुवचने झल्येत् (*bahuvacane jhalyet*). यजत्र (*yajatra*) — root यज देवपूजादिषु (*yaja devapūjādiṣu*); suffix *atran* by अमिनक्षियजि (*aminakṣiyaji*)— (U. Sū. 3-384, as printed, zoomed); vocative, nighāta by आमन्त्रितस्य च (*āmantritasya ca*).

*(A short rule closes Ṛk 3.)*

### Printed p. 284 (PDF 303)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189". Ṛk 4: Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha begun.)*

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> पाहि नो अग्ने पायुभिरजस्रैरुत प्रिये सदन आ शुशुक्वान् ।
> मा ते भयं जरितारं यविष्ठ नूनं विदन्मापरं सहस्वः ॥ ४ ॥

> *pāhi no agne pāyubhirajasrairuta priye sadana ā śuśukvān |*
> *mā te bhayaṃ jaritāraṃ yaviṣṭha nūnaṃ vidanmāparaṃ sahasvaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> पाहि । नः । अग्ने । पायुऽभिः । अजस्रैः । उत । प्रिये । सदने । आ । शुशुक्वान् ।
> मा । ते । भयं । जरितारं । यविष्ठ । नूनं । विदत् । मा । अपरं । सहस्वः ॥ ४ ॥

> *pāhi | naḥ | agne | pāyu 'bhiḥ | ajasraiḥ | uta | priye | sadane | ā | śuśukvān |*
> *mā | te | bhayaṃ | jaritāraṃ | yaviṣṭha | nūnaṃ | vidat | mā | aparaṃ | sahasvaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; "Ā. 3-7" and "anavarataiḥ" zoomed.)*

*Gist:* uses — the two uses are stated under Ṛk 2; also the anuvākyā of the oblation in the Āgneya animal sacrifice (Ā. 3-7); *nūnam* = today; *aparam* = at another time, or another (person).

> पाहि न इत्यस्या विनियोगद्वयमग्ने त्वं पारयेत्यत्रोक्तं ॥ तथाग्नेयपशावेष्यैव हविषोऽनुवाक्या । तथा च सूत्रितं । पाहि नो अग्ने पायुभिरजस्रैः प्र वः शुक्राय भानवे भरध्वं । आ ३-७ । इति ॥
> हे अग्ने नोऽस्मानजस्रैरनवरतैरविच्छिन्नैः पायुभिः पालनप्रकारैः पाहि । पालय । उतापि च प्रिये सदने तव प्रियभूते यागगृह आ सर्वतः शुशुक्वान् दीप्यमानो भवेति शेषः । किंच हे यविष्ठ युवतम ते तव जरितारं गरितारं स्तोतारं मां नूनमद्य भयं मा विदत् । मा लभतां । माप्नोतु । हे सहस्वो बलवन्नग्ने अपरमपरस्मिन्काले भयं मा विदत् । अपरमन्यं वा मा विदत् ॥

> *pāhi na ityasyā viniyogadvayamagne tvaṃ pārayetyatroktaṃ ‖ tathāgneyapaśāveṣyaiva haviṣo 'nuvākyā | tathā ca sūtritaṃ | pāhi no agne pāyubhirajasraiḥ pra vaḥ śukrāya bhānave bharadhvaṃ | ā 3-7 | iti ‖*
> *he agne no 'smānajasrairanavaratairavicchinnaiḥ pāyubhiḥ pālanaprakāraiḥ pāhi | pālaya | utāpi ca priye sadane tava priyabhūte yāgagṛha ā sarvataḥ śuśukvān dīpyamāno bhaveti śeṣaḥ | kiṃca he yaviṣṭha yuvatama te tava jaritāraṃ garitāraṃ stotāraṃ māṃ nūnamadya bhayaṃ mā vidat | mā labhatāṃ | māpnotu | he sahasvo balavannagne aparamaparasminkāle bhayaṃ mā vidat | aparamanyaṃ vā mā vidat ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; नः (*naḥ*) — us; अजस्रैः (*ajasraiḥ*) — that are incessant and uninterrupted; पायुभिः (*pāyubhiḥ*) — by modes of protection; पाहि (*pāhi*) — protect; उत (*uta*) — and; प्रिये सदने (*priye sadane*) — in the sacrificial house that is dear to you; आ (*ā*) — all around; शुशुक्वान् (*śuśukvān*) — shine; यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*) — O Agni, who are exceedingly young; ते (*te*) — your; जरितारं (*jaritāraṃ*) — me, who am the praiser; नूनं (*nūnaṃ*) — now; भयं (*bhayaṃ*) — fear; मा विदत् (*mā vidat*) — may it not approach; सहस्वः (*sahasvaḥ*) — O Agni, who are mighty; अपरं (*aparaṃ*) — at another time too; मा (*mā*) — may fear not approach me.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, who are exceedingly young, protect us by modes of protection that are incessant and uninterrupted. And shine all around in the sacrificial house that is dear to you. O mighty … *(continued on p. 285)*

### Printed p. 285 (PDF 304)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 10" (zoomed; the Aṣṭaka numeral prints like "ಅ.ವ"). Ṛk 4: Bhāvārtha concluded, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

… Agni, may there be no fear at all for me, your praiser, whether at this time of sacrifice or at any other time.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Cherish us, Agni, with incessant bounties ; shine always in your favourite abode : let no danger, youngest (of the gods), assail your worshipper to-day ; nor, mighty one, let it assail him at any other season· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**पायुभिः (*pāyubhiḥ*)** — पालनप्रकारैः (*pālanaprakāraiḥ*) | by modes of protection. In this ṛk the use of the word पाहि (*pāhi*) indicates the act of protecting. Is not then the use of the word पायुभिः (*pāyubhiḥ*), which has the same meaning, superfluous? The answer is: in protection too there are many kinds. The word अजस्रैः (*ajasraiḥ*) indicates that in some circumstances the protection must be present at all times without a break. And that protection may be of many kinds: protecting so that no harm comes to us from enemies and from wicked kings; protecting from fears such as the fear of fire and the fear of water; protecting from calamities such as disease; protecting, by giving food, meals and the like, so that, afflicted by hunger (*kṣudbādhā*), we do not fall prey to death — it should be understood that the word पायुभिः (*pāyubhiḥ*) is used to indicate these many kinds of means of protection.

**मा (*mā*)** — here the word *mā* indicates prohibition. The intention is "may it not come about".

**जरितारं (*jaritāraṃ*)** — स्तोतारं मां (*stotāraṃ māṃ*) | me, who am praising. जरतेः स्तुतिकर्मणः (*jarateḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ*) (Ni. 10-8, zoomed) is the statement of the Nirukta.

**नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)** — for this word Yāska —

> नूनमिति विचिकित्सार्थीयो भाषायामुभयमन्वध्यायं विचिकित्सार्थीयश्च पदपूरणश्च ।

> *nūnamiti vicikitsārthīyo bhāṣāyāmubhayamanvadhyāyaṃ vicikitsārthīyaśca padapūraṇaśca |*

(Ni. 1-5, zoomed)

— has described that the word *nūnam*, besides in the Vedas (*chandas*), is used elsewhere too in the sense of doubt (*vicikitsā*), and in the Veda both in the sense of doubt and as a verse-filler (*padapūraṇa*). Durgācārya — विचिकित्सा नाम विवेकपूर्वको अवधारणाभिप्रायः (*vicikitsā nāma vivekapūrvako avadhāraṇābhiprāyaḥ*) — has explained the meaning of *vicikitsā* as reaching certainty by deliberation in situations where doubt has arisen. In this ṛk the bhāṣyakāra has explained the meaning of the word *nūnam* as "now".

**यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*)** — युवतम (*yuvatama*) | the best among the young. Since Agni always blazes up with fuel-sticks, clarified butter and the like and keeps shining, it is customary to address him as "young" … *(continued on p. 286)*

### Printed p. 286 (PDF 305)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189" (zoomed). Ṛk 4: Special Topics concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; end of Ṛk 4.)*

… as in —

> अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते कविर्गृहपतिर्युवा । हव्यवाड्जुह्वास्यः ॥

> *agnināgniḥ samidhyate kavirgṛhapatiryuvā | havyavāḍjuhvāsyaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-6, zoomed)

— in such ṛks Agni has been described by the word *yuvā*. The word is also used with reference to other deities.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** पाहि (*pāhi*) — root पा रक्षणे (*pā rakṣaṇe*); *loṭ* second person singular; at the head of the pāda, so no nighāta; by the *apit* treatment it becomes udātta. पायुभिः (*pāyubhiḥ*) — suffix *uṇ* by कृवापा— (*kṛvāpā—*) (U. Sū. 1-1, zoomed); augment *yuk* by आतो युक् चिण्कृतोः (*āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ*); end-acute by the suffix accent (as printed). शुशुक्वान् (*śuśukvān*) — root शुच दीप्तौ (*śuca dīptau*); *liṭ* replaced by *kvasu* by क्वसुश्च (*kvasuśca*); reduplication; by *vyatyaya* *ku*-substitution for the root's *ca*; by the suffix accent the *ā* after *va* is udātta. जरितारम् (*jaritāram*) — the root जॄष् (*jṝṣ*) (as it looks; zoomed), roots having many meanings, is used here in the sense of praise; *tṛc* in the agent sense, augment *iṭ*; guṇa of the *ṛ* by सार्वधातुकार्ध— (*sārvadhātukārdha—*), with *r* following; the suffix being *cit*, end-acute. यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*) — अतिशयेन युवा (*atiśayena yuvā*); suffix *iṣṭhan* by अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ (*atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau*) (Pā. Sū. 5-3-55, zoomed); elision of *van* by स्थूलदूर— (*sthūladūra—*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-156, zoomed); guṇa of the *u*, *av*-substitution; vocative, nighāta of the āmantrita. विदत् (*vidat*) — root विद्ऌ लाभे (*vidḷ lābhe*); *luṅ* by माङि लुङ् (*māṅi luṅ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-175, zoomed) with *māṅ* as upapada; third person singular *tip*, its *i* elided by इतश्च (*itaśca*); the root being *ḷdit*, *aṅ* for *cli* by पुषादिद्युतादि— (*puṣādidyutādi—*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-55, zoomed); being *ṅit*, no laghūpadha guṇa; no augment *aṭ* by न माङ्योगे (*na māṅyoge*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-74, zoomed); standing after a non-verb, nighāta. सहस्वः (*sahasvaḥ*) — *ru* in the vocative by मतुवसो रु संबुद्धौ (*matuvaso ru saṃbuddhau*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-1, zoomed); nighāta by आमन्त्रितस्य च (*āmantritasya ca*).

*(Rule "—:o:—" closes Ṛk 4.)*

### Printed p. 287 (PDF 306)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 10". Ṛk 5: Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha.)*

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(The Saṃhitā prints "agneva" without the avagraha (zoomed); transcribed as printed.)*

> मा नो अग्नेव सृजो अघायाविष्यवे रिपवे दुच्छुनायै ।
> मा दत्वते दशते मादते नो मा रीषते सहसावन्परा दाः ॥ ५ ॥

> *mā no agneva sṛjo aghāyāviṣyave ripave ducchunāyai |*
> *mā datvate daśate mādate no mā rīṣate sahasāvanparā dāḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> मा । नः । अग्ने । अव । सृजः । अघाय । अविष्यवे । रिपवे । दुच्छुनायै ।
> मा । दत्वते । दशते । मा । अदते । नः । मा । रिषते । सहसाऽवन् । परा । दाः ॥ ५ ॥

> *mā | naḥ | agne | ava | sṛjaḥ | aghāya | aviṣyave | ripave | ducchunāyai |*
> *mā | datvate | daśate | mā | adate | naḥ | mā | riṣate | sahasā 'van | parā | dāḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; "Ā, Gṛ. 2-1-6" zoomed, comma as printed.)*

*Gist:* use — in the cake-offering on one potsherd to Acyuta Bhauma the āśaya is offered with this ṛk (Ā. Gṛ. 2-1-6); *aviṣyu* = desirous of eating; *śunam* = happiness.

> अच्युताय भौमायैककपालपुरोडाशहोमे मा नो अग्न इत्यनयाशयमभिजुहोति । तथा च सूत्रितं । मा नो अग्नेऽव सृजो अघायेत्येनमाशयेनाभिजुहोति । आ, गृ. २-१-६ । इति ॥
> हे अग्ने नोऽस्मानघाय हिंसकायाविष्यवे । अविष्यतिरत्तिकर्मा । अत्तेच्छवे दुच्छुनायै । शुनं सुखं । दुष्टसुखकारिणे । दुःखकारिण इत्यर्थः । तस्मै रिपवे मावसृजः । मा त्याक्षीः । तदधीनं मा कुर्वित्यर्थः । तथा नोऽस्मान्दत्वते दंतवते दशते खादते सर्पादये मावसृजः । तथा नोऽस्मानदतेऽदंतकाय शृंगादिभिर्घातिने मावसृजः । तथा रिषते हिंसकाय तस्करराक्षसादये हे सहसावन् सहस्विन् मा परा दाः । पराभूतं मा देहि । सर्वथा न देहीत्यर्थः ॥

> *acyutāya bhaumāyaikakapālapuroḍāśahome mā no agna ityanayāśayamabhijuhoti | tathā ca sūtritaṃ | mā no agne 'va sṛjo aghāyetyenamāśayenābhijuhoti | ā, gṛ. 2-1-6 | iti ‖*
> *he agne no 'smānaghāya hiṃsakāyāviṣyave | aviṣyatirattikarmā | attecchave ducchunāyai | śunaṃ sukhaṃ | duṣṭasukhakāriṇe | duḥkhakāriṇa ityarthaḥ | tasmai ripave māvasṛjaḥ | mā tyākṣīḥ | tadadhīnaṃ mā kurvityarthaḥ | tathā no 'smāndatvate daṃtavate daśate khādate sarpādaye māvasṛjaḥ | tathā no 'smānadate 'daṃtakāya śṛṃgādibhirghātine māvasṛjaḥ | tathā riṣate hiṃsakāya taskararākṣasādaye he sahasāvan sahasvin mā parā dāḥ | parābhūtaṃ mā dehi | sarvathā na dehītyarthaḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; नः (*naḥ*) — us; अघाय (*aghāya*) — to the one who injures (the most sinful); अविष्यवे (*aviṣyave*) — the glutton; दुच्छुनायै (*ducchunāyai*) — and the one who causes sorrow; रिपवे (*ripave*) — to the enemy; मा अव सृजः (*mā ava sṛjaḥ*) — do not abandon (us) and make (us) subject to him; दत्वते (*datvate*) — to those that have teeth and the like; दशते (*daśate*) — and that bite, serpents and the like; मा (*mā*) — do not make (us) be caught and suffer; नः (*naḥ*) — us; अदते (*adate*) — to creatures that, without teeth, injure (with means such as horns); मा (*mā*) — do not let (us) be caught; (likewise) रिषते (*riṣate*) — do not abandon (us) to any other creature that does harm; सहसावन् (*sahasāvan*) — O mighty Agni; मा परा दाः (*mā parā dāḥ*) — do not make me the prey of defeat and disgrace.
