*Gist:* O Adhvaryus, fill with Soma juices that Indra, lord of the wealth of heaven, mid-region and earth, as a granary is filled with barley.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अध्वर्यवः (*adhvaryavaḥ*)—O Adhvaryus. यः (*yaḥ*)—the Indra who. दिव्यस्य (*divyasya*)—belonging to the world of heaven. वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*)—of all wealth. राजा (*rājā*)—is lord (so also). यः (*yaḥ*)—who. पार्थिवस्य (*pārthivasya*)—of the wealth of the vast mid-region. क्षम्यस्य (*kṣamyasya*)—of the terrestrial wealth, is the master. तं (*taṃ*)—that. इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra. यवेन (*yavena*)—with barley. ऊर्दरं न (*ūrdaraṃ na*)—as a granary is filled. सोमेभिः (*somebhiḥ*)—with Soma juices. पृणत (*pṛṇata*)—fill. तत् अपः (*tat apaḥ*)—such a rite. वः (*vaḥ*)—(for) your (welfare). अस्तु (*astu*)—may it be.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Adhvaryus, fill with Soma juices, as a granary is filled with barley, that Indra who is lord of all the wealth belonging to the world of heaven, and likewise of all the riches connected with the mid-region and the earth. May such a rite bring you welfare.

### Printed p. 750

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā; Maṃ. 2, A. 2, Sū. 14; p. 750.*

**Printed English translation**

Priests, fill with libations, as a granary(is filled) with barley, Indra, who is lord of the riches of heaven, of mid-heaven, of earth; and may such(pious) act be for your(good).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

यः दिव्यस्य वस्वः पार्थिवस्य क्षम्यस्य(वस्वः) राजा (*yaḥ divyasya vasvaḥ pārthivasya kṣamyasya(vasvaḥ) rājā*)—य इंद्रो द्युलोकार्हस्य वस्वो वसुनो राजा भवति। यश्च पार्थिवस्य पृथिवीशब्देन विस्तीर्णमंतरिक्षमुच्यते । तत्रत्यधनं पार्थिवं । तस्य राजा । यश्च क्षम्यस्य क्षमा भूमिः तत्रत्यं धनं क्षम्यं । तस्य च राजा भवति । (*ya iṃdro dyulokārhasya vasvo vasuno rājā bhavati| yaśca pārthivasya pṛthivīśabdena vistīrṇamaṃtarikṣamucyate | tatratyadhanaṃ pārthivaṃ | tasya rājā | yaśca kṣamyasya kṣamā bhūmiḥ tatratyaṃ dhanaṃ kṣamyaṃ | tasya ca rājā bhavati |*) Here the word पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*) is read among the names of the mid-region (Ni. 2-10); therefore the sage has described Indra as king (lord) of all the wealth that is in the heaven-world, in the mid-region and on the earth.

तं ऊर्दरं न पृणत यवेन इंद्रं सोमेभिः (*taṃ ūrdaraṃ na pṛṇata yavena iṃdraṃ somebhiḥ*)—Fill Indra, the owner of all wealth in earth, mid-region and heaven (that is, Indra's belly), with Soma juices, as a granary is filled with barley. In the previous Ṛk Indra's belly was compared to the udder of a cow filled with milk; in this Ṛk it is compared to a granary filled with barley. On the word ऊर्दर (*ūrdara*) Yāska has given this explanation:

ऊर्दरं कृदरमित्यावपनस्य । ऊर्दरमुद्दीर्णं भवंति ऊर्जे दीर्णं वा । तमूर्दरं न पृणता य वेन इत्यपि निगमो भवति। तमूर्दरमिव पूरयति यवेन । कृदरं कृतदरं भवति ॥ (*ūrdaraṃ kṛdaramityāvapanasya | ūrdaramuddīrṇaṃ bhavaṃti ūrje dīrṇaṃ vā | tamūrdaraṃ na pṛṇatā ya vena ityapi nigamo bhavati| tamūrdaramiva pūrayati yavena | kṛdaraṃ kṛtadaraṃ bhavati ‖*) ((२ २-२०) (*(2 2-20)*) [reference as printed; the digits and spacing are as supplied])

The word ऊर्दर (*ūrdara*) is stated, as ऊर्दरं कृदरं (*ūrdaraṃ kṛdaraṃ*), among the twenty-six "dviśa" names (Ni. 3-20); "dviśa names" are two words with one and the same meaning, that is, the two words ऊर्दरं कृदरं (*ūrdaraṃ kṛdaraṃ*) are synonyms. The word कृदर (*kṛdara*) is read among the names of houses (Ni. 3-13). The two words ऊर्दर (*ūrdara*) and कृदर (*kṛdara*) are names of an आवपन (*āvapana*) (a house for storing grain); or else, because it is filled up to the top, or because it is stored for food, a granary is called ऊर्दर (*ūrdara*). Having explained thus, he gave the present Ṛk itself as the example. This word ऊर्दर (*ūrdara*) is read in the Ṛgveda [printed ऋग्वदल्लि (*ṛgvadalli*), sic] only in this Ṛk; it is not used anywhere else.

### Printed p. 751

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 14; Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 751.*

(Continuing the Special Topics of Ṛk 11.) This word occurs once in the Rigved a (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-11) [as supplied] when reference is made to filling Indra with Soma as one fills an ऊर्दद (*ūrdada*) [as supplied; evidently a misreading of ऊर्दर] with grain (यव (*yava*)). Sayana renders it "granary" but Roth and Zimmer Seem [sic] more correct in simply making it a measure for holding grain or garner, (Vedic Index of names and subjects. p. 106) — this is the opinion of some English scholars. But since Sāyaṇa's explanation follows the opinion of Yāska, that alone is acceptable.

#### Ṛk 12

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अ॒स्मभ्यं॒ तद्व॑सो दा॒नाय॒ राधः॒ सम॑र्थयस्व ब॒हु ते॑ वस॒व्यं॑ ।
> इंद्र॒ यच्चि॒त्रं श्र॑व॒स्या अनु॒ द्यून्ब्र॒हद्व॑देम वि॒दथे॑ सु॒वीराः॑ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अस्मभ्यं । तत् । वसो इति । दानाय । राधः । सं । अर्थयस्व । बहु । ते । वसव्यं ।
> इंद्र । यत् । चित्रं । श्रवस्याः । अनु । द्यून् । बृहत् । वदेम । विदथे । सुवीराः

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> वसो सर्वस्य वासक वसुमन्ता हे इंद्र स्तोतृभ्योऽस्मभ्यं तद्राधो धनं
> दानाय । उपलक्षणमेतत् । भोगाय च समर्थयस्य । देहि । अस्मान् संगम-
> येत्यर्थः ॥ अर्थ याचने चुरादिरदंत आत्मनेपदी ॥ ते तव तद्बहु प्रभूतं
> वसव्यं ॥ वस्वेव वसव्यं । वस्वादित्वात् स्वार्थिको यत् ॥ तादृशं प्रभूतं धनमस्ति
> खलु । चित्रं चायनीयं यद्धनमनु द्यून् अन्वहं ॥ कालाध्वनोरिति द्वितीया ॥
> श्रवस्याः । भोग्यमिच्छेः ॥ अंतर्णीतण्यर्थत्पादकर्मकत्वं । यथा रोदितीति । स
> त्वन्यः । द्वे ह्यत्र कर्मणी उद्देश्यकर्म च विधेयकर्मांतर्भूतं । उद्देश्य-
> कर्मणा सकर्मको भविष्यति । यथा माणवकं पुत्रीयतीति भाष्य उदाहृतं । पा.
> ३-१-८-२ । श्रवःशब्दाच्छंदसि परेच्छायां क्यच् । तदंतस्य लेट्यडागमे रूपं ॥
> सुवीराः कल्याणपुत्रपौत्राः संतो वयं विदथेऽस्मिन्यज्ञॆ बृहत् प्रभूतं शस्त्रादिकं
> वाक्यं वदेम ॥

*Gist:* O Indra, lord of wealth, give us that abundant wealth for giving and for enjoyment; we, blessed with fine sons, will recite great śastra-hymns at this sacrifice.

### Printed p. 752

*Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā; Maṃ. 2, A. 2, Sū. 14; p. 752.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

वसो (वसो (*vaso*))—O wealthy one. इंद्र (इंद्र (*iṃdra*))—O Indra. चित्रं (चित्रं (*citraṃ*))—which is of many kinds and also delightful. यत् (यत् (*yat*))—which wealth. अनु द्यून् (अनु द्यून् (*anu dyūn*))—every day. श्रवस्याः (श्रवस्याः (*śravasyāḥ*))—whether we wish to enjoy it, or you wish us to enjoy it. ते (ते (*te*))—belonging to you, बहु (बहु (*bahu*))—abundant, वसव्यं (वसव्यं (*vasavyaṃ*))—rich in possessions: तत् राधः (तत् राधः (*tat rādhaḥ*))—that wealth. अस्मभ्यं (अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*))—to us. दानाय (दानाय (*dānāya*))—both for giving and for enjoyment. समर्थयस्व (समर्थयस्व (*samarthayasva*))—give completely. सुवीराः (सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*))—we, accompanied by excellent sons. विदथे (विदथे (*vidathe*))—at this sacrifice. बृहत् (बृहत् (*bṛhat*))—abundant śastra and other mantras. वदेम (वदेम (*vadema*))—we shall recite.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O wealthy Indra, give us completely that wealth which we wish to enjoy every day, which is abundant and rich in possessions with you, for giving and for enjoyment alike. We, accompanied by excellent sons, shall recite abundant śastra and other mantras at this sacrifice.

**Printed English translation**

Possessor of riches, exert your ability to bestow wealth upon us; for yours is great affluence: may you, Indra, be disposed to grant us exceeding abundance day by day, so that, blessed with worthy descendants, we may glorify you at(our) sacrificibe [sic].

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Having so far described in many ways the heroic deeds of Indra, the seer now, in this Ṛk, the last of the sūkta, praises Indra by way of conclusion and prays that he give wealth and the like.

वसो—सर्वस्य वासक वसुमन्वा हे इंद्र । (*vaso—sarvasya vāsaka vasumanvā he iṃdra |*) Two kinds of meaning are given for this word: "O Indra, who provides a dwelling-place for all", or "O Indra, who possesses wealth".

अस्मभ्यं दानाय राधः समर्थयस्व (*asmabhyaṃ dānāya rādhaḥ samarthayasva*)—The intention is: give us wealth both for giving to others and for our own enjoyment.

बहु ते वसव्यं (*bahu te vasavyaṃ*)—By this sentence the sense is suggested that Indra has abundant wealth and the like, and therefore is able to give wealth and the like to those who praise him.

### Printed p. 753

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 15; Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 753.*

इंद्र यत् चित्रं श्रवस्याः अनु द्यून् (*iṃdra yat citraṃ śravasyāḥ anu dyūn*)—O Indra, Indra is prayed to give us, who desire wealth, wealth and other things of many kinds every day.

बृहत् वदेम विदथे सुवीराः (*bṛhat vadema vidathe suvīrāḥ*)—the commentary says: सुवीराः कल्याणपुत्रपौत्राः संतो वयं विदथेऽस्मिन्यज्ञे बृहत् प्रभूतं शस्त्रादिकं वाक्यं वदेम (*suvīrāḥ kalyāṇaputrapautrāḥ saṃto vayaṃ vidathe 'sminyajñe bṛhat prabhūtaṃ śastrādikaṃ vākyaṃ vadema*). That is: accompanied by excellent sons and grandsons and by valiant attendants, we shall recite the śastra and other mantras abundantly at this sacrifice, for your pleasure, Indra; as was said in the preceding sūktas, the seer expresses this wish at the end of this sūkta too.

*The fifteenth sūkta.*

**Introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed)**

> प्र घा नव्येति दशर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं गार्त्समदं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । अत्रा-
> नुक्रमणिका प्र घ दशेति ॥ दशरात्रे षष्ठेऽहनि निष्केवल्ये त्रीणि सूक्तानि । तत्रेदं
> द्वितीयं । षष्ठस्येति खंडे सूत्रितं । एंद्र याहुप नः प्र घा नव्याभूरेक इति
> निष्केवल्यं । आ. ९-१ । इति ॥ त्रैकमामके निष्केवल्ये प्र घा नव्येत्येषा सूक्तमु-
> खीया । उशनःस्तोमे सूत्रितं । त्र्यर्यमा मनुषो देवताता प्र घा नव्य
> महतो महानि । आ. ९.५ । इति ॥

*Gist:* The fifteenth sūkta, *pra ghā navya*, has ten ṛks; the fourth sūkta of the second anuvāka; seer Gṛtsamada, deity Indra, metre Triṣṭubh; used in the Daśarātra, sixth day, in the Niṣkevalya śastra, and in the Traikamāmaka (Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, Ā. 9-1; Ā. 9.5).

**Anuvāda (Kannada)**

Translation—This sūkta beginning प्र घा नस्वस्य (*pra ghā nasvasya*) [as supplied; the Sanskrit above reads प्र घा नव्य (*pra ghā navya*)] is the fourth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has ten ṛks. Gṛtsamada is the seer of this sūkta, Indra the deity, Triṣṭubh the metre. The Anukramaṇikā says प्र घ दश (*pra gha daśa*) and so on. In the sacrifice called Daśarātra, on the sixth day, when the Niṣkevalya śastra mantras are recited, three sūktas are recited; of them this sūkta is the second. This matter is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section षष्ठस्य (*ṣaṣṭhasya*), by the sūtra एंद्र याह्युप नः प्र घा नस्व्याभूरेक इति निष्केवल्यं (*eṃdra yāhyupa naḥ pra ghā nasvyābhūreka iti niṣkevalyaṃ*) (Ā. 8-1) [as supplied; the Sanskrit above has Ā. 9-1]. Also in the Niṣkevalya śastra mantras recited in the sacrifice called Traikamāmaka, one Ṛk, the first Ṛk of this sūkta, प्र घा नस्वस्य (*pra ghā nasvasya*), is to be recited, as set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra by the sūtra त्र्यर्यमा मनुषो देवता प्र घा नस्वस्य महतो महानि (*tryaryamā manuṣo devatā pra ghā nasvasya mahato mahāni*) (Ā. 9-5).

### Printed p. 754

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3 (as printed), Sūkta 15; p. 754.*

## Sūkta 15 (Maṇḍala 2)

**Heading of the sūkta (as supplied)**

Om. Sūkta 15. Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 15. Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 15, 16. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Seer: Gṛtsamada (printed गृत्समदॆः (*gṛtsamadèḥ*)). Deity: Indra. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> प्र घा॒ न्व॑स्य मह॒तो म॒हानि॑ स॒त्या स॒त्यस्य॒ कर॑णानि वोचं ।
> त्रिक॑द्रुकेष्वपिबत्सु॒तस्या॒स्य मदे॒ अहि॒मिंद्रो॑ जघान ॥ १ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्र । घ । नु । अस्य । महतः । महानि । सत्या । सत्यस्य । करणानि । वोचं ।
> त्रिकद्रुकेषु । अपिबत् । सुतस्य । अस्य । मदे । अहिं । इंद्रः । जघान ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> गृत्समदो ब्रूते । महतो बलवतः सत्यस्य सत्यसंकल्पस्यास्येंद्रस्य सत्यानि
> यथार्थानि महानि महांति करणान्यस्मिन् सूक्ते वक्ष्यमाणानि कर्माणि नु अद्य
> प्र वोचं । प्रकर्षण ब्रवीमि ॥ वच परिभाषणे । छंदसि लुङ्ङिट् इति वर्तमाने
> लुजि अस्यतिवक्तिख्यातिभ्योऽज् । वच उम् ॥ घेति प्रसिद्दौ । कानि तानि उच्यंते!
> त्रिकद्रुकेषु ज्योतिर्गौरायुरित्येवंरूपेष्वाभिप्लविकेष्टहःसु सुतस्याभिषुतं सोम-
> मिंद्रोऽपिबत् । ततः पीतस्यास्य सोमस्य मदे हर्षॆ संजाते सतींद्रोऽहिं
> वृत्रमसुरं जघान । हतवान् ॥

*Gist:* Gṛtsamada speaks: I now proclaim the true, great deeds of the mighty and truthful Indra; at the Trikadruka days he drank the pressed Soma and, in the joy of it, slew Ahi (Vṛtra).

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

महतः (*mahataḥ*)—endowed with power, and सत्यस्य (*satyasya*)—of truthful nature; अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra. सत्या (*satyā*)—what is real, महानि (*mahāni*)—endowed with great qualities; करणानि (*karaṇāni*)—of the deeds, the distinction (continued on the next page).

### Printed p. 755

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 15; Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 755.*

**Pratipadārtha (continued)**

वैशिष्ट्यवन्नु (*vaiśiṣṭyavannu*) (the distinction). नु (*nu*)—now. प्र वोचं (*pra vocaṃ*)—I shall declare, proclaiming in an exceptional manner. घ (*gha*)—that is to say. त्रिकद्रुकेषु (*trikadrukeṣu*)—on the days of the Trikadruka. सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—the pressed Soma juice. अपिबत् (*apibat*)—(Indra) drank. अस्य (*asya*)—from drinking this Soma juice. मदे (*made*)—when joy arose. इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra. अहिं (*ahiṃ*)—the demon Vṛtra. जघान (*jaghāna*)—slew.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

I shall now proclaim in an exceptional manner the distinction of the deeds of Indra, who is endowed with power and truthful in nature, deeds that are real and endowed with great qualities. That is: on the days of the Trikadruka Indra drank the pressed Soma juice, and when joy arose from drinking this Soma juice Indra slew the demon Vṛtra.

**Printed English translation**

Verily, I proclaim the great and authentic deeds of the mighty and true(Indra); of him who drank the effused juices at the Trikadruka rites, and in his exhilaration slew Ahi.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this sūkta it is described how Indra drank Soma and, in the joy that arose from it, performed various heroic deeds. In each Ṛk one or two heroic deeds of Indra are described, and the statement that Indra did such a deed in the exhilaration of drinking Soma is made by the sentence सोमस्य ता मद इंद्रश्चकार (*somasya tā mada iṃdraścakāra*). This sentence is repeated at the end of every Ṛk like a refrain (the supplied text prints परितवागिदॆ (*paritavāgidè*), evidently a slip for the word meaning "repeated").

The word घ (*gha*) is used in the sense of "well known". For the convenience of the metre the vowel is lengthened in the Saṃhitā-pāṭha.

प्र घ नु अस्य महतः महानि सत्या सत्यस्य करणानि वोचं (*pra gha nu asya mahataḥ mahāni satyā satyasya karaṇāni vocaṃ*)—the commentary says: बलवतः सत्यसंकल्पस्येंद्रस्य यथार्थानि वक्ष्यमाणानि महांति कर्माणि आद्य प्रकर्षण ब्रवीमि (*balavataḥ satyasaṃkalpasyeṃdrasya yathārthāni vakṣyamāṇāni mahāṃti karmāṇi ādya prakarṣaṇa bravīmi*). That is: I shall now describe well the real and grand deeds, many and heroic, of Indra, who is endowed with great strength and valour; the seer says this in the opening sentence of the sūkta, and accordingly in every Ṛk he describes some qualities or deeds of Indra and says that Indra did such a deed in the elation of drinking Soma.

त्रिकद्रुकेषु अपिबत् सुतस्य अस्य मदेः अहिं इंद्रः जघान (*trikadrukeṣu apibat sutasya asya madeḥ ahiṃ iṃdraḥ jaghāna*) (so printed, मदेः (*madeḥ*))—Indra drank the Soma pressed and prepared on the first three days, called Jyotiḥ, Gauḥ and Āyuḥ, of the sacrifice named Abhiplava, and by its exhilaration (joy) destroyed the demon Vṛtra; thus the slaying of Vṛtra, the chief heroic deed of Indra,

### Printed p. 756

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 15; p. 756.*

**Special Topics (continued)**

is described at the beginning. The various meanings of the word अहि (*ahi*) we have explained at length before.

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अ॒वं॒शे द्याम॑स्तभायद्बृ॒हंत॒मा रोद॑सी अप्पणदं॒तरि॑क्षं ।
> स धा॑रयत्पृथि॒वीं प॒प्रथ॑च्च॒ सोम॑स्य॒ ता मद॒ इंद्र॑श्चकार ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अवंशे । द्यां । अस्तभायत् । बृहंतं । आ । रोदसी इति । अपृणत् । अंतरिक्षं ।
> सः । धारयत् । पृथिवीं । प्रप्रथत् । च । सोमस्य । ता । मदे । इंद्रः । चकार ॥२॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> अवंश आकाशे द्यां द्योतमानं सूर्यं द्युलोकं वास्तभायत् ।
> इंद्रोऽस्तभ्नात् । अनवलंबनस्य तस्यावस्थापनमकरोदित्यर्थः ॥ स्तंभु इति सौत्रो
> धातुः क्रादिः । लजु व्यत्ययो बहुलमित्यहावपि शायजादेशः ॥ बृहंतं महदंत-
> रिक्षं रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ चापृणत् । स्वतेजसा पूरितवान् । किंच स इंद्रः पृथि-
> वीं विस्तीर्णां भूमिं धारयत् । आधारयत् । तथा पप्रथच्च । एनां भूममप्रथ-
> यत् ॥ प्रथ प्रख्याने । ण्यंतस्य लुजु चजु रूपं । चङ्गन्यतरस्यामिति मध्योदा-
> त्तत्वं ॥ सोमस्य मदे हर्षे संजाते सति तानीमानि कर्माणींद्रश्चकार ॥

*Gist:* Indra, in the empty sky, fixed heaven (or the sun), filled the great atmosphere and the two worlds with his splendour, held the earth and spread it out; all this in the exhilaration of Soma.

The grammatical remarks of the commentary (the root *stambh*, the substitution of the Vedic ending, the root *prath* in the causative aorist and its accent) are not explained here.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अवंशे (*avaṃśe*)—in the sky, which has no support. द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the heaven, or the shining sun (the supplied text prints सूरनन्नु (*sūranannu*)). अस्तभायत् (*astabhāyat*)—established. बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*)—great. अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the atmosphere also. रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth. आपृणत् (*āpṛṇat*)—filled (with his splendour). सः (*saḥ*)—that Indra. पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the extended earth (printed विस्त्रतवाद (*vistratavāda*)). धारयत् (*dhārayat*)—held up. पप्रथच्च (*paprathacca*)—and made it known so that it is famous in the world. सोमस्य (*somasya*)—from drinking Soma juice. मदे (*made*)—when joy arose. ता (*tā*)—these great deeds. इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra. चकार (*cakāra*)—performed.

### Printed p. 757

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 15] Ṛgvedasaṃhitā; p. 757.*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Indra fixed the heaven and the shining sun in the unsupported sky. He filled the great atmosphere and heaven and earth with his splendour. That Indra upheld the extended earth and made it renowned. When joy arose from drinking the Soma juice, Indra performed these great deeds.

**Printed English translation**

Who fixed the heaven in unsupported(space), and filled the spacious firmament, and heaven, and earth,(with light): he it is who has upheld and has made the earth renowned: in the exhilaration of the Soma, Indra has done these(deeds).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

अवंशे (*avaṃśe*)—आकाशे (*ākāśe*): "in the sky, or in the atmosphere" is the commentator's explanation. The word अवंश (*avaṃśa*) occurs in the Ṛgveda in this Ṛk and in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-58-1; nowhere else.

द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—द्योतमानं सूर्यं द्युलोकं वा (*dyotamānaṃ sūryaṃ dyulokaṃ vā*): either of two meanings may be taken, the shining sun or the world of heaven (svarga). And there is the etymological statement that द्युः (*dyuḥ*) is a name of the day (अहः (*ahaḥ*)) (Ni. 1-7). The word द्यौः (*dyauḥ*) is read among the names of day (Ni. 2-21), and there is also the explanation द्यौरादित्यो भवति (*dyaurādityo bhavati*) ("heaven is the sun"). Here, as the commentator says, the meaning sun or heaven-world may be given to the word.

In this Ṛk it is said that Indra fixed the sun in the sky, which has no support or foundation; that he filled the atmosphere and heaven and earth with his boundless splendour; and that he made the earth stand firm so that it does not move. These are the heroic deeds he performed, and it is said that he did all these deeds out of the joy born of drinking Soma.

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> सद्मे॑व॒ प्राचो॒ वि मि॑माय॒ मानै॒र्वज्रे॑ण॒ खान्य॑तृणन्न॒दीनां॑ ।
> वृथा॑सृजत्प॒थिभि॑र्दीर्घया॒थैः सोम॑स्य॒ ता मद॒ इंद्र॑श्चकार ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सद्मइव । प्राचः । वि । मिमाय । मानैः । वज्रेण । खानि । अतृणत् । नदीनां ।
> वृथा । असृजत् । पथिभिः । दीर्घयाथैः । सोमस्य । ता । मदे । इंद्रः । चकार ॥
> ॥ ३ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> प्राक्प्रवणान् कुर्वंति तद्वत् सिंधून् लोकान्वानृजून्वा मानैः परिमाणैः प्राचः
> प्राज्मुखान्विमिमाय । इंद्रो विशेषेण निर्मितवान् । तथा नदीनां खानि निर्गमन-
> द्वाराणि वज्रेण चातृणत् । अखनत् । तृदि हिंसानादरयोः । रुधादि । लज् ॥ तथा च
> मंत्रः । इंद्रो अस्मा अरदद्वज्रबाहुः । ३-३३-६ । इति । तथा दीर्घयाथैर्बहु-
> कालं गंतवैः पथिभिर्मार्गेर्वृथास्पृजत् । अनायासेन ता नदीः सृष्टवान् । सोम-
> स्यॆति सिद्धार्थ इति ॥

*Gist:* As men build a sacrificial house by measures, Indra measured out the eastern quarters (or the worlds); he dug the outlets of the rivers with the thunderbolt and sent them forth without effort along long courses.

The grammatical remark of the commentary (the root *tṛd*, of the Rudhādi class, with the Vedic ending) is not explained here.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

सद्म इव (*sadma iva*)—as a sacrificial house is measured and built with measuring instruments. मानैः (*mānaiḥ*)—with measures. प्राचः (*prācaḥ*)—the east-facing quarters. वि मिमाय (*vi mimāya*)—measured out and built in a special manner. नदीनां (*nadīnāṃ*)—for the rivers. खानि (*khāni*)—the outlets for flowing. वज्रेण (*vajreṇa*)—with the thunderbolt. अतृणत् (*atṛṇat*)—dug (and). दीर्घयाथैः (*dīrghayāthaiḥ*)—flowing for a long time. पथिभिः (*pathibhiḥ*)—by paths. वृथा (*vṛthā*)—without effort (without hindrance). असृजत् (*asṛjat*)—created so that they flow. सोमस्य (*somasya*)—by the drinking of Soma juice. मदे (*made*)—when joy arose. ता (*tā*)—these great deeds. इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra. चकार (*cakāra*)—performed.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

As one measures and builds a sacrificial house with measuring instruments, Indra measured out and built the east-facing quarters in a special manner. He dug outlets for the rivers to flow in a special manner

### Printed p. 759

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 15] Ṛgvedasaṃhitā; p. 759.*

**Bhāvārtha (continued)**

and by paths flowing for a long time he created them so that they flow without hindrance. When joy arose from drinking the Soma juice, Indra performed these great deeds.

**Printed English translation**

(He it is) who has measured thc [sic] eastern(quarters) with measures like a chamber; who has dug with the thunderbolt the beds of the rivers, and has easily sent them forth by long-continued paths: in the exhilaration of the Soma, Indra has done these(deeds).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this Ṛk three heroic deeds of Indra are described. सद्मेव प्राचो वि मिमाय मानैः (*sadmeva prāco vi mimāya mānaiḥ*)—Indra built the quarters beginning with the east according to the measures by which sacrificial houses must be built. Here सद्म (*sadma*) may mean a sacrificial house, or it may mean an ordinary dwelling-house. But for an ordinary house there is no rule that it must have just such a measure; only when a sacrificial house is built must it be built following the rules and regulations relating to it. Therefore, from the use of the word मानैः (*mānaiḥ*) ("by measures") in this sentence, the meaning "sacrificial house" for the word सद्म (*sadma*) is what is to be understood.

वज्रेण खानि अतृणत् नदीनां (*vajreṇa khāni atṛṇat nadīnāṃ*)—Since the thunderbolt is Indra's chief instrument for any work he has to do, it is described here that Indra dug with the thunderbolt the channels in which the rivers flow, or the river-beds. In this matter, as an example of the same meaning, the passage इंद्रो अस्मै अरदद्वज्रबाहुरपाहन्वृत्रं परिधिं नदीनां । (*iṃdro asmai aradadvajrabāhurapāhanvṛtraṃ paridhiṃ nadīnāṃ |*) (Ma. Saṃ. 3-33-6 [as printed]) has been given.

वृथा असृजत् पथिभिः दीर्घयाथैः (*vṛthā asṛjat pathibhiḥ dīrghayāthaiḥ*)—Indra created the river-beds mentioned above effortlessly, that is, without any kind of labour, as rivers flowing by paths of long duration or very great length. Here the word वृथा (*vṛthā*) means "effortlessly". When we have to do any work, much labour must be spent; but Indra created the beds of all the rivers, extending over many yojanas, without any labour, is the meaning intended. For the word दीर्घयाथैः (*dīrghayāthaiḥ*) the meaning "flowing for a very long time or for a very great distance"

**Special Topics (continued)**

it can be said to have two kinds of meaning: "flowing". पथिभिः (*pathibhiḥ*) पथिभिः (*pathibhiḥ*) means "by paths" or "by river-beds". In this sentence the word नदीः (*nadīḥ*) ("the rivers") must be supplied.

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स प्र॑वो॒ळ्हन्प॑रि॒गत्या॑ द॒भीते॒र्विश्व॑मधा॒गायु॑धमि॒द्दे आ॒ग्नौ ।
> सं गोभि॒रश्वै॑रसृज॒द्रथे॑भिः॒ सोम॑स्य॒ ता मद॒ इंद्र॑श्चकार ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सं । गोभिः । अश्वैः । असृजत् । रथेभिः । सोमस्य । ता । मदे । इंद्रः । चकार ॥४॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> प्राक्किल चुमुरिधुनिप्रभृतयोऽसुरा दभीतेः पुरं संरुध्य परिगृह्य तस्मात्पु-
> रान्निरगुरिति कथा । स इंद्रो दभीतेः । दभीतिर्नाम कश्चिद्राजर्षिः । तस्य प्रवोळ्हान्
> प्रवोढन् ॥ सहिवहोरोदवर्णस्येत्योत्वं ॥ प्रकर्षेण तं दभीतिं वहतस्तानसु-
> रान् मध्यॆ मार्गं परिगण्य तेषां विश्वं सर्वमायुधमिद्धेऽग्नौ दीप्यमाने
> वह्नावधाक् । अधाक्षीत् ॥ दहेर्लुजि मंत्रे घसेत्यादिना चेर्लुक् ॥ पश्चात्तं
> दभीतिं गोभिरश्वै रथेभी रथैश्च समसृजत् । संयोजितवान् । सोमस्यादि सिद्ध-
> मिति ॥

> *prākkila cumuridhuniprabhṛtayo 'surā dabhīteḥ puraṃ saṃrudhya parigṛhya tasmātpu-*
> *rānniraguriti kathā | sa iṃdro dabhīteḥ | dabhītirnāma kaścidrājarṣiḥ | tasya pravoḷhān*
> *pravoḍhan ‖ sahivahorodavarṇasyetyotvaṃ ‖ prakarṣeṇa taṃ dabhītiṃ vahatastānasu-*
> *rān madhyè mārgaṃ parigaṇya teṣāṃ viśvaṃ sarvamāyudhamiddhe 'gnau dīpyamāne*
> *vahnāvadhāk | adhākṣīt ‖ daherluji maṃtre ghasetyādinā cerluk ‖ paścāttaṃ*
> *dabhītiṃ gobhiraśvai rathebhī rathaiśca samasṛjat | saṃyojitavān | somasyādi siddha-*
> *miti ‖*

Gist: In the past the Asuras Chumuri, Dhuni and others besieged the city of Dabhiti and seized him; Indra met them on the way, burnt all their weapons in the fire and gave Dabhiti their cattle, horses and chariots. The commentary then adds grammatical remarks (on प्रवोळ्हान् (*pravoḷhān*) and अधाक् (*adhāk*)), not explained here.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

सः (*saḥ*)—Indra. दभीतेः (*dabhīteḥ*)—the royal sage named Dabhiti. प्रवोळ्हान् (*pravoḷhān*)—the Asuras who were carrying (him) off. परिगत्य (*parigatya*)—confronting. विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—their entire. आयुधं (*āyudhaṃ*)—weapons. इद्दे (*idde*)—in the kindled. आग्नौ (*āgnau*)—fire. अधाक् (*adhāk*)—he burnt. गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with (the Asuras') cattle. अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)—with horses. रथेभिः (*rathebhiḥ*)—with chariots. समसृजत् (*samasṛjat*)—he united Dabhiti (with them). सोमस्य (*somasya*)—by the drinking of Soma juice. मदे (*made*)—when joy arose. ता (*tā*)—these great deeds. इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra. चकार (*cakāra*)—performed.

### Printed p. 761

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 15] Ṛgvedasaṃhitā; p. 761.*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Indra confronted the Asuras who were carrying off the royal sage Dabhiti, and burnt all their weapons in the kindled fire. Their cattle, horses and chariots he caused to be given over to Dabhiti. When joy arose from drinking the Soma juice, Indra accomplished these great deeds.

**Printed English translation**

Encountering the(Asuras), carrying off Dabhiti, he burnt all their weapons in a kindled fire, and enriched(the prince) with their cattle, their horses, and their chariots: in the exhilaration of the Soma, Indraa [sic] has done these(deeds).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this Ṛk Indra's protection of the royal sage Dabhiti is described. In Ṛk 1-112-23 of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā it is said that the Aśvins protected Dabhiti. But since everywhere else it is Indra who is said to have protected Dabhiti, it is only right that this heroic deed be attributed to Indra. Dabhiti has been mentioned on page 707 of this same part. The commentator says: in the past the two Asuras named Chumuri and Dhuni besieged the city of the royal sage Dabhiti and, while they were fleeing with him abducted, Indra killed those Asuras and protected Dabhiti; this is the story, and it is what is described in this Ṛk.

इंद्रो धुनिं च चुमुरिं च दंभयञ्छद्धामनस्या शृणुते दभीतये । (*iṃdro dhuniṃ ca cumuriṃ ca daṃbhayañchaddhāmanasyā śṛṇute dabhītaye |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-113-9)

स्वप्नेनाभ्युप्या चुमुरिं धुनिं च जघंथ दस्युं प्र दभीतिमावः । (*svapnenābhyupyā cumuriṃ dhuniṃ ca jaghaṃtha dasyuṃ pra dabhītimāvaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-15-9)

त्वं नि दस्युं चुमुरिं धुनिं चास्वापयो दभीतये सुहंतु । (*tvaṃ ni dasyuṃ cumuriṃ dhuniṃ cāsvāpayo dabhītaye suhaṃtu |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-19-4) (the reference is printed twice, the second time with the abbreviation Ma. Saṃ.)

In these Ṛks it is said that Indra made the Asuras Chumuri and Dhuni fall into a deep sleep, that is, swoon, and so released and protected Dabhiti.

तव ह त्यदिंद्र विश्वमाजौ सस्तो धुनीचुमुरी या ह सिष्वप् । (*tava ha tyadiṃdra viśvamājau sasto dhunīcumurī yā ha siṣvap |*)
दीदयदित्तुभ्यं सोमेभिः सुन्वन् दभीतिरिध्मभृतिः पक्थ्यंर्कैः ॥ (*dīdayadittubhyaṃ somebhiḥ sunvan dabhītiridhmabhṛtiḥ pakthyaṃrkaiḥ ‖*) (Ma. Saṃ. 6-20-13)

### Printed p. 762

*Running head: 762 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; [Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 15].*

त्वं श्रद्धाभिर्मंदसानः सोमैर्दभीतये चुमुरिमिंद्र सिष्वप् । (*tvaṃ śraddhābhirmaṃdasānaḥ somairdabhītaye cumurimiṃdra siṣvap |*) (Ma. Saṃ. 6-26-6)

In these Ṛks it is said that Indra drank the Soma juice prepared by Dabhiti, was gladdened by it, put the Asuras Chamuri and Dhuni to sleep in battle, and protected the royal sage Dabhiti who was being harmed by them.

अस्वापयद्दभीतये सहस्रा त्रिंशतं हथैः । दासानामिंद्रो मायमा । (*asvāpayaddabhītaye sahasrā triṃśataṃ hathaiḥ | dāsānāmiṃdro māyamā |*) (Ma. Saṃ. 4-30-21)

In this Ṛk it is said that, to protect Dabhiti, Indra by the power of his magic put to sleep 30000 (thirty thousand) Dasyu people who were his enemies. These thirty thousand Dasyus may have been the soldiers of the Asuras Chamuri and Dhuni; the main sense is that in the battle they fought with Dabhiti, Indra bewildered the enemy soldiers and protected Dabhiti. It must be called a peculiarity of this subject that wherever Indra is said to have protected Dabhiti, it is said that he put the enemy soldiers, or Dabhiti's chief enemies, the Asuras Dhuni and Chamuri, into a sleep by his magic.

Further, one or two matters concerning the protection of Dabhiti that are not found in the other descriptions of it are stated in this Ṛk: that the enemies carried Dabhiti off (from his town); that their weapons were thrown into the burning fire and destroyed; and that Indra brought the enemies' cattle, horses, chariots and so on into Dabhiti's possession. These are found only in this Ṛk; the description of Dabhiti's protection in the other Ṛks does not have them. But the putting of Dabhiti's enemies to sleep is mentioned there. Probably the expression "put to sleep" is used in the sense of "made them swoon" or "bewildered them".

> त उ॒त्स्नाय॑ र॒यिम॒भि प्र त॑स्थुः॒ सोम॑स्य॒ ता मद॒ इंद्र॑श्चकार ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 763

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 15] Ṛgvedasaṃhitā; p. 763.*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । ईं । महीं । धुनिं । एतोः । अरम्नात् । सः । अस्नात्यन् । अपारयत् । स्वस्ति ।
> ते । उत्स्नाय । रयिं । अभि । प्र । तस्थुः । सोमस्य । ता! मदे । इंद्रः । चकार॥

Gist: Atimūrti is a one-day sacrifice, and this Ṛk opens the Marutvatīya recitation; the commentary explains धुनिं (*dhuniṃ*) as a river that shakes off the sins of the praisers, and says Indra made the river shallow so that the sages could cross; the grammatical remarks are not explained here.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

सः (*saḥ*)—Indra. महीं (*mahīṃ*)—the great; ईं धुनिं (*īṃ dhuniṃ*)—and sin-destroying this river. एतोः (*etoḥ*)—for the passage (of the sages). अरम्यात् (*aramyāt*)—(reducing the water) he stilled. सः (*saḥ*)—the same Indra. आस्नात्यन् (*āsnātyan*)—the sages who were unable to cross. स्वस्ति (*svasti*)—in safety. अपारयत् (*apārayat*)—he conveyed across. ते (*te*)—those great sages. उत्स्नायॆ (*utsnāyè*)—having crossed the river. रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—towards the wealth they aimed at. प्र तस्थुः (*pra tasthuḥ*)—set out. सोमस्य (*somasya*)—by the drinking of Soma juice. मदे (*made*)—when joy arose. ता (*tā*)—these great deeds. इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra. चकार (*cakāra*)—performed.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Indra stilled this great, sin-destroying river so that the sages might pass. The same Indra conveyed in safety the sages who were unable to cross. Those great sages, having crossed the river, set out towards the wealth they aimed at. When joy arose from drinking the Soma juice, Indra performed these great deeds.

**Printed English translation**

He tranquillized this great river,(so that it) might be crossed; he conveyed across it in safety(the sages) who had been unable to pass over it

### Printed p. 764

*Running head: 764 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 15].*

and who, having crossed, procceded [sic] to realize the wealth they sought: in the exhilaration of the Soma, Indra has done these(deeds).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

This Ṛk is prescribed as the first Ṛk of the sūkta at the start of the Marutvatīya śastra mantras in the one-day sacrifice named Atimūrti; this is made explicit by the sūtra स ईं महीं धुनिमेतोररम्णात् (*sa īṃ mahīṃ dhunimetoraramṇāt*) in the section अतिमूर्तिना (*atimūrtinā*) of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 9-8).

धुनिं (*dhuniṃ*)—The word धुनयः (*dhunayaḥ*) is read among the names of rivers (Ni. 2-24). The commentator explains this word: धुनोति स्तोत्थणां पापानीति धुनिः परुष्ठि नदी (*dhunoti stotthaṇāṃ pāpānīti dhuniḥ paruṣṭhi nadī*), that is, because it destroys the sins of those who praise, it is a धुनिः (*dhuniḥ*), a river; here he explains it as the river Paruṣṭī (printed षरुष्ठि (*ṣaruṣṭhi*)). In the Nirukta the commentator on the Nirukta says: धुनयः । धूञ् कंपने भौवादिः । धुन्वंति कंपयंति तीरवृक्षादीनि, कंपंते वा स्वयं गमनशीलत्वात् (*dhunayaḥ | dhūñ kaṃpane bhauvādiḥ | dhunvaṃti kaṃpayaṃti tīravṛkṣādīni, kaṃpaṃte vā svayaṃ gamanaśīlatvāt*); that is, the word धुनि (*dhuni*) is formed from the root धूञ् कंपने (*dhūñ kaṃpane*); rivers are called धुनयः (*dhunayaḥ*) because they make the trees on the banks tremble, or because the water itself trembles, being of a moving nature as it flows.

सः ईं महीं धुनिं एतोः अरम्मात् (*saḥ īṃ mahīṃ dhuniṃ etoḥ arammāt*)—महाजलां नदीमल्लोदकामकरोदित्यर्थः (*mahājalāṃ nadīmallodakāmakarodityarthaḥ*). The main sense is that this Indra, by reducing the water of a great river, filled with much water, deep, wide-bedded and in flood, made it possible for people to cross. In former times it was not possible for ordinary people to cross great rivers flowing deep and wide. To cross rivers with much water and wide beds, such as the Sindhu and the Gaṅgā, was a great problem. There were no big boats. To cross by other means, such as a small boat or a coracle, was dangerous. There was not even a name for bridges. In such times crossing rivers, or helping others across, was regarded as a great feat of daring. Therefore it is described that Indra reduced the river's water itself and made crossing possible, and this is mentioned as one of Indra's exploits.

सः अस्नात्यन् आपारयत् स्वस्ति (*saḥ asnātyan āpārayat svasti*)—तरणासमर्थान् ऋषीन् क्षेमेणापारयत् (*taraṇāsamarthān ṛṣīn kṣemeṇāpārayat*). Indra conveyed in safety the sages who, unable to cross the great rivers, were in difficulty. In this sentence the word अस्नात्यन् (*asnātyan*) means only "unable to cross", so

### Printed p. 765

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 16] Ṛgvedasaṃhitā; p. 765.*

it need not be said that Indra conveyed only sages. It may be said that he conveyed kings or the warriors on the kings' side who praise Indra, or other people. Moreover, because of the following sentence ते उत्साय रयिं अभि प्र तस्थुः (*te utsāya rayiṃ abhi pra tasthuḥ*), "they crossed the river and went forward to gain wealth" (that is, because the word रयिं (*rayiṃ*), "for the gaining of wealth", is used in this sentence), those who cross the river for gain of wealth and go to other countries may be kings, kings' soldiers, merchants seeking wealth, ordinary people and so on, any of them. It cannot be said that it applies only to sages. Even if sages desire wealth, they need not travel through countries for it; they can obtain it simply by praying to Indra.

Gist: Indra turned the river Sindhu, flowing east, to face north by his greatness; he crushed Ushas's cart with his thunderbolt and, with swift forces, scattered the slow, weak ones. The commentary adds grammatical remarks on the root व्रश्च (*vraśca*), not explained here.

### Printed p. 766

*Running head: [Maṃ. 2, A. 2, Sū. 15] Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā; p. 766.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

He, Indra; the river Sindhu (that was flowing eastwards) by his greatness turned so that it flows northwards (*udañcam*, "northward"); of Ushas, the goddess of dawn, the weak (*ajavasaḥ*) armies, with his swift (*javinībhiḥ*) forces, scattering and destroying them completely (*vivṛścan*); her cart (*anaḥ*) with his thunderbolt he ground to pieces (*saṃ pipeṣa*); in the exhilaration produced by drinking Soma; these great deeds; Indra; did.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Indra, by his greatness, made the river that was flowing eastwards flow northwards. Scattering and destroying completely the weak armies of the goddess Ushas with his own swift forces, he ground her cart to pieces with his thunderbolt. Indra did these great deeds when he was exhilarated by drinking Soma.

**Printed English**

By his great power he turned the Sindhu towards the north; with his thunderbolt he ground to pieces the waggon of the dawn, scattering the tardy enemy with his swift forces, in the exhilaration of the Soma, Indra has done these(deeds).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

सः उदंचं सिंधुं अरिणात् महित्वा (*saḥ udaṃcaṃ siṃdhuṃ ariṇāt mahitvā*): the Sanskrit gloss given here is स इंद्रः सिंधुं प्रांचं संतं महित्वा (*sa iṃdraḥ siṃdhuṃ prāṃcaṃ saṃtaṃ mahitvā*) followed by स्वकीयेन महिन्नोदंचमरिणात् उदज्मुखमकरोत् (*svakīyena mahinnodaṃcamariṇāt udajmukhamakarot*). The text says here that Indra, by his greatness, turned a river that was flowing towards the east so that it flows towards the north. It is not clear whether the word सिंधुं (*siṃdhuṃ*) here means any river in general or the famous river called Sindhu. Since the Sindhu does not flow either towards the east or towards the north, some other river must be meant; it is not possible to say which. Because this same matter is indicated in Ṛg-veda Saṃhitā 4-30-11, the river may perhaps be the Vipāśī, as said there. Or, because the river Sindhu is mentioned in Ṛg-veda Saṃhitā 4-30-12, it may be the Sindhu after all.

वज्रेण अनः उषसः संपिपेष (*vajreṇa anaḥ uṣasaḥ saṃpipeṣa*): Indra crushed, that is, ground to powder, with his thunderbolt the cart or chariot of the goddess Ushas. This matter—

(The page ends here, mid-sentence; the continuation, from p. 767 onwards, belongs to a part that is already done elsewhere.)

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist: Long ago maidens mocked the lame and blind sage Parāvṛj; he praised Indra, gained eyes and feet, and then saw and overtook them.*

> पुरा किल कन्यकाश्चक्षुर्हीनं पादहीनं परावृजं जिघृक्षुमृषिं दृष्ट्वाभिदु-
> द्रुवुः । ततः स ऋषियिंद्रं स्तुत्वा चक्षुः पादं च लेभे । तदेतदाह । कनीनां कन्य-
> कानामपगोहमपगोहनं तिरोभावं विद्वान् परावृगृषिराविर्भवन् सर्वेषां
> प्रत्यक्षो भवन् उदतिष्ठत् । श्रोणः पूर्वं पंगुरिदानीमिंद्रस्य प्रसादाद्विभग्न-
> जानुस्ताः कन्याः प्रति स्थात् । पूर्वमंधोऽधुना चक्षुर्लाभाद्व्यचष्ट । ताः कन्यका
> विशेषेण पश्यति स्म । तानीमानि कर्माणि स इंद्रश्चकार ॥

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

कनीनां (*kanīnāṃ*)—of the maidens. अपगोहं (*apagohaṃ*)—the disappearance (hiding). विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—knowing. सः परावृक् (*saḥ parāvṛk*)—that sage named Parāvṛk. आविर्भवन् (*āvirbhavan*)—becoming visible to all. उदतिष्ठत् (*udatiṣṭhat*)—stood up. श्रोणः (*śroṇaḥ*)—having formerly been lame, and having by Indra's favour got his leg properly. प्रति स्थात् (*prati sthāt*)—he chased those maidens and caught them. अनक् (*anak*)—having formerly been blind and now having got eyes. व्यचष्ट (*vyacaṣṭa*)—he saw them all. सोमस्य (*somasya*)—by the drinking of the soma juice. मदे (*made*)—when exhilaration arose. ता (*tā*)—these great deeds. इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra. चकार (*cakāra*)—did.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The Kannada (the label is printed बानार्थ (*bānārtha*), as supplied): "The sage named Parāvṛk, knowing the disappearance (hiding) of the maidens who were mocking him, became visible to all and stood up. Having formerly been lame, and having by Indra's favour got his leg properly, he chased those maidens and caught them. Having formerly been blind, and afterwards having got eyes, he saw them all. When exhilaration arose from the drinking of the soma juice, Indra did these great deeds." *(The text twice prints कनैयर (*kanaiyara*) for कन्यॆयर (*kanyèyara*), as supplied.)*

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

Conscious of the disappearancee [sic] of the damsels, tho(Rishi) [sic] Paravrij, becoming manifest, stood up; the lame man overtook(them), the blind man beheld(them): in the exhilaration of the Soma, Indra has done these(deeds).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

परावृक् (*parāvṛk*)—He is a sage. He was lame and blind. It is said in many places that by Indra's favour he obtained legs and eyes. We have described him at length on pages 715–717 of this same volume.

### Printed p. 769

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 6 V. 16", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "769". The page begins with the continuing commentary on the preceding Ṛk.)*

सः विद्वान् अपगोहं कनीनां आविः भवन् उदतिष्ठत् परावृक् (*saḥ vidvān apagohaṃ kanīnāṃ āviḥ bhavan udatiṣṭhat parāvṛk*)—The Kannada: "In former times there was a very intelligent sage named Parāvṛk. He had no legs and was lame. His eyes also could not see; therefore he was blind. Seeing this, some maidens (girls), out of mischief, came near him and, troubling him in various ways, went on mocking him. If he resisted, they would run far away. This sage, being lame, had no strength to catch them. Therefore he praised Indra, and Indra, pleased with his prayer, gave him legs and eyes. By that he became able to walk and see like everyone. That is what is described in this Ṛk. While those maidens were looking on, this sage appeared before them and stood up. Until then those maidens were not visible to him; now they became visible. Until then he had no strength to walk. Now, because legs had come, he stood up before them like everyone else, or chased them and caught them. This is the main purport."

प्रति श्रोणः स्थात्—पूर्वं पंगुरिदानीमिंद्रस्य प्रसादाद्विभग्नजानुस्ताः कन्याः प्रति स्थात् । (*prati śroṇaḥ sthāt—pūrvaṃ paṃguridānīmiṃdrasya prasādādvibhagnajānustāḥ kanyāḥ prati sthāt |*) The Kannada: "Formerly he was lame without legs. Now, because legs had come by Indra's favour, he stood up before those maidens."

वि अनक् अचष्ट—पूर्वमंधोऽधुना चक्षुर्लाभाद्व्यचष्ट । ताः कन्याका विशेषेण पश्यति स्म । (*vi anak acaṣṭa—pūrvamaṃdho 'dhunā cakṣurlābhādvyacaṣṭa | tāḥ kanyākā viśeṣeṇa paśyati sma |*) The Kannada: "Having formerly been blind, he could see nothing. Now, because eyes had come, he saw well those maidens (कन्निकॆयरन्नु (*kannikèyarannu*)) who were before him. This is the main purport."

> सोमस्य मदे सति चकारेति ॥

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra) दस्युं (*dasyuṃ*)—the violent, चुमुरिं (*chumuriṃ*)—Asura named Chumuri, धुनिं च (*dhuniṃ ca*)—and the Asura named Dhuni; स्वप्नेन (*svapnena*)—with long sleep, अभ्युप्य (*abhyupya*)—joining (them), जघंथ (*jaghaṃtha*)—you have killed. दभीतिं (*dabhītiṃ*)—the royal sage named Dabhiti; प्र आवः (*pra āvaḥ*)—you have protected fully. रंभी चित् (*raṃbhī cit*)—(Dabhiti's) chamberlain holding a staff; अत्र (*atra*)—in this battle; हिरण्यं (*hiraṇyaṃ*)—the wealth (of the Asuras); विविदे (*vivide*)—obtained. सोमस्य (*somasya*)—by drinking soma juice; मदे (*made*)—when exhilaration arose; इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra; ता (*tā*)—these great deeds; चकार (*cakāra*)—did.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, you have joined the violent Asura named Chumuri and the Asura named Dhuni with long sleep. You have fully protected the royal sage named Dabhiti. Dabhiti's chamberlain holding a staff obtained the wealth of the Asuras in this battle. When exhilaration arose from the drinking of soma juice, Indra did these great deeds.

**English Translation** *(as printed; continues on the next page)*

You have slain the Dasyus, Chumuri and Dhuni, having cast them into(profound) sleep: you have protected Dabhiti, whilst his chamberlain

### Printed p. 772

*(Header: "772", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 2 A. 2 Sū. 15".)*

gained in that(contest) the gold(of the Asuras); in the exhilaration of the Soma, Indra has done these(deeds).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

स्वप्नेन अभ्युप्य चुमुरिं धुनिं च जघंथ दस्युं (*svapnena abhyupya chumuriṃ dhuniṃ ca jaghaṃtha dasyuṃ*)—O Indra, Indra is praised as having, to protect the royal sage named Dabhiti, made the Asuras Chamuri and Dhuni, together with their soldiers, sleep-bound (stupefied) on the battlefield. We have explained this matter at length on pages 551–552 of Volume 10.

रंभी चित् (*raṃbhī cit*)—वेत्रधारी चास्य दौवारिकोऽत्रास्मिन्युद्धे तयोरसुरयोर्हि-रण्यं धनं विविदे लेभे (*vetradhārī cāsya dauvāriko 'trāsminyuddhe tayorasurayorhi-raṇyaṃ dhanaṃ vivide lebhe*). Here, for the word रंभी (*raṃbhī*), Sāyaṇa has given the meaning *vetradhārī*, that is, one holding a cane in his hand: Dabhiti's servant or doorkeeper. The main purport is that after Indra had defeated the Asuras Chumuri and Dhuni in the battle, Dabhiti's servant seized their wealth and so on on Dabhiti's behalf. *(The sentence is printed without its final verb, as supplied.)*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, that donation given by you, possessing abundant wealth, assuredly fulfils the desired object of the sacrificer who praises you, in an excellent manner. That opulent donation which proceeds, Indra, from you, assuredly bestows npon [sic] him who praises you the boon(that he desires): grant it to(us) your adorers: do not yon [sic], who are the object of adoration, disregard our prayers; so that, blessed with worthy descendants, we may glorify you at this sacrifice.

## Sūkta 16

*(Printed title: "ಹದಿನಾರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು" — "The sixteenth sūkta".)*

**Sāyaṇa's introduction (Sanskrit, printed as running prose in the supplied text):** it begins प्र वः सतां (*pra vaḥ satāṃ*) and names the sūkta as the fifth, of nine Ṛks, Gārtsamada, to Indra; it quotes the Anukramaṇikā प्र वो नवांत्या त्रिष्टुब् (*pra vo navāṃtyā triṣṭub*), says the ninth is Triṣṭubh and the rest Jagatī, and that in the third paryāya of the Atirātra the Acchāvāka's śastra uses the sūkta प्र वः सतां (*pra vaḥ satāṃ*); the Āśvalāyana sūtra in the khaṇḍa Atirātra is quoted: प्र वः सतां प्रो द्रोणे हरयः कर्माग्मन्निति याज्या (*pra vaḥ satāṃ pro droṇe harayaḥ karmāgmanniti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-4).

**Anuvāda**

The Kannada: "This sūkta, प्र वः सतां (*pra vaḥ satāṃ*), is the fifth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has nine Ṛks. Gṛtsamada is the ṛṣi; Indra is the deity. Since the Anukramaṇikā says प्र वो नवांत्या त्रिष्टुप् (*pra vo navāṃtyā triṣṭup*), the last Ṛk of this sūkta, the ninth, is in the Triṣṭup metre; the remaining Ṛks are in Jagatī. The application of this sūkta is for the śastra mantras to be recited by the priest called Acchāvāka in the third paryāya of the sacrifice called Atirātra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the khaṇḍa called Atirātra, प्र वः सतां प्रो द्रोणे हरयः कर्माग्मन्निति याज्या (*pra vaḥ satāṃ pro droṇe harayaḥ karmāgmanniti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-4)."

*(Two Oṃ lines are printed, "॥ ಓಂ ॥" and "॥ ಒಂ ॥", as supplied.)*

**सूक्त—16**

॥ मंडल—2 ॥ अनुवाक—2 ॥ सूक्त—16 ॥
॥ अष्टक—2 ॥ अध्याय—6 ॥ वर्ग—17, 18 ॥

Number of Ṛks in the sūkta—9. Ṛṣi—Gaitsamada [as printed]. Devatā—Indra. Chandas—Ṛks 1 to 8 Jagatī; 9 Triṣṭup. *(Printed "೦-೮ ಜಗತೀ", the first numeral as supplied.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(O sacrificers) vaḥ—on your behalf; satāṃ—among the great gods; jyeṣṭhatamāya—to Indra, the most excellent; samidhāne—blazing; agnāviva—in the fire itself; haviḥ—the oblation; pra bhare—I offer; suṣṭutiṃ—excellent praise also I offer. ajuryaṃ—himself free from decay (but); jarayantaṃ—making all others decay; ukṣitaṃ—sprinkled with soma juice (the soma-drinker); sanāt—ancient; yuvānaṃ—ever young; indraṃ—Indra; avase—for protection; havāmahe—we call.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O sacrificers, for you I offer the oblation into the blazing fire for Indra, the most excellent among the great gods, and in the same way I recite praise. We call for protection Indra, who is free from decay, who makes others decay, who is sprinkled with soma juice, ancient and ever young.

### Printed p. 776

**Printed English translation (Ṛk 1)**

I bear the libation for you to the best of the holy(gods, to be poured) on the kindled fire,(and I offer to him fitting praise): we invoke for(our) protection the ever-youthful Indra, the undecaying, the causer cf [sic] decay, sprinkled(with the Soma libation).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)** *(heading printed "ವಿಶೇಷವಿವರಗಳು")*

वः सतां ज्येष्ठतमाय अग्नाविव समिधाने हविः प्र भरे (*vaḥ satāṃ jyeṣṭhatamāya agnāviva samidhāne haviḥ pra bhare*)—the bhāṣya says: "O sacrificers, for your sake I prepare the oblation in the very blazing fire for Indra, the best of the great gods." In Kannada: "O sacrificers, for you I offer the oblation into the kindled fire, addressed to Indra, the best of all the gods," says the ṛṣi Gṛtsamada. On Indra's being the best of all the gods:

अयग्ं राजा जगतश्चर्षणीनां । स एव वीरः स उ वीर्यावान् । स एक राजो जगतः परस्पाः (*ayagṃ rājā jagataścarṣaṇīnāṃ | sa eva vīraḥ sa u vīryāvān | sa eka rājo jagataḥ paraspāḥ*) ... अथैकराजो अभवज्जनानां (*athaikarājo abhavajjanānāṃ*) ... इंद्रो देवानामभवत्पुरोगाः (*iṃdro devānāmabhavatpurogāḥ*) (Tai. Brā. 2-8-3-21-22; "ಪರಸ್ಪಾಃ" as supplied)

इंद्रो ना अकामयत । जैष्ठ्यं देवानामभिजयेयमिति (*iṃdro nā akāmayata | jaiṣṭhyaṃ devānāmabhijayeyamiti*) (Tai. Brā. 3-1-5-2; "ನಾ" as supplied)

In passages such as these it is stated that Indra is the best of the gods.

अजुर्यं जरयंतं (*ajuryaṃ jarayaṃtaṃ*)—the bhāṣya: अजरणीयं सर्वमन्यज्जरयंतं (*ajaraṇīyaṃ sarvamanyajjarayaṃtaṃ*). Indra alone is free from decay and free from the changes of age such as old age, but he makes the lives of other beings wane. That is, unlike other beings he is not subject to time; he is always of one condition, ever young: this is the main idea. The use of the words सनात् (*sanāt*) (*sanāt*), "ancient, always existing", and युवानं (*yuvānaṃ*) (*yuvānaṃ*), "ever young, always in the state of youth", in this verse makes this idea clear.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

bṛhataḥ—of great nature; yasmāt indrāt ṛte—without which Indra; īṃ—this world; kiṃcana—would not have existed at all; asmin—in that Indra; viśvāni vīryā—all powers; adhi saṃbhṛtā—are gathered; jaṭhare—in the belly; somaṃ—soma juice; bharati—(Indra) carries filled; tanvi—in his body; sahaḥ—strength; mahaḥ—brilliance (he bears); haste—in the hand; vajraṃ—the thunderbolt (he holds); śīrṣaṇi—in the head; kratuṃ—knowledge, he has obtained.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Without that Indra of great nature this world would not have existed at all; in that Indra all powers are gathered. Indra has filled his belly with soma juice. In his body he bears strength and brilliance. In his hand he holds the thunderbolt. In his head he has obtained knowledge.

### Printed p. 778

*(Header: "778 Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā । Maṃ. 2 A. 2. Sū. 16."; the supplied text reads "ಗಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ" for "ಸಾಯಣ…".)*

**Printed English translation (Ṛk 2)**

For without that mighty Indra, this(world) were nothing: in him all powers whatever are aggregated: he receives the Soma juice into his stomach, and in his body(exhibits) strength and energy: he bears the thunderbolt in his hand, and wisdom in his head.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)** *(heading printed "ವಿಶೇಷವಿವರಗಳು")*

यस्मात् बृहतः इंद्रात् ऋते किं ईं चन (*yasmāt bṛhataḥ iṃdrāt ṛte kiṃ īṃ cana*)—Apart from this greatly glorious Indra, that is, if Indra were not there, this world would not exist, or nothing would exist; or, before Indra's great glory how much is this small world? Two meanings are given. The main idea is that this world has been made by Indra; Indra is the cause of this world. For:

विश्वानि अस्मिन् संभृता अधि वीर्या (*viśvāni asmin saṃbhṛtā adhi vīryā*)—the bhāṣya: अस्मिन्निंद्रे सर्वाणि सामर्थ्य्यन्यधि अधिकं संभृतान्यासते (*asminniṃdre sarvāṇi sāmarthyyanyadhi adhikaṃ saṃbhṛtānyāsate*) (spelling as supplied). In this Indra alone all powers and capacities are concentrated. Since all powers are abundantly filled in Indra, there is no room for the world or for other things to exist without Indra. On this the Śruti passage केंद्रादृते पवते धाम किं चन (*keṃdrādṛte pavate dhāma kiṃ cana*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-69-6) is cited. [The supplied text prints केंद्रादृते (*keṃdrādṛte*) here, whereas the bhāṣya of this Ṛk quotes नेंद्रादृते (*neṃdrādṛte*); noted, not changed.] The main idea is that everything proceeds from Indra's glory, that is, from his powers and capacities.

In the second half of this Ṛk Indra's form is described. Indra has filled his belly with soma juice, bears strength and brilliance in his body, holds the thunderbolt in his hand, and bears knowledge in his head (that is, in the brain); that is, Indra's intelligence is superior. The main idea is that Indra's powers and capacities, such as these, are surpassing.

चन (*cana*)—This word consists of the two particles च (*ca*) and न (*na*). च (*ca*) indicates चित् (*cit*), and न (*na*) the sense of negation. Hence the word चन (*cana*) means "not at all".

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist: Indra's strength cannot be overcome by heaven and earth, his chariot cannot be stopped by oceans or mountains, and no one can withstand his thunderbolt when he travels many leagues to slay the asuras. Grammatical tail on the suffix and the accent of paribhve and on the root aś.*

> हे इंद्र ते तवेंद्रियं बलं क्षोणीभ्यां द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां न परिभ्ये ।
> न परिभवनीयं ॥ कृत्यार्थे तवैकेन्नेन्यत्वन इति केन्प्रत्ययः । उदात्तस्वरितॆयोरिति
> स्वरितत्वं ॥ किंच ते रथः समुद्रॆः पर्वतैश्च न परिभवनीयः । ते वज्रमायुधं
> कश्चन पुमान् नान्वश्योति । न व्याप्प्नोति परिभवितुं ॥ अशू व्याप्त् । व्यत्ययेन
> पस्मैपदं ॥ यद्यदासुरवधार्थं दिग्विजयकाले पुरु पुरूणि बहूनि योजना यो-
> जनानि पतसि । गच्छसि । तदा तव बलादि न परिभवनीयमिति समन्वयः ॥

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra; ते (*te*)—your; इंद्रियं (*iṃdriyaṃ*)—might; क्षोणीभ्यां (*kṣoṇībhyāṃ*)—by heaven and earth; न परिभ्वे (*na paribhve*)—cannot be surpassed; ते (*te*)—your; रथः (*rathaḥ*)—chariot; समुद्रैः (*samudraiḥ*)—by oceans; पर्वतैः (*parvataiḥ*)—by mountains; न (*na*)—cannot be stopped; यत् (*yat*)—when (for the conquest of the quarters); आशुभिः (*āśubhiḥ*)—with your swift horses; पुरु (*puru*)—many; योजना (*yojanā*)—leagues; पतसि (*patasi*)—you traverse (then); ते (*te*)—your; वज्रं (*vajraṃ*)—thunderbolt; कश्चन (*kaścana*)—any asura or human enemy; न अन्वश्नोति (*na anvaśnoti*)—is not able to withstand.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, your might cannot be surpassed even by heaven and earth. Your chariot cannot be stopped by oceans or by mountains. When you set out with your swift horses to conquer the quarters and cross many leagues, no asura or human enemy is able to withstand your thunderbolt.

### Printed p. 780

*(Header: "780 Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [Maṃ. 2 A. 2. Sū. 16]".)*

**Printed English translation (Ṛk 3)**

Thy might, Indra, is not to be overcome by(that of) heaven and earth; nor is you ohariot [sic] (to be stopped) by oceans or by mountains: no one can escape from your thunderbolt, when yon [sic] traverse many leagues with rapid(horses).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

This Ṛk describes Indra's extraordinary strength and power. The ṛṣi has explained it clearly.

न क्षोणीभ्यां परिभ्ये त इंद्रियं (*na kṣoṇībhyāṃ paribhye ta iṃdriyaṃ*)—हे इंद्र तव बलं द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां न (*he iṃdra tava balaṃ dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ na*) परिभवनीयं । (*paribhavanīyaṃ |*) O Indra, your strength is not surpassed even by heaven and earth (earth and sky). That is, the purport is that your strength is greater than the strength possessed by heaven and earth. The word क्षोणिः (*kṣoṇiḥ*) is read among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5). But since the dual क्षोणीभ्यां (*kṣoṇībhyāṃ*) is used in this passage, the bhāṣyakāra has explained the word as heaven and earth. The word क्षोणि (*kṣoṇi*) is formed from the root टुक्षु रुक्षु शब्दे (*ṭukṣu rukṣu śabde*) (adādi, parasmaipada) [spelling as supplied]. क्षूयते शब्दते, स्तूयते स्तोतृभिः । कुवंत्यस्यां भूतानीति वा । (*kṣūyate śabdate, stūyate stotṛbhiḥ | kuvaṃtyasyāṃ bhūtānīti vā |*) क्षोणीति ईकारांतं केचित् पठंति । (*kṣoṇīti īkārāṃtaṃ kecit paṭhaṃti |*) Because it is praised by the singers, or because creatures make sound upon it, the earth is called kṣoṇi. The word is read both as क्षोणिः (*kṣoṇiḥ*) ending in i and as क्षोणी (*kṣoṇī*) ending in ī. In the present Ṛk the form ending in ī is used.

इंद्रियं (*iṃdriyaṃ*)—बलं । (*balaṃ |*) This is Sāyaṇa's explanation: strength. The word इंद्रिय (*iṃdriya*) is read among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9). But here the bhāṣyakāra gives the meaning strength. For the word इंद्रिय (*iṃdriya*) there is the sūtra sentence—

इंद्रियमिंद्रलिंगमिंद्रदृष्टमिंद्रसृष्टमिंद्रजुष्टमिंद्रदत्तमिति वा । (*iṃdriyamiṃdraliṃgamiṃdradṛṣṭamiṃdrasṛṣṭamiṃdrajuṣṭamiṃdradattamiti vā |*) (5-3-93). This word is formed from the root इदि पुमैश्वर्ये (*idi pumaiśvarye*) (bhū., parasmaipada) [as supplied]—इंद्रस्य लिंगं । धनेन हि ऐश्वर्ययुक्त इति व्यज्यते । (*iṃdrasya liṃgaṃ | dhanena hi aiśvaryayukta iti vyajyate |*) That which is endowed with lordship; that is, indriya means wealth. यद्वा इंद्रेण दृष्टं इंद्रियं । (*yadvā iṃdreṇa dṛṣṭaṃ iṃdriyaṃ |*) A thing seen by Indra is called indriya. यद्वा इंद्र आत्मा तत्कृतेन शुभाशुभेन (*yadvā iṃdra ātmā tatkṛtena śubhāśubhena*) कर्मणा सृष्टं । (*karmaṇā sṛṣṭaṃ |*) Indra means the self (ātman); the fruit, in the form of good and bad action, made by the self, is called indriya. इंद्रजुष्टं ना आत्मना सेवितं तद्दारेण भोगोत्पत्तेः । (*iṃdrajuṣṭaṃ nā ātmanā sevitaṃ taddāreṇa bhogotpatteḥ |*) What is served by the self; that is, the means of enjoyment and the like arising from the actions one has done. This too is called indriya. इंद्रदत्तं वा इंद्रेण पूर्वकर्मणा वा अस्तुपदत्तं । (*iṃdradattaṃ vā iṃdreṇa pūrvakarmaṇā vā astupadattaṃ |*) What is given by Indra, or by Indra's

### Printed p. 781

*(Header: "[A. 2. A. 6. V. 17.] Ṛgvedasaṃhitā 781".)*

or his own earlier action, is called indriya. Thus the word इंद्रिय (*iṃdriya*) has various meanings. In modern Sanskrit the word indriya conveys the sense of bodily power (power arising from the senses or the limbs of the body). There is the nigama passage ओजो बलमिंद्रियं वीर्यं (*ojo balamiṃdriyaṃ vīryaṃ*).

इंद्र ते रथः समुद्रॆः पर्वतैः न(परिभ्वे) (*iṃdra te rathaḥ samudrèḥ parvataiḥ na(paribhve)*)—The chariots ordinarily used by men travel only on easy roads. If there are obstacles on the way, such as rivers, reservoirs and mountains, they cannot cross them and stop. But neither ocean nor mountain can obstruct Indra's chariot. It has an unobstructed power of movement; whatever obstacle comes, it can remove it and go forward. The ṛṣi describes the greatness of the chariot as this very distinction of Indra's chariot.

ते वज्रं न कश्चन अनु अश्नोति (*te vajraṃ na kaścana anu aśnoti*)—O Indra, just like the power of your chariot, your thunderbolt too has extraordinary power. The main idea is that no man is able to face the blow of this thunderbolt.

यत् आशुभिः पतसि योजना पुरु (*yat āśubhiḥ patasi yojanā puru*)—यद्यदासुरवधार्थं दिग्विजयकाले (*yadyadāsuravadhārthaṃ digvijayakāle*) बहूनि योजनानि गच्छसि तदा तव बलादि न परिभवनीयमिति समन्वयः । (*bahūni yojanāni gacchasi tadā tava balādi na paribhavanīyamiti samanvayaḥ |*) O Indra, all the things said above happen when you go many leagues with your horses to slay the asuras. That is, when you travel many leagues with your famous horses called Harī for the conquest of the quarters, neither oceans nor mountains, nothing at all, causes an obstacle to your chariot. Your chariot goes passing over everything; your strength is greater than that of heaven and earth; your thunderbolt has no rival. This is the main idea of this Ṛk.

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> विश्वे॒ ह्य॑स्मै यज॒ताय॑ धृ॒ष्णवे॒ क्रतुं॒ भरं॑ति वृष॒भाय॒ सश्च॑ते ।
> वृषा॑ यजस्व ह॒विषा॑ वि॒दुष्ट॑रः॒ पिबें॑द्र॒ सोमं॑ वृष॒भेण॑ भा॒नुना॑ ॥ ४ ॥

> *viśve hyasmai yajatāya dhṛṣṇave kratuṃ bharaṃti vṛṣabhāya saścate |*
> *vṛṣā yajasva haviṣā viduṣṭaraḥ pibeṃdra somaṃ vṛṣabheṇa bhānunā ‖ 4 ‖*

### Printed p. 782

*(Header: "782 Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [Maṃ. 2 A. 2. Sū. 16]".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> विश्वे । हि । अस्मै । यजताय । धृष्णवे । क्रतुं । भरंति । वृषभाय । सश्चते ।
> वृषा । यजस्व । हविषा । विदुःतरः । पिब । इंद्र । सोमं । वृषभेण । भानुना ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist: the many (men) perform the sacrifice for Indra, the adorable, bold showerer of wishes; so the sacrificer, a showerer of Soma and most wise, should worship him with oblations; and Indra is bidden to drink the Soma together with the radiant Agni. Grammatical tail on bharanti (unaccented by hi), viduṣṭaraḥ (Vedic samprasāraṇa and the change to ṣ) and the like.*

> हे यजमान विश्वे सर्वे जना यजताय सर्वैर्यजनीयाय धृष्णवे
> शत्रूणां धर्षणशीलाय वृषभाय कामानां वर्षित्रॆ सश्चते सज्जमानाय स्तुत्यादि-
> कर्मवत्तु स्तोतृषु एतादृशायेंद्राय क्रतुं यज्ञादिलक्षणं कर्म भरंति हि ।
> हरंति खलु । प्रणयंतीत्यर्थः ॥ भरंति । हियोगादनिघातः ॥ यस्मादेवं तस्मा-
> द्वृषा सोमरससेचनसमर्थो विदुष्टरः ॥ विद्वच्छब्धात्तरपि छांदसं संप्रसारणं ।
> शासिवसिघसीनां चेति संहितायां षत्वं ॥ विद्वत्तरस्तं हविषा तमिंद्रं यजस्व ।
> इदानीमिंद्रं संबोध्याह । हे इंद्र वृषभेण कामानां वर्षकेण भानुना दीप्य-
> मानेनाग्निना सह सोमं पिब ॥

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(O sacrificer) viśve (विश्वे (*viśve*))—all men; yajatāya (यजताय (*yajatāya*))—worthy of sacrifice; dhṛṣṇave (धृष्णवे (*dhṛṣṇave*))—destroyer of enemies; vṛṣabhāya (वृषभाय (*vṛṣabhāya*))—giver of what is wished; saścate (सश्चते (*saścate*))—associated with praise and the like; asmai (अस्मै (*asmai*))—to (for) Indra; kratuṃ (क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*))—sacrificial rites; bharanti hi (भरंति हि (*bharaṃti hi*))—certainly perform (therefore). vṛṣā (वृषा (*vṛṣā*))—able to offer the Soma juice; viduṣvaraḥ [sic, as supplied] (विदुष्वरः (*viduṣvaraḥ*))—wise; you also; haviṣā (हविषा (*haviṣā*))—with oblations; yajasva (यजस्व (*yajasva*))—worship (Indra). indra (इंद्र (*iṃdra*))—O Indra; vṛṣabheṇa (वृषभेण (*vṛṣabheṇa*))—shedding (pouring out) the things wished; bhānunā (भानुना (*bhānunā*))—with the radiant Agni; somaṃ (सोमं (*somaṃ*))—the Soma juice; piba (पिब (*piba*))—drink.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O sacrificer, all men perform sacrificial rites for Indra, who is worthy of sacrifice, a destroyer of enemies, a giver of what is wished, and associated with praise and the like. Therefore do you also worship Indra with oblations. O Indra, drink the Soma juice together with the radiant Agni, who showers what is wished.

### Printed p. 783

*(Header: "[A. 2. A. 6. V. 17.] Ṛgvedasaṃhitā 783".)*

**Printed English translation (Ṛk 4)**

All men offer worship to that adorable, powerful, and munificent (Indra), who is associated (with praise): therefore, (do you), who are liberal and most wise, worship him with oblations; and drink, Indra, the Soma, together with Agni, the showerer (of benefits).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

This Ṛk has two main sentences. In the first the sacrificer is addressed and told to offer oblations to Indra; in the second Indra is addressed and prayed to drink, together with Agni, the Soma juice offered by the sacrificer.

In this Ṛk and in several following Ṛks the words वृषभाय (*vṛṣabhāya*), वृषा (*vṛṣā*), वृषभेण (*vṛṣabheṇa*) and the like are used. Since these words are formed from the root वृषु-सेचने (*vṛṣu-secane*) (bhvādi, parasmaipada), the general sense can be given as "able to shed (pour)", that is, as the rain pours water abundantly, so one who pours out things wished for and the like. The meaning must be taken so as to suit each context and not to conflict with the sense of the root. Thus, since the word वृषभाय (*vṛṣabhāya*) in this Ṛk is an epithet of Indra, the meaning कामानां वर्षित्रे (*kāmānāṃ varṣitre*), "one who showers what is wished (that is, gives specially)", is given; since the word वृषा (*vṛṣā*) is an epithet of the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice, the meaning "one who sheds (pours) the Soma juice, that is, the sacrificer who presses and prepares the Soma juice" is given; and since the word वृषभेण (*vṛṣabheṇa*) is an epithet of the word भानुना (*bhānunā*), the meaning "by Agni, who showers things wished, as said before" is given, each explained so as to fit its context.

विदुष्टरः (*viduṣṭaraḥ*)—विद्वत्तरः। विदुषां श्रेष्ठतमः । (*vidvattaraḥ| viduṣāṃ śreṣṭhatamaḥ |*) The best among the wise; that is, one who knows everything, a discerning person, is the sense.

भानुना (*bhānunā*)—The word भानु (*bhānu*), formed from the root भा दीप्तौ (*bhā dīptau*) (adādi, parasmaipada), is read among the names of the day (Ni. 2-21). But since the word भानु (*bhānu*) means "shining", two meanings can be given: the shining sun, or Agni. Here, as Indra's association with Agni is the greater, the meaning of भानुना (*bhānunā*) as "together with Agni" is fitting.

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> वृष्णः॒ कोशः॑ पवते॒ मध्व॑ ऊ॒र्मिवृ॑ष॒भान्ना॑य वृष॒भाय॒ पात॑वे ।
> वृष॑णाद्व॒यू वृ॑ष॒भासो॒ अद्र॑यो॒ वृष॑णं॒ सोमं॑ वृष॒भाय॑ सुष्वति ॥ ५ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> वृष्णः । कोशः । पवते । मध्वः । ऊर्मिः । वृषभअन्नाय । वृषभाय । पातवे ।
> वृषणा । अध्वर्यू इति । वृषभासः । अद्रयः । वृषणं । सोमं । वृषभाय । सुस्वति॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist: for Indra the showerer, the Soma juice flows, quickening sacrificers and drinkers; the two Adhvaryus and the pressing-stones press the Soma for Indra, the best of gods. Grammatical tail on the root pav (accent), and on suṣvati (śluḥ, and ra for da).*

> हे इंद्र वृष्णः फलस्य वर्षितुर्मध्वो मदकरस्य सोमस्य कोशो रस
> ऊर्मिरनुष्ठात्कृणां पात्कणां च प्रेरकः सन् पवते । गच्छति ॥ पव गतौ । अनुदा-
> त्तेत् ॥ किमर्थं । वृषभान्नाय । बलवर्षकाण्यन्नानि यस्य स तथोक्तः । तादृशाय
> वृषभाय कामानां वर्षित्र इंद्राय पातवे । पानार्थं पवत इति समन्वयः । किंच
> वृषणा सोमरससेचनसमर्थावध्वर्यू अध्वर्युप्रतिप्रस्थातारौ वृषभासो वर्षका
> अद्रयोऽभिषवग्रावाणश्च वृषणं स्वर्गादिफलस्य सेक्तारं सोमं वृषभाय देवानां
> श्रेष्ठाय तुभ्यं सुष्वति । सुन्वंति ॥ सुनोतेर्लटि बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य श्लुः ।
> अदभ्यस्तादिति रोऽदादेशः ॥

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(Indra—O Indra) vṛṣaḥ (वृषः (*vṛṣaḥ*))—giving fruit; madhvaḥ (मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*))—intoxicating; of the Soma; kośaḥ (कोशः (*kośaḥ*))—the juice; ūrmiḥ (ऊर्मिः (*ūrmiḥ*))—being a stimulant to the performers of the rite and to those who drink; vṛṣabhānnāya (वृषभान्नाय (*vṛṣabhānnāya*))—one who has strength-increasing food; vṛṣabhāya (वृषभाय (*vṛṣabhāya*))—and a showerer of things wished, of you; pātave (पातवे (*pātave*))—for drinking; pavate (पवते (*pavate*))—flows. vṛṣaṇā (वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*))—able to press the Soma juice; adhvaryū (अध्वर्यू (*adhvaryū*))—the Adhvaryu and the Pratiprasthātṛ, both; vṛṣabhāsaḥ (वृषभासः (*vṛṣabhāsaḥ*))—serving as means of pressing the juice; adrayaḥ (अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*))—the pressing-stones (stones for pressing); vṛ. ṣaṇaṃ [sic, as supplied: "ವ. ಷಣಂ"] (व. षणं (*va. ṣaṇaṃ*))—giving the fruit of heaven and the like; somaṃ (सोमं (*somaṃ*))—the Soma juice; vṛṣabhāya (वृषभाय (*vṛṣabhāya*))—for you, the best among all the gods; suṣvati (सुष्वति (*suṣvati*))—they press.

### Printed p. 785

*(Header: "[A. 2. A. 6. V. 17.] Ṛgvedasaṃhitā 785".)*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, this Soma juice, fruit-giving and exhilarating, flows for your drinking, being a stimulant to the sacrificers and to those who drink it, you who have strength-increasing food and who shower what is wished. The Adhvaryu and the Pratiprasthātṛ, both able to press out the juice, and the pressing-stones (rocks), the instruments of pressing, press for you, the best of all the gods, the Soma juice that gives heaven and the like.

**Printed English translation (Ṛk 5)**

The juice of the gratifying and exhilarating(Soma), the exciter(of) those who drink it, flows to the showerer(of benefits), the dispenser of food, for his beverage: the two priests, the sprinklers of the oblation; and the stones(that express the juice), offer to the best(of the deities), the Soma, the shedder(of blessings).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

The page opens with the Sanskrit explanation of the Ṛk's words (the same sense as the bhāṣya above) followed by a Kannada rendering. The Kannada says: the juice of the Soma creeper, when the creeper is crushed and pressed with the stones, comes out little by little and gathers together at the bottom of the stone (adri); it gives delight to those who press the creeper and to those who drink. The sage describes such a juice as being prepared for Indra's drinking. The word कोशः (*kośaḥ*) in this passage denotes the large vessel in which the Soma juice is collected and kept; it is made of wood or of leather, and the Soma juice, pressed and strained, is poured into it. But in the present Ṛk the word कोशः (*kośaḥ*) (the container) is itself used to indicate the Soma juice that fills it. पवते (*pavate*): root पव गतौ (*pava gatau*) ("pava, in the sense of going"): "goes" means that the Soma juice coming out of the crushed creeper runs and flows. वृषभान्नाय (*vṛṣabhānnāya*) is explained in Sanskrit as "he whose foods increase strength"; that is, for Indra who has strength-increasing food, or who gives food, for his drinking.

The next Sanskrit passage explains अध्वर्यू (*adhvaryū*) and अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*): the two (Adhvaryu and Pratiprasthātṛ) are able to sprinkle (pour) the Soma juice, and the pressing-stones (ग्रावाणः (*grāvāṇaḥ*)) shower; they press the Soma, the sprinkler of the fruit such as heaven, for you, the best of the gods. The Kannada then says (continued on p. 786): the officiating priests called Adhvaryu and Pratiprasthātṛ, who are able or skilful in pressing the Soma juice, and the stones that help in the pressing, press the wished-for Soma juice for Indra and make it ready, this being the meaning. Since the dual अध्वर्यू (*adhvaryū*) is used here, it must be understood to indicate the two priests, the Adhvaryu and his helper the Pratiprasthātṛ. When the Soma is pressed and prepared for Indra, the stones called अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*) or ग्रावाणः (*grāvāṇaḥ*), used in the pressing, are likewise helpful to the priests who can press it. With their help the priests press the Soma juice and prepare it for Indra; this is the main purport.

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> वृषा॑ ते॒ वज्र॑ उ॒त ते॒ वृषा॒ रथो॒ वृष॑णा॒ हरी॑ वृष॒भाण्यायु॑धा ।
> वृष्टो॒ मद॑स्य वृषभ॒ त्वमी॑शिष॒ इंद्र॒ सोम॑स्य वृष॒भस्य॑ तृप्लुहि ॥ ६ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> वृषा । ते । वज्रः । उत । ते । वृषा । रथः । वृषणा । हरी इति । वृषभाणि । आयुधा ।
> वृष्णः । मदस्य । वृषभ । त्वं । ईशिषे । इंद्र । सोमस्य । वृषभस्य । तृप्नुहि ॥ ६ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist: Indra's thunderbolt, chariot, two horses and other weapons are all "showerers" of wishes; he is lord of the Soma and is bidden to be satisfied with it. Grammatical tail on the root tṛp (the cerebral ṇ-rule, Pā. 8-4-39, as printed, being optional in the Veda).*

> स्वामी भवसि । हे इंद्र वृषभस्य वर्षकेण सोमस्य सोमेन तृप्लुहि । तृप्तो भव॥
> तृप प्रीणने स्वादिः । क्षुभ्यादिषु । पा. ८-४-३९ । नृमनतृप्नोतीति पठितं । तथापि

### Printed p. 787

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)—O Indra, giver of what is wished. ते (*te*)—your. वज्रः (*vajraḥ*)—thunderbolt. वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—it is a showerer of desires. उत (*uta*)—and. ते (*te*)—your. रथः (*rathaḥ*)—chariot also. वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—a showerer of desires. हरी (*harī*)—your horses called Hari. वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—are able to shower fruit. आयुधा (*āyudhā*)—the other weapons. वृषभाणि (*vṛṣabhāṇi*)—are capable. वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)—showering. मदस्य (*madasya*)—and intoxicating, to the Soma. त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you yourself. ईशिषे (*īśiṣe*)—are the lord. इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra. वृषभस्य (*vṛṣabhasya*)—having the capacity to sprinkle. सोमस्य (*somasya*)—with the drinking of the Soma. तृप्नुहि (*tṛpnuhi*)—be satisfied.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, giver of what is wished, your thunderbolt is a showerer of desires, and your chariot also is a showerer of desires. Your horses called Hari are able to shower fruit. In the same way your other weapons are powerful. You yourself are the lord of the Soma that showers and intoxicates. O Indra, be satisfied by drinking the Soma that has the capacity to sprinkle.

**Printed English translation (Ṛk 6)**

Your thunderbolt, Indra, is the rainer(of bounties): your chariot, the showerer(of blessings); your two horses, the shedders(of desires); your weapons, the diffusers(of wishes); you reign, showerer(of benefits), over the inebriating beverage, the sprinkler(of delight):satiate yourself, Indra, with the good-diffusing Soma.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this Ṛk the sage describes Indra's thunderbolt, his chariot, his two horses called हरी (*harī*), and his other weapons (apart from the thunderbolt) as all granting the wished-for fruit to those who praise him; and then, "You, such an Indra, are lord also of the Soma juice that gives every fruit. Therefore drink this excellent Soma juice which we have pressed and prepared, and be satisfied": thus the sage prays to Indra.

*Notes on the text as supplied (not corrected):* the Saṃhitā and the bhāṣya quotation read तृप्लुहि (*tṛpluhi*) while the Pada and the Pratipadārtha read तृप्नुहि (*tṛpnuhi*); the Saṃhitā reads वृष्टो (*vṛṣṭo*) where the Pada has वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*) and the bhāṣya वृष्णो (*vṛṣṇo*); the Bhāvārtha and Special Topics headings on p. 785 were garbled in the supplied text (labels only, repaired); the bhāṣya has त्वमेदेशिषे (*tvamedeśiṣe*) (as supplied; the Pada and Pratipadārtha have ईशिषे (*īśiṣe*)).
